docs.title: DB2 Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The DB2 Discovery addon monitors IBM Db2 databases remotely. A Discovery task connects to each database you list and turns the result into Pandora FMS agents and modules: connection availability, database performance summary, transaction log utilization, database size, active connections and buffer pool cache statistics. It can also run your own read-only SELECT queries and publish their result as modules.

A Discovery task generates one agent per target database. Nothing is installed on the database server: the addon connects over TCP/IP from the Discovery server with a database user and password.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.db2, version 1.2 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the Discovery server to each Db2 listener (TCP, default port 50000) Required The addon connects with the TCP/IP protocol A Db2 user with the grants listed in Database user Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement Db2 server versions and platforms Not validated No Db2 version matrix has been recorded for this addon Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to every Db2 listener you want to monitor.
  2. A database user and password for the databases, with the grants described below. The same user and password are used for every target of the task.
  3. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it.

No IBM Db2 client has to be installed on the Discovery server.

docs.title: Database user
docs.text:
Each option reads Db2 administrative views, so the user needs SELECT access to the views of the options you enable. When a query is refused, the addon reports an error that asks you to verify the grants (see Troubleshoot).

Option Db2 view read Always SYSIBMADM.ENV_INST_INFO (instance service level, shown as the agent operating system version) Get database summary SYSIBMADM.MON_DB_SUMMARY Check transactional log utilization SYSIBMADM.MON_TRANSACTION_LOG_UTILIZATION Check DB size SYSIBMADM.ADMINTABINFO Get number of connections SYSIBMADM.MON_CONNECTION_SUMMARY Retrieve cache statistics SYSIBMADM.BP_HITRATIO Execute custom queries Whatever objects your own queries read

No official source identifies a narrower set of privileges than these reads; grant only what the options you enable need.

The password is written to the task's temporary configuration file on the Discovery server while the task runs. Use a dedicated user for Pandora FMS.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.db2

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, DB2 is available when creating Discovery tasks of the application type.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task and choose DB2. The console presents the fields in two steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. DB2 Base — targets and credentials:

    • DB2 target strings: the databases to monitor, one SERVER:PORT/DATABASE per entry, separated by commas or one per line. Lines starting with # are comments. See Target format.
    • User and Password: the Db2 credentials. Both are required.

  2. DB2 Detailed — execution and what to collect:

    • Max threads: how many targets are processed in parallel.
    • Target agent: names for the generated agents.
    • Custom module prefix: text added in front of every module name.
    • Get database summary, Check transactional log utilization, Get number of connections, Check DB size and Retrieve cache statistics: enable each group of modules. All are enabled by default.
    • Execute custom queries and Custom queries: run your own queries. The text box is shown when Execute custom queries is enabled. See Custom queries.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to the agents the task creates.

docs.title: Target format
docs.text:
Each target identifies a host, optionally a port, and a database:

Form Host Port Database <HOST>:<PORT>/<DATABASE> <HOST> <PORT> <DATABASE> <HOST>/<DATABASE> <HOST> 50000 <DATABASE>

A database name is required to connect. A target without one (<HOST> or <HOST>:<PORT>) is accepted but cannot connect, so its agent reports DB2 connection as 0.

Example for two targets:

# Production
<DB2_HOST_1>:50000/<DATABASE_1>, <DB2_HOST_2>/<DATABASE_2>

docs.title: Agent names
docs.text: By default the agent is named after its target string, for example <HOST>:<PORT>/<DATABASE>. To choose other names, fill Target agent with a comma-separated list, one name per target and in the same order as the targets. A target without a matching name keeps its target string as the agent name.

docs.title: Custom queries
docs.text:
Custom queries let you publish any SELECT result as a module. They apply to every target of the task. Each query is a block of lines between check_begin and check_end; each line is a key followed by its value. Lines starting with # are comments.

check_begin
name Blocked applications
description Applications waiting on a lock
operation value
datatype generic_data
target SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SYSIBMADM.SNAPLOCKWAIT
max_warning 5
max_critical 10
check_end

check_begin
name Lock waits (detail)
operation full
target SELECT AGENT_ID, LOCK_MODE, LOCK_OBJECT_TYPE FROM SYSIBMADM.SNAPLOCKWAIT
crontab */30 * * * *
check_end
Key Required Description name Yes Module name. A query without it is skipped target Yes The query. Only statements that start with SELECT (case-insensitive) are accepted; any other statement is removed and reported in the task information operation No value returns the first column of the first row as a single value. Any other value, or none, returns all rows as text datatype No Module type: generic_data, generic_data_string or generic_proc. Default generic_data_string. Always generic_data_string when operation is not value description No Module description. Default Execution OK, or the database error when the query fails crontab No Five-field cron expression that schedules the query. See below min_warning, max_warning, min_critical, max_critical No Numeric thresholds of the module str_warning, str_critical No String thresholds of the module

When operation returns all rows, each row becomes one line with its columns separated by |. An empty result is published as No output. for string modules.

The console comes with two example queries (DB Blocks and Blocking elements) already loaded in the Custom queries box.

Scheduling with crontab. A query with a crontab runs only when at least one occurrence of the expression is pending since its last successful run, and the run time is saved between task executions. A query that fails is retried on the next task execution. The first time a scheduled query is seen, only an occurrence that falls inside the current task interval counts, so enabling an old daily or monthly schedule does not run it immediately. A scheduled query that is not due produces no value in that execution, so define its module as asynchronous. An expression that does not have five fields, or is invalid, is skipped and reported in the task information.

Known limitations of this version. Treat these keys and placeholders as not available:

  • target_databases is read, but a query runs on every target only when it is omitted or set to all. A list of specific database names makes the query run nowhere.
  • The placeholder $__self_dbname mentioned in the console help is replaced by an empty string, not by the database name.
  • The keys unit, interval, parent, inverse_warning and inverse_critical that appear in the console help are not applied to the module.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes reports:

    • Total agents: agents generated, one per target.
    • Targets up: targets the addon connected to.
    • Targets down: targets it could not connect to.

    The connection errors are recorded in the task's execution information.

  2. The agents. One per target, named after the target or the Target agent list.

  3. The modules. Every agent has DB2 connection, 1 when the connection succeeded. The remaining modules appear only when the connection succeeded; see Understand the results.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Property Value Agent name and alias The Target agent entry for the target, or the target string when there is none Operating system DB2 Operating system version The instance service level read from SYSIBMADM.ENV_INST_INFO; Discovery when it could not be read Address The host of the target Group and interval Those of the Discovery task

When a target cannot be reached, its agent is still generated with DB2 connection set to 0 and no other module.

docs.title: Modules generated
docs.text:
Module names are prefixed with Custom module prefix when one is set.

Module Type Condition Description DB2 connection generic_proc Always 1 when the connection and a test query succeeded, 0 otherwise AGENT_WAIT_TIME_PERCENT, CF_WAIT_TIME_PERCENT, IO_WAIT_TIME_PERCENT, LOCK_WAIT_TIME_PERCENT, NETWORK_WAIT_TIME_PERCENT, RECLAIM_WAIT_TIME_PERCENT, RQST_WAIT_TIME_PERCENT, ROUTINE_TIME_RQST_PERCENT, TOTAL_BP_HIT_RATIO_PERCENT, TRANSACT_END_PROC_TIME_PERCENT generic_data Get database summary Percentages from MON_DB_SUMMARY, unit % APP_RQSTS_COMPLETED_TOTAL, AVG_RQST_CPU_TIME generic_data Get database summary Completed application requests and average request CPU time from MON_DB_SUMMARY Log utilization percent generic_data Check transactional log utilization Percentage of the transaction log in use; the description states the KB used and available Database size generic_data Check DB size Sum of the data, index, long, LOB and XML object sizes of all tables, in MB. The module name ends with a space Active connections generic_data Get number of connections Number of rows in MON_CONNECTION_SUMMARY cache hit ratio (<BUFFER_POOL>) generic_data Retrieve cache statistics Index hit ratio of each buffer pool, in %. The plugin sets default warning and critical thresholds on these modules; review them in the module configuration Your custom queries As defined Execute custom queries One module per query that applies and is due

The summary, log, size, connection and cache groups are independent: if one query is refused, its modules are missing but the others are still created.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. It takes four file paths and prints a JSON result:

pandora_db2 --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --target_databases <PATH_TO_TARGETS> [--target_agents <PATH_TO_AGENTS>] [--custom_queries <PATH_TO_QUERIES>]
Argument Required Content --conf Yes Configuration file described in Configuration file --target_databases Yes Targets, in the format of DB2 target strings --target_agents No Agent names, in the format of Target agent --custom_queries No Custom queries, in the format of Custom queries

The result contains a summary with Total agents, Targets up and Targets down, an info key with messages when something went wrong, and monitoring_data with the agents and modules. The exit code is 1 when a required parameter is missing, an input file cannot be read or a worker fails.

The configuration file contains the password: protect it with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Run time notes
docs.text:
• The addon removes the contents of its Db2 client diagnostic directory at the start of every execution.
  • Each target uses one connection that is closed when the target has been processed. The number of parallel connections never exceeds the number of targets.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the info field of the JSON execution result, which is shown in the task's execution information.

  • Parameter [user] not defined, Parameter [password] not defined or Database targets not defined: a required field is empty. The task ends with exit code 1 and generates nothing.
  • A connection error and Targets down greater than zero: the database could not be reached. Check the host, port and database name of the target, the credentials and the network path. The agent is still generated with DB2 connection set to 0.
  • A target without a database name: it cannot connect; use the <HOST>:<PORT>/<DATABASE> form.
  • DB2 error, please verify you have grants to ...: the user cannot read the view used by that option (summary, log utilization, database size, number of connections or hit ratio). Grant SELECT on it or disable the option.
  • Removed [<query>] from custom queries, only select queries are allowed.: the target of a custom query does not start with SELECT.
  • Invalid custom query crontab expression: the crontab of a query does not have five fields or is invalid; the query is skipped.
  • A custom query module is missing: the query has no name or target, it has a crontab that is not due, or it uses a target_databases list (see Custom queries).
  • Failed to execute query: ... in a module description: the database rejected the custom query.
  • Can't update custom query crontab state: the addon cannot write the schedule state, so the scheduled query may run again on the next execution.
  • Error while runing single thread: an unexpected error stopped one worker; the exit code is 1.

docs.title: Digital Ocean Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Digital Ocean Discovery addon monitors the droplets of a DigitalOcean account. It queries the DigitalOcean API with an API token and turns the result into Pandora FMS agents and modules: droplet status, CPU, memory, load and network traffic, file system usage, the date of the latest backup, the date of every snapshot and the account balance.

A Discovery task generates two kinds of agents:

  • One global agent for the account, with the number of droplets and the account balance and usage figures.
  • One agent per monitored droplet, with its status, performance and backup modules.

By default every droplet returned by the API is monitored. You can restrict the task to the droplets of one DigitalOcean project and discard individual droplets by name.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.digitalocean, version 1.0 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the Discovery server to api.digitalocean.com Required The addon calls the DigitalOcean API over HTTPS DigitalOcean API token Required See Create the API token Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to the DigitalOcean API.
  2. A DigitalOcean API token with read access, described below.
  3. Droplet monitoring enabled in DigitalOcean on every droplet whose CPU, memory, load and traffic modules you need. Droplets without it still generate an agent, with the Status, backup, snapshot and file system modules but without the CPU, memory, load and traffic modules.
  4. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it.

The addon ships its own executable, bin/pandora_digitalocean, so nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server to run a task.

docs.title: Create the API token
docs.text:
The addon sends only read requests (GET) to the DigitalOcean API. Create a personal access token in the DigitalOcean control panel (API section) and paste it in the task. The token must allow the addon to read:

Data Used for Droplets Listing the droplets and their status, features and networks (always) Droplet metrics CPU, memory, load, bandwidth and file system modules Droplet backups and snapshots Backup and snapshot modules Account balance Global agent modules (always) Projects and project resources Only when Filter project is enabled

The token is shown only once when DigitalOcean creates it; store it safely. DigitalOcean lets you create a new one at any time.

The token is stored in the task definition and written, in clear text, to the temporary configuration file the Discovery server uses to run the addon. Restrict access to the Pandora FMS console users that can edit Discovery tasks, and prefer a token created only for Pandora FMS.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.digitalocean

Load it into Pandora FMS.

Once loaded, Digital Ocean is available in the Cloud section when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from the Discovery cloud applications and choose Digital Ocean. The console presents all the fields in a single step, Digital Ocean base; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  • Digital Ocean token: the API token.
  • Use prefix and Prefix: text added in front of the name and alias of every generated agent. Prefix is shown when Use prefix is on.
  • Filter project and Project: monitor only the droplets that belong to the DigitalOcean project with that name. Project is shown when Filter project is on.
  • Discard droplets and Select the droplets to be discarded: skip individual droplets by name. The list is a JSON array of droplet names, for example ["ubuntu-s-1vcpu-1gb-sfo3-01","ubuntu-s-1vcpu-4gb-sfo3-03"]. It is shown when Discard droplets is on.
  • Max threads: number of groups the droplets are divided into.
  • Tentacle IP and Tentacle port: where the generated agent data is sent. They rarely need changing.

The image shows the wizard with Use prefix on; Project and the discard list appear when Filter project and Discard droplets are turned on.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to the agents the task creates.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes successfully reports Total agents: the global agent plus one agent per monitored droplet. A task that does not complete successfully records the errors in its execution information instead.

  2. The agents. One global agent, whose alias is Digital Ocean (with the prefix, when set), and one agent per droplet, with the droplet name as alias.

  3. The modules. Every droplet agent has a Status module. The performance modules appear only on droplets with monitoring enabled; see Understand the results.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Alias Notes Global agent <prefix>Digital Ocean One per task. Described as DigitalOcean global agent Droplet agent <prefix><droplet name> One per monitored droplet. Described as DigitalOcean Droplet. Its address is the second IPv4 network entry that DigitalOcean reports for the droplet

Agent identity is derived from the prefix and the name, not from the task or the droplet ID. The same task or another task that produces the same prefix and name reports to the same agent and keeps its history. Renaming a droplet in DigitalOcean, or changing the prefix, creates new agents. Two droplets with the same name share one agent.

docs.title: Modules per agent
docs.text:
Global agent

Module Type Description Droplets generic_data Number of droplets that DigitalOcean reports for the account Month to data balance generic_data Current month's incurred charges (month_to_date_balance) Account balance generic_data Total available funds in the account Month to date usage generic_data Current month's service usage

Droplet agent

Module Type Condition Description Status generic_proc Always 1 when the droplet status is active, 0 otherwise Cpu % generic_data Droplet monitoring enabled CPU used, in % Mem % generic_data Droplet monitoring enabled Memory used, in % Load 1, Load 5, Load 15 generic_data Droplet monitoring enabled Average system load over the last one, five and fifteen minutes Public inbound, Public outbound generic_data Droplet monitoring enabled Incoming and outgoing traffic on the public interface Private inbound, Private outbound generic_data Droplet monitoring enabled Incoming and outgoing traffic on the private interface <backup name> generic_data The droplet has backups Creation date of the latest backup. Unit _timeticks_ <snapshot name> generic_data The droplet has snapshots One module per snapshot with its creation date. Unit _timeticks_ <device> generic_data File system metrics returned by DigitalOcean for the droplet One module per file system device with its usage, in %

Backup, snapshot and file system modules take their names from the backup, the snapshot and the device. A new snapshot or a different latest backup therefore creates a new module.

docs.title: How the values are obtained
docs.text:
• The addon reads the DigitalOcean monitoring metrics for the last hour at each execution.
  • Cpu % is 100 minus the idle share of the hourly mean CPU time by mode.
  • Mem % is computed from the most recent total and available memory samples of that hour.
  • Load, bandwidth and file system values are the mean of the samples of that hour. The addon does not convert the bandwidth values: they are shown as the DigitalOcean monitoring API returns them.
  • Backup and snapshot values are the creation date expressed as timeticks, which the console displays as an elapsed time.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. The executable takes a single parameter, the path to a configuration file described in Configuration file:

./pandora_digitalocean --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

It sends one data file per agent and prints a JSON summary:

{"summary": {"Total agents": 12}}

When errors occur, the JSON also contains an info key with the messages and the exit code is 1. The configuration file contains the API token in clear text; protect it with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the info field of the JSON execution result, which is shown in the task's execution information.

  • The task fails and no agent is generated: the token is missing, invalid or expired, or the Discovery server cannot reach api.digitalocean.com.
  • The task fails after listing droplets and no droplet agent appears: the global agent reads the account balance before any droplet agent is created. Check that the token can read the account balance.
  • Error extracting information from droplets: with Filter project enabled, the project name was not found. The match is exact and case-sensitive; check the spelling against the project in DigitalOcean.
  • Every droplet is monitored although a project is selected: the project exists but has no droplets, so the filter restricts nothing and the run covers the whole account. Assign the droplets to the project in DigitalOcean and check the project name with the previous entry.
  • Error while parsing configuration zones or instances: the discard list is not a valid JSON array. Use double quotes, for example ["<DROPLET_NAME>"]. While the list is invalid, no droplet is discarded.
  • A droplet is still monitored after discarding it: the name must match the droplet name exactly, including case.
  • Droplet agents without Cpu %, Mem %, load and traffic modules: droplet monitoring is not enabled on that droplet in DigitalOcean.
  • Error while running threads: there were no droplets to monitor after applying the project filter and the discard list.
  • Agents that stop updating after a rename: the agent identity depends on the droplet name and the prefix; see Agents generated.

docs.text:

docs.title: Elasticsearch Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Elasticsearch Discovery addon monitors an Elasticsearch cluster through its REST API. Instead of building a single agent, it splits the monitoring by functional role and creates one agent per role:

  • A primary metrics agent with the indexing, search, merge, cache, segment and translog statistics of all indices, once for the primary shards and once for the total (primary plus replica) shards.
  • A cluster agent with the cluster health: status, number of nodes and shard allocation.
  • One agent per node with operating system, process, JVM, thread pool, transport, HTTP, circuit breaker, cache and disk metrics, plus the index statistics seen by that node.

Each role is optional and can be switched on or off in the Discovery task. Individual metrics can be excluded by name.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.elastic, version 1.0 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the Discovery server to the Elasticsearch HTTP(S) port Required The addon queries the cluster health, node statistics and index statistics APIs Access to the Elasticsearch cluster with read permission on those APIs Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement Elasticsearch server versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to the Elasticsearch node you point the task at (IP address and port, usually 9200).
  2. Credentials when the cluster requires authentication. The user and password are optional in the task; the addon authenticates with basic authentication only when both are set. The account must be able to call the cluster health, node statistics and index statistics APIs. This page does not prescribe a narrower role, because no official statement of the minimum privileges was recorded.
  3. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it. The addon sends the generated agent data with Tentacle by default, so the Tentacle server address must be reachable from the Discovery server.

The addon package ships everything it needs to run, so nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.elastic

Load it in Management > Discovery > Manage disco packages.

Once loaded, Elasticsearch is available in Management > Discovery > Applications when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from Management > Discovery > Applications > Elasticsearch. After the generic task definition (name, Discovery server, group, interval), the console presents two steps. Every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. ElasticSearch Basic — connection and transfer:

    • ElasticSearch IP and ElasticSearch Port: address of the Elasticsearch node. Both are mandatory.
    • User and Password: optional credentials.
    • Verify SSL: connect over HTTPS when enabled and over HTTP when disabled. Enabled by default.
    • Verify Certs: validate the TLS certificate of the server. Disabled by default.
    • transfer mode, tentacle ip and tentacle port: how the generated agent data reaches Pandora FMS. They rarely need changing.

  2. ElasticSearch Detailed — naming and metric selection:

    • agent prefix, Agent group, Custom module prefix and Module group: names applied to the generated agents and modules.
    • Primary metrics, Nodes Metrics and Cluster Metrics: choose which agents are created. All three are enabled by default.
    • Exclude primary metrics, Exclude nodes metrics and Exclude cluster metrics: shown when the matching metrics option is enabled. Names of the modules that must not be created, see Exclude metrics.

The task interval defined in the generic step becomes the interval of the generated agents.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes reports Total Agents and Total Modules. Errors found while querying the cluster are recorded in the task execution information.

  2. The agents. One primary metrics agent, one cluster agent and one agent per node, depending on the metrics options you enabled. With all options enabled and a single-node cluster the task creates three agents.

  3. The modules. Open the cluster agent: it has 13 modules such as cluster_status and number_of_nodes.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Alias Created when Modules Primary metrics <agent prefix>_primary_metrics Primary metrics is enabled 192 Cluster <agent prefix>_cluster_metrics Cluster Metrics is enabled 13 Node <agent prefix>_node_metrics_<node name> Nodes Metrics is enabled; one per node reported by the cluster 285

The agent name is derived from the alias, so agent identity depends only on the agent prefix and the role (and the node name), not on the task or the cluster address. Use a distinct agent prefix for each cluster; two tasks with the same prefix write to the same agents. When agent prefix is empty the alias starts with an underscore, for example _cluster_metrics.

All agents are created in the Agent group when it is set, report the description Created by elasticsearch plugin and have no parent, operating system or address. The module counts above are the counts before applying exclusions and Custom module prefix.

docs.title: Module groups
docs.text:
• Primary metrics agent: the statistics of all indices (_all) for the primary shards, named primaries_<metric>, and for all shards, named total_<metric>. Both sets contain the same 96 metrics.
  • Cluster agent: cluster name and health status, nodes, shard allocation and pending tasks.
  • Node agent: operating system, process, JVM, thread pools, transport, HTTP, circuit breakers, indexing pressure and caches of the node, the disk space of its data paths, and the index statistics of the node (the same 96 metrics, named _<metric>).

When Custom module prefix is set, every module name becomes <prefix>_<name>. Module group is applied to every module.

docs.title: Exclude metrics
docs.text:
Each exclusion field accepts a comma-separated list. Every entry is matched, case-insensitively, as a regular expression against the module name; a module whose name matches any entry is not created. Because the match is a search and not an exact comparison, cache removes every module with cache in its name, and ^total_ removes only the modules that start with total_.

  • Separate entries with commas. A list written one entry per line is not split into several entries.
  • Exclusions are evaluated on the module name before the Custom module prefix is added.
  • An invalid regular expression makes the query of that role fail; the error is recorded in the execution information and no agent is created for that role.
  • On the nodes role, do not use a pattern that matches the text node_name. The node name is carried in an internal entry of the same set; if it is excluded, the agent creation stops with Error create agent <prefix>: 'node_name': no node agent is created and the agents of the roles that follow (the cluster agent) are not created either.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The package ships the executable bin/pandora_elasticsearch, which can run outside a Discovery task with a configuration file described in Configuration file:

./pandora_elasticsearch --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

It sends one data file per agent and prints a JSON summary:

{"summary": {"Total Agents": 1, "Total Modules": 13}}

With --as_server_plugin 1 the executable prints only 1 when at least one agent was created and no error was recorded, and 0 otherwise. Use this form when running it as a server plugin:

./pandora_elasticsearch --as_server_plugin 1 --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

The configuration file contains the password in clear text. Protect it with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the information of the task execution (or the JSON output of a manual execution).

  • Error file: <path> does not exist: manual execution with a missing or empty --conf path.
  • Error while reading configuration file: ...: the configuration file cannot be parsed.
  • Error: Could not connect to OpenSearch primary|node|cluster with <host>:<port>: the cluster could not be reached for that role. The text mentions OpenSearch even when the target is Elasticsearch. Check the IP, port, firewall and the Verify SSL setting: a cluster that serves HTTPS needs it enabled, one that serves plain HTTP needs it disabled.
  • An index that does not exist: the primary metrics query reports Error: Could not connect to OpenSearch primary with <host>:<port>. The specific message Error: The index does not exist in the cluster. is not produced in this version, so read that connection message as a missing index when the rest of the cluster answers normally.
  • Error: when attempting to obtain node data ... or ... cluster statistics ...: the cluster answered with an error, for example because the account lacks permission. The message includes the error returned by the cluster.
  • Unable to obtain OpenSearch metrics.: no role produced data. Either all three metrics options are disabled, or every query failed.
  • Fewer agents than expected: a role that fails is skipped without stopping the others, so the task can finish with only some agents. Read the execution information for the failing role.
  • Authentication fails although credentials are set: a password that contains the % character is not read correctly from the configuration file the task generates, and the addon then connects without credentials. Avoid % in the password of the account used by the task.
  • Error create agent <prefix>: ...: building the agent of a role failed after the data was read. In the nodes role it usually follows an exclusion pattern, see Exclude metrics.

docs.text:
Used by manual execution. One key = value per line, with no section header. A key that is missing is read as empty (0 for numbers, off for booleans). Boolean values accept yes, true, t, y and 1; any other value is off.

docs.title: Google Cloud Compute Engine Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Google Cloud Compute Engine Discovery addon monitors Google Cloud Compute Engine virtual machine instances and the zones that contain them. It queries the Compute Engine and Cloud Monitoring APIs of a Google Cloud project and turns the result into Pandora FMS agents and modules: instance state and, optionally, CPU, memory, disk, IOPS and network performance.

A Discovery task generates three kinds of agents:

  • A global statistics agent (optional) with the number of monitored instances.
  • One agent per monitored zone, with summary modules aggregated over the monitored instances of that zone.
  • One agent per monitored instance, with its state and performance modules. The instance agent is a child of its zone agent.

A zone can be selected as a whole, in which case every instance it contains is monitored, including instances created later. Individual instance selection is not available in this version: monitor the zone that contains the instances you need.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.gcp.ce, version 1.1 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the Discovery server to the Google Cloud APIs Required The addon calls the Compute Engine API (compute, v1) and the Cloud Monitoring API (monitoring, v3) Service account key of the Google Cloud project to monitor Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. See Prerequisites Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to the Google Cloud APIs, directly or through an HTTP proxy.
  2. A service account key (the JSON key file) of the Google Cloud project that contains the instances, registered in the Pandora FMS credential store as a Google Cloud Platform credential. The key must include the project_id and client_email fields; the addon monitors the project named in project_id.
  3. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it.

The addon ships its own executables, bin/pandora_gcp_ce and bin/google_instances, so nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server to run a task.

docs.title: Google Cloud permissions
docs.text:
The addon performs read-only requests with the service account. Which ones it issues depends on the options you enable:

API request Used for Compute Engine instances.aggregatedList Listing zones and instances (always) Cloud Monitoring projects.timeSeries.list CPU, memory, disk, IOPS and network values (when Scan and general monitoring is enabled)

Grant the service account roles or permissions that allow these two requests on the project. No specific predefined role has been verified for this version, so choose the narrowest role that covers them in your organization.

Treat the key file as a secret: anyone who holds it can act as the service account.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.gcp.ce

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, Google Cloud Compute Engine is available in the Cloud section when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from the Discovery cloud applications and choose Google Cloud Compute Engine. The console presents the fields in three steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. Task Setup — credentials, execution and agent options:

    • GCP Credentials: the Google Cloud credential registered in the credential store.
    • Max threads: number of groups the monitored zones and instances are divided into.
    • Use proxy and Proxy url: route the Google Cloud requests through a proxy.
    • Tentacle IP, Tentacle port and Tentacle extra options: where and how the generated agent data is sent. They rarely need changing.
    • Add global stats agent and Stats agent name: create the global agent and optionally name it.

  2. Instance explorer — a tree of zones and instances read from your Google Cloud project with the selected credential. Check a zone to monitor it and all of its instances. The tree lists the instances grouped by machine type for reference; selecting an individual instance does not add it to the task in this version.

  3. Metrics — the performance values collected:

    • Scan and general monitoring: enables the options below.
    • Cpu performance summary, IOPs performance summary, Disk performance summary, Network performance summary and Memory performance summary: shown only when Scan and general monitoring is enabled.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to the agents the task creates.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes successfully reports:

    • Total agents: all agents generated, including the global agent when enabled.
    • Zones agents: zones monitored.
    • Instances agents: instances monitored.

    A task that does not complete successfully records the errors in its execution information instead.

  2. The agents. One per selected zone, one per instance and, when enabled, the global agent. Instance agents are children of their zone agent.

  3. The modules. Every instance agent has State and Instance State (bool). Performance modules appear only on running instances; see Understand the results.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Alias Parent Notes Global agent The Stats agent name, or Google Cloud Platform when empty None Created only when Add global stats agent is enabled Zone agent The zone name, for example europe-west1-b The global agent when a Stats agent name was given. With Add global stats agent disabled, the zone agent still declares Google Cloud Platform as parent, and that agent is not created One per selected zone Instance agent The instance name Its zone agent One per instance, created once even when both the instance and its zone are selected. The agent version is the machine type and the address is the internal IP address of the last network interface followed by its external address, when it has one; on an instance with several interfaces only the last one is kept

Agent identity does not depend on the task. Zone agents are identified by the service account (client_email) and the zone, and instance agents by the service account and the instance name. The global agent is identified by the service account when it has no name, and by the Stats agent name otherwise. Moving a zone or instance between tasks that use the same service account keeps reporting to the same agent and preserves its history.

All agents report the operating system name Google, and compute engine as the operating system version for zones and instances.

docs.title: Modules per agent
docs.text:
Global agent

Module Type Description GCP CE Instances count generic_data Instances found in the selected zones and instances

Zone agent

Module Condition Description summary.google.compute engine.instances Always Instances monitored in the zone summary.google.compute engine.CPUUtilization Scan and general monitoring and Cpu performance summary CPU of the running instances divided by the number of instances in the zone summary.google.compute engine.Ram Used, summary.google.compute engine.SwapInBytes, summary.google.compute engine.SwapOutBytes Scan and general monitoring and Cpu performance summary Sum over the running instances that report these values. SwapOutBytes repeats the swap-in value in this version summary.google.compute engine.DiskReadBytes, summary.google.compute engine.diskWriteBytes Scan and general monitoring and Disk performance summary Sum over the running instances, in Bytes summary.google.compute engine.diskAverageIOLatency Scan and general monitoring and Disk performance summary Sum of the average I/O latency of the running instances that report it summary.google.compute engine.DiskReadOps, summary.google.compute engine.DiskWriteOps Scan and general monitoring and IOPs performance summary Sum over the running instances summary.google.compute engine.NetworkPacketsIn, summary.google.compute engine.NetworkPacketsOut Scan and general monitoring and Network performance summary Sum over the running instances, in packets summary.google.compute engine.NetworkBytesIn, summary.google.compute engine.NetworkBytesOut Scan and general monitoring and Network performance summary Declared in bytes, but this version fills them with the packet counts of the same instances

Instance agent

Module Type Condition Description State generic_data_string Always Instance status as reported by Google Cloud Instance State (bool) generic_proc Always 1 when the status is RUNNING, 0 otherwise CPUUtilization generic_data Running, Cpu performance summary CPU usage Memory % Used generic_data Running, Memory performance summary, value available Percentage of memory used, in % Ram Used, SwapInBytesCount, SwapOutBytesCount generic_data Running, Memory performance summary, value available Memory used in the VM and memory read into and written to the guest's own swap space. In this version SwapOutBytesCount reports the swap-in value. Reported by Google Cloud only for VMs of the e2 family DiskReadBytes, DiskWriteBytes generic_data Running, Disk performance summary Disk bytes read and written, in Bytes DiskAverageIOLatency generic_data Running, Disk performance summary, value available Average disk I/O latency Disk % Used generic_data Running, Disk performance summary, value available Percentage of disk used, in % DiskReadOps, DiskWriteOps generic_data Running, IOPs performance summary Disk read and write operations NetworkPacketsIn, NetworkPacketsOut generic_data Running, Network performance summary Network packets received and sent, in packets NetworkBytesIn, NetworkBytesOut generic_data Running, Network performance summary Network bytes received and sent, in bytes TCPConnections generic_data Running, Network performance summary, value available TCP connections

"Value available" means that Cloud Monitoring returned a data point for the metric. The module is not created otherwise.

docs.title: How values are obtained
docs.text:
• Performance values are read from Cloud Monitoring over a window as long as the task interval, with a minimum of 300 seconds, and the first data point returned is used.
  • Performance modules are created only for instances in the RUNNING state.
  • Memory % Used, Disk % Used and TCPConnections come from metrics published under agent.googleapis.com; the other performance values come from compute.googleapis.com/instance/.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. The executable takes a single parameter, the path to a configuration file described in Configuration file:

./pandora_gcp_ce --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

It prints a JSON summary and sends one data file per agent using the configured transfer mode:

{"summary": {"Total agents": 35, "Zones agents": 5, "Instances agents": 29}}

When errors occur, the JSON also contains an info key with the messages and the exit code is 1.

In local transfer mode the data files are moved to data_dir. In any other mode they are sent with Tentacle, and the tentacle_client executable must be available in the PATH of the user running the addon.

A configuration file contains the service account key encoded in creds_b64. Protect the file with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the info field of the JSON execution result, which is shown in the task's execution information.

  • The instance tree is empty: the Instance explorer step prints Error while parsing credentials: <error> when the credential is not valid base64-encoded JSON or lacks project_id. Otherwise check the connectivity, the proxy and the permissions of the service account for the Compute Engine API.
  • Error while parsing configuration zones or instances: in a configuration file, gcp_zones or gcp_instances is not a valid JSON array.
  • Cannot create client to Google Compute API or Cannot create client to Google Monitoring API: the addon could not create the API client. Check the connectivity and the proxy settings.
  • Fewer agents than expected: only the zones and instances you checked are monitored.
  • No performance modules on an instance: the instance is not RUNNING, Scan and general monitoring is disabled, or the matching option is disabled.
  • Error while runing single thread: processing of a group of targets stopped with the error that follows. This can happen when Cloud Monitoring returns no data point for a performance metric of an instance. The remaining targets of that group do not produce agents in that run.
  • Memory, Disk % Used or TCPConnections modules are missing: Cloud Monitoring returned no data point for those metrics, which are only available when the VM publishes them.
  • Errors reaching Google Cloud through a proxy: check Proxy url. If it has no scheme, http:// is added to it.
  • Tentacle error:: the data file could not be sent. The message includes the error returned by the Tentacle client.

Used by manual execution. One key = value per line. List values are JSON arrays. Numeric options accept 1 to enable and 0 to disable; a value that is not a number is read as 0. Unknown keys are ignored.

docs.title: HAProxy Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The HAProxy Discovery addon monitors HAProxy load balancers through the CSV export of the HAProxy statistics endpoint (/stats;csv). It reads that export and turns each statistic of each proxy into a Pandora FMS module: sessions, bytes transferred, queues, errors, health checks, HTTP response classes, timings and the operational status of every frontend, backend and server.

The addon creates one agent per HAProxy URL. A Discovery task accepts several URLs at once, so a single task covers a whole set of HAProxy instances. Each agent contains one module per available statistic and per proxy row, plus a numeric status module for every row that you can use to alert on DOWN, MAINT or STOP states.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.haproxy, version 1.0 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity HAProxy statistics endpoint serving the CSV export, over HTTP or HTTPS, with or without basic authentication Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. See Enable the statistics endpoint Network reachability from the Discovery server to the statistics endpoint Required The addon performs one HTTP request per URL Specific HAProxy releases Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. The statistics endpoint must be enabled and reachable from the machine that runs the addon. Enabling it is covered in Enable the statistics endpoint.
  2. Credentials, only when the endpoint is protected with HTTP basic authentication.
  3. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it.

The addon is distributed as a self-contained executable, bin/pandora_haproxy, so nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server to run a task.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.haproxy

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, HAProxy is available in Management → Discovery → Application when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Enable the statistics endpoint
docs.text: For the addon to obtain the statistics, HAProxy must expose its statistics page. Enabling it is done by editing the HAProxy configuration file, haproxy.cfg (by default /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg). Pick the variant that matches how the endpoint should be protected. None of them needs the stats admin option, because the addon only reads data.

docs.title: Minimal configuration (no authentication, no SSL)
docs.text:
Add a dedicated frontend for the statistics:

frontend stats
    bind *:8404
    stats enable
    stats uri /stats
    stats refresh 10s

The URL to give to the addon is the host and port, without a path:

http://<HAPROXY_HOST>:8404

The addon appends /stats;csv to the path you provide instead of replacing it, so the address of the statistics page does not work as it is: http://<HAPROXY_HOST>:8404/stats is requested as http://<HAPROXY_HOST>:8404/stats/stats;csv and HAProxy answers 404. Enter the host and port alone, or a URL that already ends in stats;csv. See How the URL is normalized.

docs.title: Basic authentication
docs.text:
Define a userlist and require authentication in the statistics frontend:

frontend stats
    bind *:8404
    stats enable
    stats uri /stats
    stats refresh 10s

    acl auth_ok http_auth(stats_users)
    http-request auth realm stats if !auth_ok

userlist stats_users
    user <USERNAME> password <PASSWORD_HASH>

Generate the password hash, which HAProxy reads in crypt(3) format, with:

openssl passwd -6 <PASSWORD>

Give the addon the same user name and password in the Username and Password fields.

docs.title: SSL/TLS
docs.text:
Serve the statistics over HTTPS by adding ssl crt to the bind line:

frontend stats
    bind *:8404 ssl crt /etc/haproxy/certs/stats.pem
    stats enable
    stats uri /stats
    stats refresh 10s

To create a self-signed certificate for testing:

openssl req -x509 -nodes -days 365 -newkey rsa:2048 \
  -keyout /etc/haproxy/certs/stats.key \
  -out /etc/haproxy/certs/stats.crt \
  -subj "/CN=localhost"
cat /etc/haproxy/certs/stats.crt /etc/haproxy/certs/stats.key > /etc/haproxy/certs/stats.pem

Use a URL with the https:// scheme in the task. Enable Verify SSL only when the certificate is valid for the host name in the URL and its issuer is trusted by the Discovery server; leave it disabled for self-signed certificates.

docs.title: SSL and authentication together
docs.text:
Combine both blocks in the statistics frontend:

frontend stats
    bind *:8404 ssl crt /etc/haproxy/certs/stats.pem
    stats enable
    stats uri /stats
    stats refresh 10s

    acl auth_ok http_auth(stats_users)
    http-request auth realm stats if !auth_ok

userlist stats_users
    user <USERNAME> password <PASSWORD_HASH>

After editing haproxy.cfg, reload the service:

sudo systemctl reload haproxy

docs.title: Confirm the endpoint responds
docs.text:
Before creating the task, request the CSV export by hand from the Discovery server. Quote the URL, because ; is a special character in the shell:

curl -u <USERNAME>:<PASSWORD> 'http://<HAPROXY_HOST>:8404/stats;csv'

Passing a password on the command line exposes it in the shell history and in the operating system process list. Omit -u when the endpoint has no authentication. For an HTTPS endpoint with a self-signed certificate add -k.

The first line of the answer must be a header that starts with # pxname,svname,qcur,qmax,..., followed by one row per frontend, backend and server. If this request fails, the task fails too: fix it here rather than in the console.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from Management → Discovery → Application → HAProxy. After the generic task-definition step, the console presents the fields in two steps. Every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. HAProxy Basic — the endpoints and how to reach them:

    • HAProxy Stats URLs: statistics URLs, separated by commas or one per line. Each URL generates one agent. Mandatory.
    • Username and Password: only when the endpoint requires HTTP basic authentication. Authentication is sent only when both are filled in.
    • Verify SSL: validate the certificate of an https:// URL. Disabled by default.
    • Transfer mode, Tentacle IP and Tentacle port: how the data reaches Pandora FMS. native lets the Discovery server read the data directly; tentacle sends it with the Tentacle client. The Tentacle fields only matter in tentacle mode.

  2. HAProxy Advanced — optional shaping of the result:

    • Module prefix: prepended to every created module name.
    • Monitor frontends, Monitor backends and Monitor servers: choose which kinds of proxy rows produce modules. All three are enabled by default.
    • Allow list and Deny list: regular expressions to include or exclude modules by name.

The task's own group and interval come from the generic task-definition step: they are applied to the agents the task creates.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from Management → Discovery → Task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes successfully reports:

    • Total Agents: the number of agents generated by the task.
    • Total Modules: the number of modules generated by the task.

    Expect one agent per URL you entered. A URL that could not be read is reported as an error in the execution information instead.

  2. The agents. One per URL, with the alias set to the host:port of the URL, for example <HAPROXY_HOST>:8404.

  3. The modules on each agent. Modules are named <prefix><proxy>_<server>_<statistic>, for example app_FRONTEND_scur or app_BACKEND_status. Every proxy row has a status module, whose value follows the mapping in The status module.

If the task reports no agents, work back through Confirm the endpoint responds and then Troubleshoot.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
The addon creates one agent per HAProxy URL. The agent name is the MD5 hash of the URL's host:port, and the alias is that host:port itself, for example <HAPROXY_HOST>:8404. When a URL has no host:port, the whole URL is used instead. The agent description is HAProxy stats agent created by discovery plugin.

Because the identity comes from the endpoint and not from the task, moving a URL between tasks keeps reporting to the same agent and preserves its history. Two URLs with the same host:port therefore resolve to the same agent.

docs.title: Modules generated
docs.text:
HAProxy reports one CSV row per frontend, one per backend and one per server, and the addon creates modules from each row:

  • status module: created for every row, regardless of the Monitor frontends, Monitor backends and Monitor servers options, so that you can always alert on DOWN, MAINT and STOP. See The status module.
  • Statistic modules: one module per statistic of the row that has a value. Numeric values are created as generic_data modules and text values as generic_data_string. Statistics with an empty value are not created.

A statistic module is created only when its row type is enabled: rows of type frontend (type=0), backend (type=1) or server (type=2) follow Monitor frontends, Monitor backends and Monitor servers. Rows of any other type, such as sockets (type=3), are not governed by those options.

Module names have the form <prefix><proxy>_<server>_<statistic>, where <proxy> and <server> are the pxname and svname columns of the row. For frontend and backend rows svname is FRONTEND or BACKEND. Apostrophes and double quotes are removed from names and descriptions.

The addon creates a module for every column the endpoint returns, apart from the columns listed in Statistics that do not create modules. A HAProxy release that exports additional numeric columns therefore produces additional modules. The Reference describes the columns the addon documents.

docs.title: The status module
docs.text:
The status module is generic_data and converts the HAProxy status text into a number, from best to worst:

HAProxy status Value UP 5 OPEN 4 NOLB 3 MAINT 2 STOP, STOPPING 1 DOWN 0 Any other status -1

Only the first word of the HAProxy status is used, so UP 2/3 is read as UP. The module is created with the thresholds warning 2 to 4 and critical 0 to 2, so a DOWN or MAINT row raises a critical state and a NOLB row a warning, without further configuration.

docs.title: Filtering modules
docs.text:
The Allow list and Deny list are regular expressions searched (not anchored) in the module name as built from the row, <proxy>_<server>_<statistic>, without the Module prefix. For example, .*_wredis|.*_wretr matches every wredis and wretr module and status|scur|smax matches every module whose name contains one of those three words.

  • The allow list is applied first, then the deny list.
  • An empty list does nothing. An invalid regular expression is ignored: an invalid allow list allows everything and an invalid deny list excludes nothing.
  • Both lists also apply to the status module. An allow list that does not match status removes it.

docs.title: How the URL is normalized
docs.text: For each URL, the addon requests the CSV export. It appends /stats;csv to the path of the URL when the path does not already end in stats;csv, and it adds the norefresh parameter to the query when it is missing. Each request has a fixed timeout of 10 seconds. Because the suffix is appended and not substituted, http://<HAPROXY_HOST>:8404 is requested as http://<HAPROXY_HOST>:8404/stats;csv?norefresh, whereas http://<HAPROXY_HOST>:8404/stats is requested as http://<HAPROXY_HOST>:8404/stats/stats;csv?norefresh and fails with 404.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task, which is the fastest way to confirm an endpoint before wiring it into a task. It has two input modes:

  • Simple mode passes the URLs on the command line with --urls.
  • Advanced mode passes a configuration file with --conf plus a targets file with --conf_targets. This is the mode the Discovery task itself uses.
# Simple mode
./pandora_haproxy --urls http://<HAPROXY_HOST_1>:8404,http://<HAPROXY_HOST_2>:8404 \
    --user <USERNAME> --password <PASSWORD> --ssl false

# Advanced mode
./pandora_haproxy --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --conf_targets <PATH_TO_TARGETS>

Passing a password on the command line exposes it in the shell history and in the operating system process list. Prefer the configuration file for anything but a one-off check, and protect that file with restrictive permissions.

The run prints a JSON summary of the execution. In native mode the collected data is exposed in the summary's monitoring_data field, for the Discovery server to consume; in tentacle mode the addon generates one XML file per agent and sends it to the Pandora FMS server with the Tentacle client. When errors occur, the summary includes them in its info field.

--as_server_plugin true replaces the summary with a single 1 (at least one agent was created without errors) or 0, so the addon can be wired as a server plugin.

In simple mode (--urls), the module prefix, transfer mode, Tentacle address and interval parameters are accepted but not applied: the addon uses the defaults (no prefix, native, 127.0.0.1:41121 and 300 seconds), and no agent group is sent with the agents. To change them, use advanced mode with --conf.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the execution information of the task (the info field of the JSON summary in a manual run), which names the failing URL.

  • HTTP error for <url>: HTTP Error <code> for <url> — the endpoint answered with an error status. 401 means that the credentials are missing or wrong: check Username and Password (both must be filled in for authentication to be sent) against the userlist. 404 usually means that the URL and the stats uri of HAProxy do not combine: the addon appends /stats;csv to the path you give, so a URL that already ends in /stats requests /stats/stats;csv. Enter the host and port alone, or a URL that already ends in stats;csv.
  • Request error for <url>: ... — the request could not be completed: connection refused or timed out (10 seconds), wrong port, firewall, or a certificate error. For a certificate error on an HTTPS endpoint, disable Verify SSL for a self-signed certificate or install the issuing CA on the Discovery server.
  • Error parsing CSV for <url> or No stats data returned for <url> — the URL answered but not with the CSV export, or with no rows. Check it with the curl command in Confirm the endpoint responds.
  • No modules created for <url> — the row filters removed everything. Review Allow list, Deny list and the Monitor options.
  • All requests failed when trying to obtain HAProxy stats — no URL produced an agent.
  • No URLs provided or No valid URLs after parsing — HAProxy Stats URLs is empty after splitting on commas and line breaks.
  • Error: --conf_targets is required when using --conf or Error: no valid targets found in <file> — in a manual advanced-mode run, the targets file is missing or empty.
  • The endpoint answers by hand but not from the task — the request leaves from the Discovery server, not from your workstation. Check the network path and any acl rules of the statistics frontend.
  • Module prefix, transfer mode, Tentacle address or interval seem ignored in a manual run — see the note in Manual execution.
  • A status module has value -1 — HAProxy reported a status that is not in the table of The status module, for example a row with no health check.
  • Fewer modules than expected — check the row-type options and the allow and deny lists, and remember that empty statistics and the columns in Statistics that do not create modules never create modules.

docs.title: Task parameters
docs.text: The console presents the task fields in two steps.

docs.title: HAProxy Basic
docs.text: Field Macro Type Default Notes HAProxy Stats URLs _haproxyUrls_ textarea — Mandatory. Comma separated or one per line. Each URL creates one agent Username _haproxyUser_ string empty HTTP basic authentication user, optional Password _haproxyPassword_ password empty HTTP basic authentication password, optional. Authentication is sent only when both user and password are set Verify SSL _verifySSL_ checkbox off Validate the certificate of an HTTPS URL. Leave off for self-signed certificates Transfer mode _transferMode_ select native native: the Discovery server reads the agent data directly. tentacle: the addon sends the data with the Tentacle client Tentacle IP _tentacleIp_ string 127.0.0.1 Tentacle server address, used in tentacle mode Tentacle port _tentaclePort_ number 41121 Tentacle server port, used in tentacle mode

docs.title: HAProxy Advanced
docs.text: Field Macro Type Default Notes Module prefix _prefixModules_ string empty Prepended to every module name Monitor frontends _monitorFrontends_ checkbox on Create statistic modules for frontend rows (type=0) Monitor backends _monitorBackends_ checkbox on Create statistic modules for backend rows (type=1) Monitor servers _monitorServers_ checkbox on Create statistic modules for server rows (type=2) Allow list _allowList_ string empty (all) Regular expression; only modules whose name matches are created Deny list _denyList_ string empty (none) Regular expression; modules whose name matches are not created

docs.title: Command-line parameters
docs.text:
./pandora_haproxy --urls <URLs> [options]
./pandora_haproxy --conf <path> --conf_targets <path>
Parameter Default Description --urls — HAProxy statistics URLs, separated by commas. Each URL generates one agent. Either --urls or --conf is required --user — User for HTTP basic authentication, optional --password — Password for HTTP basic authentication, optional --ssl true Verify the HTTPS certificate (true or false) --prefix empty Prefix for module names. Not applied in simple mode -tm, --transfer_mode native native or tentacle. Not applied in simple mode -ti, --tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1 Tentacle server address. Not applied in simple mode -tp, --tentacle_port 41121 Tentacle server port. Not applied in simple mode -in, --interval 300 Monitoring interval in seconds. Not applied in simple mode --allow_list empty (all) Regular expression to include only modules whose name matches --deny_list empty (none) Regular expression to exclude modules whose name matches --monitor_frontends true Create statistic modules for frontend rows (type=0) --monitor_backends true Create statistic modules for backend rows (type=1) --monitor_servers true Create statistic modules for server rows (type=2) --as_server_plugin false Return a single 1 or 0 instead of the JSON summary --conf — Path to the configuration file --conf_targets — Path to the file with the HAProxy URLs. Mandatory when --conf is used

Boolean values accept true, yes, t, y and 1 (any letter case) as true; anything else is false.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The Discovery task builds this file from its own fields; a manual advanced-mode run supplies it with --conf. Use a [CONF] section with one key=value per line. The URLs are not read from this file but from the targets file.

Key Default when missing Description username empty HTTP basic authentication user password empty HTTP basic authentication password verify_ssl false Verify the HTTPS certificate prefix empty Prefix for module names transfer_mode none native or tentacle. Always set it: when the key is missing, the run does not use native tentacle_ip empty Tentacle server address, used in tentacle mode tentacle_port empty Tentacle server port, used in tentacle mode agents_group empty Name of the agent group, used in tentacle mode agents_group_id empty Id of the agent group, used in native mode interval 0 Monitoring interval in seconds. Always set it allow_list empty Regular expression to include only modules whose name matches deny_list empty Regular expression to exclude modules whose name matches monitor_frontends true Create statistic modules for frontend rows monitor_backends true Create statistic modules for backend rows monitor_servers true Create statistic modules for server rows

Example:

[CONF]
username=<USERNAME>
password=<PASSWORD>
verify_ssl=true
prefix=haproxy_
transfer_mode=native
tentacle_ip=127.0.0.1
tentacle_port=41121
interval=300
agents_group_id=<GROUP_ID>
allow_list=
deny_list=.*_wredis|.*_wretr
monitor_frontends=true
monitor_backends=true
monitor_servers=true

Targets file (--conf_targets), one URL per line, comma separated, or both:

http://<HAPROXY_HOST_1>:8404
http://<HAPROXY_HOST_2>:8404
