docs.title: HP One View Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The HP One View Discovery addon monitors the server hardware and the appliance managed by an HP OneView environment. It connects to the OneView appliance with a user name and password and turns the result into Pandora FMS agents and modules. Optionally, it turns the active alerts of OneView into Pandora FMS events.

A Discovery task can generate:

  • One agent per server (optional), with its health status, state and power state, plus the latest utilization metrics that OneView reports for it.
  • One appliance agent (optional) with the capacity, availability and used percentage of each resource reported by the appliance health status.
  • Events (optional) for the active or locked alerts of OneView, created in the appliance agent.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.hp.oneview, version 1.0 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the Discovery server to the HP OneView appliance Required The addon connects to the appliance with the credentials of the task HP OneView user with read access to server hardware and appliance health Required Prerequisite. The roles needed are not documented for this addon Specific HP OneView versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to the HP OneView appliance.
  2. An HP OneView user name and password that can read servers and the appliance health.
  3. Only to create events from alerts, all of the following:
    • A Pandora FMS API v2 token and the URL of the Pandora FMS console.
    • The numeric ID of the Pandora FMS group in which events are created.
    • Read access, from the Discovery server, to the Pandora FMS server configuration file (default /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf) and network access to the Pandora FMS database defined in it. The addon reads the database connection settings from that file to find the ID of the appliance agent.
  4. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it.

The addon ships its own executable, bin/pandora_hponeview, so nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server to run a task.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.hp.oneview

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, HP One View is available when creating Discovery tasks, in the application (app) section.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from the Discovery applications and choose HP One View. The console presents the fields in two steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. HP one view base — connection and delivery:

    • IP: address of the HP OneView appliance.
    • User and Password: credentials of the OneView user.
    • Tentacle IP and Tentacle port: where the generated agent data is sent. The defaults are 127.0.0.1 and 41121.

  2. HP one view Detailed — what to collect:

    • Use prefix and Prefix: prepend a text to the agent aliases and module names.
    • Scan appliances and Scan servers: create the appliance agent and the server agents. Both are on by default.
    • Scan alerts: create events from OneView alerts. On by default. It reveals API Url, API Token, Server conf and Events ID group.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to the agents the task creates.

Alerts are on by default but need API Url, API Token and Events ID group to work. If you do not need events, disable Scan alerts; otherwise the task reports an error on every run.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes successfully reports:

    • Total agents: all agents generated, servers and appliance.
    • Total server agents: server agents generated.
    • Total alerts: events created from alerts.

    Errors are recorded in the execution information of the task.

  2. The agents. One per server when Scan servers is on, and the appliance agent when Scan appliances is on.

  3. The modules. Each server agent has status, state and powerState; see Understand the results.
  4. The events, when Scan alerts is on. The appliance agent must already exist, so on the very first run the alert step is skipped with an error that asks you to run the task again. Run it a second time to create the events.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Alias Operating system Notes Server agent <prefix><server name> Operating system and model reported by OneView, as <operatingSystem> <model> One per server of the OneView environment Appliance agent <prefix> Appliances Not set One per Pandora FMS installation, see the note below

The server agent identity is derived from the prefix and the server name. The appliance agent identity is always the same, whatever the prefix or the OneView environment: two tasks, even against different appliances, report to the same appliance agent.

docs.title: Modules per agent
docs.text:
Server agent

Module Type Description <prefix>status generic_proc 1 when the OneView status of the server is OK, 0 otherwise <prefix>state generic_data_string Server state reported by OneView <prefix>powerState generic_data_string Power state reported by OneView <prefix><metric name> generic_data One module for each utilization metric returned by OneView for the server, with its latest sample. The metrics available depend on the server

Appliance agent

For each resource listed in the appliance health status, where <resource_id> and <resource_type> are those reported by OneView:

Module Type Description <prefix><resource_id> <resource_type> available generic_data_string Available amount, as reported by OneView <prefix><resource_id> <resource_type> capacity generic_data_string Capacity, as reported by OneView <prefix><resource_id> <resource_type> used_percent generic_data Used percentage in %, calculated as 100 - (available × 100 / capacity) and rounded to two decimals. It is 0 when the capacity is 0

The numeric part is read by taking the first run of digits, commas and dots in the value and replacing commas with dots, so a thousands separator is read as a decimal separator. A value with more than one separator, such as 1,234,567, makes the calculation fail and the appliance produces no modules in that run. The unit text of the values is ignored.

docs.title: Events from alerts
docs.text: When Scan alerts is on, the addon reads the first 10 alerts that OneView returns. For every one of them whose state is Active or Locked, it creates a Pandora FMS event whose text is the description of the alert, assigned to the appliance agent and to the group set in Events ID group. The event severity is critical for a Critical alert and warning for a Warning alert. An alert of any other severity keeps the severity of the previous alert in the same run, so a Critical alert followed by one of another severity also produces a critical event. The addon does not check whether the event already exists, so the same alert generates a new event on every run while it stays active.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. The executable takes a single parameter, the path to a configuration file described in Configuration file:

./pandora_hponeview --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

It prints a JSON summary and sends one data file per agent using the configured transfer mode:

{"summary": {"Total agents": 3, "Total server agents": 2, "Total alerts": 0}}

When errors occur, the JSON also contains an info key with the messages.

The configuration file holds the OneView password and the API token in clear text. Protect the file with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only the first 10 alerts returned by OneView are evaluated on each run.
  • A server whose data cannot be read is skipped without an error message.
  • The Max threads field is shown in the console, but this version of the addon does not use it.
  • If a file named config.json exists next to the executable, its content replaces the OneView connection data of the task.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the info field of the JSON execution result, which is shown in the task's execution information.

  • Error connecting: ...: the connection to the OneView appliance failed. Check IP, User, Password and network access.
  • Error alerts: if it is the first execution of the plugin, try again, it will be generated in the second execution: the appliance agent does not exist yet in Pandora FMS. Run the task again.
  • Error alerts: missing same parameter check events_id_group,api_url and token_api: Scan alerts is on but one of Events ID group, API Url or API Token is empty.
  • error getting id_agent appliance: ...: the addon could not read the Pandora FMS server configuration file or connect to the database it defines. Check Server conf and database access from the Discovery server.
  • Events are not created but no error is shown: the appliance agent could not be found. Enable Scan appliances so that it exists.
  • Error API cant create event: ...: the request to the Pandora FMS API failed. Check API Url, which must end with / (for example https://<PANDORA_FMS_URL>/pandora_console/), and the token.
  • Fewer server agents than expected: a server whose data could not be read is skipped without a message.
  • error with server: ..., Error appliances: ..., Error servers: ...: the data of the server or the appliance could not be processed; the message includes the cause.

docs.title: HP one view base
docs.text: Field Macro Type Default Notes IP _ip_ string — Mandatory. Address of the HP OneView appliance User _user_ string — Mandatory Password _password_ password — Mandatory Tentacle IP _tentacleIP_ string 127.0.0.1 Server that receives the agent data Tentacle port _tentaclePort_ number 41121 Tentacle port

docs.text:

Shown when Use prefix is on Scan appliances _scanAppliances_ checkbox on Appliance agent Scan servers _scanServers_ checkbox on Server agents Scan alerts _scanAlerts_ checkbox on Events from alerts. Reveals the four fields below API Url _apiUrl_ string — Optional in the console, required for events. The API call that creates events does not validate TLS certificates. The API token is stored in the task configuration; use a token with the minimum permissions needed to create events.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
Used by manual execution. One key = value per line, with no section header.

Key Default Description agents_group_name empty Group of the generated agents interval 300 Agent interval, in seconds transfer_mode tentacle Transfer mode of the data files tentacle_client tentacle_client Tentacle client executable tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1 Tentacle server address tentacle_port 41121 Tentacle server port data_dir /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Destination of the data files in local mode prefix empty Prefix for agent aliases and module names ip empty Address of the HP OneView appliance user empty OneView user password empty OneView password server_conf /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf Pandora FMS server configuration file events_id_group empty Group ID of the events api_url empty Pandora FMS console URL, ending with / token_api empty Pandora FMS API v2 token scan_alerts 1 1 creates events from alerts; any other value disables it scan_appliances 1 1 creates the appliance agent; any other value disables it scan_servers 1 1 creates the server agents; any other value disables it

Example:

docs.title: Hyper-V Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Hyper-V Discovery addon monitors a Microsoft Hyper-V host and the virtual machines (VMs) it runs. It connects remotely to the host over WinRM, runs read-only queries and turns the result into Pandora FMS agents and modules: host memory, drives and Virtual Machine Management service state, and, for each VM, its state, CPU, memory, uptime, replication, network adapters and virtual disks.

A Discovery task generates two kinds of agents, depending on the options you enable:

  • One agent for the Hyper-V host (optional), with host-level modules.
  • One agent per VM, with the modules of the enabled scan options. VMs are not agents of their own operating system: the addon sees them only through the host.

Nothing is installed on the Hyper-V host or inside the VMs.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.hyperv, version 1.1 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity WinRM listener on TCP port 5985 of the Hyper-V host, reachable from the Discovery server Required The addon connects to http://<host>:5985/wsman Account accepted by the host through HTTP Basic authentication that can run the Hyper-V PowerShell cmdlets Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. See Permissions curl command available on the Discovery server Required The addon runs curl to talk to the host Windows Server and Hyper-V versions of the monitored host Not validated No version has been recorded for this addon Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to TCP port 5985 of the Hyper-V host. Port 5985 is the WinRM HTTP port; the addon does not use HTTPS (5986).
  2. WinRM enabled on the Hyper-V host, accepting HTTP Basic authentication over the unencrypted HTTP listener.
  3. A user and password for the host, registered in the Pandora FMS credential store as a custom credential that provides the keys user and password.
  4. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it.

The addon ships its own executable (bin/pandora_hyperV), so nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server except the curl command.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
The addon runs the Hyper-V PowerShell queries Get-VM, Get-VMHost, Get-VMNetworkAdapter, Get-VMHardDiskDrive and Get-VHD, plus read-only queries of the host operating system, drives and the vmms service, through the WinRM session. The account therefore needs permission to open a WinRM session on the host and to run those cmdlets. No official source identifies a narrower set of roles, so no least-privilege policy is documented here; use a dedicated account for Pandora FMS and grant it only what those queries need.

The task is read-only: it does not start, stop, change or create anything on the host.

docs.title: Security considerations
docs.text:
The addon authenticates with HTTP Basic over http:// on port 5985. The user and password travel Base64-encoded, which is not encryption, so anyone who can observe the traffic between the Discovery server and the host can read them. Run the task only on a network you trust or isolate that path. Use a dedicated account with a password used for nothing else.

The addon does not verify TLS certificates, because it does not use TLS.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.hyperv

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, Hyper-V is available when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from the Discovery applications and choose Hyper-V. The console presents the fields in two steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. Hyper-V Connection — where and how to connect, and how agents are named:

    • Hyper-V IP: address or name of the Hyper-V host. Required.
    • HyperV Credentials: the custom credential with the user and password keys. Required.
    • Agent prefix (optional): text placed before the name of every generated agent. Defaults to HyperV.
    • Agent autodisable mode: disables the agent when all its modules become unknown until data returns.

  2. Monitoring Tokens and Filters — what is monitored:

    • Scan Hypervisor: creates the agent of the Hyper-V host. Off by default.
    • Scan VM: creates one agent per VM. On by default.
    • Scan Networking: adds the network adapter modules of each VM. Off by default.
    • Scan Storage: adds the virtual disk modules of each VM. Off by default.
    • Regexp to filter agents and Allow regexp: only VMs whose name matches the pattern are created. Allow regexp is shown when the checkbox is on.
    • Regexp to discard agents and Deny regexp: VMs whose name matches the pattern are not created. Deny regexp is shown when the checkbox is on.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to every agent the task creates.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that connects successfully reports:

    • hyperv_host: the host the task queried.
    • VMs: VMs found on the host, before the allow and deny filters are applied.
    • Agents: agents generated.

    When the addon cannot connect, the summary shows status as ERROR, the host, and a message that identifies the cause; see Troubleshoot.

  2. The agents. One per VM that passes the filters and, when Scan Hypervisor is enabled, one for the host.

  3. The modules. With Scan VM enabled, every VM agent has State, CPU Usage and the other modules listed in Modules per agent. A VM in the Off state has State set to 3, which is critical.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Name Address Notes Host agent <prefix> <ComputerName> The Hyper-V IP value Created only when Scan Hypervisor is enabled. ComputerName is the name reported by the host; the Hyper-V IP value is used when the host returns none. Operating system Windows, version Windows Server VM agent <prefix> <VM name> First usable IPv4 address of the VM; the Hyper-V IP value when it has none One per VM that passes the filters. Operating system Windows, version Windows

Details that apply to both:

  • The prefix is separated from the name by a space. In the prefix, characters other than letters, digits, ., _ and - are replaced with _, and trailing _ and spaces are removed. In the VM name, characters other than letters, digits, ., _, - and spaces are replaced with _. With an empty prefix the name is the host or VM name alone.
  • A usable IPv4 address excludes loopback (127.x) and link-local (169.254.x) addresses. The address is taken from the VM first and from its network adapters second.
  • Agent identity depends on the agent name: changing Agent prefix, or renaming a VM, creates a new agent instead of updating the existing one.
  • VM agents are not children of the host agent.
  • With Scan VM disabled, VM agents are still created when Scan Networking or Scan Storage is enabled, and they contain only those modules. When none of the three options applies, no VM agent is created.

docs.title: Modules per agent
docs.text:
Host agent

Module Type Description HyperV Connection Status generic_proc 1 when the WinRM connection works. Always present Memory Used Percent generic_data Percentage of host memory in use, in % DiskUsed_<drive> generic_data Used space of each file-system drive with used space, in GB. The free space is in the description VMMS Service Status generic_data State of the Hyper-V Virtual Machine Management service: 1 Stopped, 2 StartPending, 3 StopPending, 4 Running, 5 ContinuePending, 6 PausePending, 7 Paused; 0 when the service is not found. Critical at 1 and 2

When the host queries fail, the agent is still created with only HyperV Connection Status.

VM agent, Scan VM

Critical at 3 CPU Usage generic_data CPU usage, in % Memory Assigned MB generic_data Memory assigned to the VM, in MB Memory Demand MB generic_data Memory demanded by the VM, in MB Uptime generic_data VM uptime, in timeticks Status generic_data_string Operational status text reported by Hyper-V Generation generic_data VM generation Replication State generic_data 0 Disabled, 1 ReadyForReplication, 2 InitialReplicationInProgress, 3 Replicating, 4 Synced, 5 Recovered, 6 Committed, 7 Suspended, 8 Resynchronizing, 9 ResynchronizeSuspended, 10 Error

VM agent, Scan Networking: four modules per network adapter of the VM. <nic> is the adapter name with characters other than letters, digits, ., _ and - replaced with _; when a VM has several adapters with the same name, _1, _2 and so on are appended.

Module Type Description <nic>-connected generic_proc 1 when the adapter is connected, 0 otherwise <nic>-status generic_data 1 when connected, 4 when not. Warning from 2 to 3, critical at 4 <nic>-switchname generic_data_string Virtual switch name; 0 when none <nic>-ipaddresses generic_data_string Comma-separated IP addresses; 0 when none

Module Type Description disk<n>-path generic_data_string Path of the virtual disk file disk<n>-SizeGB generic_data Maximum configured size, in GB disk<n>-FileSizeGB generic_data Size of the file on the host, in GB disk<n>-DiskType generic_data 1 Fixed, 2 Dynamic, 3 Differencing disk<n>-DiskFormat generic_data_string Disk format, for example VHD or VHDX

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. The executable takes the path to a configuration file described in Configuration file:

./pandora_hyperV --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

It prints a JSON document with the summary, the monitoring_data of every agent and, when errors occur, an info key with the messages. The exit code is 1 when an error was recorded.

A configuration file contains the credential encoded in credentials. Protect it with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Local mode
docs.text:
With --execute_local the executable runs the PowerShell queries on the machine where it is started instead of connecting over WinRM. No hyperv_host or credentials are needed, and any credential in the file is ignored. The machine must be the Hyper-V host and have PowerShell (pwsh, powershell.exe or powershell) available.

./pandora_hyperV --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --execute_local

In this mode it prints only the monitoring_data as indented JSON, and the host agent contains HyperV Local Status instead of HyperV Connection Status. Add --save_file to write that JSON to hyperv_local_<hostname>_<timestamp>.txt in the current directory instead of printing it; --save_file is rejected without --execute_local. The Discovery task does not use local mode.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the info field of the JSON execution result, shown in the task's execution information.

When the connection probe fails, the task ends with the exit code 1, status ERROR and one of these messages:

  • Unable to authenticate to host '<host>' authentication failed.: HTTP 401. Check the user and password in the credential and that the host accepts Basic authentication.
  • Access denied when connecting to host '<host>'.: HTTP 403. The account is not allowed to open a WinRM session.
  • Unable to reach host '<host>' connection timed out.: no answer within 15 seconds to connect or 30 seconds in total. Check routing and firewalls.
  • Unable to connect to host '<host>' verify WinRM is enabled and the firewall allows TCP 5985.: connection refused. WinRM is not listening on 5985.
  • Unable to connect to the specified host '<host>'. Error: ...: any other failure, such as an unresolvable name (Unable to resolve host), an unreachable host or a missing curl. The message includes the error.

Other signals appear in info with exit code 1:

  • Missing required parameter: hyperv_host: the host is empty.
  • Missing credentials (user or password empty) or Error while parsing configuration credentials: ...: the credential lacks user or password, or is not valid Base64-encoded JSON.
  • Configuration file not found: ... or Error reading config: ...: the configuration file passed with --conf is missing or unreadable.

Situations that do not fail the task:

  • The task succeeds but creates no agents: the connection works but the Hyper-V queries returned nothing or failed. The messages ([vms] Get-VM error: ...) are only in info, and the summary reports VMs as 0. Check that the account can run the cmdlets listed in Permissions and that the Hyper-V role is installed on the host.
  • Fewer VM agents than VMs: the allow or deny regular expression filtered them out. VMs counts the VMs found before filtering.
  • A VM agent has no network or disk modules: Scan Networking or Scan Storage is disabled, or the host could not read that VM's adapters or disks. Disks whose file cannot be read by Get-VHD are skipped.
  • A VM has no address of its own: the VM reports no usable IPv4 address, for example because the integration services are not running, so the agent uses the Hyper-V IP value.
  • A VM agent shows State critical: the VM is turned off (State 3). The agent keeps reporting; the other modules keep the values Hyper-V returns.

docs.title: Hyper-V Connection
docs.text: Field Macro Type Default Notes Hyper-V IP _hypervhost_ string empty Required. Address or name of the Hyper-V host HyperV Credentials _credentials_ credential select (custom) — Required. Must provide the keys user and password Agent prefix (optional) _agentprefix_ string HyperV Optional. Text before the agent name; see Agents generated Agent autodisable mode _agentautodisable_ checkbox off Disables the agent when all its modules become unknown until data returns

docs.text:
Field Macro Type Default Notes Scan Hypervisor _monitorHypervisor_ checkbox off Creates the host agent Scan VM _tokenVM_ checkbox on Creates one agent per VM with the VM modules Scan Networking _tokenNetworking_ checkbox off Adds network adapter modules to each VM agent Scan Storage _tokenStorage_ checkbox off Adds virtual disk modules to each VM agent Regexp to filter agents _regexpFilter_ checkbox off Shows Allow regexp Allow regexp _allowRegexp_ string empty Optional. Only VMs whose name matches are created Regexp to discard agents _regexpDiscard_ checkbox off Shows Deny regexp Deny regexp _denyRegexp_ string empty Optional. VMs whose name matches are not created

Both regular expressions are searched anywhere in the VM name, ignoring case, and are tested against the VM name without the prefix. They apply to VM agents only; the host agent is not filtered. A VM must pass the allow expression and not match the deny expression.

Used by manual execution and written by the Discovery task from the fields above. One key = value per line. Flags accept 1, true, yes or on to enable.

credentials       = <BASE64_CREDENTIALS>
agent_prefix      = HyperV
agents_group_id   = 0

agent_autodisable = 0

scan_vm           = 1
scan_networking   = 1

docs.title: IoT Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The IoT Discovery addon monitors the messages that devices and sensors publish to an MQTT broker. It subscribes to one or more MQTT topic filters, stores every message it receives, and lets you define filters that turn the matching messages into Pandora FMS agents and modules.

The integration has two cooperating parts:

  • The IoT server is a service that connects to the MQTT broker, subscribes to the configured topic filters and stores each received message in a local database. It is managed from the Pandora FMS console.
  • The Discovery application runs as a Discovery task. On every run it reads the messages that have not been processed yet, applies your filters, and sends the result to Pandora FMS as agents and modules.

For example, if temperature sensors publish a reading every minute, a filter can keep only the readings above a threshold and expose them as a module that you can alert on.

The task creates one agent per distinct filter_topic value defined in your filters, with one module per filter that matched a message. See Understand the results.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.iot, version 1.1 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions An MQTT broker reachable from the IoT server host Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement Network access from the Discovery server to the IoT server database Required The task reads the database file path you configure MQTT protocol versions and specific broker products Not validated No broker or protocol version matrix has been recorded Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. A reachable MQTT broker, with the host, port and, if required, user and password.
  2. Permission to subscribe to the topics you want to monitor. The broker, not the addon, accepts or rejects each topic filter.
  3. The IoT server installed on the machine that receives the messages. It stores the messages in a local database, so the Discovery task must be able to read that database file at the path you configure. The default location is /opt/pandora/pandora_iot_server/db/pandora_iot.db.
  4. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to execute the task and an administrator user for the console settings.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Load the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.iot

Once loaded, the IOT application is available when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Enable the IoT server
docs.text:
The Pandora FMS server can start and stop the IoT server for you. To enable it:

  1. In the console, open Management → Settings → System Settings → General Setup, go to the Features tab and turn on Enable IOT Server. Click Update.
  2. A new IoT Server page appears under System Settings. Configure the broker connection there. See Configure the IoT server.

When Pandora FMS server starts with the feature enabled, it writes the IoT server configuration file from the console settings (default path /etc/pandora/pandora_iot_config.ini) and starts the pandora_iot_server service with systemctl. If the feature is disabled, the server logs that the IoT daemon is disabled and does not start the service.

The IoT server package installs the executable /usr/bin/pandora_iot_server, the configuration file /etc/pandora/pandora_iot_config.ini and the pandora_iot_server.service systemd unit, which runs as root. The package file names for each operating system have not been recorded for this version.

docs.title: Configure the IoT server
docs.text:
Open Management → Settings → System Settings → IoT Server and complete the broker connection. Every field is documented in IoT Server console settings. The minimum is:

  • Server host and Server port of the MQTT broker.
  • Server topic: the topic filter to subscribe to, for example factory/+/temperature.

To subscribe to several topic filters, enter a JSON array on a single line:

["factory/+/temperature", "factory/+/humidity", "alerts/#"]

The complete value, including brackets and quotes, must fit in the 200 characters the field accepts.

Settings saved in the console reach the IoT server when Pandora FMS server regenerates the configuration file and starts the service, that is, when Pandora FMS server starts. Restart the Pandora FMS server, or the pandora_iot_server service when you edit the file by hand, after changing the connection.

The broker password is stored in the console and written in clear text to the IoT server configuration file. Restrict access to that file and use a broker account that can only subscribe to the topics you need.

TLS is used only when both Enable SSL (ssl = 1) and Trust SSL certificate (trust_ssl = 1) are on, and in that case the broker certificate is not verified. With Enable SSL on and Trust SSL certificate off, the IoT server connects without TLS. Certificate verification is not available.

docs.title: Create the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from Management → Discovery → Application → IOT. The console presents the fields in two steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. Iot base:

    • DB path: path of the IoT server database file.
    • Time window: see Task parameters. It does not currently restrict the messages that are read.
    • Tentacle IP, Tentacle port and Tentacle extra options: where and how the generated agent data is sent. They rarely need changing.

  2. Iot detailed:

    • Max threads: number of processes used to evaluate the messages.
    • Filter messages modules: the filter definitions that decide which messages become modules. See Define the message filters.

The task interval and group are the ones you set on the task; the generated agents use them.

docs.title: Define the message filters
docs.text:
The Filter messages modules field holds one block per filter. A filter starts with filter_begin and ends with filter_end, each alone on its line. Inside the block, each line is the option name, whitespace, and its value. Do not add a colon after the option name, quotes around the value or a trailing comment. Lines outside a block, and lines that start with #, are ignored.

filter_begin
filter_module_name Temperature __regex1__
filter_module_type generic_data
filter_topic ^sensors/.*/livingroom$
filter_topic_exact_match 0
filter_message_capture_regex Temp: (\d+)
filter_module_value __regex1__
filter_end

A message passes a filter when it matches both filter_topic and filter_message. One message can pass several filters. See Filter options for every option.

docs.title: Match by topic or message
docs.text:
filter_topic and filter_message are evaluated against the topic and the content of each stored message. Their matching mode is set by filter_topic_exact_match and filter_message_exact_match:

  • 0 (default): the value is a regular expression, searched anywhere in the text. Anchor it with ^ and $ to match the whole text.
  • 1: the value is plain text, and the filter matches when the text contains it. Despite the option name, this is not an equality test: sensors/temperature/ matches the topic sensors/temperature/livingroom.

An empty or omitted value matches any topic or message.

docs.title: Capture values from the message
docs.text:
Use captures to put parts of the message in the module name or value.

With filter_message_capture_regex, each capture group of the expression is stored in __regexN__, where N is the position of the group. For the message Temp: 85 C and this filter:

filter_message_capture_regex Temp: (\d+) (\w)
filter_module_value __regex1__ __regex2__

the module value is 85 C.

With filter_message_capture_json, give one or more JSONPath expressions separated by |. Every expression starts with $, which is the root of the JSON document, and the result of each is stored in __jsonN__, where N is the position of the expression. When an expression returns several values, they are joined with ,. For this message:

{"message":"Move up right","data":{"yaw_direction":"right","pitch_direction":"up"}}

this filter:

filter_begin
filter_module_name __topic__ get right
filter_module_type generic_data_string
filter_topic testtopic/rgb/test/action/
filter_topic_exact_match 1
filter_message Move up right
filter_message_exact_match 1
filter_message_capture_json $.data.yaw_direction|$.data.pitch_direction|$.message
filter_module_value __topic__ | Yaw: __json1__ | Pitch: __json2__ | Message: __json3__
filter_end

creates a module named testtopic/rgb/test/action/ get right with the value testtopic/rgb/test/action/ | Yaw: right | Pitch: up | Message: Move up right.

__topic__ is replaced with the topic of the message that matched. A macro that has no captured value is replaced with an empty string. If the message is not valid JSON, every __jsonN__ macro is empty.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
1. Confirm the IoT server is receiving messages: the service is active and the database file exists and grows. See Operate.
  2. Publish a test message to a topic your filter matches.
  3. Force the task from Management → Discovery → Task list.

  4. When the task finishes, check its summary:

    • Total agents: number of agents generated.
    • Total messages: number of modules generated from messages that passed a filter.

  5. Open the generated agent and confirm it has the module and value your filter produces.

docs.title: How a run works
docs.text:
Each run reads from the database every message that has not been processed yet and evaluates it against all your filters. Keep these rules in mind:

  • Every message read is marked as processed, even when it matches no filter. Changing a filter does not make the task reprocess earlier messages.
  • Agents: one agent is created per distinct filter_topic value, and its name is that value exactly as written in the filter, not the MQTT topic of the message. Filters that share the same filter_topic text share an agent. Set filter_topic in every filter, and prefer plain text or a readable pattern, because a regular expression becomes the agent name.
  • Modules: within one run and one agent, the first module generated with a given name is kept and later messages that resolve to the same name are discarded. Use __topic__ or captured values in filter_module_name when several topics or messages should produce separate modules.
  • Timestamps: the task reads messages stored after the time given by the effective time window; see the note in Task parameters.
  • Retention: independently of processing, the IoT server deletes stored messages older than the retention period (default 86400 seconds), checking at the configured cleaning interval.

docs.title: Generated agents and modules
docs.text: Item Content Agent Named after the filter_topic value. Group and interval are the task's. Module name filter_module_name after macro substitution. Module type filter_module_type, for example generic_data_string or generic_data. Module value filter_module_value after macro substitution.

docs.title: Check the IoT server service
docs.text:
systemctl status pandora_iot_server
journalctl -u pandora_iot_server

The IoT server writes its own log to log_location/log_name (default /var/log/pandora/pandora_iot.log) with rotation. To also see the log on the terminal when you run the server manually, start it with -v.

docs.title: Inspect the stored messages
docs.text: The messages are stored in the table pandora_mqtt_data of a SQLite database, with the columns topic, message, unix_timestamp and processed (0 when not yet processed, 1 when processed).

docs.title: Limits and behavior
docs.text:
• Subscriptions use QoS 0. It is not configurable.
  • All topic filters share one broker connection. Adding filters does not add connections.
  • Subscriptions are submitted again after each reconnection.
  • At debug log level the IoT server writes all its settings to the log, including the broker password. Do not leave debug enabled on a production system with credentials.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text: Symptom Check The task reports that the database file cannot be found The DB path does not exist from the Discovery server. Confirm the path and that the file is readable from that machine. The task reports Failed to connect The file exists but does not contain the pandora_mqtt_data table. Confirm that the path is the IoT server database. The task reports an error parsing filters The filter text could not be read. Check that each block has filter_begin and filter_end and that the file is plain text. Total agents is 0 No unprocessed message passed a filter. Confirm that messages are arriving and that filter_topic and filter_message match them. Remember that earlier runs mark messages as processed. Modules are missing for some messages Several messages resolve to the same module name in the same agent. Only the first is kept. Include __topic__ or captured values in the module name. A module value contains an unreplaced or empty macro The capture did not match. Test the regular expression or JSONPath against a real message. An invalid regular expression is ignored; an invalid JSONPath expression stops the task. The IoT server does not start Check journalctl -u pandora_iot_server and the IoT server log. Confirm that Enable IOT Server is on and that the service user can write to the database and log directories. Startup fails with Invalid topic configuration The topic value is a malformed JSON array. Use one line, double quotes and at least one non-empty string. Do not add a trailing comma. Messages are not stored Check the broker host, port, protocol and credentials, and the broker permissions for each topic filter. A subscription rejected by the broker is written to the IoT server log.

docs.title: Processor options
docs.text: The Discovery application runs its processor with the task configuration (--conf) and the filter definitions (--filter_conf), both generated from the wizard. It also supports --verbosity to write debug output, which the task does not pass.

docs.title: JMX Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The JMX Discovery addon monitors Java applications through Java Management Extensions (JMX). It connects to the JMX endpoint of each target you configure, reads the attributes of the MBeans you choose and turns them into Pandora FMS agents and modules.

A Discovery task generates one agent per JMX target. Each agent contains one module per MBean attribute collected. You choose what is collected in two ways, which can be combined:

  • MBeans selected in the console. The console connects to a reference JMX endpoint and shows the MBeans it exposes. Every attribute of each selected MBean is collected, on every target of the task.
  • Custom metrics. An explicit list of MBean/attribute entries, optionally with thresholds.

The same selection is applied to all the targets of a task, so group in one task only targets that expose the same MBeans.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.jmx, version 1.2 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity A Java runtime available on the Pandora FMS server that runs the task Required The addon starts a Java virtual machine to open the JMX connections Network access from the Discovery server to each JMX endpoint Required The addon opens one JMX connection per target Java runtime versions, Java vendors and application servers Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. A Java runtime installed on the Pandora FMS server that runs the Discovery task, available to the user that runs it.
  2. Remote JMX enabled on every monitored Java application, reachable from the Discovery server. See Enable remote JMX.
  3. The JMX service URL of every target, for example service:jmx:rmi:///jndi/rmi://<TARGET_HOST>:<JMX_PORT>/jmxrmi.
  4. JMX credentials, only when the target requires authentication.

docs.title: Enable remote JMX
docs.text:
The monitored application does not need extra software, but it must be started with the JVM options that enable remote JMX. The following set enables it on the local host without authentication or TLS and is meant only for a test environment:

-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote
-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.authenticate=false
-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.ssl=false
-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.port=<JMX_PORT>
-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.rmi.port=<JMX_PORT>
-Djava.rmi.server.hostname=localhost

To require authentication, set -Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.authenticate=true and add the password and access files:

-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.password.file=<PATH_TO_PASSWORD_FILE>
-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.access.file=<PATH_TO_ACCESS_FILE>

To connect from another host, java.rmi.server.hostname must be an address the Discovery server can reach. The exact options for your application and the protection of the password file are defined by the Java application, not by this addon.

docs.title: Credential handling
docs.text:
• The user and password entered in the task are stored with the task definition and sent to the JMX server as the JMX credentials.
  • While the console loads the list of MBeans, it passes the user and password as arguments to the helper executable, so they can be visible in the process list of the Pandora FMS server during that operation.
  • A configuration file used in manual execution contains the password in clear text. Protect it with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.jmx

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, JMX is available in the Applications section when creating Discovery tasks.

The addon ships its own executables, bin/pandora_jmx and bin/get_jmx_tree.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from the Discovery applications and choose JMX. The console presents the fields in three steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. JMX Basic — targets and credentials:

    • Instances target strings: the targets to monitor, one or several per line, separated by commas. Each target is a JMX service URL, optionally followed by | and the agent name to use. Lines that start with # are ignored.
    • JMX Url: the reference endpoint used only to list the available MBeans in the next step. It does not define a target.
    • Auth basic, User and Password: credentials for the JMX connections. User and password are shown when Auth basic is enabled.

  2. JMX Mbeans — a tree of the MBeans exposed by the JMX Url endpoint, read with the credentials of the previous step. Select the MBeans to collect. Every attribute of each selected MBean is collected on all the targets.

  3. JMX detailed — execution, naming and filtering options:

    • Max threads: number of targets processed in parallel.
    • Use prefix for modules and Use prefix for agents: prefixes added to the generated module names and agent names.
    • Tentacle IP, Tentacle port and Tentacle extra options: where the generated agent data is sent. They rarely need changing.
    • Regexp to filter modules and Regexp to discard modules: keep or discard metrics by regular expression.
    • Custom Metrics: explicit MBean/attribute entries with optional thresholds.
    • Rename default modules and Modules names: assign your own module names.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to the agents the task creates.

docs.title: Custom metrics
docs.text:
Write one metric per line using the format <MBean>/<attribute>, optionally followed by thresholds separated by |. Each threshold is a keyword and a value separated by a space. Lines that start with # and empty lines are ignored.

java.lang:type=Threading/ThreadCount
java.lang:type=Threading/TotalStartedThreadCount|min_warning 30|min_critical 45
java.lang:type=Memory/HeapMemoryUsage/used
  • The thresholds supported by the addon are min_warning, max_warning, min_critical and max_critical.
  • To read one field of a composite attribute, append its name after the attribute, as in java.lang:type=Memory/HeapMemoryUsage/used.
  • If you reference a composite attribute without a field, a module is created for each of its fields; thresholds are not applied to those modules.

docs.title: Rename modules
docs.text:
Module names default to <MBean>/<attribute>, for example java.lang:type=Threading/ThreadCount. To replace a name, enter one line in Modules names with the original name, a | and the new name:

java.lang:type=Threading/ThreadCount | Threads.count

The original name must match the default name exactly, without the module prefix. When Use prefix for modules is enabled, the prefix is added after the renaming.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes reports Total agents, the number of agents generated. Errors and warnings are recorded in the task's execution information.

  2. The agents. One per target, in the group of the task. The agent alias is the agent name given after | in the target, or the JMX service URL when none is given, with the agent prefix when one is configured.

  3. The modules. One per collected attribute. Check that the attributes you selected or listed as custom metrics appear and have values.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Item Value Agents One per target in Instances target strings Alias The text after | in the target, or the target itself when there is none; preceded by the agent prefix when configured Agent name An identifier derived from the alias, including the prefix. The same alias reports to the same agent across runs and tasks Description Created by JMX plugin Group and interval The group and interval of the Discovery task

Changing the agent name or the agent prefix of a target creates a different agent, so keep them stable to preserve the history.

docs.title: Modules generated
docs.text:
Each collected attribute produces one module. Its type depends on the value read:

Value read Module type Value Integer, long, float or double number generic_data The number Boolean generic_proc 1 for true and 0 for false Any other value generic_data_string The value as text

A module whose text value is True or False is not created. Attributes that cannot be read, because they do not exist on a target or are unavailable, produce a warning in the execution information and no module.

The attributes of the selected MBeans are filtered by the regular expressions of the task; the custom metrics are also filtered by them. Thresholds in custom metrics are set on the generated module.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task with three files:

./pandora_jmx --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --target_instances <PATH_TO_TARGETS> [--target_metrics <PATH_TO_METRICS>]
  • --conf: configuration file described in Configuration file. Mandatory.
  • --target_instances: the targets, in the same format as Instances target strings. Mandatory.
  • --target_metrics: the custom metrics, in the same format as Custom Metrics. Optional.

It prints a JSON document with the summary (Total agents) and, when there are messages, an info field, and sends one data file per agent with Tentacle. The exit code is 1 when the configuration or targets file cannot be read.

docs.title: Execution tuning
docs.text: Max threads (threads) is the number of worker processes. Each worker takes targets from a shared queue, so more workers than targets add no benefit. Each worker starts its own Java virtual machine, which consumes memory on the Pandora FMS server.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the execution information of the task (the info field in manual execution).

  • Failed to connect: <error>: the connection to a target failed. Check the JMX service URL, the network path, the JMX port and the credentials, and that the application was started with remote JMX enabled.
  • Failed processing <url>: <error>: an error occurred while collecting a target.
  • [WARNING] Failed to read attributes from <MBean>: <error>: a selected MBean could not be read on a target, for example because it does not exist there.
  • [WARNING] Could not read '<attribute>' from MBean '<MBean>': the attribute does not exist, is transient or cannot be read. The module is not created.
  • Database targets not defined: Instances target strings is empty or contains only comments. The task generates no agents.
  • Error while parsing configuration zones or instances: <error>: the jmx_mbeans value is not a valid JSON list (manual execution).
  • Failed to read custom attributes: <error> and Failed to parsing module names: <error>: the custom metrics or the module names could not be read.
  • No MBeans appear in the second step: check the JMX Url, the credentials and the network path from the Pandora FMS server to that endpoint.
  • Fewer modules than expected: review the regular expressions; a metric that does not match Allow regexp, or that matches Deny regexp, is not created.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
Used by manual execution. It has a [CONF] section and an optional [MODULE_NAMES] section. Values are key = value pairs.

Key Default Description jmx_url empty Reference endpoint. Read for compatibility with the task; targets come from --target_instances user empty JMX user password empty JMX password jmx_mbeans [] JSON list of MBean names whose attributes are all collected, for example ["java.lang:type=Threading","java.lang:type=ClassLoading"] module_prefix empty Prefix for module names agent_prefix empty Prefix for agent aliases agents_group_name jmx Group of the generated agents interval 300 Agent interval, in seconds. A value that is not a number is read as 0 threads 4 Worker processes. A value that is not a number is read as 0 transfer_mode tentacle local writes the data files locally; any other value sends them with Tentacle tentacle_client tentacle_client Tentacle client executable tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1 Tentacle server address tentacle_port 41121 Tentacle server port tentacle_opts empty Accepted, not passed to the Tentacle client in this version data_dir /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Accepted for compatibility with the other Discovery addons temporal /tmp Accepted for compatibility with the other Discovery addons allow_regexp empty Only metrics that match are created deny_regexp empty Metrics that match are not created

The [MODULE_NAMES] section holds one original name | new name per line.

Example:

[CONF]
user = <USERNAME>
password = <PASSWORD>
jmx_url = service:jmx:rmi:///jndi/rmi://<TARGET_HOST>:<JMX_PORT>/jmxrmi
module_prefix = app.
agent_prefix = app.
agents_group_name = jmx
interval = 300
threads = 2
transfer_mode = tentacle
tentacle_ip = <TENTACLE_SERVER_IP>
tentacle_port = 41121
allow_regexp =
deny_regexp =
jmx_mbeans = ["java.lang:type=Threading","java.lang:type=ClassLoading"]

[MODULE_NAMES]
java.lang:type=Threading/ThreadCount | Threads.count

docs.title: Kubernetes Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Kubernetes Discovery plugin connects to the Kubernetes API server of a cluster and discovers its workloads and infrastructure: nodes, pods, deployments, namespaces, services, component statuses and the API health endpoints. It generates one Pandora FMS agent per discovered resource and fills it with availability, capacity and performance modules read from the API.

The plugin generates agents for:

  • the cluster itself, through a global Kubernetes agent;
  • every node, when Scan Nodes is enabled;
  • every deployment with condition data, when Scan Deployments is enabled;
  • every pod already scheduled to a node, when Scan Pods is enabled.

The global agent also carries the cluster-wide API status, health endpoints, service count, namespace count and component statuses.

The plugin runs as a Discovery task: the console creates the task, the Discovery server runs the plugin, and the generated agents and modules are created automatically. The task delivers the generated agent data through Tentacle.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Plugin version 1.3 (pandorafms.kubernetes) Documented target The version this page describes, as identified by the package definition. See Plugin identity A Kubernetes cluster exposing the API server over HTTPS Required The plugin connects to https://<host>:<port> and reads the API resources. Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement A Bearer token that can read the queried API resources Required The plugin authenticates with Authorization: Bearer <token> to list nodes, pods, deployments, services, namespaces and component statuses. Health and component endpoints may require elevated permissions. Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement The Kubernetes Metrics API (metrics.k8s.io) for CPU and memory usage Required for CPU and memory modules Node and container CPU and memory modules are read from /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1. Without it, node and pod agents are still generated, but those modules are omitted A specific Kubernetes version Not validated No published test record establishes compatibility with a concrete Kubernetes release Host operating system running the plugin Not validated No published test record establishes operating-system compatibility

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. A Pandora FMS server with Discovery enabled to run the task, and the console to define it.
  2. A Kubernetes API server reachable from the Discovery server, addressed by host and port. The plugin always uses HTTPS; enter the host without a scheme.
  3. A Bearer token for the API server. It is required to read the protected endpoints; grant it read access to the resources the task queries and no more. The Scan API health checks and Scan component statuses options may need elevated API permissions, as noted in the task tips.
  4. A target agent group and a monitoring interval for the generated agents. Both come from the Discovery task and are inherited by every generated agent.
  5. Network reachability to the Tentacle destination, because the task transfers the generated agent data through Tentacle.
  6. The plugin is distributed as a Pandora FMS Discovery application (.disco package) that the Discovery server executes on the Pandora FMS server.

Direct API connections use HTTPS without certificate verification: the server identity is not authenticated, so self-signed certificates work. Restrict network access accordingly. Proxy mode uses the supplied proxy URL and omits the Bearer header. The token is entered in the task and written to its configuration; restrict access to both. For manual runs, keep the token in a protected configuration file, not in shell commands.

docs.title: Check target access
docs.text:
Before creating the task, verify the Metrics API and the node/pod metrics with an account authorized for the target cluster:

kubectl get --raw /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/
kubectl top node
kubectl top pod --all-namespaces

If the cluster does not expose the Metrics API, node and pod agents are still generated, but their CPU and memory modules are omitted. These diagnostic commands do not grant the plugin token any permissions.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text: Obtain the .disco package from the Kubernetes Marketplace entry and load it in Discovery from Management → Discovery → Extension manager. Once loaded, Kubernetes appears under the Applications category of the Discovery wizard. This page covers package 1.3.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text: Create the task from Management → Discovery → Applications → Kubernetes. The wizard walks through the generic task definition and two plugin steps: Kubernetes base and Kubernetes detailed. Every field is documented in Task parameters.

docs.title: Step 1 — Task definition
docs.text: The generic step asks for the task name, the agent group and server on which the task runs, and the interval. The group and the interval are passed to the plugin and inherited by every generated agent.

docs.title: Step 2 — Kubernetes base
docs.text:
Connection details and the Tentacle destination:

  • Kubernetes host is the address or hostname of the API server.
  • Kubernetes port is the API server port.
  • Kubernetes token is the Bearer token used to authenticate against the API.
  • Use prefix shows Prefix, the text prepended to generated agent identities. Clear Prefix when disabling this option: a populated prefix is still applied in this version.
  • Filter namespace restricts discovery to a set of namespaces, and Namespace is the list of namespaces to monitor.
  • Use proxy routes the API requests through a proxy; Proxy url is that proxy.
  • Tentacle IP and Tentacle port set the Tentacle destination for the generated data. Leave the defaults unless your environment needs another Tentacle target.

docs.title: Step 3 — Kubernetes detailed
docs.text:
What to scan:

  • Scan Deployments, Scan Nodes and Scan Pods enable or disable each resource category.
  • Scan API health checks generates the API health endpoint modules. Health endpoints may require elevated API permissions.
  • Scan component statuses generates the component count and the component condition modules. Component statuses may require elevated API permissions.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Run the task from Management → Discovery → Task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary shows the overall progress and a summary with the number of node agents, pod agents and deployment agents generated, and the total number of agents.
  2. The agents. Expect the global Kubernetes agent plus one agent per discovered node, deployment and scheduled pod. Node and pod agents are generated even when the Metrics API is unavailable; deployment agents require returned condition data.
  3. The modules. Every generated agent carries the modules of its resource; a reachable cluster with the Metrics API available populates the CPU and memory values. Do not treat the summary counters as proof of successful data ingestion.
  4. The execution information. A successful run reports no errors; any per-request failure is recorded there.

If the task fails before generating anything, the host, the port, the network reachability and the token are the first things to check.

docs.title: Agents and identity
docs.text:
The plugin creates one agent per discovered resource. Agent names are built from the original resource name plus the optional prefix.

Agent Name Parent agent Global [Prefix]Kubernetes — Node [Prefix]<node> The global agent Deployment [Prefix]<deployment> Kubernetes (without the prefix) Pod [Prefix]<namespace>/<pod> The node agent that runs the pod

Node agents refer to the prefixed global agent; deployment agents refer to the unprefixed Kubernetes parent even when a prefix is set. Each pod agent refers to its prefixed node and uses the pod IP as its address. The global agent is described as Kubernetes global agent, node agents as Kubernetes node, deployment agents as Kubernetes deployment and pod agents as Kubernetes pod.

Node and pod agents do not depend on the Metrics API: when it is unavailable, they are still generated without CPU and memory modules. Only pods already scheduled to a node are discovered: a pod without an assigned node is skipped, as are resources the API returns without a name. Pod identities include the namespace, so equal pod names in different namespaces do not collide; deployment identities do not include the namespace, so equal deployment names in different namespaces can collide. Use separate prefixes for different clusters; namespace filtering does not add a namespace to the deployment identity.

Changing Prefix later changes the identity of every generated agent. The Filter namespace option applies only to deployments and pods, because nodes are cluster-scoped. Namespace matching is exact and case-sensitive, and the list is entered as a JSON array, for example ["default","kube-system"]. When Filter namespace is enabled, list at least one namespace: an empty list matches no workload and no deployment or pod agent is generated.

docs.title: Modules by agent
docs.text:
Every agent receives the modules of its resource. The values are read from the API during every task run; the exact name, type and unit of each module are listed in Generated modules.

Agent Modules it carries Global API status, API health endpoints, service count, namespace count, component statuses, deployment count Node Pod usage against the node allocatable, node conditions and, when the Metrics API is available, CPU and memory usage Deployment Replica counts, readiness and availability of the deployment Pod Pod phase and conditions, container count and, when the Metrics API is available, per-container CPU and memory usage

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The plugin can also be run outside the Discovery wizard with a configuration file. This is useful for testing connectivity or for a one-off run. Write a configuration file with the key=value pairs listed in Configuration file keys, then run the plugin entry point with the file as argument:

pandora_kubernetes --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

For example, this direct-mode configuration enables every resource category and scan option. Replace every placeholder before use; the example has not been executed:

ip=<TARGET_HOST>
port=<API_PORT>
token=<API_TOKEN>
agents_group_name=<AGENT_GROUP>
interval=300
transfer_mode=tentacle
tentacle_ip=<TENTACLE_HOST>
tentacle_port=41121
prefix=<CLUSTER_PREFIX>
use_prefix=1
use_namespace=1
filter_namespace=["default","kube-system"]
use_proxy=0
deployments=1
nodes=1
pods=1
health_checks=1
component_checks=1

Execution returns a Discovery JSON summary and generates XML for each agent. An illustrative summary is {"summary":{"Total agents":4,"Nodes agents":1,"Pods agents":1,"Deployments agents":1}}; these counters describe generation, not confirmed delivery.

The operational CLI input is --conf (-h/--help displays help). When the plugin runs as a Discovery task, the server builds that file from the task fields. Manual examples have not been executed against a live target.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text: Symptom Check The execution reports a request error Confirm Kubernetes host and Kubernetes port, that the API server is reachable from the Discovery server, and that the host does not include a scheme. Requests fail with 401 or 403 The token is missing, invalid or lacks read access to the queried resources. Health checks and component statuses may need elevated permissions. Check access to the exact paths in the API reference; no validated role definition is provided here. No deployments or pods are generated but nodes are Review Scan Deployments and Scan Pods, and Filter namespace: when it is enabled, names must match exactly and in the same case, and an empty list matches nothing. Expected pods are missing Only pods already scheduled to a node are discovered. A pod in Pending without an assigned node is not generated. Node CPU and memory modules are missing The Kubernetes Metrics API is not available in the cluster. The node agent is still generated. Some global, health or component modules are missing Those endpoints returned 401, 403 or 404, or the corresponding scan option is disabled. The plugin skips an optional endpoint that is not accessible instead of failing the whole run. API status is 0 The /healthz endpoint did not return ok. Check the API server health itself. If /healthz is inaccessible, the module is omitted. A deployment has no agent Check Scan Deployments, namespace filtering and returned deployment conditions. Deployment Available looks healthy despite a failing condition It reflects the first condition's type, not its Boolean status. Check replica counts and cluster conditions directly. API requests time out Requests use a fixed 5-second timeout and it is not configurable. Confirm the latency between the Discovery server and the API server. Tentacle transfer fails Confirm the Discovery server can reach Tentacle IP on Tentacle port. The global agent uses proxy mode but is not authenticated When Use proxy is enabled the plugin sends requests to Proxy url and does not add the Bearer token.

docs.title: Configuration file keys
docs.text:
The Discovery task builds this file from its own fields; a manual run supplies it with --conf. It is a plain text file of key=value lines.

Required manual inputs are ip, port and, for protected endpoints, token in direct mode; proxy_url in proxy mode; and transfer_mode=tentacle with tentacle_ip for delivery. Other keys are optional and use the defaults below. Protect the file because it contains the token.

Name Required Default Description ip Direct mode Empty API server host, without a scheme port Direct mode Empty API server port token Protected direct endpoints Empty Bearer token agents_group_name No Empty manually; task group Target agent group interval No 300 Agent interval in seconds; task interval in Discovery transfer_mode For delivery Empty manually; tentacle in task Use tentacle for the documented transfer path tentacle_ip For Tentacle Empty manually; 127.0.0.1 in task Transfer destination tentacle_port No 41121 Transfer port use_prefix No 0 Shows the task prefix field; does not suppress a populated prefix prefix No Empty Prefix applied to agent identities use_namespace No 0 1 enables workload namespace filtering filter_namespace When filtering [] JSON array; exact namespace matches use_proxy No 0 1 uses proxy_url without the Bearer header proxy_url Proxy mode Empty Base URL including scheme deployments No 1 1 collects deployments and generates deployment agents nodes No 1 1 collects nodes and generates node agents pods No 1 1 collects pods and generates pod agents health_checks No 1 1 generates the API health endpoint modules component_checks No 1 1 generates the component status modules data_dir No Empty Accepted but does not select an output directory

docs.title: Command line
docs.text: Command Description pandora_kubernetes --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> Runs the plugin with a configuration file

docs.title: Global agent
docs.text:
Module name Type What it reports API status generic_proc 1 when /healthz returns ok, 0 otherwise; created only when /healthz responds One module per health endpoint generic_proc 1 when the response is ok, 0 otherwise; only when Scan API health checks is enabled and the endpoint responds Services generic_data Number of services; omitted if the request is not accessible Namespaces generic_data Number of namespaces; omitted if the request is not accessible Components generic_data Number of component statuses; only when Scan component statuses is enabled and the request is accessible <component>.<condition> generic_data 1 when the component condition status is TRUE, 0 otherwise Deployments generic_data Number of deployments; 0 when Scan Deployments is disabled

Health module names and their exact paths are listed in API requests. A module is created only for an endpoint that responds. Optional endpoint failures do not prevent the global agent from being transferred.

docs.title: Node agents
docs.text:
Module name Type Unit What it reports Pods generic_data — Pods counted during collection on the node Pods (%) generic_data % Collected pod count against the node's allocatable pod capacity; omitted when the capacity is missing CPU (cores) generic_data cores CPU used by the node. Requires the Metrics API CPU (%) generic_data % CPU used against the allocatable CPU. Requires the Metrics API Memory (bytes) generic_data bytes Memory used by the node. Requires the Metrics API Memory (%) generic_data % Memory used against the allocatable memory. Requires the Metrics API NetworkUnavailable, MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure generic_proc — 1 when the corresponding condition is False, 0 otherwise Ready generic_proc — 1 when the condition is True, 0 otherwise

Node agents are generated even when the Metrics API is unavailable; the CPU and memory modules are then omitted. Pods counts pods processed from the returned data, not an independently validated count of every pod on the node.

docs.title: Deployment agents
docs.text:
