docs.title: KVM Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-19.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The KVM Discovery plugin connects to KVM hypervisors and reads their inventory and state through virsh and ps, either over SSH or locally on the machine that runs the task. It creates a two-level agent hierarchy in Pandora FMS:

  • one agent per KVM host, named KVM <host>;
  • one agent per virtual machine, named <vm> (<host>) and created as a child of its host agent.

Host agents carry the libvirtd status and, when Monitor KVM server performance is enabled, the RAM and CPU usage of the KVM server, including its RAM consumption in bytes. Virtual machine agents carry the VM power state and, for running VMs, the number of assigned vCPUs, the CPU usage per vCPU, the memory usage in percent and the memory consumption in bytes. CPU usage is a gauge: the plugin samples virsh domstats --vcpu twice around a one-second window and translates the vCPU time delta into a per-vCPU percentage. For running VMs, the plugin also resolves the VM IPv4 address with virsh domifaddr and uses it as the agent address when one is available. The plugin only generates Discovery data; the task re-executes on its configured interval to refresh the inventory and the module values.

The plugin runs as a Discovery task: the console creates the task, the Discovery server runs the plugin, and the generated agents and modules are created automatically.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Plugin version 1.0 (pandorafms.kvm) Documented target The version this page describes, as identified by the package definition. A Pandora FMS server with Discovery enabled Required The integration runs as a Discovery task created from the console. libvirt with virsh on every monitored host Required Every metric is read through virsh, and the libvirtd process check decides whether a host is up. SSH access to every remote target Required Remote targets are monitored over SSH on the configured port; only local targets run without it. A Linux distribution, KVM or libvirt version of the monitored hosts Not validated No published test record establishes compatibility with a concrete distribution or libvirt release. Operating system of the server that runs the task Not validated No published test record establishes operating-system compatibility.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• A Pandora FMS server with Discovery enabled to run the task, and a console to define it.
  • On every monitored KVM host: libvirt installed with the virsh command available, and the libvirtd daemon running. A host without libvirtd is still generated, with KVM Server status = 0 and without performance or VM modules.
  • An SSH account on every remote host allowed to run ps and virsh. Reading libvirt usually requires membership in the libvirt group or root.
  • For SSH key authentication: a private key readable by the user that runs the discovery task, with its public key installed on every monitored host. Optionally, a known_hosts file with the host keys of those hosts to enable host key verification.
  • For Pandora credentials authentication: a custom credential in the Pandora credential manager that stores the SSH username and password.
  • A target agent group and a monitoring interval for the generated agents. Both come from the Discovery task and are inherited by every generated agent.
  • A local target runs ps and virsh on the machine that executes the task, so use it only when the task runs on the KVM host itself.
  • Network reachability from the Discovery server to every remote host on the SSH port. With Transfer mode set to tentacle, the configured Tentacle destination must also be reachable.
  • The plugin is distributed as a Pandora FMS Discovery application (.disco package) that the Discovery server executes on the Pandora FMS server.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
From the Marketplace. Open Marketplace → Search in the console, find the KVM Discovery entry and click Install. Installation requires an administrator account. The package is installed directly and KVM appears under the Applications section of the Discovery wizard.

Manual installation. Load the .disco package from Management → Discovery → Manage disco packages: choose Select a file, pick the package, and click Upload DISCO. After loading, KVM appears in the package list and under the Applications section of the Discovery wizard.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text: Create the task from Management → Discovery → Applications → KVM. The wizard walks through the generic task definition and three plugin steps: KVM Connection, Authentication and KVM Monitoring Options. Every field is documented in Task parameters.

docs.title: Step 1 — Task definition
docs.text: The generic step asks for the task name, the agent group and server on which the task runs, and the interval. The group and the interval are passed to the plugin and inherited by every generated agent.

docs.title: Step 2 — KVM Connection
docs.text:
The target list and the connection settings:

  • KVM hosts is the target list, one entry per line; comma-separated values are also accepted inside a line. At least one entry is required. Each entry is user@host, host or local:
  • user@host connects to host over SSH as user, which overrides the configured authentication user;
  • host connects to host over SSH with the default SSH user (key mode) or the credential user (credentials mode);
  • local runs ps and virsh on the machine that executes the task and uses no authentication.
  • SSH port is the SSH port used to connect to the remote hosts. Default 22.
  • Command timeout is the SSH connection and command timeout in seconds. Default 10.
  • Authentication mode selects how the plugin authenticates: SSH key or Pandora credentials. The next step renders the fields of the selected mode.

docs.title: Step 3 — Authentication
docs.text:
The fields of this step depend on the Authentication mode selected in the previous step.

In SSH key mode:

  • SSH private key path is the path to the SSH private key on the Pandora server, readable by the user that runs the discovery task. Required in this mode.
  • Default SSH user is the user used for targets without an explicit user@ prefix. The user@ part of a target overrides it.
  • SSH known_hosts file: when set, the host key of every target is verified against this file and unknown hosts are rejected. When empty, unknown host keys are accepted.

In Pandora credentials mode:

  • Pandora credentials is the custom credential selected from the Pandora credential manager. Required in this mode.
  • SSH known_hosts file behaves as in key mode.

docs.title: Step 4 — KVM Monitoring Options
docs.text:
What the task monitors and how the data is delivered:

  • Monitor KVM server performance, when enabled, adds the KVM Server RAM usage (%), KVM Server RAM consumption (bytes) and KVM Server CPU usage (%) modules to the host agent. The KVM Server status module is always created.
  • Monitor virtual machines, when enabled, creates one agent per virtual machine and the Number of VMs module on the host agent.
  • Allow list is a regular expression applied to VM names: only matching VMs get an agent. Empty allows every VM.
  • Deny list is a regular expression applied to VM names after the allow list: matching VMs are excluded. Empty denies no VM.
  • Transfer mode selects how the generated data reaches Pandora FMS. native lets the Discovery server read the agent data directly; tentacle sends the generated agent files to Tentacle IP on Tentacle port with the Tentacle client.
  • Tentacle IP and Tentacle port are the Tentacle destination used in tentacle mode. Defaults 127.0.0.1 and 41121.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Run the task from Management → Discovery → Task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary shows the overall progress and a summary with Total Targets, Total Agents and Total Modules.
  2. The agents. Expect one host agent (KVM <host>) per reachable target, plus one agent per monitored virtual machine, created as a child of its host agent.
  3. The modules. A host with libvirtd running carries KVM Server status and, depending on the enabled options, the server performance modules and Number of VMs. Every VM agent carries Status of <vm>; a running VM also carries its vCPU and memory modules.
  4. The execution information. A successful run reports no errors; connection or command failures, and the reason why a module was omitted, are recorded there.

The example above reports one target, two agents and ten modules: the KVM host agent with five modules and one of its virtual machines with the other five. If the task fails before generating anything, the target list, the SSH connectivity and the selected credentials are the first things to check.

docs.title: Agents and identity
docs.text:
The plugin creates one agent per KVM host and one agent per virtual machine, with the host agent as the parent of each of its VM agents. Every generated agent belongs to the task's agent group, inherits its interval and carries one of the following aliases. With Transfer mode native, generated agents also report KVM as their operating system.

Element Agent alias Parent agent KVM host KVM <host> — Virtual machine <vm> (<host>) The host agent

<host> is the host part of the target as written in KVM hosts. The host agent reports that host as its address (no address for local targets), and a running VM agent uses the VM IPv4 address when it can be resolved.

Generated data also carries stable extra_data markers that identify the origin of each element. Names are normalized to lowercase and characters other than letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores are replaced with underscores:

Element Marker Host agent kvm:host:<host> VM agent kvm:vm:<host>:<vm> Host module kvm:metric:<host>:<metric> VM module kvm:metric:<host>:<vm>:<metric>

docs.title: Modules by agent
docs.text:
The module values are read from each target during every task run; the exact name and creation condition of each module are listed in Generated modules.

Agent Modules it carries KVM host libvirtd status; with Monitor KVM server performance: RAM usage, RAM consumption and CPU usage of the KVM server; with Monitor virtual machines: the number of defined virtual machines Virtual machine VM power state; for running VMs: assigned vCPUs, CPU usage per vCPU, memory usage in percent and memory consumption in bytes

A host without libvirtd keeps its agent with KVM Server status = 0 and no other modules, and generates no VM agents.

The virtual memory usage of a running VM is measured on the host as the resident memory of the domain against its current memory allocation, so it reports what the VM consumes on the host rather than the memory assigned to it, and it can exceed 100%.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The plugin can also be run outside the Discovery wizard with a configuration file and a targets file. This is useful for testing connectivity, for a one-off run, or for a custom schedule.

Write a [CONF] configuration file with at least the authentication mode and its values, and a targets file with one entry per line in the same formats as KVM hosts. Then run pandora_kvm --conf <config_file> --targets_file <targets_file>. All parameters are documented in Configuration file.

[CONF]
auth_mode = key
ssh_key_path = <PATH_TO_SSH_KEY>
ssh_user = <USER>
ssh_port = 22
timeout = 10
transfer_mode = native
interval = 300
agents_group_id = <GROUP_ID>
monitor_host = 1
monitor_vms = 1

In credentials mode use auth_mode = credentials and credentials = <BASE64_CREDENTIAL> instead of ssh_key_path. The credential value is an encoded username and password, not an encrypted one, so protect the configuration file as a secret.

docs.title: Execution behavior
docs.text:
• Targets are processed sequentially, in the order they are listed. A connection or command error on one target is recorded in the execution information and the remaining targets are still processed.
  • VM CPU usage is sampled per host, not per VM: when at least one VM is running, the plugin reads virsh domstats --vcpu twice, one second apart, and uses the measured window for the percentage. A run takes about one extra second per host with running VMs, and the sampling window is not configurable.
  • When the default virsh list --all returns no virtual machines, the plugin retries the listing with /usr/bin/virsh -r -c qemu:///system and uses that connection for the VM metrics of the host.
  • When the console leaves an unresolved macro placeholder in the generated configuration, for example credentials in SSH key mode, the plugin treats the value as empty.
  • A non-running virtual machine still gets its agent with its status module; its performance modules are not created.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text: Symptom Check The task reports Error connecting to <host> Confirm SSH reachability and the port. In key mode check SSH private key path and Default SSH user; in credentials mode check the selected credential. The task reports SSH key authentication requires a key path The task runs in SSH key mode but SSH private key path is empty. Set the path or switch to Pandora credentials. The task reports Invalid Pandora credentials The credential is missing, is not a valid custom credential or has an empty password. Select a custom credential in the Authentication step. The connection is rejected and SSH known_hosts file is set The host key of the target is missing or has changed. Update the file (ssh-keyscan -p <port> <host>) or clear the field. The task reports No agents were created for any target Every target failed. Review the per-target errors in the execution information, starting with connectivity and credentials. The task reports Error listing VMs on <host> Run virsh list --all on the host with the same user and confirm the libvirt permissions. The host agent has KVM Server status = 0 libvirtd is not running on that host, or the SSH user cannot see its processes. No VM agents although the host is up Confirm Monitor virtual machines is enabled and review the Allow list and Deny list expressions. An invalid regex is ignored: it neither allows nor denies anything. The Number of VMs module is not created Monitor virtual machines is disabled. Assigned vCPUs of <vm> or Virtual CPU usage of <vm> (%) is missing A virsh domstats --vcpu sample was missing in either read, the vCPU time delta was negative (the VM restarted between samples) or the command failed. The reason is recorded in the execution information. Virtual memory consumption of <vm> (bytes) is missing virsh dommemstat failed and the virsh dominfo fallback could not read the used memory. Virtual memory usage of <vm> (%) is still created and reports 0. The reason is recorded in the execution information. The KVM Server RAM or KVM Server CPU modules are not created Monitor KVM server performance is disabled, libvirtd is not running, or virsh nodememstats / virsh nodecpustats --percent failed. Both RAM modules are omitted together. A VM agent has no address virsh domifaddr returned no usable IPv4 address (no NIC, no DHCP lease yet or IPv6 only). This is best effort and not an error.

docs.text: Field Macro Type Default Notes Monitor KVM server performance _monitorHost_ checkbox on Adds the KVM server RAM and CPU modules to the host agent Monitor virtual machines _monitorVms_ checkbox on Creates one agent per virtual machine and the Number of VMs module on the host agent Allow list _allowList_ string — Regex for VM names. Empty allows all Deny list _denyList_ string — Regex for VM names, applied after the allow list. docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The Discovery task builds a configuration file for the plugin, and a manual execution uses the same format. It is a plain text file with a [CONF] section of key = value lines.

Parameter Default Description auth_mode key key or credentials. An empty value falls back to credentials when credentials has a value, and to key otherwise ssh_key_path — Path to the SSH private key. Required in key mode ssh_user — Default SSH user for targets without an explicit user@ prefix known_hosts — SSH known_hosts file. When set, host keys are verified and unknown hosts are rejected credentials — Credential produced by the Pandora credential manager: a base64 JSON value with user and password ssh_port 22 SSH port used to connect to the KVM hosts timeout 10 SSH connection and command timeout in seconds transfer_mode native native or tentacle tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1 Tentacle destination tentacle_port 41121 Tentacle destination port interval Task interval (300 from the command line) Interval assigned to the generated agents agents_group Task group Agent group name used in tentacle mode agents_group_id Task group ID Numeric agent group used in native mode allow_list — Regex allow list for VM names deny_list — Regex deny list for VM names monitor_host 1 Set to 0 to disable the KVM server performance modules monitor_vms 1 Set to 0 to disable virtual machine discovery prefix — Prefix added to the generated agent aliases and module names. The Discovery task never sets it

Command-line values act as defaults for this file; a parameter present in the configuration file overrides its command-line counterpart.

In credentials mode the selected credential is stored as the base64 JSON value in the task configuration, or in credentials in a manual configuration file. This is an encoding, not encryption: protect the Pandora FMS console, the configuration file and the file permissions of anything that stores it. The SSH private key stays on the server and is referenced by path.

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text: The plugin generates the following modules per agent. Created when is the condition under which the module appears.

docs.title: KVM host agent
docs.text: Module Type Unit Created when KVM Server status generic_proc — Always. 1 when at least one libvirtd process runs on the host, 0 otherwise KVM Server RAM usage (%) generic_data % Monitor KVM server performance enabled and libvirtd running KVM Server RAM consumption (bytes) generic_data bytes Same condition as the RAM usage module KVM Server CPU usage (%) generic_data % Monitor KVM server performance enabled and libvirtd running Number of VMs generic_data — Monitor virtual machines enabled and libvirtd running. Counts the entries returned by virsh list --all

docs.title: Virtual machine agent
docs.text:
Module Type Unit Created when Status of <vm> generic_proc — Always. 1 when the VM is running, 0 otherwise Assigned vCPUs of <vm> generic_data — Running VM with a complete CPU sample Virtual CPU usage of <vm> (%) generic_data % Running VM with a complete CPU sample Virtual memory usage of <vm> (%) generic_data % Running VM Virtual memory consumption of <vm> (bytes) generic_data bytes Running VM whose used memory can be determined

A module that depends on a measurement that could not be read is omitted and the reason is recorded in the task execution information; the rest of the agent modules are still created. Virtual memory usage of <vm> (%) is always created for a running VM and reports 0 when its measurement fails.

docs.title: Commands run on the target
docs.text:
Metric Command libvirtd status ps aux \| grep libvirtd \| grep -v grep \| wc -l VM list virsh list --all (fallback: /usr/bin/virsh -r -c qemu:///system list --all) KVM server RAM virsh nodememstats KVM server CPU virsh nodecpustats --percent VM vCPUs and CPU usage virsh domstats --vcpu, twice around a one-second window VM memory virsh dommemstat <vm> (fallback: virsh dominfo <vm>) VM IP address virsh domifaddr <vm> (running VMs, best effort)

The virsh binary is resolved with whereis virsh | cut -f2 -d' ' and falls back to /usr/bin/virsh.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
Command Description pandora_kvm --conf <config_file> --targets_file <targets_file> Runs the plugin with a configuration file and a targets file pandora_kvm --conf <config_file> --targets_file <targets_file> --as_server_plugin true Server plugin mode: returns 1 when at least one agent was created and 0 otherwise

Every configuration parameter has an equivalent command-line flag with the same meaning (--auth_mode, --ssh_key_path, --monitor_vms, and so on), except agents_group, agents_group_id and prefix, which are configuration-file only. --as_server_plugin is command-line only.

docs.title: Meraki Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Meraki Discovery addon monitors Cisco Meraki network devices through the Meraki Dashboard REST API. For one Meraki network it reads the status of the devices of three product types, appliance, switch and wireless, and turns the result into Pandora FMS agents and modules: device status, appliance uplink status and performance score, switch port status and traffic, wireless throughput and connected clients, and optionally the aggregated appliance traffic of the network.

A Discovery task generates these agents:

  • One agent per appliance with its status and uplink status.
  • One agent per switch with its status and the status and traffic of each port.
  • One agent per wireless device with its status, throughput and client count.
  • One network traffic agent (optional) with the aggregated traffic of the appliances of the network.

The task authenticates with a Bearer token and sends the generated agent data to Pandora FMS with Tentacle.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.meraki, version 1.1 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the Discovery server to the Meraki Dashboard API Required Every request goes to the API URL configured in the task Meraki API Bearer token with access to the organization Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon Specific Meraki hardware models and firmware Not validated No model or firmware matrix has been recorded

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to the Meraki Dashboard API (the task form suggests https://api.meraki.com/api/v1 as the URL).
  2. A Meraki API Bearer token that can read the organization, its networks and their devices. The addon only issues read (GET) requests.
  3. The organization ID and, for the network to monitor, its name (or part of it) and its network ID. See Configure the Discovery task for how each value is used.
  4. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it. The generated data is sent with Tentacle, so the Tentacle server address and port must be reachable from the Discovery server.

The addon ships its own executable, bin/pandora_meraki, so nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server to run a task.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.meraki

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, Meraki is available among the applications when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from Management → Discovery → Application → Meraki. The console presents the fields in two steps, Meraki base and Meraki Detailed; every field is documented in Task parameters.

One task monitors one network. To monitor several networks, create one task per network.

  1. Meraki base — connection and target:

    • ID: text that identifies the network by name. The addon looks for the first network of the organization whose name contains this text (a plain substring match, not a regular expression) and monitors the devices that belong to it.
    • Token: the Meraki API Bearer token.
    • Url: the API base URL, for example https://api.meraki.com/api/v1.
    • Organization: the organization ID.
    • Network: the ID of the network. It is used as-is in the network-level requests (aggregated appliance traffic and wireless usage), so enter the ID of the same network selected with ID.
    • Use location and Location: secondary groups added to the generated agents.
    • Tentacle IP and Tentacle port: where the generated agent data is sent.

  2. Meraki Detailed — naming and scope:

    • Use prefix, Agent Prefix and Module Prefix: prefixes added to agent and module names.
    • Interval monitoring: time window of the switch port statistics, in seconds.
    • Use API and the Api fields: reserved fields that this version does not use. See Task parameters.
    • Name Agent Hostname: name the agents after the device name instead of its serial number.
    • Scan appliances, Scan switches, Scan wireless and Scan Appliance Traffic Network: which device types and data to collect.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to the agents the task creates.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from Management → Discovery → Task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes successfully reports:

    • Total agents: all agents generated.
    • Total appliance agents, Total switches agents and Total wireless agents: agents per device type.
    • Total network appliance traffic agents: 1 when the network traffic agent was generated.

    A task that does not complete successfully records the errors in its execution information instead.

  2. The agents. Their aliases start with the agent prefix (if any) followed by Appliance_, Switch_ or Wireless_ and the device name or serial number.

  3. The modules. Every device agent has a status module. See Understand the results for the rest.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Alias Address Secondary groups Appliance <agent prefix>Appliance_<name or serial> Public IP address of the device Location, plus Router Switch <agent prefix>Switch_<name or serial> Public IP address of the device Location, plus Switch Wireless <agent prefix>Wireless_<name or serial> Public IP address of the device Location, plus Access Points Network traffic <agent prefix> Traffic Appliance_<Network> None Location
  • With Name Agent Hostname enabled, switch and wireless agents use the device name, falling back to the serial number when the device has no name; when disabled, the serial number is used. Appliance agents also read the flag, but they take the name from the switch data, which the appliance path does not have: with Name Agent Hostname enabled the run stops with an error when it reaches an appliance. Disable it to create appliance agents named after the serial number.
  • The agent identity is derived from the agent prefix and the name or serial used. Changing the prefix or the Name Agent Hostname setting, or renaming a device, produces a new agent instead of updating the previous one.
  • Only devices that belong to the monitored network and whose type is enabled (Scan appliances, Scan switches, Scan wireless) produce agents.
  • Agents report with the task group and interval.

docs.title: Modules per agent
docs.text:
Module names are shown without the module prefix.

Appliance agent

Module Type Condition Description status generic_proc Always 1 when the device status is online, 0 otherwise. The description carries the status reported by Meraki perfScore generic_data When Meraki returns a performance score for the device Performance score, in % Uplink <interface>_ifOperStatus generic_proc One per uplink reported for the device 1 when the uplink status is active, 0 otherwise. The description carries the uplink status

Switch agent

Module Type Condition Description status generic_proc Always 1 when the device status is online, 0 otherwise Port <portId>_ifOperStatus generic_proc One per port 1 when the port status is Connected, 0 otherwise Port <portId>_ifOutOctets generic_data One per port Traffic sent by the port, in Kbps Port <portId>_ifInOctets generic_data One per port Traffic received by the port, in Kbps

Wireless agent

Module Type Condition Description status generic_proc Always 1 when the device status is online, 0 otherwise totalKbps generic_data When Meraki returns usage data Total throughput, in Kbps sentKbps generic_data When Meraki returns usage data Throughput sent, in Kbps receivedKbps generic_data When Meraki returns usage data Throughput received, in Kbps clientCount generic_data When Meraki returns the client count Clients connected

Network traffic agent (when Scan Appliance Traffic Network is enabled)

Module Type Description Traffic appliance <Network> total_sent generic_data Sum of the data sent over all the applications reported by Meraki for the appliances of the network Traffic appliance <Network> total_recv generic_data Sum of the data received over the same applications Traffic appliance <Network> total_clients generic_data Sum of the number of clients over the same applications

docs.title: How the values are obtained
docs.text:
• Device status, appliance uplink status and the device list are read for the whole organization and then filtered by the monitored network.
  • The switch port statistics cover the last Interval monitoring seconds.
  • The wireless throughput and client count, and the network appliance traffic, are read for the last 86400 seconds (24 hours) and are not configurable.
  • For wireless devices, the module values are the first data point that Meraki returns for the device.
  • The network traffic agent is generated whenever Scan Appliance Traffic Network is enabled, even when Scan appliances is disabled.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. The executable takes a single parameter, the path to a configuration file described in Configuration file:

./pandora_meraki --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

It prints a JSON execution result with the summary and any error messages, and sends one data file per agent using the configured transfer mode. In tentacle mode (the default) the tentacle_client executable must be available in the PATH of the user running the addon.

The configuration file contains the Bearer token. Protect it with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the information of the JSON execution result, which is shown in the task's execution information.

  • error: id its required, error: base url its required, error: bearer token its required, error: organization its required, error: network its required: the named setting is empty. All five are mandatory.
  • Meraki nets could not be obtained.: the request to list the networks of the organization did not return data. Check the Url, the Organization ID, the validity of the Token and the connectivity to the API.
  • Request Error: <detail>: the connection to the API failed. The detail carries the error of the HTTP client.
  • Error: 204 : Data could not be obtained. and Error: 204 : PerfScore data could not be obtained.: Meraki answered without content for a request. The corresponding modules are not created.
  • No agents are generated: the text in ID does not match the name of any network of the organization, the monitored network has no devices of the enabled types, or the device types are disabled.
  • No perfScore or Uplink modules on an appliance: Meraki did not return performance or uplink data for that device.
  • No wireless modules besides status: the network-level wireless requests returned no data for the device in the last 24 hours.
  • Error getting switch data: <detail>, Error getting wireless data: <detail> or Error getting appliance data: <detail>: the data of a device could not be processed. The detail carries the cause.
  • Data does not reach Pandora FMS: check Tentacle IP and Tentacle port, and the connectivity to the Tentacle server.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
Used by manual execution. One key = value per line, without sections. Numeric options accept 1 to enable and 0 to disable; a value that is not a number is read as 0.

Key Required Default Description id Yes — Text contained in the name of the network to monitor base_url Yes — API base URL bearer_token Yes — Bearer token organization Yes — Organization ID network Yes — Network ID used in the network-level requests location No empty Secondary groups of the agents agents_group_name No empty Group of the generated agents interval No 300 Agent interval, in seconds agent_prefix No empty Prefix of the agents module_prefix No empty Prefix of the modules interval_monitoring No 3600 Time window of the switch port statistics, in seconds agentname_hostname No 1 1 names agents after the device name, 0 after the serial number scan_appliance No 1 Appliance agents scan_switch No 1 Switch agents scan_wireless No 1 Wireless agents scan_traffic_appliance_network No 1 Network traffic agent transfer_mode No tentacle tentacle sends the data files with Tentacle; local moves them to the default Pandora FMS data directory (/var/spool/pandora/data_in/) tentacle_address No 127.0.0.1 Tentacle server address tentacle_port No 41121 Tentacle server port tentacle_client No tentacle_client Tentacle client executable tentacle_opts No empty Extra Tentacle client options. docs.title: MongoDB Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-09-08.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The MongoDB Discovery plugin connects to MongoDB deployments and databases and turns their state and performance into Pandora FMS agents and modules. It reads a list of targets given as connection URIs, authenticates with the user embedded in each URI, and collects engine metrics through the serverStatus, dbStats and other commands.

A Discovery task creates one agent per target. When Scan databases is enabled it also collects per-database metrics, and when Create agent per database is enabled it creates one agent per discovered database. Custom queries can be defined to add one module per query and database.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Plugin version 1.6 (pandorafms.mongodb) Documented target The version this page describes, as identified by the package definition. See Plugin identity. A reachable MongoDB deployment Required The plugin establishes remote connections to each target through its connection URI. Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. A MongoDB user with the read or dbAdmin role on the monitored databases Required Needed for the database-level commands. Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. See Prepare MongoDB access. A MongoDB user with the clusterMonitor or clusterAdmin role Required Needed for the server statistics. Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. A specific MongoDB version Not validated No published test record establishes compatibility with a concrete MongoDB release. A specific Pandora FMS version Not validated No published test record establishes console or server version compatibility. A specific host operating system Not validated No published test record establishes operating-system compatibility for the machine that runs the plugin.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. A Pandora FMS server with Discovery enabled to run the task, and a console to define it.
  2. Connectivity between the Pandora FMS server and each MongoDB deployment (default port 27017).
  3. A MongoDB user with the required roles. See Prepare MongoDB access.
  4. A target agent group and a monitoring interval for the generated agents, taken from the Discovery task.

The plugin is distributed as a Pandora FMS Discovery application (.disco package) with its Python dependencies bundled, so no extra Python libraries have to be installed on the Discovery server.

docs.title: Prepare MongoDB access
docs.text:
The user used by the task must reach each deployment over the network and hold the roles the monitor needs. From the official prerequisites:

  • For databases: the read or dbAdmin role on the databases to be monitored.
  • For server statistics: the clusterMonitor or clusterAdmin role.

Grant the user only the access required by your monitoring policy; the plugin only reads and never changes MongoDB data or configuration.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text: Load the .disco package from Management → Discovery → Extension manager (the Manage disco packages view). The package is available from the Pandora FMS library. Once loaded, MongoDB appears under the Applications category of the Discovery wizard.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from Management → Discovery → Applications → MongoDB. The generic first step defines the task; the package adds MongoDB Base, MongoDB Detailed and MongoDB custom. Every field is documented in Task parameters.

Step 1 — Task definition. Name, agent group, server and interval. The group ID and the interval are passed to the plugin and applied to every generated agent.

Step 2 — MongoDB Base. The targets to connect to:

  • MongoDB target strings is the list of instances to monitor, comma-separated or one per line. Each target is a MongoDB connection URI, for example mongodb://172.17.0.2:27017 or mongodb+srv://monitor.user:password@cluster.example.com/my_db. Lines starting with # are comments.

Step 3 — MongoDB Detailed. Execution, agent layout and which metrics to collect:

  • Max threads distributes the targets across parallel workers.
  • Target agents sets the agent names for the targets, matching the position of the target list; a blank entry uses the target string.
  • Use prefix for modules and Custom module prefix prepend a prefix to every generated module name.
  • Scan databases collects the per-database metrics of each target, and Create agent per database creates one agent per database, with Custom database agent prefix naming them.
  • Agent autodisable mode creates the generated agents in Pandora FMS mode 2, which disables an agent when all its modules become unknown.
  • Check engine uptime, Retrieve query statistics, Analyze connections, Retrieve latency statistics and Retrieve network statistics select the engine metric groups collected.

Step 4 — MongoDB custom. The custom queries:

  • Execute custom queries enables the custom queries, and Custom queries defines them.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from Management → Discovery → Task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary reports Total agents, Targets up and Targets down. Targets up are the targets the plugin managed to connect to.

  2. The agents. One agent appears per reachable target, named by the Target agents list or by the target string. With Create agent per database, one agent appears per discovered database.

  3. The engine modules. A reachable target carries its connection, uptime, query, connection, latency and network modules according to the enabled toggles.

  4. The database modules. With Scan databases enabled, each database carries its collections, indexes, size, status and custom query modules.

Targets that cannot be reached are counted in Targets down and do not produce agents.

docs.title: Agents and identity
docs.text:
The plugin creates one agent per target by default. The agent name is the value from the Target agents list that matches the target position, or the target string when none is given. Each generated agent reports MONGODB as its operating system, its os_version is the MongoDB version returned by the server information (or Discovery when it cannot be read), and it belongs to the task's group (by ID) with the task interval. With Agent autodisable mode enabled the agents are created in Pandora FMS mode 2. The generated agents are returned in the plugin JSON output.

With Create agent per database, the plugin also creates one agent per database, named <Custom database agent prefix><target agent> <database name>, and counts them in Total agents.

The databases to monitor are collected from the deployment when Scan databases is enabled. When a target lists databases after | in its URI, only those are monitored; appending ! to the URI excludes the listed ones and monitors the rest. The engine metrics always go to the target agent, and the per-database metrics go to the database agents when Create agent per database is enabled, or to the target agent otherwise.

docs.title: Modules by agent
docs.text:
Agent Created when Modules it carries Target agent A target is reachable MONGODB connection, the engine metrics enabled by the toggles, and the per-database modules when Scan databases is enabled without Create agent per database Database agent Create agent per database enabled and a database is discovered The <database> metrics and the custom query modules

Module names are <Custom module prefix> plus the module name; the database modules also include the database name. The exhaustive module inventory and the toggle that enables each group are in Generated modules and agents.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The plugin can run outside Discovery, from a Pandora FMS agent or directly from the command line, with a configuration file and the target, agent and custom-query files created manually:

./pandora_mongodb --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --target_databases <PATH_TO_TARGETS> --target_agents <PATH_TO_AGENTS> --custom_queries <PATH_TO_QUERIES>

Only --conf and --target_databases are required; --target_agents and --custom_queries are optional. The plugin connects to each target in parallel according to Max threads and produces the agents and modules in its Discovery JSON output.

The target list holds the connection URIs, which may embed a username and a password. Restrict them to the account that runs the plugin and keep them out of shared directories, logs and version control.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text: Symptom Check No agent is created and the target is reported Targets down Confirm the deployment is reachable from the Pandora FMS server on its port (default 27017), that the MongoDB service is running, and that the connection URI is correct. Engine modules are missing and the execution information logs command errors The user needs the clusterMonitor or clusterAdmin role for the server statistics (serverStatus), and read or dbAdmin on the monitored databases. Grant those roles. Per-database modules are missing Enable Scan databases. A target without a | database list and with Scan databases off only produces the engine modules. Database agents are not created Enable Create agent per database. Without it, the database modules are placed on the target agent. Custom query modules are missing The query must be inside check_begin/check_end, use a permitted read command, and be run with Scan databases enabled. Check the crontab expression if the query is scheduled. Expected modules are missing Review the Detailed toggles: a disabled group produces no modules.

docs.title: Task parameters
docs.text: The console presents the task fields in three steps after the generic task definition. The macro column is the identifier used in the generated task configuration.

docs.title: MongoDB Base
docs.text: Field Macro Type Default Notes MongoDB target strings _dbstrings_ textarea — List of MongoDB connection URIs. Required

docs.title: MongoDB Detailed
docs.text: Field Macro Type Default Notes Max threads _threads_ number 1 Workers that distribute the targets Target agents _engineAgent_ textarea — Agent names for the targets, matching the target list position; blank uses the target string Use prefix for modules _usePrefixmodule_ checkbox off Enables the module prefix Custom module prefix _prefixModuleName_ string — Prefix prepended to every module name. Shown only when Use prefix for modules is enabled Scan databases _scanDatabases_ checkbox off Collects the per-database metrics of each target Create agent per database _agentPerDatabase_ checkbox off Creates one agent per database Custom database agent prefix _prefix_ string — Prefix for the database agents. Shown only when Create agent per database is enabled Agent autodisable mode _agentautodisable_ checkbox off Creates agents in Pandora FMS mode 2, which disables an agent when all its modules become unknown Check engine uptime _checkUptime_ checkbox on Server uptime Retrieve query statistics _queryStats_ checkbox on Query operation counters Analyze connections _checkConnections_ checkbox on Connection counters Retrieve latency statistics _checkLatency_ checkbox on Operation latencies Retrieve network statistics _checkNetwork_ checkbox on Network traffic counters

docs.title: MongoDB custom
docs.text: Field Macro Type Default Notes Execute custom queries _executeCustomQueries_ checkbox on Enables the custom queries Custom queries _customQueries_ textarea — Definition of the custom queries. Shown only when Execute custom queries is enabled

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The Discovery task builds a temporary --conf file from its own fields. A manual run supplies it directly. The file has a [CONF] section; the plugin reads it without a section header.

Key Default Description agents_group_id 10 ID of the group where the agents are created interval 300 Monitoring interval in seconds, inherited by the agents threads 1 Number of parallel workers modules_prefix Empty Prefix for the module names execute_custom_queries 1 Enables the custom queries analyze_connections 0 Connection counters engine_uptime 0 Server uptime query_stats 0 Query statistics network 0 Network statistics latency 0 Latency statistics scan_databases 0 Collects the per-database metrics agent_per_database 0 Creates one agent per database agent_autodisable 0 Creates agents in Pandora FMS mode 2 when enabled db_agent_prefix Empty Prefix for the database agents cron_state_dir Empty Folder for the custom query crontab state; derived from the task temporary path

docs.title: Target databases
docs.text:
The --target_databases file holds one or more MongoDB connection URIs, comma-separated or one per line. Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored. A URI may include a comma inside a replica-set connection string.

mongodb://172.17.0.2:27017
mongodb://monitor.user:s3cur3P@ss@mongo-prod-01.internal.company.com:27017/my_db

To monitor specific databases of a target, append | and separate the databases with ;:

mongodb://172.17.0.2:27017|my_db;test

To monitor every database except a set, append ! before the |:

mongodb://172.17.0.2:27017!|my_db;test

docs.title: Target agents
docs.text: The optional --target_agents file holds one agent name per target, comma-separated or one per line. The position of each name matches the position of the corresponding target in the target list; blank lines are ignored. A blank entry leaves the agent named after the target string.

docs.title: Command-line execution
docs.text:
The plugin accepts a configuration file, a target databases file, an optional target agents file and an optional custom queries file:

./pandora_mongodb --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --target_databases <PATH_TO_TARGETS> --target_agents <PATH_TO_AGENTS> --custom_queries <PATH_TO_QUERIES>
Option Description --conf Required path to the configuration file --target_databases Required path to the file with the target instances --target_agents Optional path to the file with the target agent names --custom_queries Optional path to the file with the custom queries

Example configuration file:

[CONF]
agents_group_id=10
interval=300
threads=1
modules_prefix=
execute_custom_queries=1
engine_uptime=1
query_stats=1
analyze_connections=1
latency=1
network=1
scan_databases=1
agent_per_database=0

docs.title: Custom queries
docs.text:
Each custom query creates one module per matching agent and database and is defined between check_begin and check_end:

Field Description name Module name description Module description operation value returns a single value, full returns all rows as a string datatype generic_data, generic_data_string or generic_proc min_warning, max_warning Numeric warning thresholds str_warning String warning condition warning_inverse 1 inverts the warning threshold interval min_critical, max_critical Numeric critical thresholds str_critical String critical condition critical_inverse 1 inverts the critical threshold interval module_interval Module interval, as a multiplier of the agent interval crontab 5-field cron expression; the query runs only when the date/time matches. Empty runs every interval target The command, one of dbStats, collStats, find, count, aggregate, listCollections target_instances Targets or agents where the module is created; all or empty applies to all target_databases Databases where the module is created; all or empty applies to all ignore_databases Databases where the module is not created

The custom queries are executed against the monitored databases during the database scan, so Scan databases must be enabled for them to run. The target accepts the $__self_dbname reserved word, which is replaced by the database name currently being analyzed. The supported commands are read-only; dbStats, collStats, find, count, aggregate and listCollections are allowed, other commands are rejected.

check_begin
name Query count
description Number of documents
operation value
datatype generic_data
min_warning 10
target db.coll.count({})
target_databases all
check_end

docs.title: Generated modules and agents
docs.text:
Module names are [<Custom module prefix>]<module name>, and the database modules also include the database name.

Target agent (one per reachable target)

Always created:

  • MONGODB connection: generic_proc, 1 when the target is reachable, 0 otherwise.

Created when the matching toggle is enabled:

  • Check engine uptime: Uptime (generic_data, estimated time of activity).
  • Retrieve query statistics: queries command, queries delete, queries getmore, queries insert, queries query, queries update (generic_data, operation counters).
  • Analyze connections: connections current, connections available, connections totalCreated (generic_data).
  • Retrieve latency statistics: operationlatencies.reads latency, operationlatencies.reads ops, operationlatencies.writes latency, operationlatencies.writes ops, operationlatencies.commands latency, operationlatencies.commands ops (generic_data).
  • Retrieve network statistics: network bytesIn, network bytesOut, network numRequests (generic_data).

Database modules (on the target agent or on the database agent, created when Scan databases is enabled, for each database found on the target)

  • <database> collections: generic_data, number of collections.
  • <database> indexes: generic_data, number of indexes.
  • <database> indexSize: generic_data, total size of all indexes (bytes).
  • <database> views: generic_data, number of views.
  • <database> objects: generic_data, number of documents.
  • <database> avgObjSize: generic_data, average document size (bytes).
  • <database> dataSize: generic_data, total size of the data (bytes).
  • <database> storageSize: generic_data, space used on disk (bytes).
  • <database> totalSize: generic_data, sum of the data and index size (bytes).
  • <database> fsUsedSize: generic_data, space used on the file system (bytes).
  • <database> fsTotalSize: generic_data, total file system size (bytes).
  • <database> status: generic_data, 1 when the database responds, 0 otherwise.
  • The custom query modules that match the database.

docs.title: Microsoft SQL Server Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-09-21.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Microsoft SQL Server Discovery plugin connects to Microsoft SQL Server instances and databases and turns their state and performance into Pandora FMS agents and modules. It reads a list of target instances, connects with a SQL Server login, and collects instance-wide metrics and per-database metrics through system views and performance counters.

A Discovery task creates one agent per target instance by default, and one agent per database when Create agent per database is enabled. Each agent carries the instance metrics of its target and the metrics of the databases it monitors. Custom queries can be defined to add one module per query and target.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Plugin version 1.16 (pandorafms.mssql) Documented target The version this page describes, as identified by the package definition. See Plugin identity. A reachable Microsoft SQL Server instance Required The plugin establishes remote connections to each monitored instance. Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. A SQL Server login with VIEW SERVER STATE Required Needed to read the instance system views and execution requests. Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. See Prepare SQL Server access. A SQL Server login with SELECT Required Needed to run the custom queries against tables and views. Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. The Microsoft ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server and unixODBC Required Needed only when ODBC mode is enabled; the plugin connects through that ODBC driver name. A specific Pandora FMS version Not validated No published test record establishes console or server version compatibility. A specific host operating system Not validated No published test record establishes operating-system compatibility for the machine that runs the plugin.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. A Pandora FMS server with Discovery enabled to run the task, and a console to define it.
  2. Connectivity between the Pandora FMS server and each Microsoft SQL Server instance (default port 1433).
  3. A SQL Server login with the required permissions. See Prepare SQL Server access.
  4. A target agent group and a monitoring interval for the generated agents, taken from the Discovery task.
  5. For ODBC mode, the Microsoft ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server and unixODBC installed on the machine that runs the plugin.

The plugin is distributed as a Pandora FMS Discovery application (.disco package) with its Python dependencies bundled, so no extra Python libraries have to be installed on the Discovery server.

docs.title: Prepare SQL Server access
docs.text:
The login used by the task must reach each instance over the network and hold the permissions the monitor needs. From the official prerequisites:

  • VIEW SERVER STATE to run SELECT @@VERSION, to read sys.dm_os_sys_info (server uptime), sys.dm_exec_requests (active requests), @@MAX_CONNECTIONS (maximum allowed connections), and to run sp_who 'ACTIVE' (active sessions).
  • SELECT to execute the custom queries against the specific tables or views they target.

Grant the login the access required by your monitoring policy; the plugin only reads and never changes SQL Server configuration.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text: Load the .disco package from Management → Discovery → Extension manager (the Manage disco packages view). The package is available from the Pandora FMS library. Once loaded, Microsoft SQL Server appears under the Applications category of the Discovery wizard.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from Management → Discovery → Applications → Microsoft SQL Server. The generic first step defines the task; the package adds Microsoft SQL Server Base and Microsoft SQL Server Detailed. Every field is documented in Task parameters.

Step 1 — Task definition. Name, agent group, server and interval. The group ID and the interval are passed to the plugin and applied to every generated agent.

Step 2 — Microsoft SQL Server Base. What to connect to and how:

  • Microsoft SQL Server target strings is the list of instances to monitor, comma-separated or one per line. Each target is SERVER, SERVER:PORT, SERVER\INSTANCE or SERVER:PORT\INSTANCE. Lines starting with # are comments. To monitor specific databases of an instance, append |db1;db2; to monitor every database except a set, append ! before the |. See Target databases.
  • User and Password are the SQL Server login used to connect.
  • ODBC mode connects through the ODBC driver instead of the native pymssql driver.
  • Connection timeout and Query timeout are the maximum seconds allowed to establish the connection and to run each query. Both default to 5.
  • Enable debug writes execution traces of the task, and Debug log directory (default /tmp) is where they are stored; the directory is shown only when debug is enabled.

Step 3 — Microsoft SQL Server Detailed. Execution, agent layout and which metrics to collect:

  • Max threads distributes the targets and databases across parallel workers.
  • Target agent sets the agent names for the targets, comma-separated or one per line, matching the position of the target list; a blank entry uses the target string as the agent name.
  • Custom module prefix is prepended to every generated module name.
  • Scan databases enumerates the databases of each instance automatically.
  • Create agent per database creates one agent per database, with Custom database agent prefix naming them.
  • Autodisabled agents creates the generated agents in disabled mode, so they stay idle until you enable them in the console.
  • Enable entities file re-scan interval and Re-scan entities file interval control how often the discovered-database cache is rebuilt.
  • The Database monitoring modules and Instance monitoring modules toggles select which metric groups are collected.
  • Rename default modules and Modules names let you replace the default module labels, and Execute custom queries and Custom queries define the custom queries.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from Management → Discovery → Task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary reports Total agents, Targets up and Targets down. With Create agent per database enabled, it also reports Databases agents. Targets up are the instances the plugin managed to connect to.

  2. The agents. One agent appears per reachable target instance, named by the Target agent list or by the target string. With Create agent per database, one agent appears per discovered or listed database.

  3. The instance modules. A reachable instance carries its engine, memory, buffer, connection, query and availability metrics according to the enabled toggles.

  4. The database modules. Each monitored database carries its state, availability, transaction, log, backup, filegroup and table-space metrics according to the enabled toggles, and the custom query modules.

Targets that cannot be reached are counted in Targets down and do not produce agents.

docs.title: Agents and identity
docs.text:
The plugin creates one agent per target instance by default. The agent name is the value from the Target agent list that matches the target position, or the target string itself when none is given. Each generated agent reports MSSQL as its operating system, its os_version is the SQL Server version returned by SELECT @@VERSION (or Discovery when it cannot be read), its address is the instance host, and it belongs to the task's group (by ID) with the task interval. With Autodisabled agents enabled, every generated agent is created in disabled mode and stays idle until you enable it.

With Create agent per database, the plugin also creates one agent per database, named <Custom database agent prefix><instance> <database>, and counts them in Databases agents. The database modules are then placed on those agents.

Databases to monitor are either listed explicitly after | in the target string, or discovered by scanning when Scan databases is enabled. The list of discovered databases is persisted in the entities file, and Enable entities file re-scan interval decides when that file is rebuilt so new databases are picked up and removed ones are dropped. Explicitly listed databases are always monitored.

docs.title: Modules by agent
docs.text:
Agent Created when Modules it carries Instance agent A target instance is reachable and no Create agent per database for its databases The instance metrics of the target, plus the database metrics of the databases it monitors Database agent Create agent per database enabled and a database is monitored The database metrics of that database, plus its custom query modules

Module names are <Custom module prefix>, the database name when the module is per-database, and the module name. The exhaustive module inventory and the toggle that enables each group are in Generated modules and agents.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The plugin can run outside Discovery, from a Pandora FMS agent or directly from the command line, with a configuration file and the target, agent and custom-query files created manually:

./pandora_mssql --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --target_databases <PATH_TO_TARGETS> --target_agents <PATH_TO_AGENTS> --custom_queries <PATH_TO_QUERIES>

Only --conf and --target_databases are required; --target_agents and --custom_queries are optional. The plugin connects to each target in parallel according to Max threads and produces the agents and modules in its Discovery JSON output.

The configuration file and the target lists hold the SQL Server password in plain text. Restrict them to the account that runs the plugin and keep them out of shared directories, logs and version control. Following the Discovery workflow for task runs means the console builds these files for you.

docs.title: Timeouts and connection recovery
docs.text: Every target is subject to Connection timeout and Query timeout, both 5 seconds by default. When a query fails because the session was dropped or timed out, the plugin closes that session, reconnects and continues with the remaining checks, so one slow or interrupted query does not stop the rest of the task. A non-positive or non-numeric timeout falls back to 5.

docs.title: Debug logs
docs.text: With Enable debug on, the plugin writes JSON traces into Debug log directory (default /tmp), one file per agent and module. Each record is timestamped and carries the plugin execution ID, and covers the plugin lifecycle, every connection and query (the query text is truncated), the value and description returned by each generated module, and the final Discovery JSON. Trace files rotate once they reach 2 MB, keeping three backups. Debug logging is a diagnostic aid; leave it off for normal runs.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text: Symptom Check No agent is created and the target is reported Targets down Confirm the instance is reachable from the Pandora FMS server on its port (default 1433), that the SQL Server service is running, and that the User and Password are correct. Instance modules are missing and the execution information logs retrieval warnings The login needs VIEW SERVER STATE for the instance system views and performance counters. Grant that permission. Custom query modules are missing The query must be inside check_begin/check_end, use a SELECT statement, and the login needs SELECT on the referenced tables or views. Check the crontab expression if the query is scheduled. A database is not monitored Either list it after | in the target string or enable Scan databases. The discovered database list is cached and refreshed only after Re-scan entities file interval. Database agents are not created Enable Create agent per database. Without it, the database modules are placed on the instance agent. ODBC mode fails to connect Install the Microsoft ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server and unixODBC on the machine that runs the plugin. The connection uses that driver name. A custom query is rejected Only SELECT statements are allowed; other statements are removed and reported in the execution information. Expected modules are missing Review the Database monitoring modules and Instance monitoring modules toggles: a disabled group produces no modules. A target is slow or the task hangs Lower Connection timeout and Query timeout, and confirm the instance responds on its port. The plugin reconnects after a dropped or timed-out session and continues with the remaining checks. You need to find which query or module failed Enable Enable debug, set Debug log directory, and read the per-agent JSON traces; they include each query and the value and description returned by each generated module. Generated agents appear disabled Autodisabled agents is enabled. Enable the agents in the console, or turn the option off and run the task again.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The Discovery task builds a temporary --conf file from its own fields. A manual run supplies it directly. The file has a [CONF] section and an optional [MODULE_NAMES] section.

Engine and monitoring preferences:

Key Default Description agents_group_id 10 ID of the group where the agents are created interval 300 Monitoring interval in seconds, inherited by the agents user Empty Connection user. Required password Empty Password for the user. Required threads 1 Number of parallel workers modules_prefix Empty Prefix for the module names entities_list /tmp/mssql_entities_list.txt File that caches the discovered databases enable_entities_interval 1 Rebuilds the database cache after the interval entities_interval 300 Seconds before the database cache is rebuilt scan_databases 0 Enumerates the databases of each instance odbc_mode 0 Connects through the ODBC driver connection_timeout 5 Maximum seconds allowed to establish the connection query_timeout 5 Maximum seconds allowed for each query debug 0 Writes execution traces of the task debug_directory /tmp Directory for the debug traces agent_per_database 0 Creates one agent per database db_agent_prefix Empty Prefix for the database agent names autodisabled_agents 0 Creates the generated agents in disabled mode rename_modules 1 Applies the [MODULE_NAMES] labels execute_custom_queries 1 Enables the custom queries cron_state_dir <entities_list>.cron_state Directory that persists the custom-query crontab state

Monitoring toggles (each 1 enables the group, each 0 disables it):

Key Default Enables engine_uptime 1 Restart detection query_stats 1 SELECT/INSERT/DELETE/UPDATE query counts analyze_connections 1 Session usage count_databases 1 Database count retrieve_memory_statistics 1 Memory statistics retrieve_locks_statistics 1 Locks statistics retrieve_buffer_statistics 1 Buffer cache hit ratio and free connections monitor_latch_requests 1 Latch waits monitor_full_scans 1 Full scans check_engine_performance 1 Server CPU and I/O retrieve_users_information 1 Users information monitor_long_queries 1 Long queries retrieve_cluster_state 0 AlwaysOn cluster state retrieve_logs_statistics 1 Log statistics monitor_active_users 1 Active user transactions retrieve_transactions_statistics 1 Transactions monitor_filegroups_space 1 Filegroup space monitor_user_reserved_space 1 User table space monitor_backups 1 Backups

The [MODULE_NAMES] section maps each default module key to the label that appears in the console, for example database_size = database_size and restart_detection = restart detection. Only the enabled toggle groups are renamed.

The --conf file and the target lists hold the SQL Server password in plain text. Restrict them to the account that runs the plugin and keep them out of shared directories, logs and version control.

docs.title: Target databases
docs.text:
The --target_databases file holds one or more target strings, comma-separated or one per line. Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.

Each target follows SERVER, SERVER:PORT, SERVER\INSTANCE or SERVER:PORT\INSTANCE. To monitor specific databases of an instance, append | and separate the databases with ;:

172.17.0.4:1433\DEVENV|pandora;testing;model

To monitor every database except a set, append ! before the |:

172.17.0.4:1433\DEVENV!|pandora;testing;model

docs.title: Target agents
docs.text:
The optional --target_agents file holds one agent name per target, comma-separated or one per line. The position of each name matches the position of the corresponding target in the target list; blank lines are ignored. A blank entry leaves the agent named after the target string (its IP or FQDN).

agente1,,agente3
agente4
agente5,agente6,agente7,,agente9

docs.title: Command-line execution
docs.text:
The plugin accepts a configuration file, a target databases file, an optional target agents file and an optional custom queries file:

./pandora_mssql --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --target_databases <PATH_TO_TARGETS> --target_agents <PATH_TO_AGENTS> --custom_queries <PATH_TO_QUERIES>
Option Description --conf Required path to the configuration file --target_databases Required path to the file with the target instances --target_agents Optional path to the file with the target agent names --custom_queries Optional path to the file with the custom queries

Example configuration file:

[CONF]
agents_group_id=10
interval=300
user=<SQL_LOGIN>
password=<SQL_PASSWORD>
threads=1
modules_prefix=
execute_custom_queries=1
engine_uptime=1
query_stats=1
analyze_connections=1
count_databases=1
retrieve_memory_statistics=1
retrieve_locks_statistics=1
check_engine_performance=1
retrieve_buffer_statistics=1
retrieve_users_information=1
monitor_long_queries=1
monitor_latch_requests=1
monitor_full_scans=1
retrieve_logs_statistics=1
monitor_active_users=1
retrieve_transactions_statistics=1
monitor_filegroups_space=1
monitor_user_reserved_space=1
monitor_backups=1
connection_timeout=5
query_timeout=5
debug=0
debug_directory=/tmp
autodisabled_agents=0
agent_per_database=0
scan_databases=1

[MODULE_NAMES]
database_size=database_size
database_usage=database_usage
restart_detection=restart detection

docs.title: Custom queries
docs.text:
Each custom query creates one module per task agent and is defined between check_begin and check_end:

Field Description name Module name description Module description operation value returns a single value, full returns all rows as a string datatype generic_data, generic_data_string or generic_proc min_warning, max_warning Numeric warning thresholds str_warning String warning condition warning_inverse 1 inverts the warning threshold interval min_critical, max_critical Numeric critical thresholds str_critical String critical condition critical_inverse 1 inverts the critical threshold interval module_interval Module interval, as a multiplier of the agent interval crontab 5-field cron expression; the query runs only when the date/time matches. Empty runs every interval target The query, a SELECT only target_databases Targets or databases where the module is created; all or empty applies to all target_scope instances, databases or all; empty applies to both ignore_databases Targets or databases where the module is not created

The crontab field follows the standard 5-field format (minute hour day_of_month month day_of_week) and supports *, exact values, ranges, steps and lists. On the first run after enabling a scheduled query only an occurrence inside the current interval is picked up, so a daily or monthly query does not run immediately.

The schedule is persisted under cron_state_dir (by default next to the entities file), so consecutive Discovery executions keep the same schedule. Only successful executions advance it; a query that fails stays due and is retried on the next execution.

check_begin
name Select 1
description Number of invalid objects
operation value
datatype generic_data
min_warning 5
target SELECT 1;
target_databases all
check_end

docs.title: Generated modules and agents
docs.text:
Module names are [<Custom module prefix>][<database name> ]<module name>. The labels below are the default [MODULE_NAMES] values; with Rename default modules enabled they can be replaced.

Instance metrics (on the instance agent)

Always created:

  • database_size: generic_data, the size of the database; MB.
  • database_usage: generic_data, percentage of the database that is used; unit %.
  • server_startup: generic_data, uptime of the database server in days.
  • page_reads: generic_data_inc, database page reads per second.
  • page_writes: generic_data_inc, database page writes per second.
  • locks_used: generic_data, used lock and lock owner blocks; unit %.
  • workspace_memory: generic_data, granted workspace memory; unit %.
  • average_waittime: generic_data, average lock wait time; unit ms.

Created when the matching toggle is enabled:

  • Check engine uptime: restart detection (generic_proc, 0 when a restart is detected, 1 otherwise).
  • Retrieve query statistics: queries, insert, delete, update (generic_data, count of running queries by type, within the interval).
  • Analyze connections: session usage (generic_data, current sessions as a percentage of the maximum; unit %).
  • Count databases: database_count (generic_data, number of existing databases).
  • Retrieve memory statistics: lock_memory, connection_memory, optimizer_memory, sqlcache_memory, total_memory (generic_data, bytes).
  • Retrieve locks statistics: deadlocks (generic_data, deadlocks per second), lock_timeouts, lock_requests, lock_waits (generic_data_inc). lock_waits carries a critical threshold at 90.
  • Retrieve buffer statistics: buf_cachehit_ratio (generic_data, pages found in the buffer cache; unit %), free_connections (generic_data, free connections; unit %).
  • Monitor latch requests: latch_waits (generic_data_inc, latch requests per second).
  • Monitor full scans: full_scans (generic_data_inc, full scans per second).
  • Check engine performance: server_cpu (generic_data, CPU usage by the instance; unit %, critical at 90), server_io (generic_data_inc, I/O busy; unit %, critical at 80).
  • Retrieve users information: active_connection_ratio (generic_data_string, active to total connections; unit %), locked_users, blocked_users, active_users (generic_data).
  • Monitor long queries: long_queries (generic_data, seconds of the longest running query; unit s, critical at 600), long_queries_string (async_string, the output of the long-running queries).
  • Retrieve Cluster State: aag_cluster_quorum_state, aag_cluster_members_state <member>, aag_synchronization_health, aag_replica_synchronization_health <replica>, aag_replica_connected_state <replica>, aag_replica_recovery_health, aag_replica_operational_state, aag_db_replica_synchronization_state <database> (generic_proc), aag_listener_state <replica> (generic_data, AlwaysOn availability group and replica states, with inverted critical thresholds).

Database metrics (on the database agent, or on the instance agent when Create agent per database is disabled)

Always created:

  • availability: generic_proc, 1 when the database exists.
  • state: generic_data, the database state.

Created when the matching toggle is enabled:

  • Monitor active users: active users (generic_data, active user transactions for the database).
  • Retrieve transactions statistics: transactions (generic_data_inc, transactions per second), active transactions (generic_data).
  • Retrieve logs statistics: log_flush_waits (generic_data_inc), log_file_growths (generic_data, unit %), log_file_shrinks (generic_data), logfile_size (generic_data, MB), logfile_usage (generic_data, free space in the log files; unit %, critical at 15), log_cachehit_ratio (generic_data, unit %).
  • Monitor backups: backup_status_minutes (generic_data, minutes since the last backup), backup_status_last_backup (generic_data or generic_data_string, date of the last backup, or NEVER).
  • Monitor filegroups space: fg_free_space (generic_data, free space in the filegroups; unit %, critical at 15).
  • Monitor user reserved space: one table_space <table> module per table (generic_data, KB) and one table_space <table> free % (generic_data, unit %).
  • Execute custom queries: one module per custom query, with the datatype and thresholds defined in the query.
