docs.title: MySQL Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-09-08.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The MySQL Discovery plugin connects to MySQL instances and databases and turns their state and performance into Pandora FMS agents and modules. It reads a list of target instances, connects with a MySQL user, and collects engine metrics through SHOW GLOBAL STATUS, SHOW VARIABLES and the information_schema tables.

A Discovery task creates one agent per target instance. When Scan databases is enabled it also collects per-database metrics, and when Create agent per database is enabled it creates one agent per discovered database. Custom queries can be defined to add one module per query and database.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Plugin version 1.5 (pandorafms.mysql) Documented target The version this page describes, as identified by the package definition. See Plugin identity. A reachable MySQL instance Required The plugin establishes remote connections to each monitored instance. Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. A MySQL user with SELECT on the database tables and on the INFORMATION_SCHEMA tables Required Needed to read the engine and per-database metrics. Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. See Prepare MySQL access. A MySQL user with SHOW STATUS and SHOW VARIABLES Required Needed to read the server status and configuration variables. Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. A specific MySQL version Not validated No published test record establishes compatibility with a concrete MySQL release. A specific Pandora FMS version Not validated No published test record establishes console or server version compatibility. A specific host operating system Not validated No published test record establishes operating-system compatibility for the machine that runs the plugin.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. A Pandora FMS server with Discovery enabled to run the task, and a console to define it.
  2. Connectivity between the Pandora FMS server and each MySQL instance (default port 3306).
  3. A MySQL user with the required permissions. See Prepare MySQL access.
  4. A target agent group and a monitoring interval for the generated agents, taken from the Discovery task.

The plugin is distributed as a Pandora FMS Discovery application (.disco package) with its Python dependencies bundled, so no extra Python libraries have to be installed on the Discovery server.

docs.title: Prepare MySQL access
docs.text:
The user used by the task must reach each instance over the network and hold the permissions the monitor needs. From the official prerequisites:

  • SELECT on the database tables.
  • SELECT on the INFORMATION_SCHEMA tables.
  • SHOW STATUS to consult the status of the server.
  • SHOW VARIABLES to access the server configuration variables.

Grant the user only the access required by your monitoring policy; the plugin only reads and never changes MySQL configuration.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text: Load the .disco package from Management → Discovery → Extension manager (the Manage disco packages view). The package is available from the Pandora FMS library. Once loaded, MySQL appears under the Applications category of the Discovery wizard.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from Management → Discovery → Applications → MySQL. The generic first step defines the task; the package adds MySQL Base and MySQL Detailed. Every field is documented in Task parameters.

Step 1 — Task definition. Name, agent group, server and interval. The group ID and the interval are passed to the plugin and applied to every generated agent.

Step 2 — MySQL Base. What to connect to and how:

  • MySQL target strings is the list of instances to monitor, comma-separated or one per line. Each target is SERVER:PORT or SERVER; the default port is 3306. Lines starting with # are comments.
  • User and Password are the MySQL user used to connect.

Step 3 — MySQL Detailed. Execution, agent layout and which metrics to collect:

  • Max threads distributes the targets across parallel workers.
  • Target agent sets the agent names for the targets, matching the position of the target list; a blank entry uses the server IP address or FQDN.
  • Custom module prefix is prepended to every generated module name.
  • Scan databases collects the per-database metrics of each instance, and Create agent per database creates one agent per database, with Custom database agent prefix naming them.
  • Agent autodisable mode creates the generated agents in Pandora FMS mode 2, which disables an agent when all its modules become unknown.
  • Check engine uptime, Retrieve query statistics, Analyze connections, Retrieve InnoDB statistics and Retrieve cache statistics select the engine metric groups collected.
  • Execute custom queries and Custom queries define the custom queries.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from Management → Discovery → Task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary reports Total agents, Target agents, Databases agents, Targets up and Targets down. Targets up are the instances the plugin managed to connect to.

  2. The agents. One agent appears per reachable target instance, named by the Target agent list or by the server address. With Create agent per database, one agent appears per discovered database.

  3. The engine modules. A reachable instance carries its connection, uptime, query, connection, InnoDB and cache modules according to the enabled toggles.

  4. The database modules. With Scan databases enabled, each database carries its availability, fragmentation, size and custom query modules.

Targets that cannot be reached are counted in Targets down and do not produce agents.

docs.title: Agents and identity
docs.text:
The plugin creates one agent per target instance by default. The agent name is the value from the Target agent list that matches the target position, or the server address when none is given. Each generated agent reports MySQL as its operating system, its os_version is the value returned by SELECT @@VERSION (or Discovery when it cannot be read), its address is the instance host, and it belongs to the task's group (by ID) with the task interval. With Agent autodisable mode enabled the agents are created in Pandora FMS mode 2.

With Create agent per database, the plugin also creates one agent per database, named <Custom database agent prefix><target agent> <database name>, and counts them in Databases agents. Those agents declare the target agent as parent.

The databases to monitor are collected from SHOW DATABASES when Scan databases is enabled; the core databases mysql, information_schema, performance_schema and sys are skipped. The engine metrics always go to the target agent, and the per-database metrics go to the database agents when Create agent per database is enabled, or to the target agent otherwise.

docs.title: Modules by agent
docs.text:
Agent Created when Modules it carries Target agent A target instance is reachable MySQL connection, the engine metrics enabled by the toggles, and the per-database modules when Scan databases is enabled without Create agent per database Database agent Create agent per database enabled and a database is discovered <database> availability, <database> fragmentation ratio, <database> size and the custom query modules

Module names are <Custom module prefix> plus the module name; the database modules also include the database name. The exhaustive module inventory and the toggle that enables each group are in Generated modules and agents.

docs.text:
The plugin can run outside Discovery, from a Pandora FMS agent or directly from the command line, with a configuration file and the target, agent and custom-query files created manually:

./pandora_mysql --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --target_databases <PATH_TO_TARGETS> --target_agents <PATH_TO_AGENTS> --custom_queries <PATH_TO_QUERIES>

Only --conf and --target_databases are required; --target_agents and --custom_queries are optional. The plugin connects to each target in parallel according to Max threads and produces the agents and modules in its Discovery JSON output.

The configuration file and the target lists hold the MySQL password in plain text. Restrict them to the account that runs the plugin and keep them out of shared directories, logs and version control. Following the Discovery workflow for task runs means the console builds these files for you.

docs.text: Symptom Check No agent is created and the target is reported Targets down Confirm the instance is reachable from the Pandora FMS server on its port (default 3306), that the MySQL service is running, and that the User and Password are correct. The plugin accepts a configuration file, a target databases file, an optional target agents file and an optional custom queries file:

./pandora_mysql --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --target_databases <PATH_TO_TARGETS> --target_agents <PATH_TO_AGENTS> --custom_queries <PATH_TO_QUERIES>
Option Description --conf Required path to the configuration file --target_databases Required path to the file with the target instances --target_agents Optional path to the file with the target agent names --custom_queries Optional path to the file with the custom queries

Example configuration file:

[CONF]
agents_group_id=10
interval=300
user=<MYSQL_USER>
password=<MYSQL_PASSWORD>
threads=1
modules_prefix=
execute_custom_queries=1
engine_uptime=1
query_stats=1
analyze_connections=1
innodb_stats=1
cache_stats=1
scan_databases=1
agent_per_database=0

docs.title: Custom queries
docs.text:
Each custom query creates one module per task agent and is defined between check_begin and check_end:

Field Description name Module name description Module description operation value returns a single value, full returns all rows as a string datatype generic_data, generic_data_string or generic_proc min_warning, max_warning Numeric warning thresholds str_warning String warning condition warning_inverse 1 inverts the warning threshold interval min_critical, max_critical Numeric critical thresholds str_critical String critical condition critical_inverse 1 inverts the critical threshold interval module_interval Module interval, as a multiplier of the agent interval crontab 5-field cron expression; the query runs only when the date/time matches. Empty runs every interval target The query, a SELECT only target_databases Databases where the module is created; all or empty applies to all

The target and name fields accept the reserved word $__self_dbname, which is replaced with the database name currently being analyzed. The crontab field follows the standard 5-field format and supports *, exact values, ranges, steps and lists; on the first run after enabling a scheduled query only an occurrence inside the current interval is picked up.

check_begin
name ConnectionCount
description Number of connections
operation value
datatype generic_data
min_warning 10
target SELECT COUNT(*) AS ConnectionCount FROM $__self_dbname.processlist
target_databases all
check_end

docs.title: Generated modules and agents
docs.text:
Module names are [<Custom module prefix>]<module name>, and the database modules also include the database name.

Target agent (one per reachable instance)

Always created:

  • MySQL connection: generic_proc, 1 when the instance is reachable, 0 otherwise.

Created when the matching toggle is enabled:

  • Check engine uptime: restart detection (generic_proc, 0 when a restart is detected, 1 otherwise). The description carries the running time.
  • Retrieve query statistics: queries (generic_data_inc_abs, total), query rate (generic_data_inc), query select, query update, query delete, query insert (generic_data_inc_abs).
  • Analyze connections: current connections (generic_data, warning at 90% and critical at 98% of max_connections), connections ratio (generic_data, unit %, warning at 85 and critical at 90), aborted connections (generic_data_inc_abs).
  • Retrieve InnoDB statistics: Innodb buffer pool pages total (generic_data), Innodb buffer pool read requests, Innodb buffer pool write requests (generic_data_inc_abs), Innodb disk reads, Innodb disk writes (generic_data_inc_abs), Innodb disk data read, Innodb disk data written (generic_data_inc_abs, unit MB).
  • Retrieve cache statistics: query cache enabled (generic_proc, 1 when the query cache is enabled), query hit ratio (generic_data, unit %, created only when the query cache is enabled).

Database modules (on the target agent or on the database agent, created when Scan databases is enabled, for each database other than the core ones)

  • <database> availability: generic_proc, 1.
  • <database> fragmentation ratio: generic_data, unit %.
  • <database> size: generic_data, unit MB.
  • The custom query modules that target the database.

docs.title: NGINX Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-09-01.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The NGINX Discovery plugin automates the monitoring of NGINX servers through the ngx_http_stub_status_module (stub_status) endpoint. It reads that endpoint and turns its counters into Pandora FMS monitoring modules: active connections, accepted and handled connections, processed requests, and connections in the reading, writing and waiting states.

The plugin creates one agent per NGINX URL, with one module per available metric, plus a reachability module. A Discovery task can point at several URLs at once, so a single task covers a whole set of NGINX nodes.

A companion console extension, NGINX Monitoring, aggregates every node the plugin monitors into a single view. See NGINX Monitoring console extension.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Plugin version 1.0 (pandorafms.nginx) Documented target The version this page describes. See Plugin identity NGINX exposing stub_status over plain HTTP Tested Exercised against nginx:alpine NGINX exposing stub_status over HTTPS with basic authentication Tested Exercised against nginx:alpine with a self-signed certificate ngx_http_stub_status_module compiled into the NGINX build Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. See Prerequisites Network reachability from the Discovery server to the status endpoint Required The plugin performs an HTTP request per URL Host operating system running the plugin Not validated No host operating system has been recorded Any specific NGINX release or distribution package Not validated Compatibility was established against the endpoint contract, not a version matrix

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. The stub_status endpoint must be enabled and reachable from the machine that runs the plugin. Enabling it is covered in Enable the status endpoint.
  2. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to execute the task, and the console to define it.
  3. Credentials, only when the endpoint is protected with HTTP basic authentication.

The plugin is distributed as a self-contained executable: the packaged Discovery app ships bin/pandora_nginx, so no additional runtime has to be installed, on the Discovery server or for a manual run.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
Load the .disco package from the Pandora FMS marketplace:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/

Once loaded, the NGINX application is available when creating Discovery tasks.

The companion console extension is not part of that package. It ships with the console, under pandora_console_extensions/nginx_view/.

docs.title: Enable the status endpoint
docs.text:
For the plugin to obtain the statistics, NGINX must expose the stub_status endpoint. Enabling it is done by editing the NGINX configuration file (by default at /etc/nginx/nginx.conf or /etc/nginx/sites-available/default).

The ngx_http_stub_status_module module is not included in every NGINX build. To verify whether it is available, run nginx -V 2>&1 | grep stub_status. Most Linux distributions include it by default.

Pick the variant that matches how the endpoint should be protected.

docs.title: Minimal configuration (no authentication, no SSL)
docs.text:
Add a dedicated location for the status inside your server:

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name _;

    location /nginx_status {
        stub_status on;
        access_log off;
        allow <PANDORA_FMS_SERVER_IP>;   # Pandora FMS server IP
        deny all;
    }
}

With this configuration the plugin will consume the URL:

http://<SERVER_IP>/nginx_status

docs.title: Configuration with basic authentication
docs.text:
To protect the endpoint with username and password, define auth_basic and auth_basic_user_file in the status location:

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name _;

    location /nginx_status {
        stub_status on;
        access_log off;
        auth_basic "NGINX Status";
        auth_basic_user_file /etc/nginx/.htpasswd;
    }
}

Generate the .htpasswd file with htpasswd or openssl:

htpasswd -c /etc/nginx/.htpasswd <USERNAME>
# or
echo "<USERNAME>:$(openssl passwd -apr1 <PASSWORD>)" > /etc/nginx/.htpasswd

The second form places the password in the command line, where the shell history and the operating system process list expose it. Prefer htpasswd -c, which prompts for it.

The same username and password must be provided to the plugin through the task fields, or through --user / --password for a manual run.

docs.title: Configuration with SSL/TLS
docs.text:
To serve the statistics over HTTPS configure the certificate in the server:

server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name _;

    ssl_certificate     /etc/nginx/certs/status.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/nginx/certs/status.key;

    location /nginx_status {
        stub_status on;
        access_log off;
        allow <PANDORA_FMS_SERVER_IP>;
        deny all;
    }
}

Generate a self-signed test certificate with:

openssl req -x509 -nodes -days 365 -newkey rsa:2048 \
  -keyout /etc/nginx/certs/status.key \
  -out /etc/nginx/certs/status.crt \
  -subj "/CN=localhost"
cat /etc/nginx/certs/status.crt /etc/nginx/certs/status.key > /etc/nginx/certs/status.pem

The URL is then given to the plugin with the https:// scheme, and Verify SSL decides whether the certificate chain is validated:

  • enabled → for valid certificates in production.
  • disabled → for self-signed certificates or test environments.

docs.title: Full configuration (SSL + authentication)
docs.text:
server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name _;

    ssl_certificate     /etc/nginx/certs/status.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/nginx/certs/status.key;

    location /nginx_status {
        stub_status on;
        access_log off;
        auth_basic "NGINX Status";
        auth_basic_user_file /etc/nginx/.htpasswd;
    }
}

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name _;
    return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
}

After modifying the NGINX configuration, reload the service to apply the changes:

sudo systemctl reload nginx

docs.title: Confirm the endpoint responds
docs.text:
Before creating the task, request the status page by hand:

curl -u <USERNAME>:<PASSWORD> http://<SERVER_IP>/nginx_status

The output must be plain text with the following format:

Active connections: 291
server accepts handled requests
 16630948 16630948 31070465
Reading: 6 Writing: 179 Waiting: 106
  • Active connections: total number of active connections (includes waiting ones).
  • accepts: total connections accepted since NGINX started.
  • handled: total connections handled since NGINX started.
  • requests: total client requests processed since NGINX started.
  • Reading: connections reading request headers from the client.
  • Writing: connections writing a response to the client or processing a request.
  • Waiting: idle keep-alive connections waiting for the next request.

If this request fails, the task will fail too. Fix it here rather than in the console.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from Management → Discovery → Application → NGINX. The console presents the fields in two steps, and every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. NGINX Basic — the endpoints and how to reach them:

    • NGINX Status URLs: stub_status endpoint URLs, separated by commas or one per line. Each URL generates one agent.
    • Username and Password: only when the endpoint requires HTTP basic authentication.
    • Verify SSL: validate the certificate chain of an https:// URL. Disabled by default.
    • Transfer mode, Tentacle IP and Tentacle port: how the data reaches Pandora FMS. native lets the Discovery server read the data directly and is the default.

  2. NGINX Advanced — optional shaping of the result:

    • Module prefix: prepended to every created module name.
    • Request timeout: seconds to wait for each HTTP request. Defaults to 10.
    • Allow list and Deny list: regular expressions to include or exclude modules by name.

The task's own group and interval come from the generic task-definition step, and are passed to the plugin as the agent group and the module interval.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from Management → Discovery → Task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A successfully completed task reports:

    • Total agents: the number of agents generated by the task.
    • Total modules: the number of modules generated by the task.

    Expect one agent per URL you entered. A URL that could not be read is reported as an error in the execution information instead.

  2. The agents. One per URL, with the alias set to the endpoint's host:port.

  3. The modules on each agent. A reachable endpoint produces:

    Module Expected value Status 1 — the endpoint answered Active_connections Current active connections Accepts, Handled, Requests Accumulated counters; Pandora FMS derives the per-second rate Reading, Writing, Waiting Current connections in each state

    Module names carry the Module prefix when one was set, and the allow/deny lists can legitimately remove any of them.

  4. The console extension, when it is installed: the node should appear in Operation → NGINX Monitoring with no extra configuration.

If the task reports no agents, work back through Confirm the endpoint responds and then Troubleshoot.

docs.title: Agents and modules generated
docs.text:
The plugin creates one agent per NGINX URL. The agent name is the MD5 hash of the endpoint's netloc (host:port), and the alias is that netloc itself, for example nginx1.example.com. When a URL has no parsable netloc, the whole URL is used instead.

Because the identity comes from the endpoint and not from the task, moving a URL between tasks keeps reporting to the same agent and preserves its history.

The Status module is created for every agent by default, with value 1 when the endpoint is reachable. It can be excluded through the allow/deny lists like any other module. When the endpoint cannot be reached, the plugin reports the failure in the execution information. The remaining fields become generic_data modules (instantaneous values) or generic_data_inc modules (incremental counters, from which Pandora FMS derives a per-second rate), named <prefix><MetricName>.

docs.title: Module type mapping
docs.text: Metric Pandora FMS module type Description Status generic_proc Endpoint state (1=reachable, 0=DOWN). Allows configuring critical alerts when the value is 0. Active_connections generic_data Current active connections (gauge). Includes reading, writing, and waiting connections. Accepts generic_data_inc Accumulated accepted connections. Pandora FMS automatically calculates the per-second rate. Handled generic_data_inc Accumulated handled connections. Pandora FMS automatically calculates the per-second rate. If the rate is lower than Accepts, NGINX is dropping connections. Requests generic_data_inc Accumulated processed requests. Pandora FMS automatically calculates the per-second rate (requests/s). Reading generic_data Connections in the header-reading state (gauge). Writing generic_data Connections in the response-writing state (gauge). Waiting generic_data Idle keep-alive connections (gauge). A high value is normal when keep-alive is enabled.

docs.title: extra_data markers
docs.text:
The plugin assigns stable identifiers in the extra_data field of each agent and module, following the nginx:<kind>:<identifier> format, to allow later identification from the console, dashboards, extensions, or SQL queries:

  • Agent: nginx:target:<sanitized_url> — identifies the monitored NGINX target.
  • Status module: nginx:metric_status:<sanitized_url>
  • Metric modules: nginx:metric_<metric_name>:<sanitized_url> — for example nginx:metric_active_connections:..., nginx:metric_accepts:..., etc.

These markers do not contain the agent or module name, but the external identifier (the target URL), which is stable and meaningful at the domain level.

docs.title: NGINX Monitoring console extension
docs.text:
The plugin has a companion console extension, nginx_view, which renders a dashboard of every NGINX node the plugin monitors. It is not installed by the .disco package: the extension is part of the console, under pandora_console_extensions/nginx_view/.

Once available, it appears in the console under Operation, as NGINX Monitoring. Opening it requires the AR ACL.

The extension does not need to be told which agents to read. It discovers them from the extra_data markers the plugin writes, selecting every module whose extra_data starts with nginx:metric_ and resolving the agents that own them. Any agent created by the plugin therefore shows up automatically, with no configuration on the extension side.

It displays summary cards for the number of NGINX nodes, how many are up and down, total active connections, the aggregated request counter, and idle connections, followed by a per-node table.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The plugin has no verbose or debug flag. Its only diagnostic channel is the JSON execution summary printed to standard output, which names the failing endpoint when a request to stub_status cannot be completed.

  • The task creates no agents — every URL failed. Reproduce the request with curl as in Confirm the endpoint responds; the JSON summary of a manual run names the endpoint that failed.
  • stub_status is not available — the module is not in this NGINX build. Check with nginx -V 2>&1 | grep stub_status and use a build that includes it.
  • The endpoint answers by hand but not from the task — the request leaves from the Discovery server, not from your workstation. Check the allow/deny rules in the status location and the network path from that server.
  • HTTPS endpoint fails with a certificate error — a self-signed or internally-issued certificate does not validate. Disable Verify SSL for that task, or install the issuing CA on the Discovery server.
  • 401 on a protected endpoint — the credentials do not match auth_basic_user_file. Regenerate the entry with htpasswd and retest with curl -u.
  • Module prefix, transfer mode, tentacle address or interval seem ignored in a manual run — in simple mode (--urls) those parameters are not applied; the plugin uses native, 127.0.0.1:41121 and 300 seconds. Use the configuration file to change them.
  • Handled is consistently lower than Accepts — this is not a plugin fault: NGINX is dropping connections. Investigate the server's resource limits.

docs.title: Task parameters
docs.text: The console presents the task fields in two steps.

docs.title: NGINX Basic
docs.text: Field Macro Type Default Notes NGINX Status URLs _nginxUrls_ textarea — Mandatory. Comma separated or one per line. Each URL creates one agent Username _nginxUser_ string — HTTP basic authentication user, optional Password _nginxPassword_ password — HTTP basic authentication password, optional Verify SSL _verifySSL_ checkbox off Validate the certificate chain when using HTTPS. Disable for self-signed certificates Transfer mode _transferMode_ select native native: the Discovery server reads the agent data directly. tentacle: the plugin sends the data with the Tentacle client Tentacle IP _tentacleIp_ string 127.0.0.1 Tentacle server address, used in tentacle mode Tentacle port _tentaclePort_ number 41121 Tentacle server port, used in tentacle mode

docs.title: NGINX Advanced
docs.text:
Field Macro Type Default Notes Module prefix _prefixModules_ string — Prepended to every created module name, for example nginx_ Request timeout _reqTimeout_ number 10 HTTP request timeout in seconds Allow list _allowList_ string — Regular expression; only modules whose name matches are included. Empty means all Deny list _denyList_ string — Regular expression; modules whose name matches are excluded. Empty means none

The task's group and interval are taken from the generic task-definition step and reach the plugin as agents_group, agents_group_id and interval.

docs.title: Command-line execution
docs.text:
The plugin can also be executed by hand, which is the fastest way to confirm an endpoint and its credentials before wiring them into a task, and is also how it is used as a server plugin.

It has two input modes:

  • Simple mode passes the endpoints on the command line with --urls.
  • Advanced mode passes a configuration file with --conf plus a targets file with --targets_file. This is the mode the Discovery task itself uses.
# Simple mode
./pandora_nginx --urls http://<TARGET_HOST_1>/nginx_status,http://<TARGET_HOST_2>/nginx_status \
    --user <USERNAME> --password <PASSWORD> --ssl false

# Advanced mode
./pandora_nginx --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --targets_file <PATH_TO_TARGETS>

Passing a password on the command line exposes it in the shell history and in the operating system process list. Prefer the configuration file for anything but a one-off check.

The run returns a JSON summary of the execution. In native mode the collected data is exposed in the summary's monitoring_data field, for the Discovery server to consume; in tentacle mode the plugin generates one XML file per agent and sends it to the Pandora FMS server.

--as_server_plugin replaces the JSON summary with a single 1 (agents created without errors) or 0, so the plugin can be wired as a server plugin.

./pandora_nginx --urls <URLs> [options]
./pandora_nginx --conf <path> --targets_file <path>
Parameter Description --urls NGINX stub_status endpoint URLs, separated by commas. Each URL will generate an agent --user Username if the NGINX endpoint requires HTTP basic authentication, optional --password Password if the NGINX endpoint requires HTTP basic authentication, optional --ssl Whether to verify the URL HTTPS certificate or not, optional (default true) --prefix Prefix for module names, optional --transfer_mode Data transfer mode (native or tentacle), optional -ti, --tentacle_ip Tentacle IP, optional (default 127.0.0.1) -tp, --tentacle_port Tentacle port, optional (default 41121) --interval Monitoring interval in seconds, optional (default 300) --allow_list Regular expression to include only modules whose name matches, optional --deny_list Regular expression to exclude modules whose name matches, optional --timeout Maximum wait time for the HTTP request in seconds, optional (default 10) --as_server_plugin Return a single 1 (agents were created without errors) or 0 instead of the JSON summary, optional (default false) --conf Path to the configuration file --targets_file Path to the file containing the NGINX URLs (mandatory when using --conf)

In simple mode (--urls), the module prefix, transfer mode, tentacle address and interval parameters listed above are not applied: the plugin uses the defaults (native, 127.0.0.1:41121, 300 seconds). To change them, use the configuration file with --conf.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The Discovery task builds this file from its own fields; a manual advanced-mode run supplies it with --conf.

Key Description username HTTP basic authentication user, optional password HTTP basic authentication password, optional verify_ssl Whether to verify the HTTPS certificate, optional prefix Prefix for module names, optional transfer_mode Data transfer mode (native or tentacle), optional tentacle_ip Tentacle IP, optional tentacle_port Tentacle port, optional agents_group Name of the agent group the created agents are assigned to, optional agents_group_id Id of the agent group the created agents are assigned to, optional interval Monitoring interval in seconds, optional allow_list Regular expression to include only modules whose name matches, optional deny_list Regular expression to exclude modules whose name matches, optional timeout Maximum wait time for the HTTP request in seconds, optional

Example:

[CONF]
username=<USERNAME>
password=<PASSWORD>
verify_ssl=false
prefix=nginx_
transfer_mode=native
tentacle_ip=127.0.0.1
tentacle_port=41121
interval=300
allow_list=
deny_list=
timeout=10

Targets file (--targets_file), one URL per line or comma separated:

http://<TARGET_HOST_1>/nginx_status
http://<TARGET_HOST_2>/nginx_status

docs.title: Office 365 Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Office 365 Discovery addon monitors the health and the licensing of a Microsoft 365 tenant. It queries the Microsoft Graph API and turns the result into Pandora FMS agents and modules: the status of every Microsoft 365 service, the unresolved incidents of each service, the service announcements as log entries, and the usage of every subscribed license.

A Discovery task generates up to two agents:

  • A service health agent with, for each Microsoft 365 service, a status module and a module listing its unresolved incidents. The service announcements (maintenance and incident messages) are sent to the Pandora FMS log collector associated with this agent.
  • A licensing agent (optional) with, for each license subscribed by the tenant, modules for its status and for the units enabled, consumed and available.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.office365, version 1.1 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the Discovery server to login.microsoftonline.com and graph.microsoft.com Required The addon authenticates and queries data through these hosts Microsoft Entra ID application with the permissions listed in Microsoft Graph permissions Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated The Marketplace shows a general notice for all its integrations; no version matrix has been recorded for this addon Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to the Microsoft endpoints above.
  2. A Microsoft Entra ID application registered in the tenant to monitor, with a client secret and the application permissions described below.
  3. The tenant ID, the client ID and the client secret of that application.
  4. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it.

The addon ships its own executable, bin/pandora_o365, so nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server to run a task.

docs.title: Register the application in Microsoft Entra ID
docs.text:
The addon authenticates with the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow, with no signed-in user. Prepare the application in the Azure portal:

  1. Open Microsoft Entra ID and register a new application in App registrations. Register it in the tenant you want to monitor.
  2. In Certificates & secrets, create a client secret and copy its value immediately: Azure shows it only once.
  3. From the application overview, copy the Application (client) ID and the Directory (tenant) ID.
  4. In API permissions, add the Microsoft Graph application permissions listed below and grant administrator consent.

docs.title: Microsoft Graph permissions
docs.text:
The addon requests an application token with the https://graph.microsoft.com/.default scope, so it receives the application permissions granted to the registered application. Each data set it reads is covered by the following Microsoft Graph application permissions, according to the Microsoft Graph documentation of each endpoint:

Microsoft Graph request Used for Application permission /admin/serviceAnnouncement/healthOverviews Service status and unresolved incidents ServiceHealth.Read.All /admin/serviceAnnouncement/messages Service announcements sent as logs ServiceMessage.Read.All /subscribedSkus Licensing agent LicenseAssignment.Read.All (the least privileged option listed by Microsoft; Organization.Read.All and Directory.Read.All also work)

Grant only the permissions of the features you enable: omit ServiceMessage.Read.All when Logs is disabled and LicenseAssignment.Read.All when licensing monitoring is disabled. Do not grant the ReadWrite variants.

The client secret is a credential: store it only in the task and revoke it in Microsoft Entra ID when it is no longer needed.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.office365

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, Office 365 is available when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create a Discovery task and choose Office 365. The console presents the fields in two steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. Office365 base — access to the tenant and data destination:

    • Client ID, Tenant ID and Secret: the values of the Microsoft Entra ID application. The console treats the three of them as password fields.
    • Tentacle IP and Tentacle port: where the generated agent data is sent. The defaults are 127.0.0.1 and 41121; they rarely need changing.

  2. Office365 Detailed — agents and data to collect:

    • Agent Name: name of the service health agent.
    • Use prefix and Prefix: prefix added to the agent name and to its modules. Prefix is shown only when Use prefix is enabled.
    • Logs: send the service announcements to the Pandora FMS log collector.
    • utf8: encode the value of the incident modules as UTF-8 text.
    • Not data: do not create the status and incident modules.
    • Activate licensing monitoring, Licensing agent name and Prefix for licensing data: create the licensing agent. The last two are shown only when licensing monitoring is enabled.
    • Max threads: shown for compatibility; this version of the addon does not use it.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to the agents the task creates.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes reports Total agents and Total modules. Total agents is 2 with licensing monitoring enabled and 1 otherwise. Total modules adds the status, incident, log and licensing modules generated.

  2. The agents. The service health agent, named after Agent Name (default Pandora_O365), and, when licensing monitoring is enabled, the licensing agent (default Pandora_O365_licensing).

  3. The modules. The service health agent has a <service>_status and a <service>_active_issues module for every Microsoft 365 service; the licensing agent has the license modules described in Understand the results. Log entries appear in the log collector under the service name.

When a step fails, the task records the error in its execution information instead; see Troubleshoot.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Name and alias Group Created when Service health agent <Prefix><Agent Name> Task group Always Licensing agent <Prefix for licensing data><Licensing agent name> Task group Activate licensing monitoring is enabled

Both agents are refreshed at the task interval and report the description Agent generated by pandora_o365 plugin. The two prefixes are independent: Prefix does not apply to the licensing agent.

docs.title: Modules per agent
docs.text:
Service health agent

Module Type Condition Description <Prefix><service id>_status generic_data_string Not data disabled Status of the Microsoft 365 service as reported by Microsoft Graph. The module is warning when the status matches investigating, restoringService or extendedRecovery, and critical when it matches serviceDegradation or serviceInterruption <Prefix><service id>_active_issues generic_data_string Not data disabled Identifier and title of each unresolved incident of the service, concatenated without a separator, so consecutive incidents run together; None when the service has no unresolved incident. Description: <service> Issues Ids Log entries Log collector Logs enabled One entry per service announcement read from offset 100, with the source <Prefix>_<service>. The content is the announcement, converted to plain text. The collection is not paged, so the first 100 announcements are never collected and a tenant with fewer than 100 announcements produces no entries

<service id> is the service identifier returned by Microsoft Graph, for example the identifier of Exchange Online or Microsoft Teams.

Licensing agent

For every license (SKU) subscribed by the tenant, the agent has the following modules. <name> is the license part number returned by Microsoft Graph and each module description is the identifier of the license.

Module Type Description <Prefix><name> generic_data_string Capability status of the license <Prefix><name> consumedUnits generic_data Units consumed <Prefix><name> Units enabled generic_data Units enabled <Prefix><name> Units lockedOut generic_data Units locked out <Prefix><name> Units suspended generic_data Units suspended <Prefix><name> Units warning generic_data Units in warning state <Prefix><name> Consumed Units % generic_data Percentage of enabled units consumed, rounded to two decimals, in %. It is 0 when no unit is enabled <Prefix><name> Units Available generic_data Enabled units minus consumed units

Here <Prefix> is Prefix for licensing data.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. The executable takes a single parameter, the path to a configuration file described in Configuration file:

./pandora_o365 --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

It sends one data file per agent using the configured transfer mode and prints a JSON summary with the Total agents and Total modules counts. When errors occur, the JSON also contains an info key with the messages.

The configuration file contains the client secret. Protect it with restrictive permissions and do not keep it after the test.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the information recorded in the execution result of the task.

  • HTTP error: ... on https://login.microsoftonline.com/...: Microsoft Entra ID rejected the authentication. Check the tenant ID, the client ID and the client secret, and that the secret has not expired.
  • Request error: ...: the Discovery server cannot reach login.microsoftonline.com. Check outbound connectivity, DNS and any proxy or firewall.
  • Error requesting url: ... (<status>) on https://graph.microsoft.com/...: Microsoft Graph rejected a data request. A 403 status can indicate that the application lacks the permission of that endpoint or that administrator consent was not granted; see Microsoft Graph permissions. The message names the endpoint.
  • error with status data: ..., error logs data: ... or error with licensing data: ...: reading or processing that data set failed. The error text is appended to the message.
  • error with accounts data: ...: the configuration file cannot be read. It appears only in manual execution.
  • No _status or _active_issues modules: Not data is enabled.
  • No licensing agent: Activate licensing monitoring is disabled.
  • No log entries: Logs is disabled, Microsoft Graph returned no announcements after the first 100, or the tenant has fewer than 100 announcements.
  • Incident values show a byte string: utf8 is disabled. Enable it unless the environment requires raw bytes.

docs.title: OpenSearch Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The OpenSearch Discovery addon monitors an OpenSearch cluster through its REST API. It reads the cluster health, the statistics of every node and the aggregated index statistics of the cluster, and turns them into Pandora FMS agents and modules.

A Discovery task generates agents by functional role instead of a single agent per cluster:

  • One cluster agent with the health of the cluster: status, nodes and shard allocation.
  • One agent per node with the operating system, process, JVM, thread pool, transport, circuit breaker, cache and disk statistics of that node.
  • One primary metrics agent with the aggregated index statistics (documents, indexing, search, merges, segments, translog and more) of the primary shards and of all shards.

Each group of agents is optional: you choose which of the three metric groups the task collects, and you can exclude individual modules from each group.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.opensearch, version 1.2 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the Discovery server to the OpenSearch REST endpoint Required The addon connects to the IP address and port configured in the task Access to the Nodes stats, Cluster health and Indices stats APIs Required The addon calls these three APIs; each one is needed only for its metric group OpenSearch versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to the OpenSearch HTTP(S) port, usually 9200.
  2. Access to the cluster APIs. When the cluster requires authentication, a user and password that can read the cluster health, the node statistics and the index statistics. Credentials are optional: the addon authenticates only when both the user and the password are set.
  3. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task, the console to define it and a Tentacle server that receives the generated agent data.

The addon is distributed ready to run, so nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server to run a task.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.opensearch

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, OpenSearch is available in the applications section when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from the Discovery applications and choose OpenSearch. The console presents the fields in two steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. OpenSearch Basic — connection and data transfer:

    • OpenSearch IP and OpenSearch Port: address and port of the OpenSearch REST endpoint. Both are mandatory.
    • User and Password: credentials, both optional.
    • Verify SSL: connect over HTTPS. See Connection security.
    • Verify Certs: validate the server certificate.
    • transfer mode, tentacle ip and tentacle port: how and where the generated agent data is sent. They rarely need changing.

  2. OpenSearch Detailed — naming and metric groups:

    • agent prefix, Agent group, Custom module prefix and Module group: naming and grouping of the generated agents and modules.
    • Primary metrics, Nodes Metrics and Cluster Metrics: the metric groups to collect. Enabled by default.
    • Exclude primary metrics, Exclude nodes metrics and Exclude cluster metrics: modules to leave out of each group. Each one is shown only when its metric group is enabled.

The execution interval comes from the generic task-definition step and is applied as the interval of the generated agents.

docs.title: Connection security
docs.text:
• Verify SSL controls the protocol: enabled, the addon connects over HTTPS; disabled, it connects over plain HTTP. It is enabled by default.
  • Verify Certs controls the certificate: enabled, the addon validates the server certificate; disabled (default), it accepts any certificate. Certificate hostname verification is always disabled, even when Verify Certs is enabled.
  • With Verify SSL enabled and Verify Certs disabled the traffic is encrypted but the server is not authenticated. Use a network you trust or enable Verify Certs.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes reports:

    • Total Agents: agents generated.
    • Total Modules: modules generated across all agents.

    Errors found while collecting a metric group are recorded in the task's execution information.

  2. The agents. One cluster agent, one primary metrics agent and one agent per node, according to the metric groups you enabled.

  3. The modules. The cluster agent has cluster_status, number_of_nodes and unassigned_shards, among others; see Modules per agent.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Alias Created when Cardinality Primary metrics <agent prefix>_primary_metrics Primary metrics enabled and the statistics could be read One per task Node <agent prefix>_node_metrics_<node name> Nodes Metrics enabled and the statistics could be read One per node of the cluster Cluster <agent prefix>_cluster_metrics Cluster Metrics enabled and the statistics could be read One per task

Agent identity is derived from the alias, which includes the agent prefix. Changing the prefix of a task creates new agents instead of updating the existing ones, and the history of the previous agents is not carried over. Use a different prefix for each cluster, so two tasks never write to the same agents.

The agents are placed in the Agent group when one is set, and have no address, operating system or parent.

docs.title: Modules per agent
docs.text:
Module names are the metric name, preceded by <Custom module prefix>_ when a prefix is set.

Agent Modules Cluster Cluster name and status (green, yellow or red), number of nodes and data nodes, active, relocating, initializing, unassigned and delayed unassigned shards, active primary shards, pending tasks, unfinished fetches and the percentage of active shards Node Operating system CPU, load average and memory and swap usage; process CPU, file descriptors and virtual memory; JVM heap, non-heap, memory pools, threads and garbage collection; thread pool statistics; transport and HTTP connections and traffic; circuit breakers; indexing pressure; request cache; disk space; and the index statistics of the node Primary metrics Index statistics, prefixed primaries_ for primary shards and total_ for all shards: documents, store size, indexing, get, search, merges, refresh, flush, warmer, query cache, fielddata, completion, segments, translog, request cache and recovery

The full list is in Module reference.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. The package contains the pandora_opensearch executable, which takes the path to a configuration file described in Configuration file:

./pandora_opensearch --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

It sends one data file per agent with the configured transfer mode and prints a summary with the total agents and modules created. Errors are listed in the same output.

With --as_server_plugin 1 the addon is run as a server plugin: it prints no summary, and prints 1 when it created at least one agent without errors and 0 otherwise, including when the configuration file does not exist.

./pandora_opensearch --as_server_plugin 1 --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

The configuration file contains the OpenSearch password in plain text. Protect it with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the task's execution information, or the output of the manual execution.

  • Error: Could not connect to OpenSearch cluster with <host>:<port>: also reported as node or primary instead of cluster, depending on the metric group that failed. The endpoint is unreachable, the protocol does not match (see Verify SSL) or the credentials are rejected. Check the address, the port and the protocol from the Discovery server.
  • Error: when attempting to obtain cluster statistics and Error: when attempting to obtain node data: the request reached the cluster but failed. The message includes the error returned by OpenSearch, for example a missing permission.
  • Unable to obtain OpenSearch metrics.: no metric group produced data. Either the three metric groups are disabled or all of them failed; check the other messages.
  • Error create agent <name>: <error>: the agent could not be created or sent.
  • A group of agents is missing: the metric group is disabled, or its request failed and the cause is in the execution information. The other groups are still generated.
  • A node agent fails after adding an exclusion: an exclusion that matches the text node_name removes the node name the addon needs to create the agent. Use more specific exclusion text.
  • More modules disappeared than expected: exclusions are case-insensitive regular expressions applied to the metric name without the module prefix, so a short text can match several modules. See Excluding modules.
  • Error reading the configuration file (Error file: <path> does not exist, Error while reading configuration file): in manual execution, the path passed to --conf is wrong or the file is not readable or well-formed.

docs.title: Excluding modules
docs.text: Each exclusion box accepts a list of entries separated by commas. An entry removes every module of that group whose metric name matches it. Matching is case-insensitive and finds the entry anywhere in the name; entries are interpreted as regular expressions, so an invalid expression makes the metric group fail. For example, unassigned, active in Exclude cluster metrics removes every cluster module whose name contains unassigned or active, including unassigned_shards, active_shards and active_primary_shards.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
Used by manual execution. One key = value per line. Boolean options accept 1, true, t, yes or y to enable; any other value disables them.

Authentication is used only when user and password are both set password No empty Password verify_ssl No disabled Connect over HTTPS verify_certs No disabled Validate the server certificate transfer_mode Yes — tentacle sends the data with Tentacle tentacle_ip Yes — Tentacle server address tentacle_port Yes — Tentacle server port agent_prefix No empty Prefix of the agent aliases agents_group No empty Group of the agents module_prefix No empty Prefix of the module names module_group No empty Group of the modules token_primary_metrics No disabled Collect the primary metrics group exclude_primary_metrics No empty Modules to exclude from the primary metrics group token_nodes_metrics No disabled Collect the nodes group exclude_nodes_metrics No empty Modules to exclude from the nodes group token_cluster_metrics No disabled Collect the cluster group exclude_cluster_metrics No empty Modules to exclude from the cluster group interval No 0 Interval of the agents, in seconds. open_search_port        = 9200

docs.title: OpenShift Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-23.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
OpenShift Discovery reads the cluster API and produces a global agent plus agents for nodes, pods and deployments. The Discovery task generates agent XML and sends it through Tentacle. The global agent summarizes services, namespaces, component statuses, replication controllers and API services; resource agents report capacity, conditions and container CPU/memory.

This page covers the Discovery application, not the older OpenShift CLI/server plugin. Do not reuse that plugin's cli, user, password, project, agent_* or as_server_plugin settings here.

docs.title: Compatibility and requirements
docs.text:
Scope State Requirement or limitation pandorafms.openshift, package 1.0 Documented target Discovery application (.disco) Pandora FMS Discovery server and console Required Define and execute the application task OpenShift API reachable from Discovery Required Direct connections use https://<TARGET_HOST>:<API_PORT> Bearer token Required for protected direct endpoints Read access to the exact resources and health paths in API requests; no validated least-privilege role is supplied Metrics API (metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1) Required for node/pod discovery Discovery starts from metrics, not just from resource lists Tentacle destination Required for delivery Reachable from the Discovery server Specific OpenShift, Pandora FMS or host OS releases Not validated No release-specific compatibility or live test result is established here

Obtain the .disco package from the OpenShift Marketplace entry and load it as a Discovery application. Select the application named Openshift in its package definition. No oc executable, CLI login or project parameter is used by this task.

Ask the cluster administrator to provide API access and confirm node/pod metrics are available. The administrator must authorize the queried surface; the older CLI guide's role and local cluster setup are not a validated access policy for this application.

docs.title: Connection safety
docs.text:
Direct API requests use HTTPS without certificate verification, so they do not authenticate the server identity. Restrict network access. The task stores the token in its generated configuration file; protect task configuration and file access. Manual runs should use a protected configuration file, not a token in command arguments.

With Use proxy enabled, requests use Proxy url and omit the Bearer header. The proxy URL must include its scheme. No request timeout is configured by this package; network delays can hold up collection.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Define the task name, execution server, agent group and interval in Discovery. All generated agents inherit the task group and interval. The package defines two configuration steps, Openshift base and Openshift detailed. The exhaustive field reference is below.

  1. In Openshift base, provide Openshift host without a scheme, Openshift port, and Openshift token for direct API access. For proxy access, enable Use proxy and supply Proxy url instead.
  2. Set Tentacle IP and Tentacle port to the destination that receives the generated XML; defaults are 127.0.0.1 and 41121.
  3. In Openshift detailed, choose Scan Deployments, Scan Nodes and Scan Pods. All default to enabled.
  4. Run the task and inspect its execution information and generated agents.

There are no wizard controls for namespace filtering, prefixes, health checks, components, operators or imagestreams. The three scan switches control resource-agent generation; metrics, deployment and global requests still run when those switches are disabled.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
1. Inspect the Discovery summary: Total agents, Nodes agents, Pods agents, and Deployments agents count generated agents. They do not confirm successful Tentacle delivery.
  2. Check the global Openshift agent and the resource categories enabled in the task. Node/pod agents require complete metric, allocation, node and IP data. Deployment agents require a condition of type Available or Progressing with status True.
  3. Compare representative replica counts and CPU/memory values with the target cluster. Percentages use the node's allocatable resources, not container requests or limits.
  4. Inspect execution errors before treating missing agents or modules as absence of resources. A partial run can produce some agents and still report failures.

Do not use API status = 1 as proof of connectivity: this package always assigns that value. Check the health endpoint modules and request errors. Likewise, deployment Available is always 0 for generated deployments in this package; verify actual availability from replicas and cluster conditions.

No live cluster execution or package installation was performed for this documentation. The manual example below is unexecuted.

docs.title: Agents and identity
docs.text:
Agent Alias Parent Global Openshift None Node <NODE_NAME> Openshift Deployment <DEPLOYMENT_NAME> Openshift Pod <POD_NAME> Its node

The task does not expose a prefix. Manual configuration accepts prefix, prepending it to aliases and identities. Nodes then use the prefixed global parent and pods the prefixed node; deployments still refer to unprefixed Openshift. Pod agents use the pod IP as their address.

Pod and deployment identities omit the namespace. Equal names in different namespaces can collide; unprefixed identities can also collide across clusters. There is no namespace filter in this application. Changing a manual prefix changes generated identities; the deployment-parent limitation still applies.

docs.title: Functional summary
docs.text:
Agent Results Global Health checks, service/namespace counts and lists, components, replication-controller and API-service counts/status lists, deployment count Node Collected pod count and capacity percentage, CPU/memory and node conditions Deployment Desired, updated, ready, available and unavailable replicas; Available and Progressing modules with the limitations below Pod Phase, one condition module, container count and per-container CPU/memory

Node agents originate from node metrics; pod agents originate from pod metrics. Incomplete data can interrupt an entire processing stage and leave partial output. The node Pods count reflects processed pods with metrics, not a separately validated count of every scheduled pod.

Node conditions are not normalized to healthy = 1: every returned condition is 1 for status True, otherwise 0, including pressure conditions. Pod output contains only the last returned condition, not a module for every condition. Check the module name before interpreting its value.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
Use the distributed executable with a protected file of key=value lines:

pandora_openshift --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

Replace all placeholders in this unexecuted direct-mode example:

ip=<TARGET_HOST>
port=<API_PORT>
token=<API_TOKEN>
agents_group_name=<AGENT_GROUP>
interval=300
transfer_mode=tentacle
tentacle_ip=<TENTACLE_HOST>
tentacle_port=41121
use_proxy=0
deployments=1
nodes=1
pods=1

Execution produces Discovery JSON with generation counters and creates/transfers agent XML. An illustrative summary is {"summary":{"Total agents":4,"Nodes agents":1,"Pods agents":1,"Deployments agents":1}}. Do not apply the older server plugin's numeric success/error codes to this executable. -h/--help displays argument help.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text: Signal Check Error en la solicitud a <endpoint>: <status> Inspect host, port, endpoint reachability and HTTP status. For 401/403, check the token and authorization for that exact path. Direct host values must not contain a scheme. Can't get metrics, Error: Nodes or Error: Pods Check Metrics API responses, allocatable CPU/memory/pods, assigned nodes, pod IPs and condition data. Missing fields can interrupt collection or generation. Missing deployments or Error: Deployments Check the scan switch, returned deployment data and a True Available/Progressing condition. Available is 0 although the deployment is available A package limitation makes this value unreliable; use replica counts and cluster conditions. Progressing is 0 although that condition is True The selected status is the first matching True Available/Progressing condition. A preceding Available condition takes precedence. API status remains 1 during API failures It is a constant, not a connectivity test. Inspect health modules and execution errors. Failed health requests omit their modules. Missing global modules or Error: global_agent Inspect each request and the deployment data. Failed optional global requests can omit individual module groups; other incomplete data can prevent global-agent transfer. Only one pod condition appears This version emits only the final condition returned for the pod. Collection stalls There is no configured HTTP request timeout; inspect network connectivity and task execution. Proxy access fails Check the complete proxy base URL and its authentication arrangement; the task does not send the Bearer header in proxy mode. Agents counted but not received Check connectivity to the configured Tentacle destination; summary counters precede transfer.
