docs.title: Oracle Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-20.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Oracle Discovery plugin monitors Oracle Database instances by running SQL queries against them and turning the results into Pandora FMS monitoring modules. It collects availability, session and connection usage, query counts, restart detection, tablespace usage and status, fragmentation, cache hit ratios, and any custom SQL query the operator defines.

The plugin creates one agent per target database. When a target is an Oracle multitenant container database (CDB), it can additionally discover its pluggable databases (PDBs) and monitor them either inside the container agent or as one agent per PDB.

A target can be written as a simple HOST:PORT/SERVICE string or as a full Oracle DSN descriptor. DSN descriptors keep multi-address failover and are also used to reach PDBs, whose name is substituted as the service name.

The plugin is designed for use through the Pandora FMS Discovery system. It does not generate XML agent files: it returns the discovered agents and modules in the JSON output of the execution, and the Discovery task creates them.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Plugin version 1.12 (pandorafms.oracle) Documented target The version this page describes, identified by the package definition. See Plugin identity Oracle multitenant CDB/PDB whose PDB services are registered in the listener under a db_domain name Tested Ticket #24889 verification run: the task completed with Targets up and generated the PDB agent and its modules. See Multitenant PDB connection and service resolution Network reachability from the Discovery server to every target database listener Required The plugin opens a remote Oracle connection per target A database user able to connect and with SELECT on the views used by the enabled modules Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. See Grant the required privileges Oracle Instant Client on the Discovery server, when Thick mode is enabled Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. See Prerequisites Oracle Database 11 or earlier Not validated The official quick guide states thick mode is needed for Oracle 11 and earlier A specific Pandora FMS version Not validated No published test record establishes console or server version compatibility A specific host operating system for the machine that runs the plugin Not validated No host operating system has been recorded Oracle Database server versions Not validated Compatibility was established against the SQL queries and the connection contract, not a version matrix

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Network connectivity between the Discovery server and every target database listener.
  2. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task, and the console to define it.
  3. A database user with permission to connect, and with SELECT privileges on the views used by the modules you enable.
  4. Oracle Instant Client installed on the Discovery server, only when Thick mode is used.

The plugin is distributed as a self-contained Discovery application: the .disco package ships its own executable, so no additional runtime has to be installed for a normal run.

docs.title: Grant the required privileges
docs.text:
The connection user needs at least the CREATE SESSION privilege:

GRANT CREATE SESSION TO pandora;

Each module reads specific Oracle views. Grant only what the enabled modules need.

Module group Oracle views Grant Connections (checkConnections) V$SESSION, V$PARAMETER GRANT SELECT ON V_$SESSION TO pandora;GRANT SELECT ON V_$PARAMETER TO pandora; Uptime (checkUptime) V$SESSION GRANT SELECT ON V_$SESSION TO pandora; Query statistics (queryStats) V$SQLSTATS GRANT SELECT ON V_$SQLSTATS TO pandora; Tablespaces (checkTablespaces) DBA_TABLESPACE_USAGE_METRICS, DBA_TABLESPACES, and DBA_DATA_FILES / DBA_FREE_SPACE for the Oracle 10 and earlier fallback GRANT SELECT ON DBA_TABLESPACE_USAGE_METRICS TO pandora;GRANT SELECT ON DBA_TABLESPACES TO pandora;GRANT SELECT ON DBA_DATA_FILES TO pandora;GRANT SELECT ON DBA_FREE_SPACE TO pandora; Fragmentation (checkFragmentation) DBA_TABLES GRANT SELECT ON DBA_TABLES TO pandora; Cache (checkCache) V$LIBRARYCACHE, V$ROWCACHE, V$SYSSTAT GRANT SELECT ON V_$LIBRARYCACHE TO pandora;GRANT SELECT ON V_$ROWCACHE TO pandora;GRANT SELECT ON V_$SYSSTAT TO pandora; Multitenant PDB discovery (multitenant) V$PDBS and V$ACTIVE_SERVICES GRANT SELECT ON V_$PDBS TO pandora;GRANT SELECT ON V_$ACTIVE_SERVICES TO pandora; Database version PRODUCT_COMPONENT_VERSION GRANT SELECT ON PRODUCT_COMPONENT_VERSION TO pandora; Custom queries Depends on the query Grant SELECT on any table or view the custom queries reference

Version 1.12 reads V$ACTIVE_SERVICES to resolve the listener service name of each PDB. Without this grant the multitenant PDB discovery query fails and no PDB is monitored.

For convenience, SELECT_CATALOG_ROLE covers most V$ and DBA_ views:

CREATE USER pandora IDENTIFIED BY <PASSWORD>;
GRANT CREATE SESSION TO pandora;
GRANT SELECT_CATALOG_ROLE TO pandora;

When multitenant monitoring is used, the user must also be able to connect to each PDB and hold the module grants inside it:

ALTER SESSION SET CONTAINER = <PDB_NAME>;
GRANT CREATE SESSION TO pandora;
-- Repeat the module grants inside the PDB.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
Load the .disco package for pandorafms.oracle from the Pandora FMS Marketplace:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.oracle

Once loaded, the Oracle application is available when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from Management → Discovery → Applications → Oracle. The console presents the fields in two steps: Oracle Base and Oracle Detailed. Every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. Oracle Base — the targets and how to reach them:

    • Oracle target strings: one or more Oracle targets, separated by commas or one per line. Each line creates one agent. See Target strings.
    • User and Password: credentials used for every target in the task.
    • Thick mode and Client path: use the Oracle Instant Client; the client path is required when thick mode is enabled.
    • Multitenant: Discover and monitor PDBs within a CDB: enables PDB discovery on multitenant architectures.
    • Create agent per PDB: creates a separate agent for each discovered PDB instead of adding its modules to the container agent.
    • Enable entities file re-scan interval and Re-scan entities file interval: keep and periodically refresh the list of discovered PDBs.

    In the example above, the target string oracle-domain-mock:1521/FREE|PKI monitors the container database FREE and restricts multitenant monitoring to the PDB PKI.

  2. Oracle Detailed — monitoring scope and optional shaping:

    • Max threads: number of concurrent connections used to monitor the targets.
    • Target agent: names to assign to the generated agents, positionally matched with the target strings. Empty means the target string is used as the agent name.
    • Custom module prefix: prepended to every generated module name.
    • Check engine uptime, Retrieve query statistics, Analyze connections, Calculate fragmentation ratio, Monitor tablespaces, Retrieve cache statistics: select the module groups to create.
    • Execute custom queries and Custom queries: run operator-defined SQL and create one module per query.
    • Define tresholds: regular-expression thresholds applied to generated modules (except custom-query modules). See Thresholds.

The task's own group and interval, set in the generic task-definition step, become the agent group and the module interval.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from Management → Discovery → Task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A completed Oracle task reports:

    • Total agents: the number of agents generated by the task.
    • Targets up: targets the plugin connected to.
    • Targets down: targets it could not connect to.

    With Create agent per PDB enabled, Total agents includes the container agent plus one agent per monitored PDB.

  2. The agents. One per target string, plus one per PDB when Create agent per PDB is enabled. Every PDB agent is named <container agent> - PDB <pdb name>.

  3. The modules on each agent. A reachable target produces the availability module and one module per enabled group and discovered resource. The module list of the PDB agent shows the PDB PKI prefix on every PDB metric.

If the task reports Targets down for a target, work back through Troubleshoot.

docs.title: Agents and cardinality
docs.text:
• One agent per target string. The agent name is the target string, unless a Target agent name is given for that position. For a plain target, the filter appended after | is not part of the agent name. For a DSN target, the name is a readable label derived from the descriptor (Oracle <HOST>:<PORT>/<SERVICE>), with a short hash appended when the descriptor contains several addresses or services. The agent's OS is reported as Oracle and its OS version as the connected database version (or Discovery when it cannot be read).
  • One agent per PDB, optionally. When Create agent per PDB is enabled, each discovered PDB gets its own agent named <container agent> - PDB <pdb name>. Its address is HOST:PORT/<pdb name>, or the same generated name when the target is a DSN descriptor. When the option is disabled, each PDB's modules are added to the container agent with a PDB <pdb name> prefix.

docs.title: Module groups
docs.text:
A reachable target always produces the availability module <prefix>Oracle connection, with value 1 when the connection succeeded and 0 when it did not.

Group Modules Type Notes Availability <prefix>Oracle connection generic_proc 1 connected, 0 not connected Uptime <prefix>restart detection generic_proc 0 when the engine restarted within the last two intervals, 1 otherwise Query statistics <prefix>queries: select, <prefix>queries: insert, <prefix>queries: delete, <prefix>queries: update generic_data Number of statements of each kind active during the last interval Tablespaces <prefix>tablespace <name> free and <prefix>tablespace <name> status generic_data (%) and generic_proc Free percentage and 1 when the tablespace is ONLINE Connections <prefix>session usage generic_data (%) Current sessions against the configured maximum Fragmentation <prefix>fragmentation ratio generic_data (%) Average fragmentation ratio Cache <prefix>cache hit ratio (dictionary), <prefix>cache hit ratio (library), <prefix>cache hit ratio (buffer) generic_data (%) With default warning/critical thresholds Custom queries <prefix><query name> Per query One module per custom query

The exhaustive inventory, including PDB prefixes and default thresholds, is in Generated modules.

docs.title: Multitenant PDB connection and service resolution
docs.text:
In Oracle multitenant, a PDB is reached through its service name, but the PDB name is not necessarily the service the listener exposes. A PDB can exist while its listener service is only registered under a qualified name, for example when the database has a db_domain configured. Connecting to the PDB name alone then fails with DPY-6001: Service "..." is not registered with the listener (equivalent to ORA-12514).

The plugin resolves the service name of each PDB and tries these candidates in order:

  1. The listener service names registered for that PDB, including the service names read from the entities file.
  2. The same service names qualified with the database domain (db_domain) when the listener exposes them as fully qualified names.
  3. The PDB name itself, as a last resort.

How each candidate is applied depends on the target format:

  • Plain target (HOST:PORT/SERVICE): the plugin connects to the PDB as HOST:PORT/<service name>.
  • DSN target: the plugin rewrites the descriptor, replacing the value of SERVICE_NAME with the candidate while keeping the addresses, ports and failover settings. If the descriptor identifies the connection with a SID instead, the plugin replaces that SID clause with SERVICE_NAME=<service name>.
  • If the descriptor contains neither SERVICE_NAME nor SID, the PDB connection cannot be built and the PDB is reported in the execution information and skipped.
  • A PDB or service name that contains characters outside letters, digits and _ $ # . - is rejected as invalid.

Only when every candidate fails is a warning reported, and (with Create agent per PDB) the PDB agent is created with its connection module at value 0.

Only PDBs in READ WRITE open mode are monitored during discovery; the others are named in the execution information and skipped. PDBs restored from the entities file are monitored as cached.

The Oracle target strings field can restrict which PDBs are monitored by appending |<pdb> or |<pdb1>;<pdb2>;... to a target, as shown in Configure the Discovery task.

docs.title: Custom queries
docs.text: Each custom query generates one module on every agent the query applies to. A query can be limited to the container scope (cdb), to PDBs (pdb), or both (all), and can be scheduled with a five-field crontab expression. The target_databases key selects the agents the query applies to: matching ignores case and surrounding whitespace, and accepts the full target string, the SID, or the PDB name. all or an empty value applies the query everywhere. Scheduled queries keep their last successful execution, so an occurrence that was missed while the plugin was not running is executed on the next task run. See Custom queries reference.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The plugin reports its diagnostics in the JSON execution summary printed to standard output: connection warnings, Oracle error codes, and skipped queries are added there.

  • A DSN target cannot connect — the plugin does not fall back from a DSN descriptor to a HOST:PORT/SID connection. Check the descriptor syntax and that it is reachable.
  • A PDB is skipped with DSN contains no SERVICE_NAME or SID to replace — the DSN target used to reach the container does not contain a SERVICE_NAME or SID to substitute with the PDB name. Use a descriptor that identifies the connection with one of them.
  • A PDB is skipped as invalid — the PDB or service name contains characters outside letters, digits and _ $ # . -.
  • DPY-6001: Service "..." is not registered with the listener (or ORA-12514) — the PDB service is not reachable under the name that was tried. The plugin resolves the registered service names and the db_domain qualification automatically; if it still fails, verify that the user has SELECT on V$ACTIVE_SERVICES and that the PDB service is actually registered with the listener.
  • Targets down for a target — the container connection failed. Check network access from the Discovery server, the target string format, and the credentials.
  • No PDBs discovered — the discovery query failed (often a missing grant on V$PDBS or V$ACTIVE_SERVICES), or no PDB matches the |PDB filter in the target string.
  • A PDB is skipped — only PDBs in READ WRITE open mode are monitored; skipped PDBs are named in the execution summary.
  • ORA-00942: table or view does not exist — the monitoring user lacks SELECT on a required view. Grant the privilege for the enabled module group and re-run.
  • agent_per_pdb has no effect — it only applies when Multitenant is enabled.
  • A custom query is missing from an agent — its target_databases value does not match that agent's target string, SID or PDB name. The execution summary names the skipped query and the identifiers it was compared with.
  • An invalid crontab expression is ignored — a custom query crontab must have five fields. An invalid expression produces a warning and the query is skipped.
  • Thick mode fails to start — Client path must point to the Oracle Instant Client libraries installed on the Discovery server.

docs.title: Target strings
docs.text:
The Oracle target strings field accepts one target per line or comma separated. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored. Each target can use any of these formats:

HOST
HOST/SID
HOST:PORT
HOST:PORT/SID
HOST:PORT/SERVICE_NAME
dsn=(DESCRIPTION=(ADDRESS=(PROTOCOL=TCP)(HOST=<HOST>)(PORT=1521))(CONNECT_DATA=(SID=<SID>)))

When the port is omitted, 1521 is used. A DSN descriptor can be written with or without the leading dsn= (the comparison is case-insensitive), and can describe a failover configuration with several addresses:

dsn=(DESCRIPTION=(FAILOVER=ON)(ADDRESS_LIST=(ADDRESS=(PROTOCOL=TCP)(HOST=<HOST_1>)(PORT=1521))(ADDRESS=(PROTOCOL=TCP)(HOST=<HOST_2>)(PORT=1521)))(CONNECT_DATA=(SID=<SID>)))

For a DSN target the agent name is not the raw descriptor: the plugin builds a readable label from the first host, port and service (Oracle <HOST>:<PORT>/<SERVICE>), and appends a short hash when the descriptor contains several addresses or services.

When the target is a multitenant container and Multitenant is enabled, a PDB filter can be appended with |:

HOST:PORT/SERVICE_NAME|PDB1
HOST:PORT/SERVICE_NAME|PDB1;PDB2

Without a filter, every eligible PDB is monitored.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
A Discovery task builds this file from its own fields. A manual run supplies it with --conf.

Key Default Description agents_group_id 10 Group id assigned to the generated agents interval 300 Agent and module interval in seconds user Empty Connection user. Required password Empty Connection password. Required thick_mode 0 1 enables thick mode client_path Empty Path to the Oracle Instant Client libraries; used with thick mode threads 1 Number of concurrent monitoring threads modules_prefix Empty Prefix for generated module names multitenant 0 1 discovers and monitors PDBs agent_per_pdb 0 1 creates one agent per PDB; requires multitenant=1 execute_custom_queries 1 1 runs custom queries analyze_connections 1 1 creates the session usage module engine_uptime 1 1 creates the restart detection module query_stats 1 1 creates the query statistics modules cache_stats 1 1 creates the cache hit ratio modules fragmentation_ratio 1 1 creates the fragmentation ratio module check_tablescpaces 1 1 creates the tablespace modules (the key keeps this spelling) entities_list Task temporary file Path of the file where discovered PDBs are stored enable_entities_interval 0 1 enables the PDB list re-scan entities_interval 86400 Re-scan interval in seconds cron_state_dir Task temporary file Directory where the last successful execution of scheduled custom queries is stored

Example:

[CONF]
agents_group_id=10
interval=300
user=<USERNAME>
password=<PASSWORD>
thick_mode=0
multitenant=1
agent_per_pdb=1
execute_custom_queries=1
analyze_connections=1
engine_uptime=1
query_stats=0
cache_stats=1
fragmentation_ratio=1
check_tablescpaces=1

The configuration file and the target lists hold the database password in plain text. Restrict them to the account that runs the plugin and keep them out of shared directories, logs and version control.

docs.title: Command-line execution
docs.text:
The plugin can be executed by hand, which is the fastest way to confirm a target and its credentials before wiring it into a task.

./pandora_oracle \
    --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> \
    --target_databases <PATH_TO_TARGETS> \
    [ --target_agents <PATH_TO_AGENT_NAMES> ] \
    [ --custom_queries <PATH_TO_CUSTOM_QUERIES> ]
Parameter Description --conf Path to the configuration file --target_databases Path to the file containing the target databases --target_agents Path to the file containing the agent names, positionally matched with the targets --custom_queries Path to the file containing the custom queries

The run returns a JSON summary of the execution. The collected data is exposed in the summary's monitoring_data field for the Discovery server to consume.

docs.title: Custom queries reference
docs.text:
Each custom query is a block delimited by check_begin and check_end. Only SELECT statements are allowed.

Key Description name Module name. Mandatory description Module description target SQL query to execute. Mandatory. Only SELECT statements are accepted target_databases Comma-separated target strings, SIDs or PDB names the query applies to. Matching ignores case and surrounding whitespace. all or empty applies it everywhere target_scope cdb, pdb or all. Empty or all applies it to both scopes. pdb requires multitenant monitoring operation value returns a single value; full returns all rows as a string. Empty behaves as full datatype generic_data, generic_data_string or generic_proc. A full operation is forced to generic_data_string min_warning, max_warning Warning thresholds min_critical, max_critical Critical thresholds warning_inverse, critical_inverse Set to 1 to invert the corresponding threshold interval str_warning, str_critical String thresholds module_interval Module interval as a multiplier of the agent interval crontab Five-field cron expression. When present, the query only runs when an occurrence is due

Example:

check_begin
name Invalid objects count
description Number of invalid objects
operation value
datatype generic_data
min_warning 5
target SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ALL_OBJECTS WHERE STATUS != 'VALID'
target_scope all
check_end

The console ships a commented guide with the field and a set of example queries as the default content of the Custom queries textarea.

docs.title: Thresholds
docs.text:
The Define tresholds field applies thresholds to the generated modules by module name, except custom-query modules. One definition per line, with a regular expression matching the module name and the thresholds separated by |:

<REGEX> = <threshold>|<threshold>|...

Example:

^tablespace = min_warning 10|max_warning 20|min_critical 0|max_critical 10

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text: All module names carry the Custom module prefix when one is set. Modules created for a PDB keep the container prefix and add a PDB <pdb name> segment.

docs.title: Container agent
docs.text:

docs.title: OVH Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The OVH Discovery addon monitors OVHcloud environments through the OVHcloud API. It turns the result into Pandora FMS agents and modules: the state of Public Cloud instances, optional per-instance CPU, memory and network statistics, Public Cloud volumes, dedicated servers and, optionally, the monthly and overall costs.

A Discovery task generates four kinds of agents:

  • A global agent named OVH, with the number of instances found and, optionally, the cost modules. It is created on every run, except in January when Get monthly and overall costs is enabled: the cost calculation for the previous month fails in that month and the global agent is not generated.
  • One agent per virtual machine (Public Cloud instance), with its state and, optionally, its performance statistics.
  • One agent per volume (Public Cloud volume), with its status, size and attachment.
  • One agent per dedicated server, with its status and hardware and location attributes.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.ovh, version 1.1 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the Discovery server to the OVHcloud API Required The addon queries the OVHcloud API of the ovh-eu endpoint OVHcloud API credentials (application key, application secret and consumer key) Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon

The addon always connects to the ovh-eu OVHcloud API endpoint. Accounts that belong to a different OVHcloud API region are not covered by this version.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to the OVHcloud API.
  2. An OVHcloud application key, application secret and consumer key. The process is described in the OVHcloud guide on getting started with its API: OVHcloud API getting started.
  3. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it.

docs.title: OVHcloud API access
docs.text:
The addon only issues read requests (GET). The consumer key must be authorized for the paths that correspond to the options you enable:

Path Used for /cloud/project and /cloud/project/{project} Listing Public Cloud projects (always) /cloud/project/{project}/instance Listing virtual machines (always) /cloud/project/{project}/instance/{instance}/monitoring CPU, memory and network statistics (when Advanced statistics is enabled) /cloud/project/{project}/volume Volumes (when Scan Volumes is enabled) /dedicated/server and /dedicated/server/{server} Dedicated servers (when Scan Servers is enabled) /me/bill and /me/bill/{bill} Costs (when Get monthly and overall costs is enabled)

The application secret and consumer key are credentials: do not share them and do not paste them in tickets or screenshots.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.ovh

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, OVH is available in the Cloud section when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from Management > Discovery > Cloud and choose OVH. The console presents the fields in two steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. OVH base — credentials and where the generated agent data is sent:

    • OVH application key, OVH application secret and OVH consumer key: the OVHcloud API credentials.
    • Tentacle IP and Tentacle port: where the generated agent data is sent. They rarely need changing.

  2. OVH detailed — the resources to monitor:

    • Scan Volumes, Scan Servers and Monitor virtual machines: which resource types get agents.
    • Get monthly and overall costs: adds the cost modules to the global agent.
    • Advanced statistics: shown only when Monitor virtual machines is enabled; adds the performance modules to the virtual machine agents.
    • Autodisabled agents: creates the agents in disabled mode.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to the agents the task creates.

Enabling Advanced statistics and Get monthly and overall costs can lengthen the task execution, because each requires additional OVHcloud API requests.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes successfully reports:

    • Total agents: all agents generated, including the global agent.
    • VMs agents: virtual machine agents.
    • Storage agents: volume agents.
    • Server agents: dedicated server agents.

    A task that does not complete successfully records the errors in its execution information instead.

  2. The agents. The global agent plus one agent per virtual machine, volume and dedicated server found, according to the options enabled.

  3. The modules. The global agent has OVH VMs count; every virtual machine agent has <VM name>.status. See Understand the results.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Alias Address Notes Global agent OVH None Created on every run, except in January when Get monthly and overall costs is enabled Virtual machine agent The instance name The instance IPv4 address; empty when it has none One per instance name of every Public Cloud project: instances with the same name in different projects share one agent. Created only when Monitor virtual machines is enabled. The description includes the instance region Volume agent The volume name None Created only when Scan Volumes is enabled Dedicated server agent The server name The server IP address Created only when Scan Servers is enabled

All agents are created in the task group. When Autodisabled agents is enabled they are created in disabled mode.

docs.text:
Global agent

Module Type Condition Description OVH VMs count generic_data Always Instances found across all Public Cloud projects, regardless of Monitor virtual machines OVH total costs generic_data Get monthly and overall costs Sum of the invoices of the account, with taxes OVH month costs generic_data Get monthly and overall costs Sum, with taxes, of the invoices dated from the first day of the previous month up to the moment of the run

Virtual machine agent

Module Type Condition Description <VM name>.status generic_proc Always 1 when the instance status is ACTIVE, 0 otherwise <VM name>cpu:max, <VM name>cpu:used generic_data Advanced statistics CPU statistics reported by OVHcloud <VM name>mem:max, <VM name>mem:used generic_data Advanced statistics Memory statistics reported by OVHcloud <VM name>net:rx, <VM name>net:tx generic_data Advanced statistics Network received and sent, as reported by OVHcloud

docs.title: How agent identity works
docs.text: Each agent is identified by a hash of its prefix and name; volume and dedicated server agents also include the OVHcloud identifier of the resource. Agents with the same identity keep reporting to the same Pandora FMS agent between runs, so renaming a virtual machine in OVHcloud produces a new agent.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. The executable takes a single parameter, the path to a configuration file described in Configuration file:

./pandora_ovh --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

It prints a JSON summary and sends one data file per agent using the configured transfer mode:

{"summary": {"Total agents": 13, "VMs agents": 8, "Storage agents": 1, "Server agents": 3}}

When errors occur, the JSON also contains an info key with the messages and the exit code is 1. In tentacle mode the tentacle_client executable must be available in the PATH of the user running the addon.

A configuration file contains the OVHcloud credentials. Protect it with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the info field of the JSON execution result, which is shown in the task's execution information.

  • Error: Connector Cannot create client to OVH API: the OVHcloud API client could not be created with the credentials provided.
  • Error getting instances: Unexpected error: the Public Cloud projects or instances could not be listed. Check connectivity, the three credentials and that the consumer key is authorized for /cloud/project.
  • Error: Getting volumes, Error: Getting servers or Error: Getting costs: the corresponding request failed; the message includes the error returned by OVHcloud. Check the matching path in OVHcloud API access.
  • Error: Getting metrics ... for instance: <id>: statistics could not be obtained for that instance. Its other modules are still generated.
  • Error while reading configuration file: the configuration file given to --conf cannot be read (manual execution).
  • No virtual machine agents: Monitor virtual machines is disabled. The global agent still reports the number of instances found.
  • No statistics modules: Advanced statistics is disabled, or Monitor virtual machines is.
  • Fewer agents than expected: only the resource types enabled in the task are created, and only the Public Cloud projects, volumes and dedicated servers visible to the credentials are scanned.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
Used by manual execution. One key = value per line. Numeric options accept 1 to enable and 0 to disable; a value that is not a number is read as 0.

Key Default Description application_key — Mandatory. OVHcloud application key application_secret — Mandatory. OVHcloud application secret consumer_key — Mandatory. OVHcloud consumer key agents_group_name ovh Group of the generated agents interval 300 Agent interval, in seconds prefix empty Prefix added to every agent alias transfer_mode local local or tentacle data_dir /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Folder for the data files in local mode tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1 Tentacle server address tentacle_port 41121 Tentacle server port scan_vms 0 Virtual machine agents storage 0 Volume agents servers 0 Dedicated server agents cost 0 Cost modules advance_monitoring 0 Performance modules of virtual machines autodisabled_agents 0 Create agents in disabled mode
