Association to an open ticket Adds a followup comment and prints Succesful: Added tracking in the ticket : <TICKET_ID> Association to a solved or closed ticket, --recovery 0 Creates a new ticket and replaces the stored ID Association to a solved or closed ticket, --recovery 1 Removes the stored entry and adds the followup comment to the closed ticket The run completes Closes the GLPI session and exits

docs.title: Addon identity
docs.text: Property Value Marketplace identifier pandorafms.glpi Name GLPI Version 1.0 — the version of the Marketplace package pandorafms.glpi.1.0.zip, also reported by the addon's usage summary Category Miscelaneus License Free Marketplace last update 2026-01-28 Availability Free download Marketplace entry pandorafms.glpi

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: This integration publishes Pandora FMS alerts into a Google Chat room through an incoming webhook. The room exposes a webhook URL, and a Pandora FMS alert command posts the alert text to it, so alerts appear as messages in the room alongside the team's conversation.

docs.title: Google Chat settings: chat room
docs.text:
Once you have logged in and have been identified with your user credentials, go to the chat room (or add a new one) where the Pandora FMS alert messages will be published. Click on Manage webhooks:

In the pop-up dialog box, name the webhook and, if desired, place a link to a public online image to better identify it (visually).

Click the Save button. Then it will show a summary with a link to the documentation about this technology and a blue button inviting to create another webhook; copy the webhook identifier link as it will be used to configure Pandora FMS in the next page.

docs.title: Pandora FMS configuration: creation of an alert command
docs.text:
Open a terminal window and access the Pandora FMS server. Download (and unzip) from the Pandora FMS library the Google Chat connector CLI in the following path:

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora-gchat

Or in a location that Pandora FMS server can access. You should have installed python3 (with the modules argparse, requests and json) and python3-pip to be able to use the pandora-gchat-cli.py program. Once you have installed both, with the pip3 command you must install the requirements or dependencies (minimum versions) with the following instruction:

pip3 install -r requirements.txt

In the file test-exec.txt you will find an example that you can reuse to configure the alert command. It is recommended that from the same terminal window you send a basic test message to the chat room, for example:

Messages can be further elaborated by additional parameters, compare with the following example:

Go to the Pandora FMS Web Console and click on Alerts -> Commands -> Create.

With the help of the text that is in the file test-exec.txt complete the following fields, pay attention in the second field where you will copy the link identifier obtained in the previous page, make sure to mark its content as hidden in Pandora FMS:

Click on the Create button to save the alert command.

docs.title: Pandora FMS configuration: creating an alert action
docs.text:
The alert actions allow you to define how to launch the command. Go to menu Alerts -> Actions -> Create.

Select in Command the alert command created on the previous page, the fields will be filled in automatically. However, you can always customize the icons for Triggering and Recovery events, for example.

To save click on Create. To apply this action to either a Module or Policy, set up an alert template for this purpose.

You can get more information in the video tutorial «Create alerts in Google Chat with Pandora FMS».

docs.title: Grafana
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Grafana addon is a data source plugin for Grafana. It is not a Pandora FMS monitoring plugin: it is installed inside Grafana, it runs no process on a Pandora FMS server, and it creates no agents and no modules. It adds Pandorafms Grafana to the Grafana data source list, so Grafana panels can plot the history of numeric Pandora FMS modules.

The data comes from the Grafana API extension of the Pandora FMS console, located under pandora_console/extensions/grafana. The addon stores the base URL of that extension plus a Pandora FMS user and password, asks the extension which groups, agents and modules that user can see, and then requests the values of one module for the time range of each panel.

Two execution paths use the configured data source:

  • Panels query from the Grafana web client. The browser of each Grafana user sends the requests to the Pandora FMS console, so the browser — not only the Grafana server — must be able to reach it.
  • Alert rules are evaluated by the Grafana server. The server must reach the console too, and the server-side path of this version does not receive data (see Alert rules).

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions Grafana 10.0.3 or later Required The plugin declares grafanaDependency >=10.0.3 A Pandora FMS node console with the Grafana API extension available Required The addon appends /search and /query to the configured extension URL, and the extension answers 403 on a metaconsole node A Pandora FMS user with the read-agents privilege (AR) Required Both extension endpoints check that privilege before returning any group Grafana versions above the declared minimum Not validated No Grafana version matrix is recorded for this addon Operating system of the Grafana host Not validated The addon runs inside Grafana; no operating system is recorded

The Pandora FMS version, the Grafana version and the node console are installation requirements, not compatibility statements about other versions.

docs.title: On the Pandora FMS side
docs.text:
1. A node console, not the Metaconsole. The extension answers 403 when it runs on a metaconsole node. Point the data source at the node console that stores the agents you want to plot.
  2. The Grafana API extension served by that console. It is part of the console directory (pandora_console/extensions/grafana) and needs no separate installation on the Pandora FMS side. It answers at https://<PANDORA_FMS_URL>/pandora_console/extensions/grafana/.
  3. A Pandora FMS user with the read-agents privilege (AR) and its password. The extension returns no data when the user does not hold that privilege, and only the groups where the user holds it.
  4. A CORS origin that allows the Grafana URL. The extension sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin with the value of Setup → General → Security, field Grafana Access-Control-Allow-Origin. The default is *, which allows any origin. Set the origin of the Grafana server — scheme, host and port — to narrow it.

docs.title: On the Grafana side
docs.text:
1. Grafana 10.0.3 or later.
  2. Write access to the Grafana plugins directory and to grafana.ini, plus permission to restart Grafana. In the Linux packages the plugins directory is /var/lib/grafana/plugins.
  3. The plugin loaded as an unsigned plugin (see Allow the unsigned plugin).

docs.title: Network
docs.text:
• The browser of every Grafana user that opens a dashboard must reach the Pandora FMS console.
  • The Grafana server must reach the console to evaluate alert rules.

docs.title: Install the data source
docs.text:
1. Download pandorafms.grafana.1.0.zip from the Marketplace entry. The download is limited to licensed users.
  2. Extract the archive inside the Grafana plugins directory, so that the plugin folder sits directly under it:
cd /var/lib/grafana/plugins
sudo unzip /path/to/pandorafms.grafana.1.0.zip
  1. Restart Grafana so that it loads the plugin.

docs.title: Allow the unsigned plugin
docs.text:
The plugin is not signed, so Grafana loads it only when its identifier is listed as allowed. Add the key to /etc/grafana/grafana.ini:

[plugins]
allow_loading_unsigned_plugins = "pandorafms-pandorafmsgrafana-datasource"

When the key already lists other plugins, add this identifier to the comma-separated list. Restart Grafana again after the change.

pandorafms-pandorafmsgrafana-datasource is the data source plugin identifier and must match exactly. Without it, Grafana does not load the plugin and Pandorafms Grafana does not appear in the data source list.

docs.title: Create the data source
docs.text:
1. In Grafana open Connections → Data sources and select Add data source.
  2. Choose Pandorafms Grafana.
  3. Fill in the three fields:
Field Required Default Description Pandora extension Yes — Base URL of the Pandora FMS Grafana API extension, with the scheme and without a trailing slash or endpoint suffix: https://<PANDORA_FMS_URL>/pandora_console/extensions/grafana. The addon appends /search and /query. Pandora user Yes — Pandora FMS user with the AR privilege. Every Grafana user queries with this identity. Password Yes — Password of that user. It is stored in the data source JSON settings, not in Grafana's encrypted secure fields, because the browser sends it with every request.
  1. Select Save & Test. The test does not contact Pandora FMS (see Verify).

Notes:

  • Use an https extension URL whenever the console is served over TLS. If Grafana is served over HTTPS, the browser blocks a plain http extension URL as mixed content.
  • Any Pandora FMS user with the AR privilege works; it does not need administrator rights. It does need to see every group whose modules the dashboards must show, because the group list only contains groups where the user holds AR.

docs.title: Build a panel query
docs.text:
1. Create a dashboard, add a panel and select Pandorafms Grafana in Query.
  2. Choose Group, then Agent, then Module. The lists narrow in that order, and Module stays empty until an Agent is selected.
  3. The panel shows one series per query.
Field Default Description Label Empty Not used. The addon does not send it, and the series keeps the module name. Tip Unchecked Full-scale switch. Checked, Pandora FMS returns the stored samples. Unchecked, it returns compacted values (averages) and the series name ends in (avg). Group Empty Narrows the agent list. All (value 0) lists every agent. Only groups where the data source user holds AR appear. Agent Empty Narrows the module list to the enabled agents of the selected group; with All, to every enabled agent. Module Empty Module to plot: enabled, non-string modules of the selected agent. The module identifier is what the request carries.
  • Only Module decides the data. The extension reads the module identifier and ignores the agent value.
  • Changing Group or Agent does not clear the previous Agent or Module. The panel keeps querying the old module until you choose a new one, so re-select the module after narrowing the lists.
  • Every change in the editor reloads the three lists in full, and a change of Tip, Group, Agent or Module also runs the query. On installations with many groups, agents or modules this makes the editor slower.
  • The data source returns numeric values without unit metadata. Set the unit of the panel to match the module.
  • To compare modules, add one query per module to the same panel.

docs.title: Alert rules
docs.text: The data source declares alerting support, so a Grafana alert rule can use a Pandora FMS query. Grafana evaluates alert rules on the server, not in the browser. In this version the server-side path does not carry the extension URL and the password stored in the form, so a rule evaluated by the server does not receive data. Check Limitations before building one, and test any rule end to end before relying on it.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text: Save & Test does not check the connection. The data source returns success without contacting Pandora FMS, so a green result only means that Grafana saved the form. Run both checks below.

docs.title: Check the extension directly
docs.text:
curl -sS -u <USERNAME> \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"type":"group"}' \
  'https://<PANDORA_FMS_URL>/pandora_console/extensions/grafana/search'

curl asks for the password interactively, so the password does not appear in the shell history or in the process list. The extension accepts the standard HTTP basic authentication that curl sends.

A user with the AR privilege receives a JSON array with the All entry first, followed by one entry per group:

[{"value":0,"text":"All"},{"value":"<GROUP_ID>","text":"<GROUP_NAME>"}]

Read the result as follows:

Result Meaning A JSON array with All and your groups The extension, the console and the credentials work [] The extension reached Pandora FMS but rejected the credentials, or the user holds no AR privilege. A rejected login is not an HTTP error 403 The URL points at a metaconsole node 404 The URL, the extension directory or the web server rewrite rule is wrong

docs.title: Run a query from Grafana
docs.text:
1. Open a panel or Explore with the Pandorafms Grafana data source.
  2. Select a group, an agent and a module that has known data in the selected time range.
  3. The expected result is one series named after the module — with the (avg) suffix while Tip is unchecked — and points across the range.
  4. Check Tip and run the query again. The same series appears without the suffix and with the original samples.

If the extension check works and the panel still shows no data, read Operate and troubleshoot.

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
• One series per query. Its name is the module name reported by Pandora FMS. With Tip unchecked the addon appends (avg) to show that the values are compacted averages; with Tip checked the series keeps the original samples. The Label field does not rename the series.
  • The time range is the panel range. The extension derives the period from the range and returns the module history inside it.
  • Unknown periods are gaps. When Pandora FMS has no value, or marks the module data as unknown, the point is null and the panel draws a gap instead of a zero.
  • Only numeric modules. The module picker excludes string modules, so they cannot be plotted with this data source. Disabled agents and disabled modules are also excluded from the pickers.
  • Permissions stop at the group list. The extension authenticates the Pandora FMS user, requires AR on at least one group, and filters the group list by that permission. The agent and module lookups and the data request are resolved from the identifiers the browser sends, without checking the group permission again. Treat every Grafana user who can use this data source as able to read any numeric module whose identifier is requested.
  • One Pandora FMS identity per data source. Every Grafana user who can use the data source reads the same data with the same Pandora FMS user. Grafana's own permissions on the data source decide who can use it.

docs.title: Day-to-day operation
docs.text:
• The addon has no scheduler: it queries Pandora FMS when a panel is loaded or refreshed, and when an alert rule is evaluated. Nothing is stored on the Grafana side beyond the data source settings.
  • Each query is one request to the extension. A panel with three module queries sends three requests.
  • Keep the Grafana data source URL and the Pandora FMS console URL reachable from both the browser and the Grafana server; a change in firewalls, reverse proxies or TLS certificates breaks the panels.

docs.title: Permissions and transport
docs.text:
• The password is stored in the data source JSON settings, because the browser needs it for every query. It is not kept in Grafana's encrypted secure fields, and it is returned to the Grafana web client. Restrict who can read or edit data sources in Grafana, and use a dedicated Pandora FMS user for the addon.
  • HTTP basic authentication encodes the credentials, it does not encrypt them. Use an https extension URL so that the credentials travel encrypted.
  • The default CORS origin is *: any web origin may call the extension when it can send credentials. Set Grafana Access-Control-Allow-Origin to the Grafana origin to narrow it.
  • The Pandora FMS user needs only the AR privilege. Do not use an administrator account for the data source.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text: Symptom Cause and check Save & Test reports success but the panel shows no data Expected: the test does not contact Pandora FMS. Check the extension with the curl command in Verify The Group list is empty Rejected credentials, a user without AR, or a CORS block. Run the extension check and read the browser console The Module list is empty No Agent has been selected yet; agents and modules are also excluded when they are disabled The panel shows No data No stored values in the time range, a string module, or a module left over from a previous agent. Re-select the module and widen the range The browser console reports a CORS error Grafana Access-Control-Allow-Origin does not match the Grafana origin, or the extension URL is http while Grafana is https The extension answers 403 The URL points at a metaconsole node; use the node console The extension answers 404 Wrong path (it must end in /pandora_console/extensions/grafana), a missing extension directory, or a web server that does not apply the rewrite rules that resolve /search and /query Pandorafms Grafana does not appear in the data source list The plugin folder is not under the plugins directory, allow_loading_unsigned_plugins lacks the identifier, or Grafana was not restarted The series name ends in (avg) Tip is unchecked; check it to receive the original samples An alert rule returns no data See Limitations: the server-side evaluation path does not use the connection details stored in the form

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The Label field does nothing. The series is always named after the module, with the (avg) suffix when the values are compacted.
  • Save & Test always reports success. It does not open a connection to Pandora FMS, so it cannot detect a wrong URL, rejected credentials or an unreachable console.
  • A rejected login is not an error. When the user or the password is wrong, or the user has no AR privilege, the extension answers HTTP 200 with an empty array. The panel shows No data instead of an authentication error.
  • Alert rules cannot reach the console in this version. Grafana evaluates them on the server, and the server-side path builds its request from the data source URL and password fields, while the form stores the console URL and the password in custom fields the server side does not read. A rule therefore fails or evaluates without data. Panel queries are not affected because the browser runs them.
  • The settings contain a single Pandora FMS user, with a single set of permissions. All Grafana users who can use the data source see the same data.
  • String modules cannot be plotted, and they are not offered in the module picker.
  • The pickers load complete lists. The addon sends no text filter: the group, agent and module lists are downloaded in full each time the editor changes, and Grafana filters them in the browser.

docs.title: Data source settings
docs.text: Setting Required Default Description Pandora extension Yes — Base URL of the extension, with scheme: https://<PANDORA_FMS_URL>/pandora_console/extensions/grafana. No trailing slash and no /search or /query suffix Pandora user Yes — Pandora FMS user queried by every request Password Yes — Password of that user, stored in the data source JSON settings

docs.title: Query fields
docs.text: Field Default Description Label Empty Not used Tip Unchecked Checked: original samples. Unchecked: compacted averages with the (avg) series suffix Group Empty Group filter for the agent list; All is value 0 Agent Empty Agent filter for the module list Module Empty Module identifier sent to the extension

docs.title: Extension endpoints
docs.text:
The addon uses two endpoints relative to the configured base URL. Both accept HTTP basic authentication and return JSON.

Endpoint Purpose Request body Response <extension>/search Group, agent and module lists {"type":"group"}, {"type":"agent","extra":"<group-id>"} or {"type":"module","extra":"<agent-id>"} Array of {"value": <id>, "text": "<name>"}; groups include {"value":0,"text":"All"} <extension>/query Module values for a time range {"targets":[{"target":{"agent":"<agent-id>","module":"<module-id>","tip":<boolean>}}],"range":{"from":"<date>","to":"<date>"}} Array of objects with the series name in target and pairs of [<value>, <timestamp in milliseconds>] in datapoints

In /query only module and tip are read: the series name is the module name reported by Pandora FMS, and the agent value is ignored. Dates are accepted in any format that Pandora FMS can parse, for example ISO 8601.

docs.title: Addon identity
docs.text: Property Value Marketplace identifier pandorafms.grafana Name Grafana Version 1.0 — the version of the Marketplace package pandorafms.grafana.1.0.zip Data source plugin identifier pandorafms-pandorafmsgrafana-datasource, the value required by allow_loading_unsigned_plugins Category Miscelaneus License One — the download is limited to licensed users Availability Licensed download Marketplace last update 2025-06-25 Minimum Grafana version 10.0.3, declared by the plugin Marketplace entry pandorafms.grafana

docs.title: Slack integration
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-27.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Slack integration delivers Pandora FMS alerts to a Slack channel as chat messages. When an alert fires or recovers, Pandora FMS runs a connector on the server that processes the alert and the connector posts the alert fields through the Slack Web API, as the Slack app you authorize.

The connector ships with Pandora FMS. There is no Marketplace entry for it and nothing to download from the catalogue: the executable and the default alert command named Pandora Slack are already part of the product, and you only add the Slack side and the credentials.

Each run posts two messages by default: the alert (an emoji, a bold title, an italic description and one key : value line per data pair) and, separately, a footer message with the text PandoraFMS. Both are configurable, and the footer can be suppressed.

Optionally the connector can attach a module graph image obtained from the Pandora FMS API. That path depends on a Slack file-upload method that Slack retired, so the image is not delivered any more. The alert text is unaffected. See Understand the integration.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence A Slack workspace where you can create and install an app Required The connector authenticates with a Slack app bot token, so the app must exist and be installed in the workspace A Slack app with a bot user and the chat:write scope Required Every message is posted with chat.postMessage, which requires chat:write The app as a member of the target channel, or the chat:write.public scope Required Slack rejects a post from an app that is not in the channel with not_in_channel; chat:write.public allows public channels without joining Outbound HTTPS from the Pandora FMS server to slack.com (TCP 443) Required All calls go to the Slack Web API Pandora FMS release that ships the Pandora Slack command Not validated No release-specific record exists for this connector Operating system of the Pandora FMS server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this connector A corporate proxy or TLS interception between the server and Slack Not validated The connector has no proxy or CA option of its own; see Troubleshoot

docs.title: Create the Slack app
docs.text:
1. Open https://api.slack.com/apps and choose Create New App → From scratch.
  2. Enter a name, select the workspace that owns the channel, and confirm.
  3. Open OAuth & Permissions, scroll to Scopes → Bot Token Scopes, and add chat:write.
  4. Choose Install to Workspace and authorize the app.
  5. Copy the Bot User OAuth Token. It starts with xoxb-; this is the value the connector needs.

The connector authenticates with a bot token. An Incoming Webhook URL does not work: the connector posts through the Slack Web API, so a webhook endpoint copied into the token parameter is refused with an authentication error. Ignore instructions that ask you to enable Incoming Webhooks for this integration.

docs.title: Invite the app to the channel
docs.text: In the target channel, run /invite @<APP_NAME> and select the app you created. Slack requires the app to be a member of the conversation: a post to a channel the app has not joined fails with not_in_channel. As an alternative, request the chat:write.public scope and reinstall the app; that scope covers public channels the app has not joined, but not private channels.

docs.title: Get the channel identifier
docs.text: Open the target channel, open its details, and copy the channel ID. It starts with C for a public channel and G for a private one. A channel name also works, but the ID is the only value that survives a rename, so prefer it.

docs.title: Place the connector on the server
docs.text:
1. Make sure the connector is on the Pandora FMS server, in a directory readable and executable by the user that runs the Pandora FMS server; copy it from its package if it is not. The default command uses /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/.
  2. Install the runtime requirements that the package ships with before the first run. The package includes a requirements file for them.
  3. Make the installed path match the alert command. The shipped command calls /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora-slack-cli, without extension, while the packaged file is named pandora-slack-cli.py. Rename the file to pandora-slack-cli, or edit the command so it names the file you installed.
  4. Repeat the copy on every Pandora FMS server that can process alerts. The command is not internal to the console, so the server that fires the alert is the one that executes it.

docs.title: Edit the shipped alert command
docs.text:
The console already contains the alert command Pandora Slack. Open Alerts → Commands and edit it; if your installation does not have that command, create one with the same command line. In both cases:

  1. Replace the literal TOKEN in the command line with the bot token you copied.
  2. Leave the rest of the command line as it is, or adjust the installation path (previous step).

The shipped command line is:

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora-slack-cli -t "TOKEN" -d "_field1_" -c "_field2_" -e "_field3_" -T "_field4_" -D "_field5_"

The five fields use these descriptions and preset values in the console:

Field Console description Preset value Purpose 1 Data in coma separate keypairs data=_data_ One key=value pair per fact of the message 2 Slack channel id/name empty Channel that receives the alert 3 Title emoji :red_circle:,Red circle;:green_circle:,Green circle Emoji that prefixes the title line; the preset is a two-entry list 4 Title [PANDORA] Alert FIRED on _agent_ / _module_ Bold title line 5 Description _agent_ \| _module_ \| _data_ \| _timestamp_ Italic line under the title

The token is written in the command body, not in a field. This differs from older instructions that place it in the second field: in the shipped command, field 2 is the channel and the token is the literal TOKEN you replace. If you prefer to keep the token out of the command body, replace -t "TOKEN" with a reference to a spare field, describe that field, and tick its Hide box. Hiding a field only masks it in the console; the value is still substituted into the command line when the alert runs.

docs.title: Create or edit the alert action
docs.text:
Open Alerts → Actions and edit the action Pandora Slack, which ships as a default action. Its fields come pre-filled from the command; check three things:

  • Field 2 (channel) is empty: enter the channel ID.
  • The Triggering fields use :red_circle: and the Recovery fields use :green_circle:.
  • Triggering and Recovery have their own title and description, which you can rewrite. Keep the macros: they carry the agent, module, value and timestamp into Slack.

docs.title: Attach the action to what you monitor
docs.text: Create or edit an alert template under Alerts → Templates and add this action to it, then apply the template to the modules or the policy that must notify Slack. See the Pandora FMS manual on alerts for templates, actions and macro substitution.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the connector once by hand on the Pandora FMS server before relying on an alert:

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora-slack-cli \
  -t "<API_TOKEN>" \
  -c "<CHANNEL_ID>" \
  -d "Agent=<AGENT_NAME>,Module=<MODULE_NAME>,Status=Critical,Data=22" \
  -T "Pandora FMS test alert" \
  -D "Manual verification" \
  -F ""

A successful run prints exactly one line on standard output:

> Message sent successfully

and the channel receives one message:

:red_circle: *Pandora FMS test alert*
_Manual verification_

*Agent* : <AGENT_NAME>
*Module* : <MODULE_NAME>
*Status* : Critical
*Data* : 22

Because the example passes -F "", no footer message is posted. Remove that argument and the same run posts a second message containing only PandoraFMS.

Two checks complete the verification:

  1. The connector alone — the manual run above. If it fails here, the console cannot succeed.
  2. The console path — trigger the alert from a module with the action attached, and confirm that the message reaches the channel with the agent, module and value of that alert.

Do not use the exit status to decide whether the delivery worked: the connector exits with status 0 after a Slack error too (see Exit codes). Look at the channel and at the message the connector printed.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. An alert fires or recovers, and Pandora FMS selects the actions of the alert template.
  2. The server substitutes the alert macros in the command fields (_agent_, _module_, _data_, _timestamp_, _field1_…_field5_) and runs the command line of the alert command.
  3. The connector turns -d into the fact lines, joins them with the title, description and emoji, and calls chat.postMessage for that text.
  4. If a footer is configured, it calls chat.postMessage a second time with the footer text alone.
  5. If a module graph was requested, it fetches the image from the Pandora FMS API and tries to upload it to the channel.

The connector keeps no state and has no queue: each run is a synchronous HTTP call from the server that processes the alert. A failed call is reported on the command output and is not retried.

docs.title: Message composition
docs.text:
• The first line is the emoji followed by the title in bold: :red_circle: *<TITLE>*.
  • The second line is the description in italics. An empty description leaves an empty italic line, not no line.
  • Then a blank line and one line per data pair, with the key in bold: *<KEY>* : <VALUE>.
  • Pairs are read from left to right with = as the separator between key and value and , between pairs. A value that contains = breaks the pair: the warning Warning, error parsing keypairs values: too many values to unpack is printed and the pairs after it are dropped.
  • Slack applies its own message formatting and may rewrite parts of the text (links, for example). The connector compares the text Slack returns with the text it sent, so a rewritten message produces a traceback after the message has been delivered (see Troubleshoot).

docs.title: Delivery constraints
docs.text:
• Slack accepts roughly one message per second per channel from an app. With the default footer, every alert consumes two of those slots, and a burst of alerts to one channel can be rate limited.
  • The message is plain text with Slack markup. The connector sends no blocks, attachments or interactive elements.
  • There is no retry and no persistence: if the server cannot reach Slack at that moment, that alert is not delivered.

docs.title: Module graphs are no longer delivered
docs.text:
The graph path exists and is documented for completeness, but it cannot succeed today:

  • The connector requests the graph from the Pandora FMS external API (module_graph), decodes it and writes it to --tmp_dir as graph_<module_id>.<epoch>.png.
  • It then uploads the file with the Slack files.upload method. Slack deprecated that method and stopped it on 12 November 2025, so the upload is refused and the connector prints File Got an error: <error>. The alert text has already been sent at that point.
  • The temp file is removed at the end of the run. Two runs for the same module in the same second share the same file name.

Also note that --api_conf carries the Pandora FMS API password and API pass in the command line, so they are visible in the process list while the alert runs.

docs.title: TLS and proxies
docs.text:
• At startup the connector forces its own CA bundle, so the operating system trust store is not used. A Slack endpoint or an interception proxy with a private certificate fails verification unless the certificate is added to that bundle.
  • The connector has no proxy option. The Slack client reads HTTPS_PROXY, https_proxy, HTTP_PROXY and http_proxy from the environment of the user that runs the command, so set them in the service environment if the server needs a proxy.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The connector reports most failures on standard output and keeps going. Read the message, not the exit status.

Symptom Cause and action Got an Slack auth error: invalid_auth The token is wrong or revoked, or it is not a bot token; an Incoming Webhook URL cannot authenticate this call. Copy the Bot User OAuth Token of the installed app again. Got an Slack auth error: not_in_channel The app is not a member of the channel. Invite it with /invite @<APP_NAME>, or grant chat:write.public. Got an Slack auth error: channel_not_found The channel ID or name is wrong, or the app cannot see a private channel it does not belong to. Got an Slack auth error: missing_scope The app lacks chat:write. Add the scope in OAuth & Permissions and reinstall the app: scopes only take effect after a reinstall. Got an Slack auth error: ratelimited Too many messages to that channel in a short time. Space the alerts or remove the footer message to halve the traffic. File Got an error: <error> (for example method_deprecated) The graph upload uses the Slack method retired on 12 November 2025. Remove --api_conf and --module_graph; the text alert was already delivered. Warning, error parsing keypairs values: … and missing facts A data value contains = or the pair list is malformed. Quote values without =, or restructure the alert command. The channel shows the alert but the run ends with a traceback about assert Slack rewrote the message text, and the connector compares it with what it sent. The delivery succeeded; the failure is cosmetic. bad interpreter: No such file or directory The command calls the packaged file directly and the interpreter declared inside that file is not available on the server. Call the connector through the interpreter installed on the host, or provide the declared name. No such file or directory naming the connector path The installed path and the alert command disagree, usually because of the .py suffix. Rename the file or edit the command. A certificate verification error Private CA or TLS interception: the connector trusts only its own CA bundle (see above). The server log records exceeded the global alert timeout The command did not finish within the configured global alert timeout. Check the server's connectivity to slack.com and Slack's status. Nothing in the channel and nothing printed The action is not attached to the module, the alert is not firing, or the command line never ran. Check the alert history in the console first.

For a failure that leaves no clue, run the command line by hand with the same values the console substitutes and read the output. The connector prints its own diagnostics there.

docs.title: Command-line parameters
docs.text:
Name Required Default Description -d, --data Yes — Facts as key=value pairs separated by commas, for example Agent=<AGENT_NAME>,Module=<MODULE_NAME>,Data=22. Empty is accepted and produces no fact lines. -t, --token Yes — Slack app bot token (xoxb-…). A webhook URL is not valid here. -c, --channel Yes — Channel ID (C…, G…) or channel name. The app must be a member of the channel. -e, --emoji No :red_circle: Emoji that prefixes the title line. Slack emoji markup, for example :warning:. -T, --tittle No PandoraFMS alert Title line, in bold. The long name is --tittle, with the double t. -D, --desc No empty Description line, in italics. Empty leaves an empty italic line. -F, --footer No PandoraFMS Text of a second, separate message. An empty value (-F "") suppresses that message. --api_conf No empty Pandora FMS API details for graph generation: user=…,pass=…,api_pass=…,api_url=…. api_url defaults to http://127.0.0.1/pandora_console/include/api.php. Without user, pass and api_pass, graph generation is skipped. --module_graph No empty Graph request: module_id=…,interval=…. interval defaults to 3600 seconds. Requires --api_conf. --tmp_dir No /tmp Directory where the graph image is written before upload.

With --api_conf, the run prints Api config enable before the message. Argument errors — a missing required option, for example — are reported by the argument parser on standard error and end the run with status 2.

docs.title: Message layout
docs.text: Line Content Source 1 <emoji> *<title>* -e and -T 2 _<description>_ -D 3 empty — 4… *<key>* : <value>, one per pair -d, in the order given Separate message <footer> -F, skipped when empty

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Situation Status Message accepted by Slack 0 Slack API error (invalid_auth, not_in_channel, missing_scope, ratelimited…) 0 — the error is printed and the run ends Graph generation or upload error 0 — the alert text was already sent SIGINT or SIGTERM 0 Slack returns text that differs from the text sent 1 — traceback, after delivery Missing or invalid command-line arguments 2

docs.title: Console objects shipped with the product
docs.text: Object Detail Alert command Pandora Slack, not an internal command, so it runs the executable on the alert server Alert action Pandora Slack, shipped as a default action, with separate triggering and recovery fields Command path expected /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora-slack-cli Packaged file name pandora-slack-cli.py Marketplace entry None — the connector ships with Pandora FMS Published version None — the connector reports no version, so this page documents the behaviour observed on 2026-10-27

docs.title: Slack surface used
docs.text: Slack method Scope Used for Current state chat.postMessage chat:write The alert message and the footer message Available files.upload files:write The module graph image Retired by Slack on 12 November 2025; the upload fails

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: This integration sends Pandora FMS alerts to a Microsoft Teams channel as Adaptive Cards. A Power Automate workflow exposes a webhook for the channel, and the pandora-msteams-workflow CLI, launched from a Pandora FMS alert command, posts the alert data to it. Use it when you want alerts to reach a Teams channel with the agent, module and status rendered as readable fields rather than plain text.

docs.title: MS Teams settings: creating a channel
docs.text:
To integrate MS Teams with Pandora FMS, first go to the group where the alert messages will be sent. Once there, select the Add channel option:

Enter a name, an optional description, and the permissions so that each team member has access to the new channel, then click the Add button.

docs.title: MS Teams settings: creating an authorization URL
docs.text:
Microsoft Teams has replaced the classic "Incoming Webhooks" with Workflows (based on Power Automate). Follow these steps to get your URL directly from a channel:

  1. Select the Channel: Go to the specific team and channel where you want to receive Pandora FMS notifications.

    2. Access Workflows: - Haz clic en los tres puntos (...) junto al nombre del canal. - Selecciona la opción Workflows 3. Create a New Workflow: - Click the + New workflow or Create button. - In the template search box, type: "Send webhook alerts to channel" - Select the template with that exact name.

    ![image.png](../assets/images/integrations/teams/ZmIimage.png)
    1. Configure the Flow:

    2. Select a group and channel to send the message to.

      - Click Save. 5. Get the URL: - Once created, a confirmation screen will appear. - Copy the URL that appears by clicking the Copy webhook link button. This is the URL you should use in the -u or --url parameter of the script. 6. Finish: Everything is now configured; you can return to the chat window.

Note: If you need to retrieve the URL later, you can go to the Workflows app in the Teams sidebar, enter Manage workflows, and edit the corresponding flow.

docs.title: Pandora FMS configuration: creation of an alert command
docs.text:
The zip package where the binary comes also contains a file called test-exec.txt which contains information about additional parameters that will enrich the sent message (subtitle, color, web link button, etc.).

To create an alert command, go to the Pandora FMS Web Console and click on Alerts -> Commands -> Create.

Next, define the eight necessary fields plus the last two parameters which are constants. Make sure that field number two has the Hide box checked and enter the authorization link obtained on the previous page there.

The test-exec file that accompanies the Microsoft Teams connector CLI contains information that you can use to fill in these fields. Click the Create button to save the alert command.

docs.title: Pandora FMS configuration: creating an alert action
docs.text:
Alert actions allow you to define how to launch the command. Go to the Alerts -> Actions -> Create menu.

Select the alert command created on the previous page in Command; the fields will be filled automatically. However, you can always customize the icons or messages for Triggering and Recovery events, for example.

To save, click Create. To apply this action, whether to a Module or Policy, set an alert template for that purpose.

docs.title: Parameters and manual execution
docs.text:
Download the CLI from the Pandora FMS marketplace and unzip it on the Pandora FMS server (the recommended location is /usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora-msteams-workflow or any other where the Pandora FMS server has read and execute permissions).

It is recommended to perform a test in the command terminal with the following format:

docs.title: Script Parameters
docs.text: Parameter (Short) Parameter (Long) Description Required Default Value -u --url Teams Webhook URL. Generated by the Power Automate flow. Yes - -d --data Alert data in key=value format separated by commas. Yes - -t --alert_tittle Main title that will appear on the card. No PandoraFMS alert fired -D --alert_desc Description or additional alert text. No Alert Fired - --image URL of the image to be displayed on the card. No Pandora FMS Logo - --image_size Image size (Small, Medium, Large, Stretch). No Medium - --button URL to which the action button will redirect. No https://pandorafms.com - --button_desc Text that will be displayed inside the button. No Open web console

docs.title: 1. Basic Example
docs.text:
Sending a simple alert with the minimum required data:

./pandora-msteams-workflow \
  --url "https://your-webhook-url" \
  --data "Agent=Server_Web_01,Module=CPU_Load,Status=Critical"

docs.title: 2. Full Example with Customization
docs.text:
Customizing the title, description, button, and image size:

./pandora-msteams-workflow \
  --url "https://your-webhook-url" \
  --data "Hostname=DB-Server-05,IP=10.0.0.50,Error=MySQL service is down" \
  --alert_tittle "CRITICAL: Database Failure" \
  --alert_desc "The database service has stopped responding. Please check immediately." \
  --image "https://img.icons8.com/color/96/error.png" \
  --image_size "Large" \
  --button "https://your-pandora-console.com/index.php?sec=estado&sec2=lista_agentes" \
  --button_desc "Open PandoraFMS Console"

docs.title: Internal Operation of the --data Parameter
docs.text:
The --data parameter processes a text string and converts it into a list of "Facts" within the Teams Adaptive Card.

  • Correct format: Name=Value,OtherName=OtherValue
  • Note: Avoid using commas (,) or equals signs (=) within values, as the script uses them as delimiters.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: This integration delivers Pandora FMS alerts to a Telegram group through a Telegram bot. The console carries built-in Telegram support, so no external CLI is involved: you register a bot, add it to the group that will receive the alerts, store its API token in the console, and create an alert action that posts to the group's chat ID.

docs.title: Telegram settings: bot creation
docs.text:
First, you must create a bot in Telegram®:

  • From your account in Telegram, start a conversation with the user BotFather

  • Once the conversation is initiated, use the /startcommand:

  • Next, enter the /newbot command. You will be prompted to provide a display name for the bot and a username, which must end in “bot”.

Once these steps have been completed, you will be provided with the API key for the bot you created. It is very important to save the API key and remember the bot’s username.

docs.title: Telegram settings: create a group and add the bots
docs.text:
• The next step is to create a group.
  • During the creation of this group, add the bot created in the previous step and assign a name to the group.
  • Once the group has been created, add the bot named “getidsbot” (it is very important to add the correct bot, as there are several bots with similar alias).
  • When the bot is added, it will return the group ID. You must save it in order to complete the configuration in the Pandora console, along with the API key and the username of the bot you created and added earlier.

docs.title: Pandora FMS configuration: bot integration with alerts
docs.text:
To configure the alerts, first enter the API token in the following section:

Management → Settings → System settings → General setup → Alerts configuration → Telegram Configuration → Telegram Token

The field displays the token in plain text; take appropriate precautions to prevent it from being viewed by third parties.

Once finished, click the “Update” button to save the Telegram token in the database.

docs.title: Pandora FMS configuration: creating an alert action
docs.text:
The Telegram® plugin is fully integrated into Pandora FMS 800.

Go to the Management→Alerts→ Actions menu and in Filter select Pandora Telegram in the Command or search field. The alert actions that use the Pandora Telegram command will be displayed:

You may:

  • Use the default action on Pandora FMS.
  • Copy the previous action and customize it as needed. (It may be the case that several groups of agents use different alert actions configured according to each case)
  • Create an action based on the Telegram alert command (read-only).

In any case, the configuration is similar:

  • Indicate and select the name and group.
  • Ensure that Pandora Telegram is selected in Command list.
  • In Chat ID, enter the corresponding identifier.
  • The default Message field for Triggering is [PANDORA] Alert FIRED on _agent_ / _module_ / _timestamp_ / _data_ . See the other macros available to insert more information.
  • The default Message field for Recovery is [PANDORA] Alert RECOVERED on _agent_ / _module_ / _timestamp_ / _data_ . See the other macros available to insert more information.
  • Press the Create button if you are creating an alert action or Update if you are editing to save the parameters.

Click Create. Once you have created this alert action, it can be included in a policy, a template, or Module.

Sometimes it may take a while for a newly created bot to work properly.

docs.title: Pandora Zammad
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Pandora Zammad addon manages tickets in Zammad from the command line. Each run performs one operation against the Zammad REST API: read the ticket list, create a ticket, update a ticket or delete a ticket. It is a standalone command: it creates no agent, generates no Pandora FMS modules and keeps no state between runs.

The addon addresses the Zammad Cloud account of one subdomain. The endpoint is built from the value of -i, which is the subdomain label only:

https://<ZAMMAD_SUBDOMAIN>.zammad.com/api/v1/tickets

put and delete append the ticket ID to that path. Every request and response is JSON over HTTPS.

A successful run prints nothing. The command returns no data to the caller: the only result is the exit status, and a Zammad refusal does not always change it (see Exit status). The effect of the operation is visible only in Zammad.

The addon is not a Pandora FMS server plugin or agent plugin: a run produces no agent XML and no module value, so nothing from it is ingested by Pandora FMS.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.zammad, version 1.0 Documented target The Marketplace package this page describes. See Addon identity Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions HTTPS access from the host that runs the addon to <ZAMMAD_SUBDOMAIN>.zammad.com (TCP 443) Required Every request goes to that address; the addon has no option to change the scheme, the domain or the port A Zammad user or access token allowed to read and write tickets Required The addon authenticates with the credentials it receives and checks no permission itself A Zammad Cloud account addressed as <name>.zammad.com Required The endpoint is always https://<value of -i>.zammad.com Zammad versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon Operating system of the host that runs the addon Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version

Address scope. The URL is fixed to https://<value of -i>.zammad.com/api/v1/tickets, so -i is a subdomain label, not a URL. A self-hosted Zammad served from another domain, over plain HTTP or on a custom port is outside this interface: the addon cannot be pointed at it.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. Network access from the host that runs the addon to https://<ZAMMAD_SUBDOMAIN>.zammad.com on TCP 443.
  2. A Zammad account with API access, and one credential method: an access token, or a user and password when the instance keeps basic authentication enabled.
  3. Ticket permission for that identity. It must be able to read, create, update and delete the tickets you operate on. The addon sends the request and does not inspect the answer.
  4. Values that exist in the instance: the ticket group name, the numeric priority and state IDs, the article type and the customer. The addon does not validate them; Zammad accepts or refuses each request.

docs.title: Zammad access
docs.text:
Zammad supports token authentication and HTTP basic authentication, and either method can be disabled in an instance. The addon implements the two:

  • Access token (-t): sent in the Authorization: Token token=<API_TOKEN> header. Zammad recommends tokens over basic authentication, and the token works with the permissions of the user that created it.
  • User and password (-us and -p): sent as HTTP basic authentication.

Pass exactly one credential method. With both, the addon sends the request twice (see Credentials and transport).

The identity must be allowed to work with tickets in the target group, because the requests carry no other identity.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download pandorafms.zammad.1.0.zip from the Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users, and place the pandora_zammad executable on the host that will run it:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.zammad

The examples in this page run the executable from its own directory as ./pandora_zammad. The addon has no console component: nothing is added to the Pandora FMS console, and the host only has to reach the Zammad API.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
Every run takes the operation, the Zammad subdomain and one credential method as arguments:

./pandora_zammad -m <METHOD> -i <ZAMMAD_SUBDOMAIN> [-t <API_TOKEN> | -us <USERNAME> -p <PASSWORD>]

The addon has no configuration file and reads no environment variable: every value, including the credentials, is a command-line argument. The method is matched ignoring case.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
-m value Request Effect get GET https://<ZAMMAD_SUBDOMAIN>.zammad.com/api/v1/tickets Reads the ticket list. The response is discarded post POST on the same endpoint Creates a ticket with the ticket fields and one article put PUT .../tickets/<TICKET_ID> Sends the same fields to an existing ticket delete DELETE .../tickets/<TICKET_ID> Deletes the ticket

A value other than these four sends no request and exits 0 without output.

docs.title: Create a ticket
docs.text:
./pandora_zammad -m post -i <ZAMMAD_SUBDOMAIN> -t <API_TOKEN> \
    -tn "Printer offline on floor 2" -tg Users -tp 2 -ts 1 \
    -tt note -tsub "Printer offline" \
    -tb "The printer does not answer on the network." \
    -tc <CUSTOMER_EMAIL> -tnote "Created by Pandora FMS"

Every ticket field flag in this command is required in practice: a create or update that omits one does not send a request and stops with an error (see Command-line parameters). The addon does not validate the values; Zammad does.

The same create with basic authentication instead of a token:

./pandora_zammad -m post -i <ZAMMAD_SUBDOMAIN> -us <USERNAME> -p <PASSWORD> \
    -tn "Printer offline on floor 2" -tg Users -tp 2 -ts 1 \
    -tt note -tsub "Printer offline" \
    -tb "The printer does not answer on the network." \
    -tc <CUSTOMER_EMAIL> -tnote "Created by Pandora FMS"

docs.title: Update a ticket
docs.text:
put appends the ticket ID to the endpoint and sends the same body as post:

./pandora_zammad -m put -id <TICKET_ID> -i <ZAMMAD_SUBDOMAIN> -t <API_TOKEN> \
    -tn "Printer offline on floor 2" -tg Users -tp 2 -ts 4 \
    -tt note -tsub "Escalated" \
    -tb "The printer was replaced by the facilities team." \
    -tc <CUSTOMER_EMAIL> -tnote "Updated by Pandora FMS"

docs.title: Delete a ticket
docs.text:
delete needs the ticket ID and one credential method. The ticket field flags are not used by this method:

./pandora_zammad -m delete -id <TICKET_ID> -i <ZAMMAD_SUBDOMAIN> -t <API_TOKEN>

docs.title: Credentials and transport
docs.text:
• The credentials are command-line arguments, so the shell history keeps them and the operating system process list exposes them while the command runs. Use a dedicated Zammad identity, and protect with file permissions any script or cron entry that stores the command.
  • Never pass both -t and -p. The addon runs both authentication branches, so the request is sent twice: a post creates two tickets, and a delete follows the first removal with a second request that fails.
  • The connection is always HTTPS. The addon exposes no TLS option: certificate validation is the client default against the system trust store, and there is no flag to add a CA bundle or to accept an unverified certificate.
  • The token travels in a header, not in the URL, so it does not appear in a captured request line or in the server access log.
  • Each request has no timeout. An endpoint that accepts the connection and never answers keeps the run open (see Operate and troubleshoot).

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
A successful request prints nothing, and the exit status alone does not prove that Zammad accepted the operation. Verify the effect in Zammad.

  1. Check connectivity and authentication with a read:
./pandora_zammad -m get -i <ZAMMAD_SUBDOMAIN> -t <API_TOKEN>
echo "exit=$?"

Expected output: nothing at all, and exit=0. A wrong token, or a token without ticket permission, prints the same nothing and normally exits 0 as well, because the addon parses the body and does not evaluate the HTTP status.

  1. Create a ticket in a test group and confirm it in Zammad:
./pandora_zammad -m post -i <ZAMMAD_SUBDOMAIN> -t <API_TOKEN> \
    -tn "Pandora FMS connectivity test" -tg Users -tp 2 -ts 1 \
    -tt note -tsub "Connectivity test" \
    -tb "Test ticket created to validate the addon." \
    -tc <CUSTOMER_EMAIL> -tnote "Created by Pandora FMS"

Expected: no output, exit 0, and the ticket with its article visible in the Zammad group Users.

  1. Delete the test ticket and confirm that it is gone:
./pandora_zammad -m delete -id <TICKET_ID> -i <ZAMMAD_SUBDOMAIN> -t <API_TOKEN>
  1. Force the error path by omitting a ticket field from a create:
./pandora_zammad -m post -i <ZAMMAD_SUBDOMAIN> -t <API_TOKEN> -tn "Only a title"

The run stops before sending the request, reports the failure on standard error and exits 1.

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
The addon never writes the API response anywhere. A get run reads the ticket list and discards it, so the command cannot list tickets in a terminal; use the Zammad interface or another client for that.

-m value What the run changes in Zammad post A new ticket with the title, group, priority, state, customer and note, and one article with the subject, body and type you passed put The same fields on an existing ticket, plus one article delete The ticket is removed. The ticket field flags are not used get Nothing: the response is discarded

The request body is assembled from the flags in Request body. Flags the method does not use are still accepted and have no effect.

The exit status is not a success report. The addon checks whether the response body is JSON, not whether Zammad accepted the request. A 401, a 403, a 404 or a 422 answered with a JSON body therefore looks like a success: no output, exit 0. Only a body that is not valid JSON, or a transport failure, produces an error.

docs.title: Operate and troubleshoot
docs.text:
Each run is independent: the command sends its request and exits. There is no daemon, no cache and no state to reset, so it can be executed by hand, from cron, or from any Pandora FMS surface that runs an external command.

  • The addon reports a result only through its exit status; the ticket itself is the evidence. When the outcome matters, read the ticket in Zammad after the run.
  • The request has no timeout. Set a maximum execution time at the caller (the timeout of the surface that runs the command, or timeout(1)) so a silent endpoint cannot block the schedule.
  • Because a rejected request exits 0 like an accepted one, a wrapper that must react to failure has to check the ticket in Zammad; the exit status is not enough.
Symptom Cause and fix No output and exit 0 Normal for an accepted request, and also for a rejected one. Confirm the effect in Zammad (see Verify) 0 on standard output followed by Error requesting <Response [404]>, please check conectivity, exit 1 The API answered with a body that is not valid JSON, usually because -i does not match a Zammad Cloud account, or because a proxy returned an error page. Check the subdomain An unhandled error naming a failed request, exit 1 The retry inside the error handler also failed, so the API is unreachable: DNS, TCP 443, TLS or a firewall An unhandled error before any request is sent, exit 1 A ticket field is missing on post or put, or -id is missing on put or delete. Add every value the body needs Two tickets appear, or the operation is applied twice -t and -p were both passed. Pass exactly one credential method No request is sent and the command exits 0 Neither -t nor -p was passed, or -m has a value other than get, post, put and delete A usage error listing the required arguments, exit 2 -m or -i is missing, or a flag is misspelled Zammad rejects the ticket and the command still exits 0 The token or user lacks ticket permission, the token is wrong, or a value does not exist in the instance. The addon does not report the HTTP status The request is rejected when the text contains a double quote or a line break Values are inserted into the body without escaping, so such a value produces an invalid request. Remove the character from the text A run never returns The endpoint accepted the connection and does not answer, and there is no timeout. Interrupt the run and set a timeout at the caller
