docs.text: Property Value Marketplace identifier pandorafms.zammad Name Pandora Zammad Version 1.0 Marketplace last update 2025-06-26 Category Miscellaneous License One; the download is limited to licensed users Downloads 2 Marketplace entry pandorafms.zammad

docs.title: Command-line parameters
docs.text:
./pandora_zammad -m <METHOD> -i <ZAMMAD_SUBDOMAIN> [options]
Option Required Default Description -m, --method Yes — Operation: get, post, put or delete, ignoring case. Another value sends nothing and exits 0 -i, --ip Yes — Zammad Cloud subdomain label, not a URL. The endpoint is https://<value>.zammad.com/api/v1/tickets. The built-in help describes it as a "zendesk subdomain name" -t, --token Conditional — One credential method. Zammad access token, sent as Authorization: Token token=<value> -us, --user Conditional — Required with -p. Zammad user for HTTP basic authentication -p, --password Conditional — Required with -us. Password of that user -id, --idticket Conditional — Required for put and delete. Ticket ID appended to the endpoint -tn, --ticketname Conditional — Required for post and put. Ticket title -tg, --ticketgroup Conditional — Required for post and put. Group name -tp, --ticketpriority Conditional — Required for post and put. Priority ID -ts, --ticketstatus Conditional — Required for post and put. State ID -tt, --tickettype Conditional — Required for post and put. Article type -tsub, --ticketsubject Conditional — Required for post and put. Article subject -tb, --ticketbody Conditional — Required for post and put. Article body -tc, --ticketcustomer Conditional — Required for post and put. Customer, as the email address or the ID that Zammad expects -tnote, --ticketnote Conditional — Required for post and put. Note, sent as a top-level ticket field -h, --help No — Usage summary

The ticket field flags are optional in the command line but required for a create or an update: the body cannot be assembled without them, so the run stops with an error instead of sending a partial request. A put or delete without -id stops the same way.

docs.title: Request body
docs.text:
post and put send one JSON document. The method delete and the method get send no body.

Flag JSON field Notes -tn title -tg group -tp priority_id Sent as a string -ts state_id Sent as a string -tc customer -tnote note Top-level ticket field -tsub article.subject -tb article.body -tt article.type — article.internal Always false; there is no flag for it

The body is sent with Content-Type: application/json. The values are inserted as they arrive, without escaping, so a double quote or a line break inside a ticket field makes the body invalid.

Only the fields in this table are part of the interface: tags, owner, pending time and attachments have no flag and cannot be set from the addon.

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text: Status When 0 The API answered and the body was valid JSON, which includes 4xx responses with a JSON error body. Also the runs that send no request: no credential method, or a -m value other than the four methods 1 The body was not valid JSON: the command prints 0 and an Error requesting ... message. Also an unhandled error before or during the request: a missing ticket field, a missing ticket ID, or a connectivity failure 2 Command-line usage error: missing -m or -i, or an unrecognised flag

docs.title: Pandora Zendesk
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Pandora Zendesk addon operates tickets in a Zendesk Support site from Pandora FMS. One execution performs exactly one operation against the Zendesk API v2 of the site you name: read the ticket list, create a ticket, update a ticket or delete a ticket.

The plugin is a one-shot command. It keeps no state, reads no configuration file, holds no connection between runs and exits after a single API request. Its input is the command line: the operation, the Zendesk subdomain, one credential pair and, for the ticket operations, the ticket fields. Its result is the change made in Zendesk; on success it prints nothing on standard output and it never produces Pandora FMS module data.

Because the addon reports no values, treat it as an action rather than as a collector: it creates, edits or closes a ticket as part of a Pandora FMS workflow, and the ticket itself is where you confirm the outcome. The read operation queries the ticket list but the response is discarded, so the useful surface of this version is the write path.

docs.title: Compatibility and availability
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.zendesk, version 1.0 Documented target Marketplace entry; see Addon identity Zendesk API v2 on https://<ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN>.zendesk.com Required Every request is built against that host; see Operations and endpoints HTTPS access from the host that runs the addon to the Zendesk subdomain port 443 Required The URL scheme is fixed to https and the port is never configurable A Zendesk agent account and API token (or password) authentication Required One credential pair is mandatory in every run A Zendesk role that may list, create, update and delete tickets Required Prerequisite of the operations you run; not a compatibility statement Operating system of the host that runs the addon Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Zendesk plans and editions Not validated No Zendesk plan matrix has been recorded for this addon Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded. The Marketplace states that all its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later

The addon is published in the Pandora FMS Marketplace, with download limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.zendesk

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. A Zendesk Support site with API access enabled for the account, and the subdomain of that site at hand. The subdomain is the part before .zendesk.com: a site at https://example.zendesk.com has the subdomain example.
  2. A dedicated Zendesk agent account allowed to list, create, update and delete the tickets the plugin works with. A dedicated account keeps the Pandora FMS activity identifiable in the ticket history and its token revocable on its own.
  3. One credential pair: the account email plus an API token, or the account email plus its password. See Credentials.
  4. HTTPS egress from the host that runs the addon to the Zendesk subdomain. The plugin offers no proxy, custom certificate authority, timeout or port option, so the connection has to succeed with the default TLS settings of the host.
  5. A Pandora FMS installation where the plugin is registered and executed. See Register the plugin in the console.

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
The plugin accepts two authentication modes and sends the credentials with HTTP basic authentication:

Mode Flags What is sent API token -us <EMAIL> -t <API_TOKEN> User <EMAIL>/token with the token as password Account password -us <EMAIL> -p <PASSWORD> The email and the account password

Use the API token mode. Zendesk issues and revokes tokens per account, so the credential can be rotated without changing the account password, and password authentication has to be enabled separately in Zendesk.

The two modes are not exclusive in the code: pass exactly one of -t and -p. When both are present the plugin sends the request twice, once per mode, so a create produces two tickets and an update is applied twice. When neither is present it sends nothing and exits successfully.

The plugin has no credential file and reads no environment variable, so the credential is always a command-line argument. It is therefore visible in the shell history and in the process list of the host while the run lasts, and there it is stored in the plugin parameters configured in the console. Use a dedicated token, mark the field as a hidden value when it is registered as a server plugin and revoke the token if it is exposed. See Register the plugin in the console.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the package from the Marketplace entry and copy the pandora_zendesk executable to the host that will run it. For a server plugin, the recommended directory is the plugin directory of the Pandora FMS server:

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora_zendesk

Give the file execution permission for the user that runs the Pandora FMS server. The addon needs no companion configuration file: everything it needs arrives on the command line.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text: The addon has two configuration surfaces: the command line, used for a manual run, and the server plugin registration in the console, used to execute it from Pandora FMS. Both pass the same flags; the registration only replaces the values with console macros.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
pandora_zendesk -m <method> -i <ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN> -us <EMAIL> -t <API_TOKEN> [ticket fields]

-m and -i and -us are always mandatory. The remaining flags depend on the operation. Create a ticket:

./pandora_zendesk -m post -i <ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN> -us <EMAIL> -t <API_TOKEN> \
    -tn "Backup failure on the database server" \
    -tb "The scheduled backup did not finish. Check the job log." \
    -ts new -tp urgent -tt incident

Update the ticket with identifier 19:

./pandora_zendesk -m put -i <ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN> -us <EMAIL> -t <API_TOKEN> \
    -id 19 -tn "Backup failure on the database server" \
    -tb "Restarted the backup job." -ts open -tp high -tt incident

Delete the ticket with identifier 4:

./pandora_zendesk -m delete -i <ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN> -us <EMAIL> -t <API_TOKEN> -id 4

Read the first page of tickets:

./pandora_zendesk -m get -i <ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN> -us <EMAIL> -t <API_TOKEN>

Replace 19 and 4 with the identifiers of your own tickets. The get operation prints nothing, whatever the site contains; see Operations.

-i takes the subdomain only, never a URL: a value with https:// or with .zendesk.com produces a hostname that does not exist and the run fails to resolve it.

The ticket fields are inserted verbatim into the JSON document that is sent, so a double quote, a backslash or a line break inside -tn, -tb, -ts, -tp or -tt produces a document Zendesk rejects. Keep the values on one line and without escaping characters, or send the text through the Zendesk interface instead.

For post and put the plugin always sends all five ticket fields. A flag you omit is sent as an empty string, which is not a valid ticket value, so supply every field of the operation: -tn, -tb, -ts, -tp and -tt.

docs.title: Register the plugin in the console
docs.text:
Registering the addon as a server plugin lets Pandora FMS execute it on the server that runs the module, instead of from a terminal.

  1. Open Servers → Plugins and register a new plugin.
  2. Set a name and a description, and keep the plugin type Standard.
  3. In Plugin command, enter the absolute path of the executable on the Pandora FMS server, for example /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora_zendesk.
  4. In Plugin parameters, write the flags with the plugin macros _field1_, _field2_, ... in the place of the values. Keep the operation fixed in the parameters and leave the variable data as macros:
-m post -i _field1_ -us _field2_ -t _field3_ -tn _field4_ -tb _field5_ -ts new -tp _field6_ -tt _field7_
  1. In Macro parameters, describe each field. The example uses these values:
Field Description Example value _field1_ Zendesk subdomain, without scheme and without .zendesk.com example _field2_ Email of the Zendesk account pandora@example.com _field3_ API token of that account; mark Hide value — _field4_ Ticket subject Backup failure _field5_ Ticket comment The scheduled backup did not finish. _field6_ Ticket priority urgent _field7_ Ticket type incident

Register one plugin per operation, or one plugin whose parameters begin with the operation as a macro, because -m and the ticket fields differ between create, update and delete. Update and delete also need -id, which is another macro when the ticket identifier comes from the module.

Once registered, the plugin is available when creating plugin modules. Each module fills the fields with its own values, so the same registration serves several ticket workflows.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the addon manually before wiring it into Pandora FMS. Use a ticket you can delete, and confirm the effect in Zendesk rather than in the command output:

  1. Create a ticket with the post example of Command line and note the exit status:

    ./pandora_zendesk -m post -i <ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN> -us <EMAIL> -t <API_TOKEN> \
    -tn "Pandora FMS connectivity test" \
    -tb "Created by the Pandora FMS Zendesk addon." \
    -ts new -tp normal -tt question
echo $?

  2. The command prints nothing and echo $? reports 0. That pair does not prove that the ticket exists: it is also the output of a rejected request.

  3. Open the ticket list of the site in Zendesk and check the new ticket: its subject, comment, status, priority and type must match the flags.
  4. Delete the test ticket with the delete example and its identifier, and confirm that it no longer appears in the ticket list.

A successful run produces no standard output in any operation:

Situation Standard output Exit status Request accepted by Zendesk empty 0 No -t and no -p empty 0, nothing is sent -m value other than get, post, put or delete empty 0, nothing is sent Zendesk answered an error with a JSON body (wrong credentials, unknown ticket, invalid field value) empty 0 Transport error, or a response body that is not JSON 0 1, with a diagnostic on standard error

The 0 line of the last row is the only output the addon writes on its own. It is not a module value: it is a failure marker. See Operate and troubleshoot.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Method Zendesk request Effect get GET /api/v2/tickets Reads the first page of the ticket list and discards it. Nothing is printed post POST /api/v2/tickets Creates a ticket with the subject, comment, status, priority and type put PUT /api/v2/tickets/<id> Updates those fields of the ticket and adds the comment delete DELETE /api/v2/tickets/<id> Deletes the ticket

The response body is parsed and never printed, in every method. What the plugin leaves behind is the state of the ticket in Zendesk; what it returns to Pandora FMS is an exit status, not data.

get does not paginate: Zendesk returns the first page of the ticket list and offers the following pages in next_page, which the plugin ignores. Since the result is discarded as well, get is only useful to check that the credentials and the site name work at the transport level — and even that only when the run writes something on standard error.

For put, the comment is added, not replaced: each update appends the -tb text to the ticket as a new comment, and the plugin sends no public flag, so Zendesk records it as a public reply to the requester.

docs.title: What Pandora FMS receives
docs.text: A plugin module that executes this addon receives no module data, because the addon emits no XML and no value on standard output. The module records the execution, and the ticket in Zendesk is the result. Do not define thresholds or graphs on this module: there is nothing to measure.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
These are behaviors of this version, not configuration mistakes:

  • Every error is silent unless the connection itself fails. The plugin never checks the HTTP status. A 401 for wrong credentials, a 404 for an unknown ticket identifier and a 422 for an invalid field return a JSON error body that is parsed and discarded, so the run ends with status 0 and no message.
  • Both credentials execute the operation twice. -t and -p are handled as independent branches, so supplying both sends two requests.
  • get produces no output and reads only the first page of tickets.
  • Ticket fields are not escaped. A double quote, a backslash or a line break in a ticket field invalidates the JSON document and Zendesk rejects it, again with no visible message.
  • put and delete need -id. The flag is optional in the argument parser, but without it the URL is built from an empty identifier and the run stops with a TypeError traceback before sending anything.
  • An unsupported -m value does nothing. Any value other than get, post, put or delete, including GET-style mixed case such as Get, exits with status 0 without sending a request. The built-in help describes -m as "get or post", yet put and delete are supported.
  • The diagnostic path repeats the request. When a request raises an exception, the error handler issues the request again to build its message, and in the put and delete branches it uses a different method from the one that failed. The printed diagnostic can therefore describe a second call, and a second post can duplicate a ticket that was already created.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text: Symptom Cause What to do The run prints nothing and returns 0, but the ticket did not change Zendesk rejected the request with a JSON error: credentials, permissions, ticket identifier or field value Check the account, the token, the identifier and the five ticket fields; confirm the effect in Zendesk after every run 0 on standard output and a traceback The request raised an exception, and the retry inside the error handler raised it again Check DNS resolution and HTTPS access to <ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN>.zendesk.com from that host 0 on standard output and Error requesting <Response [<code>]>, please check conectivity The response body was not JSON, so the first attempt failed while parsing; the retry returned a response Read the status code in the message: it is the answer of the retried request TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "NoneType") to str put or delete without -id Add -id with the ticket identifier Two identical tickets after one post Both -t and -p were supplied Keep exactly one credential flag A ticket is created but the comment is empty or the update is rejected A ticket field contains a double quote, a backslash or a line break, or one of the five fields was omitted and sent empty Send all five fields on one line, without escaping characters Name or service not known, or a hostname that contains .zendesk.com twice -i received a URL or a full hostname instead of the subdomain Pass only the subdomain

docs.title: Command-line parameters
docs.text:
The addon has no configuration file and reads no environment variable. Every parameter is a command-line flag, and each flag has a long alias.

Name Alias Required Default Description -m --method Yes — Operation: get, post, put or delete. The value is compared literally, so get, GET, post, POST, put, PUT, delete and DELETE are the accepted spellings. Any other value sends nothing and exits with 0 -i --ip Yes — Subdomain of the Zendesk site, without scheme and without .zendesk.com. Host is built as https://<value>.zendesk.com -us --user Yes — Email of the Zendesk account -t --token One of -t or -p — API token. Sent as the password of the <EMAIL>/token user -p --password One of -t or -p — Account password, sent with the email in HTTP basic authentication -tn --ticketname post and put Empty string Ticket subject -tb --ticketbody post and put Empty string Ticket comment. On put it is added as a new comment -id --idticket put and delete — Identifier of the ticket to update or delete. Omitting it stops the run with a traceback -ts --ticketstatus post and put Empty string Ticket status. The built-in help describes it as "ticket body" -tp --ticketpriority post and put Empty string Ticket priority. The built-in help describes it as "ticket body" -tt --tickettype post and put Empty string Ticket type. The built-in help describes it as "ticket body"

-h and --help print the usage summary and exit with 0.

docs.title: Operations and endpoints
docs.text:
Every request is sent to https://<ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN>.zendesk.com, with the headers Accept: application/json and Content-Type: application/json.

Method Endpoint Body get GET /api/v2/tickets None post POST /api/v2/tickets {"ticket": {"subject", "comment": {"body"}, "status", "priority", "type"}} put PUT /api/v2/tickets/<id> {"ticket": {"subject", "comment": {"body"}, "status", "priority", "type"}} delete DELETE /api/v2/tickets/<id> None

The body is assembled by concatenation, with no escaping of the ticket field values.

docs.title: Ticket values
docs.text:
The plugin does not validate these values; it sends them as received and Zendesk decides whether they are accepted. The values published for this addon are:

Field Flag Accepted values Status -ts new, open, hold, pending, solved, closed Priority -tp urgent, high, normal, low Type -tt problem, incident, question, task

docs.title: Active Directory
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Active Directory addon monitors a Microsoft Active Directory domain from Pandora FMS. Each run reads the forest and the user accounts of the domain, runs the domain diagnostics dcdiag and repadmin, and writes the result as Pandora FMS modules on standard output. The Pandora FMS Windows agent that executes the addon ingests that output, so every run updates the modules of the agent installed on the domain controller.

The addon is an agent plugin: it takes a parameter file as its only argument, runs once, prints one <module> block per result and exits. It creates no agent of its own — the modules belong to the agent that runs it — and it stores no state between runs.

The output covers the state of the user accounts, the accounts that have not been used, the identity of the forest, the services that Active Directory depends on, the availability checks and the results of the domain diagnostics.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions A domain controller as the host that runs the addon Required The addon runs dcdiag and repadmin /showrepl without a target server, so both act on the local computer and on its domain role Windows PowerShell 5.0 or later with the Active Directory module Required The addon reads the forest and the accounts through the module's cmdlets, and this build cannot run on earlier versions of Windows PowerShell dcdiag and repadmin available to the account that runs the addon Required The addon executes both tools on every run A Pandora FMS Windows agent on the same host Required The agent is what ingests the modules the addon prints Windows Server versions, and domain and forest functional levels Not validated No version or functional-level matrix has been recorded Pandora FMS Windows agent versions Not validated No agent version matrix has been recorded for this addon

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. A Windows domain controller that runs the Pandora FMS Windows agent. The addon runs dcdiag and repadmin /showrepl with no target server: they diagnose the local computer and its role in the domain. Run the addon on a domain controller.
  2. Windows PowerShell 5.0 or later, with the Active Directory module and the AD DS command-line tools (dcdiag, repadmin). On a domain controller the role installs all of them. On another Windows host, install the RSAT capability that provides them, for example:
Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name "Rsat.ActiveDirectory.DS-LDS.Tools~~~~0.0.1.0"

Check that the three pieces are actually available before registering the execution:

Get-Command Get-ADForest
dcdiag /?
repadmin /?
  1. An account authorized to read the directory and run the diagnostics. The addon has no credentials of its own: everything runs under the account that starts it — by default, the account of the Pandora FMS agent service. Use that account, or configure the agent to run under a domain account with the rights the diagnostics need. No official source identifies a narrower role set than the diagnostics themselves require.
  2. Pandora FMS to receive the modules, reachable from the agent over its normal Tentacle connection.

Nothing is installed on the other domain controllers, on the member servers or on the workstations of the domain.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the addon from its Marketplace entry, whose download is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms-active_directory

Extract the package and place the active_directory.exe executable together with the adparams.txt parameter file in a folder readable by the account that runs the agent. The examples below use:

%ProgramFiles%\Pandora_Agent\plugins\active-directory\

Pandora FMS can also distribute both files through a collection; see Place the files on the agent host.

docs.title: The parameter file
docs.text:
The addon reads one parameter file, passed as its only command-line argument. The file is plain text with key=value lines, and the shipped adparams.txt is the reference:

user=all
unused=1
spnm=0
upnm=0
tests=1

The file format is strict and silent about mistakes:

  • Write the key and the value without spaces around =. user = all does not match the key and the setting is ignored.
  • Write one line per key: a repeated key is read as a list of values instead of a single value.
  • Only the text between the first = and the next = is used, so a value must not contain =.
  • Comment a line with # at the beginning to disable it. A commented or missing key leaves its block disabled; a missing user key disables the user modules, a missing unused key the unused-account modules, a missing tests key the diagnostic modules.
  • Do not move the file: the addon receives its path, and a wrong path is not reported as a file error (see Nothing appears in the console).

user accepts the literal all — one module per enabled account in the directory — or a single account name, such as a SamAccountName, to report only that account. unused, spnm, upnm and tests are switches: 1 enables the block, 0 or an empty value disables it.

docs.title: Place the files on the agent host
docs.text:
Two options are equivalent once the files are on disk:

Copy the files. Place active_directory.exe and adparams.txt in any folder the agent account can read — the examples use %ProgramFiles%\Pandora_Agent\plugins\active-directory\ — and use that path when registering the execution.

Distribute them with a collection. Create a collection in the Pandora FMS console's Collections section with a short name, upload the executable and the parameter file to it, and assign the collection to the agent. The agent writes the collection files under its installation folder, in a subfolder named after the short name, so the execution points at %ProgramFiles%\Pandora_Agent\collections\<COLLECTION_NAME>\.

docs.title: Register the execution
docs.text:
Pandora FMS runs the addon as an agent plugin: the agent executes the command on its interval and parses the <module> blocks the command prints. Register one execution per domain controller, each one pointing at the executable and at its own parameter file.

In the console, the execution is configured in the agent's plugin list; the same execution appears on the host as a module_plugin entry in pandora_agent.conf:

module_begin
module_plugin "%ProgramFiles%\Pandora_Agent\plugins\active-directory\active_directory.exe" "%ProgramFiles%\Pandora_Agent\plugins\active-directory\adparams.txt"
module_timeout 300
module_end

Replace both paths with the ones in the collection folder when you distributed the files that way.

module_timeout matters here: a run executes a full dcdiag pass, repadmin /showrepl and, with tests=1, a second dcdiag pass with fifteen tests. Set a timeout above the total time of those calls on your domain controller instead of relying on the agent's default.

A module_plugin entry without a surrounding module_begin/module_end block runs on every agent interval, which is interval 300 in the shipped agent configuration. To run the addon less often than the rest of the agent, keep the block and add module_absoluteinterval 1d (or the frequency you need) inside it.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the addon manually on the domain controller, from a PowerShell console, passing the parameter file as its only argument:

& "%ProgramFiles%\Pandora_Agent\plugins\active-directory\active_directory.exe" "%ProgramFiles%\Pandora_Agent\plugins\active-directory\adparams.txt"

A successful run prints the module blocks and exits. An excerpt of the output, reduced to the forest identity, the availability checks and one service:

<module>
<name><![CDATA[AD: Schema Master]]></name>
<type><![CDATA[generic_data_string]]></type>
<data><![CDATA[dc01.example.com]]></data>
<description>Schema Master in Active Directory</description>
</module>
<module>
<name><![CDATA[CONNECTIVITY]]></name>
<type><![CDATA[generic_proc]]></type>
<data><![CDATA[1]]></data>
<description>Active Directory connectivity</description>
</module>
<module>
<name><![CDATA[AD: Service NTDS]]></name>
<type><![CDATA[generic_proc]]></type>
<data><![CDATA[1]]></data>
<description>Active Directory related services status. OK if Running</description>
</module>

Run with no arguments, the executable prints its usage summary — the plugin name, the active_directory.exe [config_file] form and a pointer to the configuration file — and stops without generating modules. There are no options: the first argument is always taken as the configuration file, including -h.

Then check the agent: after the next run, its modules include the ones above plus the per-user, unused-account and diagnostic groups. If the console shows none of them, see Nothing appears in the console.

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
The addon groups its modules by what they describe:

  • User state. With user=all, every enabled account of the directory produces an AD User <account> module whose value is Enabled: <account>. Disabled accounts get no module. With a single account name, one module with that name reports True or False.
  • Unused accounts. With unused=1, one Unused AD User <account> module per account that is not a critical system object and is disabled, has an expired password, has never logged on, or has not logged on for more than 60 days.
  • Forest identity. AD: Schema Master, AD: Root Domain, AD: Forest Domains and AD: Global Catalogs are always produced from the forest. The last two are multi-line values when the forest has several domains or several global catalogs. With spnm=1 and upnm=1 the addon adds a block per SPN and UPN suffix.
  • Services. One AD: Service <service> module per service the addon checks: DNS, DFSR, IsmServ, Kdc, NetLogon and NTDS. The value is 1 while the service is running and 0 otherwise.
  • Availability. CONNECTIVITY and Replication admin accompany the dcdiag and repadmin calls; read the limitation below before using them as a check.
  • Diagnostics. With tests=1, one AD: Test <test> module for each test dcdiag reports as started, except Connectivity. The value is 1 when the test passed and 0 when it ran and failed.

Two behaviours need attention before you rely on these modules. First, CONNECTIVITY and Replication admin report 1 on every run of this version, whatever the diagnostics return; see Known limitation: connectivity and replication always report 1. Second, all SPN suffixes share one module name, and so do all UPN suffixes: the console keeps a single module per name, so read the run output when you need to see each suffix.

docs.title: Execution cost and scheduling
docs.text:
Every run starts two external diagnostics, and with tests=1 a third one. On a healthy domain controller they complete in seconds to minutes depending on the size of the directory and the number of replication partners; set module_timeout accordingly. The addon keeps no state, so a manual run at any time is equivalent to a scheduled one.

With user=all the addon queries every account of the directory individually, so the run time grows with the number of accounts. In a large directory, schedule the addon less often than the agent interval and raise the timeout.

docs.title: Known limitation: connectivity and replication always report 1
docs.text: CONNECTIVITY and Replication admin report 1 on every run of this version: the condition that evaluates the dcdiag and repadmin output is always true, so a failed connectivity test or a broken replication status is not reflected in the module. Treat those two modules as a run marker, not as an availability check, and use the AD: Test <test> modules and the dcdiag and repadmin output for the actual state of the domain.

docs.title: Nothing appears in the console
docs.text:
• Wrong parameter file path. The addon does not report an unreadable file: the keys resolve to empty values, the user, unused-account and diagnostic blocks stay disabled, and the run still prints the forest and service modules. Check the path in the module_plugin line or in the console execution.
  • The execution is not registered on the agent. The addon prints nothing until the agent runs it, and the agent ignores output it cannot parse. Run the command manually first, then check the agent log for the execution.
  • The agent account cannot read the executable or the parameter file. Copy both files to a folder the account can read, or assign the collection to the agent.

docs.title: A service module is missing
docs.text: When a service is not installed on the host, the addon writes an error for it and omits that module — no 0 value is reported. If a service module is missing while you expect the service to exist, run Get-Service <service> on the host: the module follows the presence of the service, not only its state.

docs.title: The parameter file does not take effect
docs.text:
Most configuration problems come from the file syntax: spaces around =, several lines for the same key, or a value that contains =. Rewrite the affected line as key=value and run the addon manually to confirm the new modules appear.

With a single account name in user, the addon writes a literal \n after the <module> and </module> tags of its block, so that block is not clean XML. If the module of a single account does not appear in the console while user=all works, use user=all and filter in the console, or keep a separate parameter file per account and check the run output first.

docs.title: No diagnostic test modules
docs.text:
• With tests empty or 0, the diagnostic block is disabled by design: set tests=1.
  • The addon creates a module only for a test that dcdiag reports as started, and reads the result in English or Spanish. When the operating system or dcdiag runs in another language, no test names are found and no AD: Test <test> modules are produced.
  • Run the same dcdiag command manually (see Diagnostics executed) and read its output: an error about an unknown test, or a test that never starts, ends in a missing module rather than in a 0.

docs.title: Parameter file
docs.text:
Passed as the only command-line argument: the file is required, every key inside it is optional. key=value lines, no spaces around =.

Name Required Default Description user No all in the shipped file all produces one AD User <account> module per enabled account. Any other value is read as a single account name and produces one module with that name. Comment the line to disable the user block. unused No 1 in the shipped file 1 produces one Unused AD User <account> module per unused account. Any other value, or a missing key, disables the block. spnm No 0 in the shipped file 1 produces one AD SPN Suffixes block per SPN suffix of the forest. Any other value disables the block. upnm No 0 in the shipped file 1 produces one AD UPN Suffixes block per UPN suffix of the forest. Any other value disables the block. tests No 1 in the shipped file 1 runs the named dcdiag tests and produces one AD: Test <test> module per started test. Any other value disables the block.

Only the first value segment is read: text after a second = is discarded. A key that appears more than once is read as several values.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
active_directory.exe [config_file]
Condition Behavior No argument Prints the usage summary and stops without generating modules One argument Reads it as the parameter file path Any further argument Ignored An argument starting with -, such as -h Treated as the parameter file path; there is no option parsing The path does not exist The run continues with empty values and prints only the forest, availability and service modules

docs.title: Diagnostics executed
docs.text:
The addon runs these commands on every execution:

Command Purpose When dcdiag Full default test set of the local domain controller Every run repadmin /showrepl Replication status of the local domain controller Every run

With tests=1 it also runs:

dcdiag /test:Advertising /test:FrsEvent /test:DRSRevent /test:SysVolCheck /test:KccEvent /test:KnowsOfRoleHolders /test:MachineAccount /test:NCSecDesc /test:NetLogons /test:ObjectsReplicated /test:Replications /test:RidManager /test:Services /test:Systemlog /test:VerifyReferences
Test reported by dcdiag Module Each started test except Connectivity AD: Test <test>

The addon reads the results in English and Spanish.

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text:
Module name Type Value AD User <account> generic_data_string Enabled: <account> with user=all; True or False for a single account Unused AD User <account> generic_data_string <account> is not beign used (spelled as emitted) AD: Schema Master generic_data_string Schema master of the forest AD: Root Domain generic_data_string Root domain of the forest AD: Forest Domains generic_data_string Domains of the forest, one per line AD: Global Catalogs generic_data_string Global catalog servers of the forest, one per line AD SPN Suffixes generic_data_string One block per SPN suffix, all with this module name AD UPN Suffixes generic_data_string One block per UPN suffix, all with this module name CONNECTIVITY generic_proc 1 on every run of this version Replication admin generic_proc 1 on every run of this version AD: Service <service> generic_proc 1 while the service is running, 0 otherwise; omitted when the service is not installed AD: Test <test> generic_proc 1 when dcdiag reports the test as passed, 0 when it ran and failed

The services checked are DNS, DFSR, IsmServ, Kdc, NetLogon and NTDS.
