The plugin is distributed as the dynamic_snmp script. Upload it to the machine that will run it:

  • Server plugin — /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/.
  • Agent plugin — the plugin directory of the endpoint.

Give the file execution permissions and make sure snmpwalk and snmpget are installed there.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text: The plugin has no configuration file: every option is passed on the command line. Choose the mode according to where the plugin runs.

docs.title: Run as an agent plugin
docs.text: Register the plugin as an agent plugin in the endpoint, with the command and its parameters, and do not use -agent. On every execution the plugin prints the module XML on standard output and the agent stores the modules under its own agent.

docs.title: Register as a server plugin
docs.text:
To let the plugin create and feed a different agent, register it in the console as a server plugin and pass -agent on every execution:

  1. Upload the plugin script to /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/ on the Pandora FMS server.
  2. Go to Servers → Plugins and click Add plugin:

  1. Set a Name, keep Plugin type as Standard, and set Max timeout. SNMP scans can take a while, so a timeout of at least 20 seconds is recommended; the global plugin_timeout of pandora_server.conf may also need to be raised.

Example description:

This plugin generates modules dynamically in the agent it's created in.
Based on the ifName, it generates modules for:
- ifOperStatus
- ifInOctets (ifHCInOctets, if available)
- ifOutOctets (ifHCOutOctets, if available)
The value returned by the module represents the number of modules generated.
  1. Set the Plugin command and the Plugin parameters. Each parameter is written as a macro _fieldX_, where X is the positional number of the parameter:

The _agentname_ and _address_ server macros fill in the agent name and the device address automatically, so the example parameters are:

-agent "_agentname_" -h "_address_" -v "_field1_" -c "_field2_" -only "_field3_" -reject "_field4_" -wmin "_field5_" -wmax "_field6_" -cmin "_field7_" -cmax "_field8_"
  1. Define each macro under Macro parameters, giving a description, a default value and, optionally, a help text:

  1. In the target agent, create a new module and choose Create a new plugin server module:

  1. In the module configuration, select the Dynamic SNMP plugin and fill in the macro fields:

On each execution the server plugin transfers the report using the selected transfer mode and prints the number of generated modules. If the agent named by -agent does not exist, it is created automatically.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually on the host that will execute it. This example scans a device over SNMPv2c in agent plugin mode:

./dynamic_snmp -h "192.168.51.1" -v "2c" -c "mycommunity"

A successful agent-plugin run prints one <module> XML block per generated module on standard output. A successful server-plugin run transfers the report and prints the number of generated modules instead.

The generated modules then appear in the target agent:

With filters and thresholds applied, only the matching interfaces are generated and the thresholds are attached to their modules:

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
The plugin walks the interface name branch first, and for every interface name it queries each configured branch. The module name is the interface name followed by the branch name, separated by an underscore, for example ge-0/0/0_ifHCInOctets or FastEthernet0/0_OperStatus.

  • Interface status. ifOperStatus is generated as a generic_proc module: 1 while the interface is operational. Values greater than 1 are forced to 0 for Pandora FMS compatibility.
  • Traffic. ifHCInOctets, ifHCOutOctets, ifInOctets and ifOutOctets are generated as incremental modules (generic_data_inc).
  • 64-bit counters. When the device answers the walk of the 64-bit counter branch (.1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.6), the plugin uses the HC branches; otherwise it falls back to the 32-bit branches.
  • Automatic typing. For custom branches the plugin detects the module type from the SNMP data type of the returned value; the type is not predefined.
  • Filters. -only keeps only the interfaces whose name matches any of its regular expressions, and -reject drops the interfaces whose name matches any of them.

docs.title: Operate and troubleshoot
docs.text:
• Enable debug output. Add -debug 1 to print diagnostic messages, prefixed with a timestamp, on standard error.
  • No modules are generated. Check connectivity to the device, the SNMP version, the community or SNMPv3 credentials, and that snmpwalk and snmpget are installed and reachable in PATH.
  • Some interfaces are missing. Review the -only and -reject regular expressions; they are matched against the interface name, so a value such as 0/0/5 excludes every interface whose name contains that string.
  • The execution times out. Large interface tables take longer to scan. Raise the module or plugin timeout and keep the interval (-interval) matched to the expected execution time.
  • A server plugin run reports no modules. Verify that the console can receive from the server: the tentacle_client address and port for tentacle mode, or the data_in path for localcopy mode.

docs.title: General parameters
docs.text: Name Required Default Description -agent <name> No — Target agent name. When set, the plugin runs as a server plugin and transfers the report; when omitted, it runs as an agent plugin and prints the modules on standard output -interval <seconds> No 300 Agent interval written in the generated report (server plugin mode). A non-numeric value or 0 falls back to 300 -group <name> No — Module group assigned to every generated module -debug 0\|1 No 0 When 1, prints timestamped diagnostic messages on standard error

docs.title: SNMP parameters
docs.text:
Name Required Default Description -v <version> Yes — SNMP version: 1, 2, 2c or 3 -h <host> Yes — IP address or host name of the device to scan -c <community> For 1, 2 and 2c — SNMP community -p <port> No 161 SNMP port of the device -d <type> No — Data type. The plugin determines each module type automatically, so this value is accepted but not applied

SNMPv3 parameters:

Name Required Default Description -n <context> No — SNMPv3 context -l <level> For 3 — Security level: noAuthNoPriv, authNoPriv or authPriv -u <name> No — SNMPv3 security name (user) -a <protocol> With authNoPriv and authPriv — Authentication protocol, such as MD5 or SHA -A <key> With authNoPriv and authPriv — Authentication key -x <protocol> With authPriv — Privacy protocol, such as DES or AES -X <key> With authPriv — Privacy key

docs.title: Monitoring and filtering parameters
docs.text: Name Required Default Description -o <oid> No .1.3.6.1.2.1 Base OID that the branch subtrees are appended to -names <subtree> No Automatic Subtree under -o used as the source of interface names -branches <name:subtree,...> No Automatic Branches to retrieve, in the form Branch1:SubTree1,Branch2:SubTree2. The subtree is appended to -o -nodefaults 1 No — Disables the default branches, so only -names and -branches are used -only <regex,...> No — Comma-separated list of regular expressions. Only interfaces whose name matches any of them are monitored -reject <regex,...> No — Comma-separated list of regular expressions. Interfaces whose name matches any of them are excluded

docs.title: Threshold and alert parameters
docs.text: Name Required Default Description -wmin <value> No — Minimum warning threshold for the generated modules -wmax <value> No — Maximum warning threshold for the generated modules -cmin <value> No — Minimum critical threshold for the generated modules -cmax <value> No — Maximum critical threshold for the generated modules -string_warning <string> (-wstr) No — String warning threshold for the generated modules -string_critical <string> (-cstr) No — String critical threshold for the generated modules -warning_inverse 0\|1 (-winv) No — Inverts the warning threshold comparison -critical_inverse 0\|1 (-cinv) No — Inverts the critical threshold comparison -alrt <name,...> No — Comma-separated list of alert templates applied to every generated module

docs.title: Data transfer parameters
docs.text:
Used only in server plugin mode.

Name Required Default Description -m <mode> No tentacle Transfer mode: tentacle or localcopy -t_ip <ip> No 127.0.0.1 Target Pandora FMS address for tentacle transfer -t_port <port> No 41121 Tentacle port -t_opts <options> No — Extra tentacle options -t_file_path <path> No /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Destination directory for localcopy transfer

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text:
For every interface and branch, the module name is <ifName>_<branch>. The default branches are:

Module name Meaning Type <ifName>_ifOperStatus Operational status of the interface: 1 when operational, 0 otherwise (values greater than 1 are forced to 0) generic_proc <ifName>_ifHCInOctets Inbound octets, 64-bit counter generic_data_inc <ifName>_ifHCOutOctets Outbound octets, 64-bit counter generic_data_inc <ifName>_ifInOctets Inbound octets, 32-bit counter generic_data_inc <ifName>_ifOutOctets Outbound octets, 32-bit counter generic_data_inc

Custom branches are generated with the same <ifName>_<branch> naming and their type detected from the SNMP data type.

docs.title: Default OID tree
docs.text:
The subtrees below are appended to the base OID (-o, .1.3.6.1.2.1 by default).

Branch 32-bit tree 64-bit tree Interface names (__names__) .2.2.1.2 .31.1.1.1.1 ifInOctets / ifHCInOctets .2.2.1.16 .31.1.1.1.6 ifOutOctets / ifHCOutOctets .2.2.1.10 .31.1.1.1.10 ifOperStatus .2.2.1.8 .2.2.1.8

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Basic SNMPv2c scan in agent plugin mode, with all defaults:

./dynamic_snmp -h "192.168.51.1" -v "2c" -c "mycommunity"

Server plugin mode with inclusion and exclusion filters. Only interfaces whose name contains Ge are monitored, and those containing 0/3 are excluded:

./dynamic_snmp -agent "Test-agentname" -h "192.168.51.1" -v "2c" -c "mycommunity" -only "Ge" -reject "0/3"

The same example over SNMPv3:

./dynamic_snmp -agent "Test-agentname" -h "192.168.51.1" -v "3" \
  -l "authPriv" -u "snmpv3user" -a "SHA" -A "PASSWORD1" -x "AES" -X "PASSWORD2" \
  -only "Ge" -reject "0/3"

Custom branches with the default monitoring disabled:

./dynamic_snmp -agent "Test-agentname" -h "192.168.51.1" -v "2c" -c "mycommunity" \
  -o ".1.3.6.1.2.1" -names ".2.2.1.2" \
  -branches "OperStatus:.2.2.1.8,AdminStatus:.2.2.1.7" -nodefaults 1

Quotes are not mandatory in the examples, but they prevent shell interpretation issues.

docs.title: Exchange
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Exchange addon monitors the health of a Microsoft Exchange Server from Pandora FMS. It runs on the Exchange server itself, under the Pandora FMS agent, as an agent plugin: every run executes Exchange management health checks and prints one XML <module> block per result, and the agent turns those blocks into modules of its own agent.

The checks are grouped in two roles and one optional extra:

  • Mailbox — database replication health, MAPI connectivity and the state of the local database copies of the DAG.
  • Client access — OWA, ActiveSync, web services (EWS), remote PowerShell, POP, IMAP, ECP, Autodiscover, Outlook client connectivity and SMTP connectivity.
  • Server load and storage, reported by every run: the submission queue, processor load, memory usage and one module triple per volume.
  • Exchange services (-services) — one module per installed Exchange service.

One run covers one server. The addon takes no parameter that names a remote Exchange server: it inspects the server where the agent runs it, so install it in the agent of every Exchange server you want to monitor.

The package contains a single entry point. The roles are selected with command-line switches (see Choose what to check), not with one script per role.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions Microsoft Exchange Server 2013, 2016 and 2019 Supported The Marketplace entry states that the plugin is designed to monitor Exchange Server 2013, 2016 and 2019 Microsoft Exchange Server 2016 Tested The addon's official guide names Exchange 2016 as the version it was tested on Microsoft Exchange Server 2010 and earlier Not validated The Marketplace entry scopes the plugin to Exchange 2013 and later Windows Server release that hosts Exchange Not validated No Windows release is recorded for this addon Pandora FMS Windows agent on the Exchange server Required The plugin is an agent plugin: it prints module XML for the agent that runs it powershell.exe available to the account that runs the agent Required The documented invocation calls powershell.exe The Exchange management cmdlets loaded in the session that runs the plugin Required The checks call Exchange management cmdlets and the addon loads none of them itself

The Exchange version is an operational requirement of the addon, not a statement about the Windows release that hosts it.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. Microsoft Exchange Server 2013, 2016 or 2019 installed on the monitored server.
  2. The Pandora FMS agent installed on that server, and running.
  3. An account for the agent that can run the Exchange management cmdlets used by the checks: Test-ReplicationHealth, Test-MAPIConnectivity, Get-MailboxDatabaseCopyStatus, Get-HealthReport and Test-SmtpConnectivity for the health checks, plus Get-Queue and Get-Service for the load and service modules. No official source names a narrower role group for this addon; grant only the permissions those cmdlets require.
  4. Those cmdlets loaded in the PowerShell session that runs the plugin. See Load the Exchange management cmdlets.
  5. powershell.exe in the search path of the account that runs the agent.

The addon stores no credentials and asks for none: every check runs with the identity of the account that runs the agent, so that account needs the access, not a separate monitoring user. Keep it as narrow as the cmdlets allow, and do not run the agent as a domain administrator to make the checks work.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
Download the addon from its Marketplace entry:

pandorafms.exchange

The package contains the plugin script. It has no configuration file: every setting is a command-line switch. Extract the package and copy the script to a folder that the account that runs the agent can read, for example C:\Program Files\pandora_agent\plugins. The commands in this page write that folder as <PATH_TO_PLUGIN> and the script file as <PLUGIN_SCRIPT>, after the name the file has inside the downloaded package.

docs.title: Add the plugin to the agent
docs.text:
The plugin is configured in the agent configuration file (pandora_agent.conf) as one module_plugin line. This line runs every check of the addon on the server that hosts the agent:

module_plugin powershell.exe -PSConsoleFile "<PATH_TO_EXCHANGE_SHELL>\<EXCHANGE_CONSOLE_FILE>" -command "& '<PATH_TO_PLUGIN>\<PLUGIN_SCRIPT>' -all 3> $NULL"
  • <PATH_TO_EXCHANGE_SHELL>\<EXCHANGE_CONSOLE_FILE> is the Exchange shell console file of the installed Exchange version, which loads the management cmdlets in the session (see Load the Exchange management cmdlets).
  • -command "& '...' -all" runs the script with the -all switch. Single quotes protect the path, so a folder name with spaces works unchanged.
  • 3> $NULL discards the warning stream of the session, so only the module XML reaches the agent.
  • The line runs once per agent interval. Restart or reload the agent after editing the file.

When the agent reads its configuration from the console (remote configuration), the module_plugin line belongs to the agent configuration stored there, and a local edit of pandora_agent.conf is overwritten by the agent.

The addon has no timeout of its own. To bound a run, use the block form with a module timeout, in seconds:

module_begin
module_plugin powershell.exe -PSConsoleFile "<PATH_TO_EXCHANGE_SHELL>\<EXCHANGE_CONSOLE_FILE>" -command "& '<PATH_TO_PLUGIN>\<PLUGIN_SCRIPT>' -all 3> $NULL"
module_timeout 300
module_end

A run cut short by the timeout produces fewer modules than a complete one.

docs.title: Choose what to check
docs.text:
The switches are independent flags, and a run without any switch behaves like -all:

Command line What the run covers No switch Mailbox and client access checks -all Mailbox and client access checks -mailbox Mailbox checks -cas Client access checks — read the warning below before using it alone -services Exchange service modules, added to the checks selected by the other switches -mailbox -services Mailbox checks and service modules -cas -services Client access checks and service modules

The load and storage modules — submission queue, processor, memory and volumes — are printed by every run, whatever the switches are.

Run the client access checks together with the mailbox checks. The client access checks ask for the health report of a server identity that the mailbox checks obtain, and a run with -cas alone has no such identity: the health report requests do not produce a result and the OWA, ActiveSync, web services, remote PowerShell, POP, IMAP, ECP, Autodiscover and Outlook modules are not printed. Only SMTP Connectivity, which does not depend on that identity, and the load and storage modules appear. Use -all, or -mailbox -cas, to obtain the complete set. The same thing happens with -all when Test-ReplicationHealth returns no row, because the client access checks reuse the identity of that result.

-services does not narrow the run. The addon treats a run with no -all, -mailbox and -cas switch as -all, and it does not look at -services in that decision, so -services on its own runs every check plus the service modules. There is no way to obtain the service modules alone: use -services together with the role switches you need, accepting that the load and storage modules are printed by every run.

docs.title: Load the Exchange management cmdlets
docs.text:
The checks call Exchange management cmdlets and the addon imports nothing itself. The invocation therefore has to load them in the same PowerShell session before the script runs. Pass the console file of the installed Exchange version with -PSConsoleFile, or load the same module at the beginning of the -command string — shown below as <EXCHANGE_SHELL_LOADER> — and then call the script:

module_plugin powershell.exe -PSConsoleFile "<PATH_TO_EXCHANGE_SHELL>\<EXCHANGE_CONSOLE_FILE>" -command "<EXCHANGE_SHELL_LOADER>; & '<PATH_TO_PLUGIN>\<PLUGIN_SCRIPT>' -all 3> $NULL"

Without those cmdlets every check fails and the run prints only the modules that do not need them — typically nothing at all. See Troubleshoot.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin by hand before wiring it into the agent. Open an Exchange Management Shell on the server, or any PowerShell session where the management cmdlets are loaded, and run:

& '<PATH_TO_PLUGIN>\<PLUGIN_SCRIPT>' -all

A successful run prints one <module> block per result on standard output and nothing else. This is an excerpt of a run against a single server; the values are illustrative and EXCHANGE01 stands for the name of the server:

<module>
<name>Message queue - EXCHANGE01</name>
<type>generic_data</type>
<data><![CDATA[0]]></data>
<description><![CDATA[Number of messages waiting to be processed under MessageCount column.]]></description>
</module>
<module>
<name>Database replication - EXCHANGE01</name>
<type>generic_proc</type>
<data><![CDATA[1]]></data>
<description><![CDATA[Test-ReplicationHealth cmdlet]]></description>
</module>
<module>
<name>DAG Status - EXCHANGE01</name>
<type>generic_proc</type>
<data><![CDATA[1]]></data>
<description><![CDATA[Get-MailboxDatabaseCopyStatus cmdlet]]></description>
</module>
<module>
<name>OWA - EXCHANGE01</name>
<type>generic_proc</type>
<data><![CDATA[1]]></data>
<description><![CDATA[OWA HealthSet .Monitors the overall health of the Outlook Web App service.]]></description>
</module>

Once the module_plugin line is in place and the agent has run it, the modules appear in the console under the agent of the Exchange server:

Check in this order:

  1. The agent modules. The agent that runs the plugin holds a module for every block of the last run.
  2. The values. The generic_proc modules report 1 when the whole check passed. A 0 is an actual failed check, not a missing one.
  3. The coverage. The number of modules of a run depends on the switches and on what the server answered; see Role coverage.

docs.title: Role coverage
docs.text:
Which checks a run performs depends on the switches, and which modules appear depends also on whether each check produced a result:

Module group -all -mailbox -cas -services Load and storage (queue, processor, memory, volumes) Yes Yes Yes Yes Mailbox (replication, MAPI, DAG) Yes Yes No No Client access, health report checks Yes No Only with a server identity No SMTP Connectivity Yes No Yes No Exchange services No No No Yes

-services only adds the service modules to the selected checks: it removes none and changes no other value.

docs.title: How a check reports its result
docs.text:
Every health check follows the same pattern, which is what makes a missing module meaningful:

  • 1 — the cmdlet returned at least one row and every row passed.
  • 0 — the cmdlet returned rows and at least one of them did not pass.
  • No module — the cmdlet returned nothing, or could not run. The run sends no value for that module at all.

A generic_proc module with the value 0 is reported as not normal by the console, so an alert configured on it fires on a check that ran and failed. A check that never runs, or that the server cannot answer, produces silence instead, and the module either does not exist yet or keeps the last value it received.

The value that counts as a pass is part of the addon: Passed or Correcto for the replication check, Success or Correcto for MAPI, and Healthy for the health report checks. See Known limitations.

docs.title: Load and storage modules
docs.text:
These modules describe the server and need no Exchange role:

Module name Type Value Message queue - <host> generic_data Messages waiting in the Submission queue CPU % - <host> generic_data Average processor load percentage Memory % - <host> generic_data Percentage of physical memory in use, rounded to two decimals Capacity(GB) - <host>-<volume> generic_data Total size of the volume, in GB, rounded to two decimals FreeSpace(GB) - <host>-<volume> generic_data Free space of the volume, in GB, rounded to two decimals Free(%) - <host>-<volume> generic_data Free space of the volume, as a percentage rounded to no decimals

<host> is the name of the server that runs the plugin. <volume> is the name of the volume as the operating system reports it, without its trailing backslash: a volume C:\ produces Capacity(GB) - EXCHANGE01-C:. One triple is printed for every volume the server reports, including volumes that have no capacity, such as an optical drive.

The queue, processor and volume modules are printed only when the corresponding query returns data; the memory module is always printed. The processor and the memory queries have no error fallback, so a failure in either of them stops the run: the modules that follow it — the volume triple and the service modules — are not printed in that run.

docs.title: Mailbox checks
docs.text:
Module name Type 1 when Database replication - <server> generic_proc Every row of Test-ReplicationHealth reports a pass MAPI Connectivity generic_proc Every row of Test-MAPIConnectivity reports a pass DAG Status - <host> generic_proc Every local database copy reports a copy queue length below 7

<server> in the replication module is the server reported by the last row of the result, and this module has no fixed suffix: its name depends on that value. MAPI Connectivity carries no server suffix.

The DAG check reads the copies hosted by the server that runs the plugin, and it treats a queue of seven logs or more as a failure. A server with no local database copy prints no DAG module.

docs.title: Client access checks
docs.text:
Each of these modules is the health of one Exchange health set, plus the SMTP probe:

Module name Health set or probe OWA - <host> OWA ActiveSync - <host> ActiveSync Web Services - <host> EWS Remote Powershell - <host> RPS POP - <host> POP IMAP - <host> IMAP ECP - <host> ECP Autodiscover - <host> Autodiscover Outlook - <host> Outlook Outlook client connectivity - <host> Outlook, requested a second time by the same run SMTP Connectivity - <host> Test-SmtpConnectivity

A health set reports 1 when every monitor of the set reports Healthy. The two Outlook modules come from two separate checks that query the same health set, so they normally carry the same value.

docs.title: Service modules
docs.text:
With -services, every installed service whose name contains MSExchange produces one module:

Module name Type Value Service <service name> generic_proc 1 while the service is running, 0 otherwise

The set of modules therefore follows the services installed on the server, and a service that is removed from the server stops producing its module. A service in any state other than running — stopped, starting, stopping — reports 0.

docs.title: Everyday operation
docs.text:
• The addon keeps no state. Each run executes the checks again, so a manual run reproduces exactly what the agent does.
  • A run makes the Exchange server perform live probes: a replication health test, a MAPI logon test, a mailbox database copy query and ten health report requests. Give the module an interval that suits that cost, and avoid running it every minute on a busy server.
  • The modules are created by the agent from the script output, so a check that starts reporting a new module does not require a console change.
  • To change what a run covers, edit the switches of the module_plugin line and restart the agent. Nothing else is stored, so there is no state to migrate.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
These are the behaviors of this version, not setup errors:

  • -cas on its own produces no client access health module. The identity the health report needs comes from the mailbox checks. Run -all instead.
  • -services also enables -all. There is no way to obtain only the service modules.
  • Outlook - <host> and Outlook client connectivity - <host> are the same probe twice. Both read the Outlook health set; the second module has no description.
  • The pass values are matched in English and Spanish only. An Exchange server localized to another language reports its results with other words, and the affected module reports 0 even though the check passed.
  • A volume without capacity still produces a Free(%) module. The addon prints the triple for every volume, so an optical drive or any other volume with no capacity appears with a percentage that has no meaning. Ignore it or filter it in the console.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
• The run prints no health module. Either the Exchange management cmdlets are not loaded in the session, the console file path is wrong or the account cannot use them, or the cmdlets run and return nothing because the account is authenticated against a different organization or the server has no role that answers that check. The load and storage modules still appear, because they do not depend on Exchange cmdlets. Run the script by hand in an Exchange Management Shell to see the error the session produced, and then check the account.
  • -cas produces SMTP Connectivity and nothing else. Expected: see Known limitations.
  • A module reports 0 for every check. Confirm the language of the server before looking for a real failure: the pass values are matched in English and Spanish only.
  • A module is missing after a change. The check returned no result. The console keeps the last value it received for that module, which can hide the gap.
  • The load modules appear but the volume triples and the service modules do not. A processor or memory query failed and ended the run at that point. The error goes to the error stream of the session, so run the script by hand to read it.
  • The agent log shows a timeout. A complete run with -all performs a dozen live probes. Raise the module timeout. Do not split the health checks into a separate -cas line: a line of its own has no server identity and prints no client access health module.

docs.title: Switches
docs.text:
Switch Type Default Effect -all flag On when no role switch is given Mailbox and client access checks -mailbox flag Off Mailbox checks -cas flag Off Client access checks -services flag Off One module per installed Exchange service, added to the selected checks

The addon declares these four switches and no other parameter. It has no verbosity, timeout, destination or credential parameter, and it prints to standard output only.

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text:
Module name Type Group Message queue - <host> generic_data Load CPU % - <host> generic_data Load Memory % - <host> generic_data Load Capacity(GB) - <host>-<volume> generic_data Storage FreeSpace(GB) - <host>-<volume> generic_data Storage Free(%) - <host>-<volume> generic_data Storage Database replication - <server> generic_proc Mailbox MAPI Connectivity generic_proc Mailbox DAG Status - <host> generic_proc Mailbox OWA - <host> generic_proc Client access ActiveSync - <host> generic_proc Client access Web Services - <host> generic_proc Client access Remote Powershell - <host> generic_proc Client access POP - <host> generic_proc Client access IMAP - <host> generic_proc Client access ECP - <host> generic_proc Client access Autodiscover - <host> generic_proc Client access Outlook - <host> generic_proc Client access Outlook client connectivity - <host> generic_proc Client access SMTP Connectivity - <host> generic_proc Client access Service <service name> generic_proc Services

Module names keep the spelling of the addon: Remote Powershell is written with a lower-case s, and MAPI Connectivity carries no server suffix.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
• Every result is one <module> block on standard output, with name, type, data and description. The agent reads them and creates the modules.
  • The errors of the health checks are discarded by the addon: a health check that fails leaves no module and no message. To see the error, run the script by hand in a session that does not redirect the error stream.
  • The addon defines no exit status of its own. A run that stops because of an error prints the modules it produced until that point.

docs.title: Addon identity
docs.text: Property Value Marketplace identifier pandorafms.exchange Name Exchange Version 1.0 — the version of the Marketplace package pandorafms.exchange.1.0.zip Category Miscelaneus Tags applications License Free Marketplace last update 2026-02-05 Availability Free download Marketplace entry pandorafms.exchange Execution model Pandora FMS agent plugin (module_plugin) on the Exchange server

docs.title: Google Drive monitoring plugin
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Google Drive monitoring plugin reports how much of a Google Drive storage quota is in use and, optionally, when one named file was last modified. Each run reads the storage quota of the Google account that authorized the plugin, turns the used share into a percentage and delivers one Pandora FMS agent with that value.

The addon is a server plugin: the Pandora FMS Plugin Server executes it and every run builds the agent document and delivers it to Pandora FMS through Tentacle or into a local data directory. Nothing is installed on the Google side, and the plugin never writes to Google Drive.

What it measures has three consequences worth stating before you configure it:

  • It reports one quota, not a file inventory. The only modules are the percentage of the storage quota in use and, when you name a file, that file's last modification time. The plugin does not list your Drive, does not report per-folder sizes and does not monitor how many files are stored.
  • It is read-only. The authorization it requests is the Google Drive metadata scope, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.metadata.readonly. The plugin reads quota and metadata only: never file contents, and it deletes, moves and uploads nothing.
  • It monitors the account that authorizes it. The quota and the named file belong to the Google account whose authorization is stored on the host, so one plugin configuration covers one Google account.

The run prints a single number, 1 or 0, on standard output. That number is the value a Pandora FMS plugin module receives; the quota and the file date go to the separate agent the plugin creates.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.googledrive, version 1.0 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions. This is a catalogue-wide statement covering the addon, not a test record for it HTTPS access from the host that runs the plugin to the Google Drive API Required Every run calls the Drive v3 API to read the quota and the file metadata A Google Cloud project with the Google Drive API enabled and an OAuth 2.0 desktop client Required The plugin authenticates with the client secret JSON of a desktop-app OAuth client A Google account that can authorize the requested scope Required The quota read and the file lookup run as the authorizing account Rocky Linux and Fedora 34 Known compatible The legacy guide for this addon records both as the systems where it was tested. Not re-validated for version 1.0 Other Linux distributions Not validated No distribution range or version matrix has been recorded for this addon tentacle_client in PATH Required when --transfer_mode is not local Tentacle delivery runs that command; the plugin has no option that changes its name Write access to /tmp Required The generated agent XML is staged in /tmp before delivery; --temporal does not change it Write access to /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Required when --transfer_mode local is used Local delivery moves the document into that directory; --data_dir does not change it A browser session on the host that performs the first authorization Required The authorization opens a local web server and a browser. On a headless host, complete it on a machine with a browser and copy token.json

No compatibility statement establishes a Google Workspace edition, a Drive plan or a Linux distribution other than the record above. Keep each claim at the scope its source proves.

docs.title: Google Cloud requirements
docs.text:
The plugin needs an OAuth client of the desktop app type. Prepare it once for the project that will own the integration:

  1. Open the Google Cloud console and select or create a project.
  2. In APIs & Services → Library, search for Google Drive API and enable it for the project.
  3. In APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen, configure the consent screen and add the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.metadata.readonly, which is the only scope the plugin requests.
  4. In APIs & Services → Credentials, choose Create credentials → OAuth client ID, set the application type to Desktop app and download the JSON file. That file is the input of --creds_json.

While the consent screen is in Testing status, only the Google accounts you add as test users can authorize the client. Add the account you want to monitor, or publish the app, before the first run.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. A Google account to monitor. One plugin configuration reads one account's quota. To monitor several accounts, run the plugin once per account with a different token.json directory and a different --agent_prefix.
  2. The client secret JSON of the desktop OAuth client, readable by the user that runs the plugin.
  3. Pandora FMS with the Plugin Server enabled on the server that will run the plugin.
  4. A delivery target: a Tentacle server reachable at --tentacle_address and --tentacle_port with tentacle_client in PATH, or a writable /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ directory.
  5. Write access to /tmp for the user that runs the Plugin Server, where the agent XML is staged.
  6. A file name, only if you want the last modification module. The file must be visible to the authorized account.

Authorize the plugin with the account whose storage you want to monitor: the quota and the named file are read as that account.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
Download the package from its Marketplace entry, whose download is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.googledrive

Copy the pandora_googledrive executable to the Pandora FMS server and give it execute permission. The recommended directory for server plugins is:

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/

sudo chmod 755 /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora_googledrive

Nothing is installed on Google Drive, and the Google account needs no agent or connector.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
The plugin has no configuration file. It takes every setting from the command line, starting from built-in defaults:

built-in defaults < command-line options

Every option is listed in Command-line parameters. This section explains the decisions that change what the plugin reads and where the result goes.

docs.title: Authorize the account
docs.text:
The plugin authenticates as an OAuth client and stores the authorization it obtains in a file named token.json, in the current working directory of the process. That relative path drives the whole authorization model:

  • When token.json exists in the working directory, the plugin loads it and does not read --creds_json or --creds_base64 at all. Later runs need no credential option.
  • When token.json does not exist, the plugin opens the OAuth flow with the client secret JSON and writes token.json when the flow finishes. Run the plugin from the directory where the authorization must live, and keep that directory for the scheduled runs.

The first authorization is interactive: the plugin starts a local web server on the port set by --port (8080 by default) and opens a browser to complete the Google sign-in. Consequences:

  • The host needs a browser session. On a headless server, authorize on a machine with a browser, in a directory of your choice, and copy the resulting token.json into the working directory of the plugin on the server. The file holds the stored authorization for that OAuth client.
  • Port 8080 must be free on the host that runs the flow. Change it with --port when another service already listens there.
  • token.json must stay readable only by the user that runs the plugin. It contains a refresh token, which is a credential.

--creds_base64 does not authenticate. The plugin decodes the value and writes it as cred.json, but then opens creds.json for the OAuth flow:

  • If creds.json does not exist in the working directory, the run stops with a FileNotFoundError traceback and leaves cred.json behind.
  • If creds.json does exist, that file is used and the decoded value is discarded after a successful run.

Both outcomes are the current behavior, not a configuration mistake. Use --creds_json <PATH_TO_CREDENTIALS_JSON> for the first authorization and token.json afterwards.

When token.json is absent, exactly one credential option must be given:

Options on the command line Result Neither --creds_json nor --creds_base64 The plugin writes a message to --log_file, prints 0 and exits with status 0. No agent is generated Both options Same result: the plugin prints 0 and exits with status 0, and the log says only one may be selected --creds_json only The OAuth flow starts with that client secret JSON

docs.title: Choose the monitored file
docs.text:
--file_name selects one file and is optional. The plugin searches the Drive of the authorized account for an exact name match, including the extension and the letter case, and reads the modification date of the first match it receives. Points to keep in mind:

  • The lookup uses the Drive v3 file search with no shared-drive options, so it resolves files in the account's own Drive. A file that lives only in a shared drive is not found.
  • A file name that contains a single quote cannot be queried, because the name is interpolated into the search expression as it is typed.
  • When the name does not resolve, the plugin prints Error al obtener la fecha de modificación: ... on standard output, generates the agent without the file module, and still prints 1. A missing module is therefore the visible symptom of a wrong name.
  • The module name is built from the text you passed, not from the name Google returns, so the two normally match.

Without --file_name, the run makes only the quota call.

docs.title: Agent and module prefixes
docs.text:
--agent_prefix and --module_prefix both default to an empty string, and they do not behave the same way:

  • --agent_prefix is prepended once to the agent alias, <agent_prefix>GoogleDrive, with no space in between. Pandora FMS identifies the agent by a hash derived from that alias, so the same prefix always updates the same agent and a different prefix creates a second one.
  • --module_prefix is applied twice to every module name, because the prefix is added when the module name is composed and again when the module is built. With no prefix, every module name starts with a space.

The resulting names, for --agent_prefix PROD_ --module_prefix PROD. and the file report.csv:

Element Name Agent alias PROD_GoogleDrive Agent identifier Hash derived from PROD_GoogleDrive (shown by the console, not typed) Quota module PROD.PROD. Google Drive Used File module PROD.PROD. report.csv

With both prefixes left empty, the same names are Google Drive Used and report.csv. Write the combined name in alerts, reports and module filters, and expect the duplication: it is the current behavior, not a rendering artifact.

docs.title: Delivery
docs.text:
The default is Tentacle delivery. --transfer_mode accepts one meaningful value:

Value Behavior tentacle (default) Sends the XML document with tentacle_client to --tentacle_address:--tentacle_port local Moves the XML document into /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Any other value, including a misspelling Also uses Tentacle; the plugin only treats the exact value local as local delivery

--tentacle_address defaults to 127.0.0.1 and --tentacle_port to 41121. Four options are accepted but not used by the delivery: --temporal, --data_dir, --tentacle_client and --tentacle_opts. The document is always staged in /tmp, local delivery always targets /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ and the Tentacle command is always tentacle_client resolved through PATH. Because none of those paths is configurable, the host must provide them: the Tentacle client in PATH, a writable /tmp, and the server's data directory at the default location when local delivery is used.

Tentacle failures are printed on standard error, but they do not change the 1 or 0 the plugin prints. See Output and exit status.

docs.title: Register the plugin in the console
docs.text:
1. Open Servers → Plugins and click Register Plugin.
  2. Set a name, the plugin type Standard, an optional maximum timeout and a description.
  3. In Plugin command, enter the full path to the executable on the Pandora FMS server: /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora_googledrive.
  4. In Plugin parameters, combine the options you need, using the plugin macros _field1_, _field2_, ... as placeholders:
--creds_json _field1_ --agent_prefix _field2_ --interval 300 --transfer_mode tentacle --tentacle_address 127.0.0.1 --tentacle_port 41121
  1. In Macro parameters, describe each field. The example uses these values:
Field Description Example value _field1_ Path to the client secret JSON of the desktop OAuth client, readable by the Plugin Server user <PATH_TO_CREDENTIALS_JSON> _field2_ Prefix for the generated agent alias PROD_

Add --file_name _field3_ and --module_prefix _field4_ only when you need them. Every flag that remains in the parameter string must receive a value: a blank macro leaves the flag without an argument and the plugin stops with an argument-parsing error instead of running. Remove the flag rather than leaving its field empty.

The credential option is only needed while token.json is missing from the working directory of the Plugin Server. Once the authorization exists, the parameter string can drop --creds_json.

After the server plugin is created, open an agent, create a plugin module and select the registered plugin. That module receives the printed 1 or 0. The quota percentage and the file date do not go into that module: they arrive in the separate agent the plugin creates.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• The authorization is the secret. token.json holds a refresh token that grants read-only access to the metadata of the authorized account. Restrict it to the plugin user (chmod 600) and do not copy it into tickets, images or repositories.
  • The client secret JSON is also a secret. It identifies the OAuth client of the project. Keep it readable only by the plugin user and outside any directory served by a web server.
  • Both files are plain text. Their protection is the file system permission model, so keep them owned by the plugin user.
  • The scope is read-only and minimal for this purpose. The plugin requests drive.metadata.readonly, which allows reading metadata but not file contents. It cannot modify the Drive.
  • Do not pass a base64 credential on the command line. The value is the client secret itself: it would appear in the shell history, in the operating system process list and in the plugin parameters stored by the console. That option also does not complete the authorization, as described above.
  • The first authorization opens a browser on the host. Complete it on a trusted machine and copy token.json, rather than exposing an interactive session on a production server.
  • A failed authorization or quota read prints a traceback. Those messages can include the Google API error text. Review them before sharing a manual run.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually from the directory that holds token.json on the Pandora FMS server:

./pandora_googledrive \
  --file_name report.csv \
  --agent_prefix PROD_ \
  --transfer_mode tentacle \
  --tentacle_address <PANDORA_FMS_SERVER> \
  --tentacle_port 41121

A successful run ends with 1 on standard output. The plugin then creates or updates the agent PROD_GoogleDrive, whose quota module reports the current percentage and whose second module reports the file date. With local delivery, check that a .data file has been moved into /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ and that the agent appears after the data server processes it.

The printed value alone is not enough to verify the integration:

  • 1 means the quota call succeeded and the agent document was built. It does not prove delivery: a Tentacle failure is printed on standard error but still leaves 1 on standard output.
  • 0 means no agent was built. The usual cause is a missing token.json with no credential option, or both credential options at once.
  • A traceback with process exit status 1 means the authorization or the quota read failed. The 1/0 value is not printed at all in that case.

Verify the data, not only the output line:

  1. Confirm the agent exists under the alias <agent_prefix>GoogleDrive.
  2. Open its modules and check that the quota percentage is plausible for the account, and that the file module shows an ISO 8601 date.
  3. If the file module is missing while the quota module reports a value, the file name did not resolve. Check the name and the shared-drive limitation above.

Use ./pandora_googledrive -h to print the usage summary in Pandora FMS style. The header reports Version = 1.0, and the summary shows the manual execution form. The form is a schematic template: it never states which of the two credential options to use, and --creds_json/creds_base64 is not a valid flag name. Pass one of the two options, as shown above.

docs.title: Agent
docs.text:
The plugin generates a single agent. Its identity is derived from --agent_prefix, so one prefix maps to one agent:

Attribute Value Alias <agent_prefix>GoogleDrive, with no space before GoogleDrive Identifier Hash derived from the alias Description Empty Interval --interval, 300 seconds by default Group --group, empty by default Operating system fields Empty Parent agent None

Running the plugin twice with the same prefix updates the same agent. Changing the prefix creates a second agent with its own module set, which is how you monitor two Google accounts from the same Pandora FMS installation.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
The plugin always generates the quota module, and the file module only when --file_name is set and the name resolves:

Module name Type Unit Value <module_prefix><module_prefix> Google Drive Used generic_data % Percentage of the storage quota in use, unrounded <module_prefix><module_prefix> <file_name> generic_data_string None Modification time Google returns for the file, as an ISO 8601 UTC string such as 2026-10-24T08:15:00.123Z

The quota module description is Percentage of space used and the file module description is Last change.

The percentage is computed as the used storage divided by the storage limit, multiplied by 100. Google reports both figures for the whole account, so the value describes the account's storage usage against its quota, not the size of one folder or the space taken by Drive files alone.

The file module publishes Google's timestamp string. Pandora FMS stores it as a text value: it is not converted to a Pandora FMS timestamp, so a threshold on that module compares strings. To detect changes, compare consecutive values or use the module history rather than a numeric threshold.

docs.title: Operate and troubleshoot
docs.text:
The plugin keeps no state between runs beyond token.json. Every execution reads the quota anew, so it can be run manually at any time without affecting the Google account.

Schedule the registered plugin module at the interval you want the data refreshed. The generated agent carries its own --interval, which is the interval Pandora FMS assigns to the agent, but its values change only when the plugin module runs. Align both.

docs.title: Output and exit status
docs.text: Result Meaning Standard output 1 The quota was read and the agent document was built. Delivery is not guaranteed Standard output 0 No agent was built: token.json was absent and the credential options were missing or both were given. Process exit status 0 Traceback, process exit status 1 The authorization or the quota read raised an error. The 1/0 value is not printed and --log_file receives nothing from that failure Argument-parsing error on standard error, process exit status 2 A flag has no value, for example a blank macro field Error al obtener la fecha de modificación: ... followed by 1 The named file did not resolve. The agent is delivered without the file module

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text:
• The run prints 0. There is no token.json in the working directory and the credential options are missing or contradictory. Authorize the account, or run the plugin from the directory that holds token.json.
  • The OAuth flow restarts on every run. The token.json written by the first authorization is not in the working directory of the current run. Remember that the file is resolved relative to the process working directory, not to the executable. Point the execution at the right directory, or move the file.
  • The run ends with a FileNotFoundError traceback in the authorization stage. It used --creds_base64 without a creds.json in the working directory. Use --creds_json for the first authorization.
  • The run ends with a TypeError traceback after the authorization. The quota read failed, for example because the quota response does not include a limit, or reports a zero limit. The plugin cannot publish a percentage in that case, and the failure is reported only as that traceback.
  • No browser opens, or the flow waits forever. The host has no browser session, or port 8080 is busy. Authorize on a machine with a browser and copy token.json, or change the port with --port.
  • Google refuses the authorization. The consent screen is in Testing status and the account is not a test user, or the scope was not added to the consent screen. Fix it in the Google Cloud project and authorize again.
  • The run prints 1 but no agent appears. The quota was read but delivery failed. Check that tentacle_client exists in PATH and can reach --tentacle_address:--tentacle_port. The plugin has no option to change the client name. For local delivery, check that /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ exists and is writable.
  • The file module never appears. The name did not resolve: check case, extension, a single quote in the name, or a file that lives only in a shared drive. The quota module keeps reporting.
  • The module names look wrong. The prefix appears twice and the name starts with a space when no prefix is used. That is how this version composes names; use the exact name in alerts and filters.
  • --transfer_mode local does not deliver to another folder. The destination is fixed. Use Tentacle delivery when the Pandora FMS server uses a different data directory.
  • The log file is missing or has an unexpected name. --log_file defaults to /tmp/exchangemail_logfile.txt, a path left over from another addon. Set it explicitly, and note that the log only records the authentication warning and one success line, which reads getting mail data even though this plugin reads Drive metadata.

Starts the interactive authorization when no token.json exists --creds_base64 No — Base64 of the client secret JSON. The decoded content is written as cred.json but the OAuth flow opens creds.json, so this option does not complete the authorization on its own --port No 8080 Local port of the OAuth callback server used during the first authorization --file_name No Empty Exact name of the file whose last modification date is published. The value is not validated before delivery; the help text mentions exchange as default, but the effective default is empty --interval No 300 Interval, in seconds, assigned to the generated agent --temporal No /tmp Accepted and not used: the agent XML is always staged in /tmp --data_dir No /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Accepted and not used: local delivery always targets /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ --transfer_mode No tentacle local moves the XML into the data directory. docs.title: IBM Z Series Mainframe
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Pandora FMS Mainframe monitors IBM Z mainframes running z/OS through the RMF Monitor III Data Portal. The addon has two parts that are installed and configured separately:

  • The Mainframe Server (mf_server), a service installed on a Linux host. It reads the RMF Data Portal over HTTP with basic authentication, turns the answer into Pandora FMS modules and delivers one agent document per mainframe. Nothing is installed on the mainframe and no agent runs on it.
  • The Z/OS console extension, which adds Operation → Z/OS to the Pandora FMS console: a browser of the portal resource tree that generates the definition of the module you pick, a list of the mainframe agents and a module status view.

This is neither an agent plugin nor a server plugin registered per module. The service is a licensed component with its own configuration directory, its own license key, its own schedule and its own delivery path, and a single instance collects for every mainframe you define in its configuration directory.

The addon is distributed through the Pandora FMS Marketplace as pandorafms.mainframe. Its download is limited to licensed users.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.mainframe, version 2.0 Documented target The Marketplace version this page describes. See Addon identity Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions. This is a published statement for the catalogue, not a test record for this addon A Pandora FMS console with the Enterprise extensions directory Required The console extension installs under enterprise/extensions and registers its menu option through the Enterprise extension interface A Pandora FMS license key Required The service logs an invalid-license error and stops when pandora_license does not hold a valid key An operating system named Mainframe in the console Required Agents are published with os_name Mainframe, and both console views select agents by that operating system name The RMF Monitor III Data Portal, reachable over HTTP with basic authentication Required Every dataportal module reads gpm/perform.xml from the portal Network access from the service host to the portal and to the Pandora FMS Tentacle port Required The service collects over HTTP and delivers with the Tentacle client A Linux host with systemd Required The installer writes a systemd unit and enables it RHEL, CentOS, Rocky Linux and AlmaLinux 8, 9 and 10, and Ubuntu 22.04 Not validated The installer recognises these releases and any other distribution prints WARNING: Not supported OS found. No test record exists z/OS versions Not validated The legacy guide states that the addon was tested on z/OS 1.10 and 1.13; no test record supports that claim RMF Data Portal versions Not validated No version matrix is recorded for this addon

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. An IBM Z mainframe with RMF Monitor III active and the RMF Data Portal serving the reports you want to collect. The portal must accept HTTP basic authentication and answer the gpm resources described in Portal requests.
  2. A Linux host with systemd for the service. It can be the Pandora FMS server host or any other host that reaches both the portal and the Tentacle server.
  3. A Pandora FMS console with the Enterprise extensions directory, to install the Z/OS extension and to receive the agent data.
  4. A Pandora FMS license key, configured in the service.
  5. Network access: HTTP to the portal, and the Tentacle port (41121 by default) to the Pandora FMS server, in both directions when you use remote configuration.

docs.title: Install the Mainframe Server
docs.text:
Unpack the package and run the installer as root from the directory it creates:

tar zxf pandorafms_mf_server-<version>.tar.gz
cd mf_server
sudo ./mf_server_installer --install

The installer:

  • copies the mf_server executable and the Tentacle client to /usr/bin;
  • copies mf_server.conf and mf_server.env to /etc/pandora;
  • creates the agent configuration directory /etc/pandora/conf;
  • writes /etc/systemd/system/mf_server.service, reloads the systemd configuration and enables the unit.

It does not start the service, and it does not touch the console. Edit /etc/pandora/mf_server.conf first (Configure), then start it:

sudo systemctl start mf_server

The unit runs the service as root, restarts it if it stops and expects it to detach into the background, so daemon 1 is required.

docs.title: Install the Z/OS console extension
docs.text:
The package ships the console extension in the extensions directory. Copy it into the Enterprise extensions directory of the console:

sudo cp -r ./extensions/* <PANDORA_CONSOLE>/enterprise/extensions/

<PANDORA_CONSOLE> is the console installation directory. After the copy, Operation → Z/OS appears in the console menu; the views it opens require the read-agents privilege (AR).

The extension is not installed by the service installer and is not removed by its uninstaller: it is a console file copy that you manage separately.

docs.title: Create the Mainframe operating system
docs.text: The service publishes every agent with the operating system Mainframe. If the console does not have that operating system, create it in Administration → Setup → OS before starting the service; the Z/OS views select agents by that name, so a missing operating system leaves them empty even when the agents exist.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
Configuration is split between the service and the console:

  • /etc/pandora/mf_server.conf holds the settings shared by every mainframe.
  • /etc/pandora/conf/*.conf holds one file per mainframe: the agent, its portal credentials and its module blocks.
  • The console holds what Pandora FMS does with the modules: thresholds set in a module block, and the remote configuration of each agent.

docs.title: Server configuration file
docs.text:
/etc/pandora/mf_server.conf uses one token value pair per line. Lines starting with # are comments, surplus white space is trimmed, an unknown token is stored without complaint and the last occurrence of a repeated token wins. Paths must be absolute: the service changes to /tmp when it detaches into the background.

This excerpt contains what you normally have to set:

# Pandora FMS license key: the service does not start without it.
pandora_license <PANDORA_LICENSE_KEY>

# Tentacle address of the Pandora FMS server, used to deliver the agents.
server_ip <PANDORA_FMS_SERVER>

# Console group for every mainframe agent (must exist in the console).
group Servers

# Directory scanned for one configuration file per mainframe.
agent_conf_dir /etc/pandora/conf

Every token, its built-in default and the value the shipped file sets are in Server configuration tokens. Restart the service after editing the file; the service does not watch it.

docs.title: Register a mainframe agent
docs.text:
Create one file per mainframe in /etc/pandora/conf. The package ships agent.conf.sample as a starting point:

sudo cp agent.conf.sample /etc/pandora/conf/<MAINFRAME_AGENT_NAME>.conf
sudo chmod 600 /etc/pandora/conf/<MAINFRAME_AGENT_NAME>.conf

agent_name <MAINFRAME_AGENT_NAME>
dataportal_url http://<RMF_DATA_PORTAL_HOST>:8803
dataportal_user <USERNAME>
dataportal_pass <PASSWORD>

module_begin
module_plugin dataportal
module_resource <RESOURCE>
module_metric <METRIC_ID>
module_end

Key points:

  • The file must end in .conf. On start the service renames it to <md5 of the agent name>.conf, which is also the name the remote configuration uses. That md5 name is the file you keep editing afterwards.
  • agent_name, dataportal_url, dataportal_user and dataportal_pass are mandatory in every file, including files that only define storage modules.
  • The service reads the directory only at start. A new file, a new module or an edited file needs sudo systemctl restart mf_server; only changes made through the console remote configuration are picked up while it runs.
  • The agent interval is not per agent: every agent takes agent_interval from the service configuration.

docs.title: Module definitions
docs.text:
A module block starts with module_begin, ends with module_end and holds module_<token> value lines. A block without module_plugin is accepted and never executed, so it is the first thing to check when a module produces no data. The console browser writes the block for you (Build a module with the RMF Data Portal Browser); the full token list is in Module definition tokens.

Only a few tokens have an effect on what Pandora FMS receives: the plugin selector, the resource and metric (or the dataset URL and record length), the collection interval and the four thresholds with their two inverse flags. module_type, module_unit, module_description, module_group and the rest of the module_* tokens are parsed but do not reach the published modules; configure those values in the console instead.

docs.title: Build a module with the RMF Data Portal Browser
docs.text:
The browser walks the portal resource tree and returns a ready-to-paste block for the metric you choose.

  1. Open Operation → Z/OS and the RMF Data Portal Browser tab.
  2. Fill in the portal address, the user, the password and the depth, and click Browse. An address without a port gets :8803.
  3. The tree starts at the portal root: the first level is a sysplex, the second the MVS images, then the I/O subsystems and processors.
  4. Click the eye icon of a resource to list its metrics.

  5. Click a metric to open a dialog with its module block:

    module_begin
module_plugin dataportal
module_description <DESCRIPTION FROM THE PORTAL>
module_type generic_data
module_resource <RESOURCE>
module_metric <METRIC_ID>
module_end

  6. Copy the block into the agent configuration: either the agent file on disk and a restart, or the agent remote configuration in the console (Operation → Z/OS → Mainframes, edit icon), which the running service applies by itself.

The browser does not store the portal credentials: they are typed again on every visit, and they travel from the browser to the console in each request.

docs.title: Storage modules
docs.text:
The storage plugin reads a dataset over FTP(S) instead of the HTTP portal, converts it from EBCDIC and publishes four modules per storage group found in it. The dataset is fetched from module_url; the RMF portal is not involved in that request:

module_begin
module_plugin storage
module_url ftp://<FTP_HOST>/<DATASET>
module_lrecl 80
module_end

Each record of the dataset must contain, in this order, P= followed by the storage group, Es= followed by the capacity, Libre= followed by the free percentage and T= followed by the description. module_lrecl is the record length and defaults to 80.

The storage_sms plugin reads a dataset with the SMS totals and publishes nine fixed modules. Each total must appear as Gb. followed by the label — Usado SMS, Reservado SMS, Usado No SMS or Reservado No SMS — one or more non-digit characters and the numeric value:

module_begin
module_plugin storage_sms
module_url ftp://<FTP_HOST>/<DATASET>
module_lrecl 80
module_end

The labels are literal: a dataset in another language produces no match, and the nine modules are then published with 0.

docs.title: Delivery to Pandora FMS
docs.text:
The service delivers every document through the Tentacle client, or copies it to a local data directory:

transfer_mode What the service does Settings that matter tentacle (default) Runs tentacle_client against server_ip:server_port tentacle_client, server_ip, server_port, optional server_opts local Copies the document to server_path server_path, which must be writable

Any other value is not supported and the document is not delivered. With xml_buffer 1 a document that could not be delivered stays in temporal and is retried on every pass, until the free space of that directory falls below temporal_min_size bytes.

docs.title: License
docs.text:
The service requires a Pandora FMS license key in pandora_license:

  • Without a key, or with a key that fails validation, the log reports Invalid license and the service exits.
  • The key's limit is enforced against the number of agents in agent_conf_dir, or against the number of module blocks, depending on the license mode. Above the limit the service exits; an expired client license only logs a warning, while an expired trial license stops it.
  • The service reports the license holder on start (Licensed to: ...) and always logs Remote configuration enabled., whatever remote_config says.

docs.title: Credentials and transport
docs.text:
• The portal password is stored in clear text in the agent file. Keep the file readable only by root (chmod 600), together with the license key in mf_server.conf.
  • The portal credentials travel in the Authorization header of every HTTP request. With an http:// portal they are not encrypted, so keep the portal on a trusted network or publish it through TLS and use an https:// dataportal_url.
  • The console browser disables TLS certificate verification. Do not expose the console over plain HTTP or to untrusted networks, because the portal user and password pass through it on every browse.
  • Use a dedicated portal user with read access only. No official source identifies a narrower role for the RMF Data Portal, and the addon performs no write operation against it.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
1. The service is running. systemctl status mf_server reports the unit as active. If it is not, read the log: the unit restarts the service, so a failure repeats every few seconds.

  2. The log shows a full start. /var/log/mf_server.log is rewritten on every start. A successful start contains these messages in order:

    • Configuration file loaded.
    • Reading agent configuration directory.
    • one Loading file <name>.conf. per agent file
    • Valid enterprise license found. and Licensed to: <holder>
    • modules: <n> Threads: <t> modules per thread: <m>
    • one Launched thread <id>. per thread
    • Waiting for data...

    With no agent file the module count is 0: the service runs and delivers no agent data.

  3. The mainframe appears in the console. Operation → Z/OS → Mainframes lists one row per agent, with the Mainframe operating system icon and a recent last contact. The agent also appears in the regular agent list.

  4. The modules carry data. Operation → Z/OS → Metrics shows the modules of every mainframe agent with their status, data and timestamp. The Monitor status filter starts at Not init, so set it to All to see modules that are already receiving data.

  5. The portal answers. From the service host, repeat one of the requests the service makes, with the same credentials, and check that the XML comes back. The service wraps the resource in double quotes, as in the example:

    curl -s -u <USERNAME>:<PASSWORD> \
  'http://<RMF_DATA_PORTAL_HOST>:8803/gpm/perform.xml?resource="<RESOURCE>"&id=<METRIC_ID>'

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
Each mainframe becomes one top-level agent in the group taken from the server configuration, with the operating system Mainframe and the interval of agent_interval. Every collection cycle produces one agent document per module block: the service reads the report, converts each row or total into a module and delivers the document. Nothing accumulates locally beyond the retry buffer.

Dataportal modules. Each row of the report becomes a module. The name concatenates the resource, a space, the metric identifier and the metric or row description, with no separator between the last two, so names look technical rather than descriptive. The type is always generic_data and the description is the one the portal publishes for that metric or row; the thresholds of the block are copied to every module it generates. A report without rows produces a document without modules: the agent keeps its last contact, but nothing new is published. The agent description is replaced by the description of the metric on every cycle.

Storage modules. Four modules per storage group, in GB, with the thresholds of the block only on STORGRP % free <group>.

SMS modules. Nine fixed totals in GB, all of them with the thresholds of the block. The addon maps the dataset labels literally: Used is the Usado amount, Free is the Reservado amount and Available is their sum. A value named Free therefore holds reserved space, not free space.

Failure behaviour. When the portal does not answer or answers with an error, the log receives the response body and the cycle publishes no modules for that block. The service then retries on the next scheduled run; no state is kept.

docs.title: Service control
docs.text:
sudo systemctl start mf_server
sudo systemctl status mf_server
sudo systemctl stop mf_server
sudo systemctl restart mf_server
tail -f /var/log/mf_server.log

The log file is truncated on every start, so a restart erases the previous run. Copy it before restarting if you need the history.

The uninstaller removes the unit, the executables, /etc/pandora/mf_server.conf, /etc/pandora/mf_server.env and the whole directory /etc/pandora/conf. On a host that also runs other Pandora FMS components, back that directory up before running mf_server_installer --uninstall.

docs.title: Run in the foreground
docs.text:
Set daemon 0 in the service configuration and run it as root:

sudo /usr/bin/mf_server /etc/pandora/mf_server.conf

The service still writes to log_file, not to standard output, and it does not detach, so the process stays in the terminal until you interrupt it. Remember to restore daemon 1 before starting the systemd unit again: the unit expects the service to detach.

With no argument, or with more than one, the service prints a usage summary and exits. That summary still lists -r and -m; neither option is accepted, and the RMF Data Portal Browser in the console replaces both.

docs.title: Known limitations of this version
docs.text:
• Every module is numeric. The published type is generic_data for all modules, whatever module_type says, so a report that returns text (partition names, status text) cannot become a usable module value.
  • Most module_* tokens do not reach the console: module_type, module_unit, module_description, module_group, module_tags, module_disabled, module_quiet, string thresholds, instructions and the flap-detection tokens are parsed and ignored. A block sent with module_group arrives with an empty group. Configure these values in the console.
  • timeout in mf_server.conf is inert. The HTTP timeout of the portal requests is the agent token timeout (5 seconds by default) and the FTP timeout is ftp_timeout.
  • secondary_mode and secondary_server_ip are inert. They only add a line to the log; no secondary delivery is implemented.
  • The service's own remote configuration does not apply. Only agent configuration files are exchanged with the console; mf_server.conf is always the file on disk.
  • The license tolerance is not applied to the number of agents. In agent mode the service stops as soon as the agent count exceeds the key limit; the ten per cent margin the code computes is never used and the warning line is unreachable. In module mode the margin is applied and the warning appears between the limit and the margin.
  • With xml_buffer 1 the service scans the whole temporal directory and sends and deletes every *.data file it finds there, not only its own. Keep temporal private: the shipped value of temporal is /tmp and the shipped value of xml_buffer is 0.
  • The SMS dataset labels are Spanish (Usado, Reservado). Any other language yields nine zero values without an error.
  • The default portal port is only applied by the browser. The service uses the scheme default when dataportal_url has no port, so write :8803 explicitly.
  • The browser's agent selector uses a fixed operating system identifier while the tables filter by the operating system name Mainframe. When the console assigns a different identifier, the Agent name selector can list no agents while the table still shows them.
  • The Metrics tab starts filtered by Not init, so a healthy agent shows no rows until you change Monitor status to All.
  • --destdir does not relocate the systemd unit, which is always written to /etc/systemd/system.
  • The systemd unit declares PIDFile=/var/run/mf_server.pid, but the service never creates that file. When systemctl status does not show the process, look for it with ps. The uninstaller removes the path anyway.

docs.text: Symptom Cause and check The service does not start and the log ends with Invalid license pandora_license is empty or invalid. Only scheme, host and port are used: the service always requests <scheme>://<host>:<port>/gpm/..., so a path is discarded and the port must be written explicitly dataportal_user Yes — Basic authentication user for the portal dataportal_pass Yes — Password for that user. Change it only together with the console views os_version No empty Agent operating system version include <file> No — Merges agent tokens from another file. docs.title: Module definition tokens
docs.text:
A block is delimited by module_begin and module_end. Only these tokens change what the service collects or publishes:

Token Applies to Description module_plugin All dataportal, storage or storage_sms. Without it the block is loaded and never executed module_resource dataportal Resource label, as returned by the portal module_metric dataportal Metric identifier, as returned by the portal module_url storage, storage_sms ftp:// or ftps:// URL of the dataset module_lrecl storage, storage_sms Record length of the dataset. Storage blocks publish four generic_data modules per storage group found in the dataset:

The only storage module that carries the block thresholds STORGRP %used <group> none 100 minus the Libre= value Free Space (DASD) - <group> GB Capacity multiplied by the free percentage divided by 100
