docs.title: Pandora InfluxDB
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Pandora InfluxDB plugin collects the internal statistics of an InfluxDB instance and publishes them as Pandora FMS modules. Each run connects to the InfluxDB HTTP API, executes the InfluxQL statement SHOW STATS once, and turns the runtime, queryExecutor, httpd, write, subscriber and cq sections of the response into modules. Nothing is installed on the InfluxDB server, and the plugin keeps no state between runs: every execution reports the counters of that moment.

The plugin supports two execution models:

  • Server plugin mode (default): each run builds an agent document and writes it into the Pandora FMS data directory, where the server ingests it. The statistics are split into five agents named after the InfluxDB section they come from.
  • Agent plugin mode (requires --as_agent_plugin 1): each run prints the modules as XML on standard output, and the Pandora FMS agent that runs the plugin stores them under its own agent.

All generated modules are of type generic_data.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.influxdb, version 1.0 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions. It is a general compatibility statement covering the plugin, not a test record for it An InfluxDB endpoint that accepts a user and a password and answers SHOW STATS Required The plugin exposes --user and --password and executes that statement; it has no token authentication option InfluxDB server versions Not validated No InfluxDB version matrix has been recorded for this addon Operating system of the host that runs the plugin Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Network access from that host to the InfluxDB HTTP API Required The plugin connects to the host and port you configure

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. An InfluxDB instance reachable over TCP from the host that will run the plugin, with its HTTP API listening on the configured port (8086 by default), and able to answer SHOW STATS.
  2. Credentials for that instance when it requires authentication: a user and a password. The plugin authenticates only when both are supplied.
  3. Pandora FMS:
    • In server plugin mode, the Pandora FMS plugin server to run the registered plugin, and a data directory processed by the data server.
    • In agent plugin mode, an agent that runs the plugin and ingests its output.
  4. The addon package installed in Pandora FMS through the console.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.influxdb

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, the plugin is registered with its parameters and becomes available in the plugin list.

The contents of the distributed package could not be inspected for this page, so no build or dependency-installation procedure is prescribed here. Use the executable that the package installs and that the plugin definition shows.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text: The plugin has no configuration file: every setting is a command-line option, documented in Command-line parameters. Choose the execution model first; the connection options are the same in both.

docs.title: Server plugin mode
docs.text:
Server plugin mode is the default: it applies unless --as_agent_plugin is 1. Each run writes one agent document per statistics section into --data_dir:

--host <INFLUXDB_URL> --port 8086 --user <USERNAME> --password <PASSWORD> --group <GROUP_ID> --data_dir /var/spool/pandora/data_in
  • --host takes the host name or IP address of the InfluxDB instance, without the scheme and without the port. Pass the port in --port.
  • --group sets the Pandora FMS group written into the five generated agent documents. Its default value is the literal genieacs, which is not a group identifier, so pass the numeric ID of an existing group. Without it, the generated documents carry that literal value in their group field.
  • --data_dir defaults to /var/spool/pandora/data_in/, the data directory of a Pandora FMS server. It must exist and be writable by the user that runs the plugin.
  • The five agents are named InfluxDB_Runtime, InfluxDB_queryExecutor, InfluxDB_Httpd, InfluxDB_Write and InfluxDB_Subscriber_cq. The plugin offers no option to rename them or to change their interval.

docs.title: Agent plugin mode
docs.text:
Agent plugin mode requires --as_agent_plugin 1. The run prints the modules as XML on standard output instead of writing agent documents:

--host <INFLUXDB_URL> --port 8086 --user <USERNAME> --password <PASSWORD> --as_agent_plugin 1

In this mode --group and --data_dir are ignored: the modules are stored under the agent that runs the plugin, not under the five section agents.

docs.title: Credentials and transport
docs.text:
• Authentication is enabled only when both --user and --password are set. With only one of them the plugin connects without credentials, and an instance that requires authentication rejects the request.
  • The plugin talks to the InfluxDB HTTP API without TLS: it exposes no option to enable it or to verify a certificate. The credentials and the statistics travel unencrypted, so keep the API on a trusted network segment or protect the path with a tunnel.
  • The password is passed as a command-line option. It can appear in the shell history of a manual run and in the process list while the plugin executes, including runs started by Pandora FMS. Restrict access to the host that runs the plugin and rotate the credential if it is exposed.

docs.title: Register the plugin in the console
docs.text:
1. Install the package (see Install the addon).
  2. Create a plugin module in an agent and select Pandora InfluxDB.
  3. Fill the host, port and credential parameters the package exposes, and keep 8086 when the HTTP API listens on its default port.
  4. In server plugin mode, also set the group and the data directory when they differ from the defaults.

In server plugin mode the module only triggers the run: the statistics appear in the five InfluxDB_* agents, not in the agent that owns the module. In agent plugin mode the modules appear under the agent that executes the plugin.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the installed plugin executable on the host that will execute it, in server plugin mode and with a test data directory, so the output can be inspected without feeding the Pandora FMS server:

<PLUGIN_EXECUTABLE> --host <INFLUXDB_URL> --port 8086 --user <USERNAME> --password <PASSWORD> --group <GROUP_ID> --data_dir /tmp/influxdb-check

Create the directory first: the plugin does not create it, and a failed write is silent. A successful run prints 1 as its last line and writes one agent document per statistics section:

InfluxDB_Runtime.<EPOCH>.data
InfluxDB_queryExecutor.<EPOCH>.data
InfluxDB_Httpd.<EPOCH>.data
InfluxDB_Write.<EPOCH>.data
InfluxDB_Subscriber_cq.<EPOCH>.data

<EPOCH> is the time of the run in seconds. Each file is an agent document with its modules:

<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<agent_data agent_name='InfluxDB_Runtime' agent_alias='InfluxDB_Runtime' parent_agent_name='' description='InfluxDB_Runtime' version='' os_name='' os_version='' timestamp='2026/10/26 10:00:00' address='127.0.0.1' group='10' interval=''>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[Alloc]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[4194304]]></data>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[Frees]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[1024]]></data>
</module>
</agent_data>

This is an excerpt with illustrative values; the real counters depend on the instance. In agent plugin mode the same connection prints <module> blocks on standard output, with no <agent_data> envelope:

<PLUGIN_EXECUTABLE> --host <INFLUXDB_URL> --port 8086 --user <USERNAME> --password <PASSWORD> --as_agent_plugin 1

<module>
    <name><![CDATA[Alloc]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[4194304]]></data>
</module>

The final 1 is printed after the module blocks. --help prints the option list and exits without collecting anything.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
In server plugin mode the plugin writes five agents, one per group of statistics:

Agent Statistics section Modules InfluxDB_Runtime runtime 15 InfluxDB_queryExecutor queryExecutor 5 InfluxDB_Httpd httpd 24 InfluxDB_Write write 9 InfluxDB_Subscriber_cq subscriber and cq 5 Agent property Value Name, alias and description The fixed section name, for example InfluxDB_Runtime Address 127.0.0.1 Group The value of --group Interval Not set by the plugin Module type generic_data for every module

docs.title: How to read the modules
docs.text:
The plugin publishes the counters exactly as SHOW STATS returns them. It does not compute rates, deltas or thresholds.

  • runtime reports memory allocation and runtime counters of the InfluxDB process.
  • queryExecutor counts the query workload.
  • httpd counts the requests handled by the HTTP API, including Flux, Prometheus and write requests.
  • write counts the write path.
  • subscriber counts subscriber writes, and cq counts continuous-query executions.

Fields whose name ends in Ns are nanoseconds and fields whose name ends in Bytes are bytes. The *Req fields are request counts.

In agent plugin mode the section grouping is lost: every module is stored under the agent that runs the plugin, and the five section agents are not created. Two module names then describe two different sections, because req appears in httpd and in write, and recoveredPanics in queryExecutor and in httpd. In server plugin mode the subscriber and cq counters are delivered together in a single InfluxDB_Subscriber_cq document.

A statistics section that returns more than one row produces the same module names once per row.

docs.title: Operation
docs.text:
• The plugin is a single collection run: it queries InfluxDB, delivers the result and exits. It keeps no state and can be executed manually at any time.
  • Schedule it from Pandora FMS (server plugin schedule) or with cron. There is no interval option: the generated agent documents carry no interval, so the execution frequency is the one you configure in the scheduler.
  • The agent document of each section is written as <agent_name>.<EPOCH>.data. An existing file is not overwritten and the write is skipped without an error, so do not run the same configuration more than once per second.
  • Use a dedicated --data_dir while testing, as shown in Verify, to inspect the documents before they reach the Pandora FMS server.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• The plugin prints its usage summary and exits with status 2 — --host is missing. It is the only mandatory option.
  • The run stops with an error from the InfluxDB client and a non-zero exit status — the request failed. Check that --host has no scheme or port, that --port matches the HTTP API, that both --user and --password are set when the instance requires authentication, and that the instance answers SHOW STATS.
  • Authentication fails although a user is configured — only one of --user and --password was supplied, so the plugin connected without credentials. Set both.
  • The run fails with a value error on --as_agent_plugin — the option expects an integer. Use 1 for agent plugin mode and 0, or nothing, for server plugin mode.
  • The run prints 1 but no agent appears in Pandora FMS — in server mode the documents were written to a directory that the server does not process, or the directory does not exist. Check --data_dir and its permissions.
  • No module XML is printed in agent plugin mode — the agent must ingest the output of the plugin execution. Check that the plugin runs under the agent and that the output starts with the <module> blocks.
  • A section is missing from the output — the run stops when the SHOW STATS response does not contain a section the plugin expects, so the sections after it are not published. Compare the output with a direct SHOW STATS query on the instance.
  • Repeated module names — the section returned several rows. See How to read the modules.

docs.title: Inventory plugin for MAC
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Inventory plugin for MAC collects hardware and software inventory from a macOS endpoint and publishes it to Pandora FMS. Each execution reads the processor model, the memory, the disk partitions, the network hardware ports and the contents of /Applications, and prints the result as an inventory document on standard output.

The addon has a single execution model: agent plugin. It takes no arguments and reads no configuration file. The Pandora FMS agent runs it from its configuration file on every agent execution and forwards the inventory document to Pandora FMS, where the data appears in the inventory view of the agent.

The addon produces inventory data only. It creates no monitoring modules, so it adds no graphs, thresholds or alerts.

docs.title: Compatibility and availability
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.mac_inventory, version 1.0 Documented target Version of the Marketplace entry. See Addon identity A macOS endpoint Required The addon reads macOS system utilities that exist only on macOS The Pandora FMS agent for macOS, able to run module_plugin entries and forward inventory data Required The addon is started from the agent configuration file A perl interpreter for the user that runs the agent Required The agent starts the addon through perl (see Add the plugin to the agent) The macOS utilities sysctl, system_profiler, top, diskutil, networksetup and ls Required Commands listed in Generated inventory modules macOS 10.13 High Sierra Not validated No reproducible record exists for this addon macOS 10.14 Mojave Not validated No reproducible record exists for this addon Any other macOS release Not validated No version matrix is recorded for this addon Pandora FMS release Not validated No release-specific record exists. The Marketplace states that its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later

The guide this page replaces lists macOS High Sierra and macOS Mojave, with Pandora FMS agent version 755, as the tested environment. That record cannot be reproduced from the addon and is not presented here as a validated compatibility statement: the macOS releases above stay Not validated until a test record for this addon exists.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. A macOS endpoint monitored by a Pandora FMS agent.
  2. The Pandora FMS agent for macOS, installed and reporting to the Pandora FMS server, and able to run module_plugin entries and forward their inventory output.
  3. A perl interpreter available to the user and the environment that run the agent.
  4. The standard macOS utilities the addon calls: sysctl, system_profiler, top, diskutil, networksetup and ls. No additional software has to be installed on the endpoint.
  5. The five inventory modules created in Pandora FMS before the first execution (see Create the inventory modules).

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
Download the package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.mac_inventory

The entry distributes version 1.0 as pandorafms.mac_inventory.1.0.zip. Copy the plugin file mac_inventory.pl to the macOS endpoint, for example to /usr/local/pandora/mac_inventory.pl, and make it readable by the user that runs the agent. There is nothing else to install: the addon has no dependencies of its own and no configuration file.

docs.title: Create the inventory modules
docs.text:
The addon supplies data for five inventory modules, and Pandora FMS stores inventory data in the inventory modules that already exist. Create these five modules in the console before the first execution, with these exact names:

Inventory module Content CPU Processor model RAM Installed memory and current memory usage DISK Disk partitions CARDS Network hardware ports APPS Contents of /Applications

The name is the link between the addon and the console: it is matched exactly, in uppercase, and the disk module is DISK in the singular, not DISKS. An inventory module with a different name receives no data, and the addon does not report the mismatch.

docs.title: Add the plugin to the agent
docs.text:
Add one line to the end of the agent configuration file pandora_agent.conf on the macOS endpoint:

module_plugin perl /usr/local/pandora/mac_inventory.pl

Then restart the agent. The line names the interpreter, perl, and the path of the plugin file; use a path without spaces. This is the whole configuration: the addon has no parameters, no configuration file, no environment variables and no flags, and the agent passes it no arguments.

module_plugin runs on every agent execution, so the inventory is collected each time the agent reports. The addon has no interval or schedule option of its own: the agent interval governs how often the inventory is refreshed.

docs.title: Run the plugin manually
docs.text:
Run the addon from a terminal on the endpoint, as the user that runs the agent:

perl /usr/local/pandora/mac_inventory.pl

A successful run prints one <inventory> document with the five <inventory_module> blocks and exits with status 0. This is the shape of the output; the values are illustrative:

<inventory>
<inventory_module>
<name><![CDATA[CPU]]></name>
<datalist>
<data><![CDATA[Apple M1]]></data>
</datalist>
</inventory_module>
<inventory_module>
<name><![CDATA[RAM]]></name>
<datalist>
<data><![CDATA[      Memory: 16 GB]]></data>
<data><![CDATA[PhysMem: 12G used (2100M wired), 3900M unused.]]></data>
</datalist>
</inventory_module>
<inventory_module>
<name><![CDATA[DISK]]></name>
<datalist>
<data><![CDATA[   0:      GUID_partition_scheme                        *500.3 GB   disk0]]></data>
<data><![CDATA[   1:                        EFI EFI                     209.7 MB   disk0s1]]></data>
</datalist>
</inventory_module>
<inventory_module>
<name><![CDATA[CARDS]]></name>
<datalist>
<data><![CDATA[Hardware Port: Wi-Fi]]></data>
<data><![CDATA[Device: en0]]></data>
</datalist>
</inventory_module>
<inventory_module>
<name><![CDATA[APPS]]></name>
<datalist>
<data><![CDATA[drwxr-xr-x  3 root  wheel  96 Jan  1 00:00 Example.app]]></data>
</datalist>
</inventory_module>
</inventory>

The addon prints the document with no header, no logging and no options. When a command it calls fails, the error goes to standard error — and therefore to the agent log — while the document is still printed.

docs.title: Check the inventory in the console
docs.text: After the next agent execution, open the inventory view of the macOS agent in the Pandora FMS console. The five modules are listed with the data collected in that run.

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
Every run prints the same five inventory modules, in this order: CPU, RAM, DISK, CARDS and APPS. Each module holds a data list whose entries are the raw output lines of the command that feeds it. The addon does not parse, convert or normalise them, so every entry is text exactly as the command printed it.

  • CPU. One entry with the processor brand string reported by the system.
  • RAM. Two entries with two different readings: the installed-memory line from system_profiler, with its label and padding, and a snapshot of current memory use from top. Both live in the same module.
  • DISK. One entry per partition line of diskutil list, including the partition-scheme line of each disk. The size and the disk identifier stay inside the raw line. Whole-disk header lines such as /dev/disk0 (internal, physical): are not matched and are not included.
  • CARDS. One entry per line of networksetup -listallhardwareports, so the module holds the hardware port, the device and the link-layer address of each port. Blank lines in the command output become empty entries.
  • APPS. One entry per line of ls -l /Applications: permissions, owner, group, size, date and bundle name. It covers /Applications only, so applications installed anywhere else are not listed.

Because the entries are raw text, the data is informational: it cannot be graphed or given thresholds, the RAM module mixes two formats in one module, CARDS publishes the hardware addresses of the endpoint and APPS publishes the file owner names of the applications.

docs.title: Run-time behavior
docs.text:
• One execution reads, prints and exits. The addon keeps no state between runs, so each run reports the inventory of that moment.
  • It writes nothing to disk and opens no network connection: the document goes to standard output, which the agent reads; anything a command writes to standard error goes to the agent log.
  • It reads no arguments. Any argument passed to it is ignored, and it has no -h or --help option.
  • It runs on every agent execution, because that is how module_plugin works.
  • Every run executes system_profiler and top -l 1, which sample the system on demand, so choose the agent interval with that cost in mind.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
These are behaviors of version 1.0, documented as they are.

  • The module names are fixed and matched exactly. DISK is singular and every name is uppercase. Data for a name that has no matching inventory module in the console has nowhere to land in the inventory, and the addon does not report it.
  • The addon has no error handling. It exits with status 0 even when a command it calls fails. When a command is missing or returns nothing, the corresponding module is still printed, with empty or partial entries, and no module is omitted.
  • On a host that is not macOS the result is empty. The commands do not exist, so the five modules are printed with empty data lists and the command errors go to standard error.
  • Running the file directly depends on its interpreter line. That line names /usr/bin/Perl, with a capital P, which resolves on the default case-insensitive macOS volume but not on a case-sensitive one. Start the addon through perl, as the agent configuration does.
  • There is no filtering or limit. Every line the commands print becomes an entry, so the APPS module can hold hundreds of entries on a workstation with many applications, and CARDS repeats the layout of the networksetup output, blank lines included.
  • The inventory is text only. No numeric module is created, so there is no trend, no threshold and no alerting surface.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text: Symptom Cause and action The inventory view of the agent shows no data The module_plugin line is missing from pandora_agent.conf, the agent has not run since the line was added, or the inventory modules do not exist. Check the line, restart the agent and create the five modules Some modules have data and others do not The missing inventory module exists with a different name. The match is exact: check the uppercase spelling and DISK in the singular perl: command not found in the agent log The interpreter is not in the environment of the agent. Install it or fix the agent PATH diskutil: command not found, system_profiler: command not found or similar in the agent log The addon is running on a host that is not macOS A module has empty entries The command that feeds it printed nothing for that entry, for example a blank line in networksetup output An application is missing from APPS It is not installed in /Applications The data does not change between runs The values are stable on the endpoint, or the agent is not executing the plugin: check the agent interval and the agent log

docs.title: Agent configuration
docs.text:
Directive Required Value module_plugin Yes perl /usr/local/pandora/mac_inventory.pl

The line goes in pandora_agent.conf on the macOS endpoint and takes effect after the agent restarts. There is no other input surface: no configuration file, no command-line options, no environment variables and no console plugin registration.

docs.title: Command-line execution
docs.text: Command Behavior perl /usr/local/pandora/mac_inventory.pl Prints the inventory document and exits with status 0 perl /usr/local/pandora/mac_inventory.pl -h Same output: the addon reads no arguments and has no help option

docs.title: Generated inventory modules
docs.text:
Module Source Entries CPU sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string One: the processor brand string RAM system_profiler SPHardwareDataType (memory line) and top -l 1 -s 0 (PhysMem line) Two: installed memory and current memory use DISK diskutil list (partition lines) One per partition line, partition-scheme line included CARDS networksetup -listallhardwareports One per output line, blank lines included APPS ls -l /Applications One per output line

These are the exact commands behind each module:

CPU    sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string
RAM    system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | grep "Memory:"
RAM    top -l 1 -s 0 | grep PhysMem
DISK   diskutil list | grep -E "[ ]+[0-9]+:.*disk[0-9]+"
CARDS  networksetup -listallhardwareports
APPS   ls -l /Applications

docs.title: Inventory SSH plugin
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Inventory SSH plugin runs a command on a network device over SSH and stores the command output in the Pandora FMS inventory of an agent. The command is chosen by the operator, so the same addon can collect a running configuration, a firmware version, or any other CLI output. Each execution connects to the device, optionally enters enable mode, optionally sends a pagination command, runs the configured command, filters the response, and writes the result to standard output. Pandora FMS stores that text as the value of the inventory module that runs the addon.

The addon is an inventory collector, not a monitoring plugin: it does not create agents or monitoring modules. It produces one text result per execution, and the inventory module decides which agent receives it. For the addon that always collects show running-config, see Cisco Inventory configuration.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions An SSH service on the device that provides an interactive shell Required The addon opens an interactive SSH shell to run the command SSH access to the device on the default SSH port (22) Required The addon connects to the SSH service without a port option A device user allowed to run the configured command Required The addon sends the command with the configured user Network device vendors, models and firmware versions Not validated No device or firmware matrix has been recorded Host operating system that runs the inventory module Not validated No operating system matrix has been recorded

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. Network access from the host that runs the inventory module to the device, over SSH on the default port.
  2. Credentials: a device user and its SSH password, plus the enable password when the device requires enable mode.
  3. The ssh_inventory executable on the host that runs the inventory module, with execute permission.
  4. Pandora FMS with an inventory module assigned to the agent that will store the command output.

No component is installed on the network device.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the addon from its Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.inventoryssh

Extract the package and copy the ssh_inventory executable to a path readable and executable by the user that runs the inventory module, for example /usr/local/bin/ssh_inventory. Keep its execute permission:

chmod 0755 /usr/local/bin/ssh_inventory

docs.title: Arguments and order
docs.text:
Pandora FMS runs the executable with positional arguments. Configure the inventory module so the values arrive in this order:

Position Argument Required Description 1 address Yes IP address or host name of the device 2 username Yes Device user 3 password Yes SSH password, or <PASSWORD>/<ENABLE_PASSWORD> when the device requires enable mode 4 command Yes Command to run, including its line terminator as an escape sequence 5 extra_command Yes Command sent before the main command, normally to disable pagination; use "" for none — --debug No Takes a value; supplying the option enables progress messages

extra_command is positional and therefore required: pass an empty string when you do not need it. --debug is an option and can appear before or after the positional values.

The argument names are the names used by the executable's help. The inventory module passes values by position, so the order matters more than any label the console shows.

docs.title: Command and pagination
docs.text:
The command is sent to the device as configured, after the addon interprets escape sequences. It must contain the line terminator: use , and add when the device requires it. The addon does not append a newline to the command, so a command without is typed on the device but not executed.

./ssh_inventory <TARGET_HOST> <USERNAME> '<PASSWORD>' 'show running-config
' 'terminal length 0'

The same addon on a device with a different CLI, for example a MikroTik device:

./ssh_inventory <TARGET_HOST> <USERNAME> '<PASSWORD>' 'system resource print

' ''

Use single quotes around the command so the shell preserves the backslashes and the addon can interpret them.

If the command contains a colon (:), the addon discards the text before the first colon and sends the rest. Avoid colons in the command, or account for that truncation.

extra_command is sent as plain text followed by a newline; escape sequences in it are not interpreted. It runs after the optional enable step and before the main command. Use it for the vendor command that disables pagination, such as terminal length 0 or no page. Pass an empty string when no extra command is needed.

docs.title: Password and enable mode
docs.text:
The password argument accepts one value or two values separated by /:

Form SSH password Enable password <PASSWORD> <PASSWORD> none <PASSWORD>/<ENABLE_PASSWORD> <PASSWORD> <ENABLE_PASSWORD>

The addon splits the value on / and uses the first segment as the SSH password and the second as the enable password. A password that itself contains / cannot be represented; segments after the second are ignored. The addon sends enable and the enable password only when an enable password is present, so a device that requires enable mode without the second value may return a privilege error or an empty result.

docs.title: Debug output
docs.text:
--debug <value> must be given a value. Supplying the option enables two progress messages on standard error regardless of the value, including --debug 0; omit the option to keep them off. The first message is Connected. Enabling... and the second is always Now dumping running-config..., whatever command you configured.

The addon has no other verbosity option.

docs.title: Register the inventory module
docs.text:
Create an inventory module in the Pandora FMS console and point it at the executable on its host. Add the module to the agent that will store the output, and enter the five values in the order above. Mark the password field as a hidden value where the console offers that option. If the console offers an inline-code mode, leave it disabled: the addon runs as an executable.

The module runs on the host of the agent to which it is assigned, so that host must reach the device. The addon does not copy anything to the device.

docs.title: Credentials and transport
docs.text:
• The SSH password and enable password are passed as command-line arguments. On a manual run they appear in the shell history and in the process list while the addon runs. In the console, they are stored in the inventory module configuration. Restrict access to the console and to the agent configuration.
  • The SSH session encrypts the credentials in transit. The addon accepts any SSH host key and does not verify it, so a man-in-the-middle on the network path can impersonate the device. Run the addon only from a trusted management network, or enforce device identity at the network layer.
  • The command output is stored as inventory data. It can contain credentials, keys, community strings and other sensitive values. Anyone who can read the agent inventory can read them. Restrict inventory access accordingly.
  • The line filter described in Understand the results is not a redaction control. Use a device user with read-only privileges, and choose commands whose output you are prepared to store.

The addon has no credential-file option, no port option, and no host-key verification option.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the executable manually from the host that will run the inventory module:

./ssh_inventory <TARGET_HOST> <USERNAME> '<PASSWORD>' 'show version\n' 'terminal length 0' --debug 1

A successful run exits with status 0 and prints the filtered command output on standard output. With --debug 1, it also prints the two progress messages on standard error:

Connected. Enabling...
Now dumping running-config...

The second message is fixed text and names running-config even when the command is show version. It is a progress message, not a statement about the command that ran.

Then check the agent inventory. The module value is the filtered text returned by the device for the configured command.

If the run prints an error or no output, see Operate and troubleshoot.

docs.title: What the module stores
docs.text:
The addon stores the command output as plain text. It does not parse the output into interfaces, routes, firmware fields or other objects, and it does not create one module per line: the filtered text is the value of the inventory module.

Before printing, the addon removes the sent command text, the text captured before the command (normally the device prompt), the last line of the response, leading and trailing whitespace, and empty lines. If the command produces no output, the module value is empty.

docs.title: Filtering
docs.text:
The filter is always applied; this version has no option to disable it. It removes any line that contains one of these values:

  • enable
  • Password:
  • the command text

The match is case-sensitive and applies anywhere in the line. Empty lines are removed afterwards. The extra_command value is not added to the filter list.

Because enable is matched anywhere, lines such as enable secret ... are removed, and so are legitimate configuration lines that contain the word. Because the command text is matched, any output line that repeats the command is removed. The filter can remove useful lines and does not guarantee that every secret is removed; treat it as output cleanup, not as redaction.

docs.title: Sensitive content
docs.text: A running configuration, a firmware inventory or a diagnostic command can expose credentials, keys and internal addresses. The filter removes some lines but not all sensitive values. Restrict access to the agent inventory and choose the command with the same care as the credentials.

docs.title: Scheduling and timing
docs.text: Run the inventory module on the interval you need. Each execution opens a new SSH session and closes it at the end. After sending the command, the addon stops waiting when it detects the prompt or when the device produces no output for 5 seconds. There is no configurable connection timeout or initial-prompt timeout; a device that stops responding can leave the execution waiting.

docs.title: Exit status and diagnostics
docs.text: Condition Status Output Successful command 0 Filtered command output on standard output SSH connection failure Non-zero The SSH error on standard error Missing or invalid argument 2 Usage summary on standard error

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The connection fails with a non-zero status — the device is unreachable, the SSH service is not on the default port, the user or password is wrong, or the device rejects the connection. Check the address, the SSH service and the credentials from the same host.
  • The output is empty — the command has no \n and was not executed, the command is not valid for the device, the user lacks the required privilege, enable mode was needed but not supplied, or extra_command failed. Run the same command manually on the device.
  • Expected lines are missing — the filter removed them because they contain enable, Password: or the command text. Check the complete response on the device and adjust the command. There is no option to disable the filter.
  • The output is truncated — the device produced no data for 5 seconds before the prompt returned, or the command takes longer than the fixed wait. There is no configurable timeout; use a command that returns its output continuously or faster.
  • The command is truncated at a colon — the addon sends only the text after the first colon. Remove the colon from the command or use a different command.
  • The password is split unexpectedly — the addon splits the password value on /. A password that contains / cannot be passed correctly.
  • --debug fails with a usage error — the option requires a value; use --debug 1.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• No SSH port option: the addon uses the SSH default port.
  • No configurable connection, initial-prompt or read timeout.
  • The command must include its own line terminator as an escape sequence.
  • Text before the first colon in the command is discarded.
  • A password that contains / cannot be represented.
  • The filter is always on, is case-sensitive, and cannot be disabled.
  • No credential file: credentials are positional arguments.
  • No host-key verification: any SSH host key is accepted.

docs.title: Command-line arguments
docs.text:
Argument Position Required Default Description address 1 Yes — IP address or host name of the device username 2 Yes — Device user password 3 Yes — SSH password, or <PASSWORD>/<ENABLE_PASSWORD> command 4 Yes — Command to run, with its line terminator as an escape sequence extra_command 5 Yes — Command sent before the main command; use "" for none --debug option No 0 Takes a value; supplying the option enables progress messages regardless of the value

-h or --help prints the usage summary and exits.

docs.title: Command preprocessing
docs.text: Step Behavior Colon split The text before the first colon is discarded; the rest, including later colons, is sent Escape interpretation Escape sequences such as \n, \r and \t in command are interpreted Line terminator No newline is appended to command; include \n (and \r when required) Extra command extra_command is sent as plain text plus a newline; its escape sequences are not interpreted

docs.title: Output processing
docs.text: Step Behavior Command removal The sent command text is removed from the response Prompt removal The text captured before the command, normally the prompt, is removed Last line The last line of the response is always removed Whitespace Leading and trailing whitespace is removed Line filter Lines containing enable, Password: or the command text are removed, case-sensitive Blank lines Empty lines are removed

docs.title: Execution and output
docs.text:
./ssh_inventory <TARGET_HOST> <USERNAME> <PASSWORD> <COMMAND> <EXTRA_COMMAND> [--debug <VALUE>]
Stream Content Standard output Filtered command output Standard error Progress messages with --debug; SSH errors Exit status 0 on success, non-zero on an SSH failure, 2 on an argument error

The addon uses the SSH default port and has no option to change it.

docs.text: Property Value Marketplace identifier pandorafms.inventoryssh Name Inventory SSH plugin Version 1.0 Marketplace last update 2025-06-25 Package pandorafms.inventoryssh.1.0.zip Executable ssh_inventory Availability Download limited to licensed users (license One)

docs.title: Journalctl plugin
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Journalctl plugin forwards the systemd journal of a Linux host to Pandora FMS. On every run it asks journalctl for the entries written since the previous run, filters them with regular expressions and prints them as Pandora FMS log entries on standard output.

It is an agent plugin: the Pandora FMS agent runs it as one of its module_plugin lines, at every agent interval, and appends the entries it prints to its own data. The plugin creates no agent, opens no network connection and needs no credential: it only reads the journal of the machine where it runs.

Collection is incremental. The plugin keeps the time of its last successful run in a single file under /tmp and asks for the journal written after that moment, so each run delivers the new entries instead of the whole journal. A regular expression narrows what is delivered, either by keeping only the lines that match or by dropping the ones that match.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.journalctl, version 1.0 Documented target The version of the Marketplace package pandorafms.journalctl.1.0.zip. See Addon identity A Linux host with systemd and journalctl in the PATH Required journalctl is the only data source of the plugin: when the command is not available the run ends with an error and prints no entries An account allowed to read the journal Required The plugin reads the journal through journalctl with the permissions of the account that runs the agent; when the journal cannot be read the command fails and the run ends with an error A Pandora FMS agent installed on the monitored host Required The plugin is executed by the agent and its output is consumed as agent plugin output Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions. It is a general Marketplace statement, not a statement specific to this addon Individual Linux distributions and versions Not validated No distribution or version matrix is recorded for this addon

The plugin runs on the monitored host itself: it reports the journal of that host only, and it has no remote execution mode and no connection to another system.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. systemd, with the journalctl command available in the PATH of the account that runs the agent. The plugin has no fallback: without the command there is nothing to read.
  2. Journal read access for that account. The agent runs the plugin as its own user and the plugin does not elevate privileges. Grant that user the journal read access of your distribution — commonly through the systemd-journal group — or run the agent under an account that already has it. When the account cannot read the journal, journalctl fails and the run aborts.
  3. A writable /tmp. The plugin checks it at the start of every run and aborts when it cannot write there, because it keeps its collection position in /tmp/journalctl_logs.index.
  4. A Pandora FMS agent on the host. The agent is what turns the printed entries into log data in the console.
  5. A Marketplace account with a licence. The download of this addon is limited to licensed users.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
Download the package from the Marketplace entry:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.journalctl

The package distributes the grep_journalctl executable — that is the file name, not the addon identifier — and no configuration file. Copy it to the plugins directory of the agent and make it executable. On a Linux agent the plugins directory is /usr/share/pandora_agent/plugins, which is also reachable as /etc/pandora/plugins:

cp grep_journalctl /usr/share/pandora_agent/plugins/
chmod 755 /usr/share/pandora_agent/plugins/grep_journalctl

The agent adds its plugins directory to the PATH, so the bare executable name is enough in the module_plugin line. An absolute path also works and is the safer choice when more than one copy of the file exists.

Instead of copying the file by hand, the agent can distribute it to its hosts as a file collection; the destination is the same plugins directory.

docs.title: Add the plugin to the agent
docs.text:
The plugin is configured in the agent configuration file (pandora_agent.conf) as one module_plugin line. Without options it delivers every new journal line of the host:

module_plugin grep_journalctl

The line runs once per agent interval, so the coverage of each run is the time elapsed since the previous run. Restart or reload the agent after editing the file.

Narrow the delivery with an inclusion filter, and name the source that will group the entries in the console:

module_plugin grep_journalctl -in 'Failed password|authentication failure' -s AuthErrors

Or drop the lines you do not want and keep everything else:

module_plugin grep_journalctl -out 'session opened|session closed' -s SystemLog

A single module_plugin line per host is enough: see One collection position per host before adding a second one.

To bound the duration of the run, use the block form and add a module timeout. The block needs no module_name: the plugin prints its own entries and the agent appends them unchanged.

module_begin
module_plugin grep_journalctl -in 'error|critical' -s SystemErrors
module_timeout 120
module_end

The single-line form has no timeout, which means a run that reads a long backlog can last longer than the agent interval. module_timeout is expressed in seconds and applies to that line only.

When the agent reads its configuration from the console (remote configuration), the module_plugin line belongs to the agent configuration stored there, and a local edit of pandora_agent.conf is overwritten by the agent.

docs.title: Quote the patterns
docs.text:
The agent executes the module_plugin line through a shell, before the plugin sees it. A pattern that contains characters such as |, (, ), $, * or & must be quoted, or the shell interprets it and the plugin receives something else:

module_plugin grep_journalctl -in 'Failed password|authentication failure'

Use single quotes: they protect every character except a single quote of its own. Double quotes also work, but the shell still expands $ inside them, so a pattern such as end$ must be written with single quotes.

docs.title: Choose the source
docs.text:
-s / --source sets the source name that the console uses to group the entries of this line. The default is Journalctl, with a capital J. Always set a non-empty value: an empty -s '' is accepted and produces entries with an empty source, which makes them hard to find and to tell apart.

Changing the source does not reset the collection position. Entries delivered before the change stay under the previous source, and new entries appear under the new one, so a renamed source looks like a new journal in the console.

docs.title: Filter the lines
docs.text:
Both filters take a regular expression that is searched anywhere in the line. They are optional and only one of them can act:

  • -in / --regex_in keeps only the lines that match.
  • -out / --regex_out drops the lines that match.

When both are given, -in wins and -out is ignored without any warning. An empty value (-in '') counts as absent, so it does not filter anything.

Matching rules:

  • The expression is a search, not a full-line match: error matches any line that contains error.
  • Matching is case-sensitive unless the pattern turns it off with (?i): -in '(?i)error' matches ERROR and Error.
  • The whole journal line is matched, including the date, the host name and the unit prefix that journalctl writes in its default output format. A pattern anchored with ^ therefore sees the timestamp, not the message text: ^error matches almost nothing, while : error or (?i)error work as expected.
  • Each physical line is matched and delivered separately. An entry whose message spans several lines arrives as several entries, and a pattern cannot match across them.
  • A pattern that is not a valid regular expression aborts the run before the journal is read, with an error message and exit status 1.

The filter acts on the collected lines, after the collection position has advanced: a line that the filter drops is not delivered later and is never reconsidered. Changing the pattern does not replay the past.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin by hand before wiring it into the agent. From the plugins directory:

./grep_journalctl

Each run executes once and exits. A successful run prints one <log_module> block per delivered line on standard output, and writes the collection position to /tmp/journalctl_logs.index:

<log_module>
    <source><![CDATA[Journalctl]]></source>
    <data>"Tm92IDExIDEyOjUzOjAyIGhvc3QwMSBzc2hkWzEzODJdOiBGYWlsZWQgcGFzc3dvcmQgZm9yIGludmFsaWQgdXNlciBhZG1pbiBmcm9tIDE5Mi4wLjIuMTA="</data>
    <encoding>base64</encoding>
</log_module>

<log_module>
    <source><![CDATA[Journalctl]]></source>
    <data>"Tm92IDExIDEyOjUzOjAzIGhvc3QwMSBzeXN0ZW1kWzFdOiBTdGFydGVkIFNlc3Npb24gNDIgb2YgdXNlciBtb25pdG9yaW5nLg=="</data>
    <encoding>base64</encoding>
</log_module>

The value of <data> is the journal line encoded in Base64, between double quotes. Decode it to confirm what was captured:

printf 'Tm92IDExIDEyOjUzOjAzIGhvc3QwMSBzeXN0ZW1kWzFdOiBTdGFydGVkIFNlc3Npb24gNDIgb2YgdXNlciBtb25pdG9yaW5nLg==' | base64 -d

Nov 11 12:53:03 host01 systemd[1]: Started Session 42 of user monitoring.

Run the same command again immediately. When no journal line was written in between, the run prints nothing on standard output, prints No new logs. on standard error and exits with status 0:

19:51:45 [INFO] No new logs.

The collection position that was written by the successful run can be read directly:

cat /tmp/journalctl_logs.index

2026-10-26 19:51:45

A manual run behaves exactly like an agent run, including the advance of that file. Use it to install, to test patterns and to diagnose, and take it into account when the agent is already running the same plugin on that host (see Everyday operation).

Once the module_plugin line is in place and the agent has run it, the entries appear in the console log viewer under the agent that runs the plugin and the source you configured:

docs.title: Log entries
docs.text:
Each delivered journal line becomes one log_module entry with three fields:

Field Content source The value of -s / --source, verbatim. The console groups the entries by this name. Default Journalctl data The journal line encoded in Base64, between double quotes encoding Always base64

Base64 is what keeps the generated XML valid: the journal can contain angle brackets, quotes and control characters, and the encoding carries them without breaking the document. The console decodes the value, so the log viewer shows the original line.

The plugin sends no module with a numeric value, no availability check and no alert template: log entries are its only output. Nothing appears in the monitoring views of the agent as a graph or as a status, so any alerting is configured in the console on top of the log data.

docs.title: What the agent does with the output
docs.text:
• The agent appends the plugin output to the data it sends to the server, so the <log_module> blocks reach Pandora FMS unchanged.
  • When the plugin exits with a status other than 0, the agent discards its entire output and records the error code in its own log. A run that fails after printing part of its entries delivers none of them.
  • The agent sends the standard error of a plugin to /dev/null. Every diagnostic of this plugin — the regex error, the journalctl failure, the missing /tmp permission, the No new logs. notice and the -v line — is therefore invisible in a scheduled run. Run the command by hand to read it.

docs.title: Coverage and the collection position
docs.text:
The plugin stores one timestamp, in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS, in /tmp/journalctl_logs.index. Each run asks journalctl for the entries since that moment:

journalctl --since "<stored timestamp>" --no-pager

The window of a run therefore starts where the previous successful run ended and finishes when the current run writes its own timestamp. That position is written at the very end of the run and only when the run completes. Three consequences follow, and they are worth knowing before you rely on the log for auditing:

  • The run covers everything since the last completed run. This includes entries written while the plugin was stopped, so a host whose agent was down for a day delivers a day of journal in the first run after it starts. There is no line limit: the whole window is read into memory and printed one entry per line.
  • A run that fails does not advance the position. Nothing is lost, but the next successful run repeats the same window, so entries can be delivered twice: after a failed journalctl, after an invalid regular expression, and after a run interrupted with Ctrl+C or killed before it finishes.
  • A small part of the window is never delivered. The position is the time at the end of the run, while the journal was read earlier in the same run. Entries written between the read and the write of the timestamp are older than the stored position when the next run starts, so they are skipped. The gap is short, but it exists.

Two smaller effects of the same design:

  • The timestamp has a resolution of one second and the query includes the entries written in that exact second, so a line written in the same second in which the previous run ended can be delivered twice.
  • The timestamp carries no time zone and journalctl reads it in the local time of the host. If the host changes its time zone or crosses a daylight-saving transition, the window between two runs shifts accordingly.

docs.title: One collection position per host
docs.text:
The file name is fixed: every execution of the plugin on the same host uses /tmp/journalctl_logs.index, whatever source, filter or account it uses. There is no per-module or per-source state.

  • Two module_plugin lines on the same host share the position. The second line finds an almost empty window, because the first one already consumed it, and each of them receives an arbitrary part of the journal. Do not run two lines: keep one and use -in to select what you need.
  • A manual run and the scheduled run share it too, so a manual run consumes the window that the agent would have delivered.

The position file lives in a shared directory

/tmp is world-writable and the file name is fixed, so any local account can create that file first, replace it, or turn it into a symbolic link. The plugin writes its timestamp with the privileges of the agent account, so a symbolic link placed there makes the run overwrite another file that this account can write. Run the agent with an unprivileged account where your installation allows it, and do not treat the content of the file as a tamper-proof record.

docs.title: First run
docs.text:
When /tmp/journalctl_logs.index does not exist, or its content cannot be read or is not a valid timestamp, the run collects the last five minutes of the journal. This is also what happens after a reboot that clears /tmp: journal entries of the five minutes before the reboot can be delivered a second time, because the journal may survive the reboot while the position does not.

To force that five-minute window again, delete the file:

rm -f /tmp/journalctl_logs.index

The next run starts from five minutes before it, whatever happened in between.

docs.title: Everyday operation
docs.text:
• One line per host. The single collection position makes a second line useless (see One collection position per host).
  • The interval sets the coverage. The agent runs the line at the agent interval, and each run covers what happened since the previous one. A shorter interval delivers more often and in smaller batches; it does not change which entries are delivered.
  • Bound long runs. After a long stop, the first run reads the whole window. Set module_timeout in a block so that a large backlog cannot delay the agent beyond the interval, and run the plugin by hand first to drain it.
  • Manual runs consume data. A manual run prints the entries to your terminal and advances the position, so the agent does not deliver them afterwards. Use the manual run for installation, for trying a pattern and for diagnosis, and expect the next agent run to be empty.
  • -v only reports the position write. The verbose mode raises the diagnostic level, but the only message it adds is the line that records the new collection position, for example 19:51:53 [DEBUG] Saved execution time: 2026-10-26 19:51:53 -> /tmp/journalctl_logs.index. It does not report the applied filters, the number of lines read or the number of entries delivered.
  • Keep the patterns stable. A filter change applies from the next run on; the lines already dropped are gone, and a line the new pattern would have kept is not recovered.

keep one module_plugin line Entries appear under the wrong source -s is missing (default Journalctl), or it was changed and the old entries stayed under their old source Set -s explicitly, and look for the previous source in the log viewer A pattern that works elsewhere matches nothing The line carries journalctl's date and host prefix, or the case does not match Remove the ^ anchor, or add (?i) Invalid regex: ... and no entries The pattern is not a valid regular expression Fix the pattern; the run stops before reading the journal, so nothing is lost Error: 'journalctl' command not found... journalctl is not installed or not in the PATH of the agent Install systemd, or make sure the PATH of the agent includes the directory that contains journalctl Error executing journalctl: ... followed by the command error journalctl failed: the account cannot read the journal, or the journal is unreadable Run journalctl --since '5 minutes ago' --no-pager as the agent user No write permissions for /tmp /tmp is not writable by the account that runs the plugin Fix the permissions or the mount options of /tmp The run ends with status 2 and a usage message An unknown option, or an option without a value Compare the line with Command-line parameters Entries disappear after a run that also failed The exit status was not 0, so the agent discarded the whole output Look for the error in a manual run: the agent already turned the standard error into /dev/null Some entries are missing between two runs They were written while the run was in progress, or the filter dropped them This is expected: the window ends at the moment the position is written The same entries arrive twice The previous run did not complete, the position was deleted, /tmp was cleared, or the two runs ended in the same second Accept it, or use the entry timestamp in the console to identify the duplicate
