docs.title: Kafka monitoring plugin
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Kafka monitoring plugin collects the performance metrics of a Kafka client and publishes them as Pandora FMS modules. Each run creates a producer and a consumer against one Kafka endpoint, takes a snapshot of the metrics both clients report, and writes the result into a Pandora FMS agent.

The plugin is a server plugin: the Pandora FMS Plugin Server executes it, and each run delivers the generated agent XML to Pandora FMS through Tentacle or into a local data directory. Nothing is installed on the Kafka broker.

What the plugin measures has three consequences worth stating before you configure it:

  • It does not read Kafka broker JMX metrics. The modules describe the producer and consumer clients that the plugin creates, not the producers and consumers of your applications, and not the broker's own MBeans.
  • It does not send or consume records. The plugin creates both clients, optionally subscribes the consumer to topics, reads the metric snapshot and closes them. It does not poll the consumer and commits no offsets.
  • It creates one agent per --bootstrap_servers entry. Two successfully processed endpoints produce two agents, even when both point to the same cluster.

The plugin prints 1 when it processed every endpoint without an exception and 0 when any endpoint raised one. That printed value is what a Pandora FMS plugin module receives. A broker that cannot be reached makes the run print 0; the value does not prove that the generated agent was delivered, so verify delivery separately (see Verify).

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.apache_kafka, version 1.1 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions. This is a catalogue-wide statement covering the addon, not a test record for it A Kafka listener reachable from the Pandora FMS server over TCP Required The plugin connects to every endpoint listed in --bootstrap_servers A listener that accepts unauthenticated PLAINTEXT connections Required The addon exposes no options for SASL authentication or TLS, so it can only use the Kafka client's default connection settings Rocky Linux Known compatible The legacy guide for this addon records Rocky Linux as the system where it was tested. Not re-validated for version 1.1 Other Linux distributions Not validated No distribution range or version matrix has been recorded for this addon Kafka broker versions Not validated No broker version matrix has been recorded for this addon tentacle_client in PATH Required when --transfer_mode is not local Tentacle delivery runs that command Write access to /tmp Required The plugin stages the generated XML in /tmp before delivery Write access to /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Required when --transfer_mode local is used The XML document is moved into that directory

No compatibility statement establishes a Kafka version range, a broker distribution or a Linux distribution other than the Rocky Linux record above. Keep each claim at the scope its source proves.

docs.title: Kafka requirements
docs.text:
1. A reachable Kafka listener. Use the listener address and port in --bootstrap_servers, for example <TARGET_HOST>:9092. Include the port explicitly in every endpoint; Kafka's default client port is 9092.
  2. A listener that accepts the client's default connection. The addon has no security_protocol, SASL or TLS options. A cluster whose listeners require SASL authentication, TLS client certificates or another authenticated protocol cannot be monitored with this version.
  3. No Kafka account or JMX access. The plugin authenticates with nothing, so it needs no Kafka user, no JMX port and no RMI credentials. If anonymous access to the listener is disabled, the connection fails and the run reports it only as a broker processing error.

The plugin does not read or write topic data, so it needs no topic ACL for the applications you monitor. Restrict the listener to the Pandora FMS server network instead of opening it broadly.

docs.title: Pandora FMS requirements
docs.text:
1. Pandora FMS with the Plugin Server enabled on the server that will run the plugin.
  2. A Tentacle server reachable at --tentacle_ip and --tentacle_port when the default Tentacle delivery is used, plus the tentacle_client command in PATH.
  3. A writable data directory when --transfer_mode local is used. The plugin moves the XML into /var/spool/pandora/data_in/; the option does not let you choose another directory.
  4. Write access to /tmp for the user that runs the Plugin Server. The generated XML is staged there before delivery.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
Download the addon from its Marketplace entry, whose download is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.apache_kafka

Copy the pandora_kafka executable to the Pandora FMS server and give it execute permission. The recommended directory for server plugins is:

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/

sudo chmod 755 /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora_kafka

Nothing is installed on the Kafka broker, and the Kafka server does not need JMX enabled.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
The plugin has no configuration file. It takes all its settings from the command line, starting from built-in defaults:

built-in defaults < command-line options

Every option is documented in Command-line parameters. This section explains the decisions that change what the plugin measures and where the result goes.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
--bootstrap_servers is mandatory and accepts a comma-separated list of Kafka endpoints in host:port form:

--bootstrap_servers <KAFKA_HOST_1>:9092,<KAFKA_HOST_2>:9092

Each non-empty item is processed independently and produces one agent. Empty items between commas are ignored. The plugin does not create one agent per cluster broker: it creates one producer and one consumer per item and names the agent after that item.

docs.title: Topics
docs.text:
The consumer can subscribe to a list of topics, a regular expression, or nothing:

  • --topics orders,payments subscribes to the listed topics.
  • --topic_regex '^prod-.*' subscribes to the topics that match the pattern.
  • When both are given, --topic_regex takes precedence and --topics is ignored.
  • When neither is given, the consumer is created without a subscription.

Subscription does not make the plugin read messages. It never polls the consumer, so no records are consumed and no offsets are committed. The consumer uses the fixed group identifier monitoring-client with automatic commit disabled.

An invalid regular expression is not rejected before the run starts: the error is printed only with --verbose, and the subscription then raises during that endpoint's processing, which makes the run print 0. Test the pattern with --verbose before registering it.

docs.title: Agent and module prefixes
docs.text:
--agent_prefix is prepended to both the name and the alias of every generated agent, and --module_prefix is prepended to every generated module name. Both default to an empty string.

--agent_prefix KAFKA_ --module_prefix METRIC_

With the broker kafka1:9092, the agent is named KAFKA_kafka1:9092, and the module producer-metrics.request-rate becomes METRIC_producer-metrics.request-rate.

docs.title: Delivery
docs.text:
The default is Tentacle delivery. --transfer_mode accepts one meaningful value:

Value Behavior tentacle (default) Sends the XML document with tentacle_client to --tentacle_ip:--tentacle_port local Moves the XML document into /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Any other value, including a misspelling Also uses Tentacle; the plugin only treats the exact value local as local delivery

--tentacle_ip defaults to 127.0.0.1 and --tentacle_port to 41121. They are only used by Tentacle delivery. Local delivery has no configurable folder: if the Pandora FMS server does not use /var/spool/pandora/data_in/, use Tentacle instead.

Tentacle failures are printed on standard error, but they do not change the 1 or 0 the plugin prints. See Output and exit status.

docs.title: Register the plugin in the console
docs.text:
1. Open Servers → Plugins and click Register Plugin.
  2. Set a name, the plugin type Standard, an optional maximum timeout and a description.
  3. In Plugin command, enter the full path to the executable on the Pandora FMS server: /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora_kafka.
  4. In Plugin parameters, combine the mandatory endpoint with the options you need, using the plugin macros _field1_, _field2_, ... as placeholders:
--bootstrap_servers _field1_ --agent_prefix _field2_ --module_prefix _field3_ --transfer_mode tentacle --tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1 --tentacle_port 41121
  1. In Macro parameters, describe each field. The example uses these values:
Field Description Example value _field1_ Kafka endpoint, including the port; several endpoints separated by commas <KAFKA_HOST>:9092 _field2_ Prefix for the generated agent names and aliases KAFKA_ _field3_ Prefix for the generated module names METRIC_

Add --topics _field4_ or --topic_regex _field4_ only when you want a subscription. Every flag that remains in the parameter string must receive a value: a blank macro leaves the flag without an argument, and the plugin exits with an argument-parsing error instead of running. Remove the flag rather than leaving its field empty.

After the server plugin is created, open an agent, create a plugin module and select the registered plugin. That module receives the printed 1 or 0. The Kafka metrics do not go into that module: they arrive in the separate agents the plugin creates.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• The addon has no user, password or token options, and no SASL or TLS settings. It connects with the Kafka client's default unauthenticated PLAINTEXT configuration.
  • Because there is no transport encryption, metrics and connection metadata travel in clear text between the Pandora FMS server and the Kafka listener. Restrict the listener to a trusted network, or do not use this addon where authentication or encryption is mandatory.
  • The plugin stores no credentials, so there is no secret to protect in a configuration file. Its command line only carries broker addresses, prefixes and delivery settings.
  • --verbose prints broker error details on standard output. Those messages can include broker addresses and exception text, so review them before sharing a manual run.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually from a terminal on the Pandora FMS server:

./pandora_kafka \
  --bootstrap_servers <TARGET_HOST>:9092 \
  --topics <TOPIC> \
  --agent_prefix KAFKA_ \
  --transfer_mode tentacle \
  --tentacle_ip <PANDORA_FMS_SERVER> \
  --tentacle_port 41121 \
  --verbose

A successful run ends with 1 on standard output. With Tentacle delivery, the agent KAFKA_<TARGET_HOST>:9092 and its modules appear in Pandora FMS after the next data processing cycle. With local delivery, check that a .data file has been moved into /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ and that the agent appears after the data server processes it.

The printed value alone is not enough to verify the integration:

  • 1 means the plugin created the producer and the consumer for every endpoint and collected their metrics without an exception. Client creation resolves the broker version over the network, so a broker that rejects or does not answer the connection produces 0 instead.
  • 1 does not prove delivery: a Tentacle failure is printed on standard error but still leaves 1 on standard output.

Verify the data, not only the exit line:

  1. Confirm the generated agent exists and its name follows the prefix rule.
  2. Open its modules and check that connection and request metrics report activity.
  3. If every value is zero, check connectivity before assuming the plugin delivered correctly.

Use ./pandora_kafka -h to print the usage summary, the plugin version and the execution example.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text:
The plugin creates one agent per successfully processed non-empty --bootstrap_servers item. Name and alias use the same value:

<agent_prefix><host:port>

For example, with --agent_prefix KAFKA_ and the endpoint kafka1:9092, the agent is KAFKA_kafka1:9092. Every generated agent has an interval of 300 seconds, the description Created by plugin and no agent group assigned.

Running the plugin twice with the same endpoint updates the same agent name. Running it with two endpoints that belong to the same cluster creates two agents with duplicated module sets.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
The plugin iterates over every metric group and metric name reported by the producer and the consumer. The module name is:

<module_prefix><metric_group>.<metric_name>

All modules are created as generic_data, without a unit and without a description. Floating-point values that are NaN, positive infinity or negative infinity are written as 0.0.

The exact catalogue depends on the Kafka client state and the Kafka version. The stable groups and representative modules are:

Source Metric group Representative modules without prefix Producer and consumer kafka-metrics-count kafka-metrics-count.count Producer producer-metrics producer-metrics.connection-count, producer-metrics.request-rate, producer-metrics.request-latency-avg, producer-metrics.outgoing-byte-rate Producer producer-node-metrics.node-<node> producer-node-metrics.node-<node>.outgoing-byte-rate, producer-node-metrics.node-<node>.request-rate, producer-node-metrics.node-<node>.response-rate Consumer consumer-metrics consumer-metrics.connection-count, consumer-metrics.request-rate, consumer-metrics.incoming-byte-rate, consumer-metrics.request-latency-avg Consumer consumer-node-metrics.node-<node> consumer-node-metrics.node-<node>.incoming-byte-rate, consumer-node-metrics.node-<node>.request-rate, consumer-node-metrics.node-<node>.response-rate Consumer consumer-fetch-manager-metrics consumer-fetch-manager-metrics.fetch-size-avg, consumer-fetch-manager-metrics.bytes-consumed-rate, consumer-fetch-manager-metrics.records-consumed-rate, consumer-fetch-manager-metrics.records-lag-max Consumer consumer-coordinator-metrics consumer-coordinator-metrics.commit-rate, consumer-coordinator-metrics.assigned-partitions

In the node groups, <node> is the numeric Kafka node identifier, for example node-1. The group name already contains it, so a full module name looks like producer-node-metrics.node-1.outgoing-byte-rate. Node groups appear only for the nodes the probe client actually contacts; the set depends on the cluster metadata returned to that client.

Both clients register their own kafka-metrics-count group, so the generated agent XML contains kafka-metrics-count.count twice: once with the producer's count and once with the consumer's count. This is expected behavior, not a duplicated agent.

docs.title: What the values represent
docs.text:
Each run creates new clients and reads their metrics immediately. The values are therefore a snapshot of a freshly created probe, not a continuous sample of your application:

  • Connection counters, request counters and request latency describe the plugin's own client connections.
  • Record and commit rates describe traffic that the probe client does not generate: the plugin sends no records, polls no records and commits no offsets, so those rates normally remain at their initial values. Byte and request rates reflect only the probe's own connection and metadata traffic, not your application's throughput.
  • Averages that need samples from the client's lifetime can be 0.0 because the plugin converts their initial NaN to zero.
  • Consumer group metrics do not reflect your application's consumer groups. The consumer uses the fixed group identifier monitoring-client, with automatic commit disabled, and never joins a group during the run.

Use the connection and request metrics to observe whether the Kafka listener is reachable and responsive from the Pandora FMS server. Do not use this addon as a substitute for Kafka broker JMX monitoring or for instrumenting application producers and consumers.

docs.title: Operate and troubleshoot
docs.text:
The plugin keeps no state between executions. Every run creates its clients, collects one snapshot, delivers one agent document and exits, so it can be run manually at any time without affecting offsets or topic data.

Schedule the registered plugin module at the interval you want. The generated agents keep their fixed 300-second interval, but their values are refreshed only when the plugin module runs; align the module interval with the desired data cadence. Use --verbose for manual diagnosis, but do not leave it in the registered parameter string: its diagnostic lines are written to standard output and become part of the value the plugin module receives.

docs.title: Output and exit status
docs.text: Result Meaning Standard output 1 Every endpoint was processed without an exception: its clients were created and their metrics collected. Delivery is not guaranteed Standard output 0 At least one endpoint raised an exception, for example because the broker was unreachable or rejected the connection. Run again with --verbose to see the detail No standard output without --verbose The bootstrap list contained no non-empty item. The process exits with status 0 Argument-parsing error on standard error A required option is missing or a flag has no value, for example a blank macro field. The process exits with status 2 Process exit status 0 with 1 or 0 on standard output Normal run. The printed number is the module value, not the process status

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text:
• The run prints 1 but no agent appears. The broker processing succeeded but delivery failed. Check that tentacle_client exists in PATH and can reach --tentacle_ip:--tentacle_port. Run manually with --verbose and read standard error; Tentacle errors do not alter the printed 1. For local delivery, check that /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ exists and is writable.
  • The run prints 0. At least one endpoint failed. Run with --verbose and read the Error with broker ... line. The usual causes are a wrong address or port, a listener that requires authentication or TLS, an invalid --topic_regex, or a malformed endpoint.
  • The run prints nothing without --verbose. --bootstrap_servers was accepted but contained no non-empty item, for example a comma or spaces only. The process exits 0 without an agent or a value. Correct the endpoint list.
  • The plugin exits before connecting. An option is missing its value. This is the usual result of leaving a _fieldN_ macro empty for a flag that you kept in the parameter string. Remove the unused flag or fill the field.
  • The agent exists but every value is zero. The probe connected, but it did not exchange further data with the cluster. Check the listener address and port, and whether the listener accepts unauthenticated PLAINTEXT connections. Remember that record and commit rates are expected to stay at their initial values because the probe sends and consumes no records, and byte and request rates reflect only the probe's own traffic.
  • The cluster requires SASL or TLS. This version cannot connect to it. The addon has no option to configure authentication or encryption; use a Kafka monitoring path that supports those settings.
  • --transfer_mode local does not deliver. The plugin always moves the XML into /var/spool/pandora/data_in/. If the Pandora FMS server uses another data directory, use Tentacle delivery instead.
  • A misspelled transfer mode still tries Tentacle. Only the exact value local selects local delivery; every other value falls back to Tentacle.
  • Values look stale. Every run returns the snapshot taken at that moment. Check the plugin module interval and the broker state rather than expecting a continuous series.

docs.title: Command-line parameters
docs.text:
./pandora_kafka --bootstrap_servers <host:port> [--topics <topic1,topic2>] [--topic_regex <regex>] [--agent_prefix <prefix>] [--module_prefix <prefix>] [--transfer_mode <mode>] [--tentacle_ip <ip>] [--tentacle_port <port>] [--verbose]
Name Required Default Description -h, --help No — Prints the usage summary, the plugin version and the execution example, then exits --bootstrap_servers Yes — Comma-separated Kafka endpoints in host:port form. Empty items are ignored. Each remaining item produces one agent --topics No Empty Comma-separated topics for the consumer subscription. Ignored when --topic_regex is set --topic_regex No Empty Regular expression for the consumer subscription. Takes precedence over --topics. An invalid pattern fails during the run --agent_prefix No Empty Prefix added to the name and alias of every generated agent --module_prefix No Empty Prefix added to every generated module name --transfer_mode No tentacle local moves the XML into /var/spool/pandora/data_in/. Any other value, including the default, uses Tentacle --tentacle_ip No 127.0.0.1 Tentacle server address for Tentacle delivery --tentacle_port No 41121 Tentacle server port for Tentacle delivery --verbose No Disabled Prints broker error and diagnostic messages on standard output

docs.title: Delivery
docs.text: Setting Value Default delivery Tentacle Tentacle client command tentacle_client, resolved through PATH Tentacle address and port --tentacle_ip and --tentacle_port Local delivery selector --transfer_mode local (exact value) Local destination /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Configurable local destination No XML staging directory /tmp Runtime dependency on the broker None; nothing is installed on the Kafka broker

docs.title: Generated agents
docs.text: Attribute Value Cardinality One agent per successfully processed non-empty --bootstrap_servers item Name <agent_prefix><host:port> Alias Same as the name Description Created by plugin Interval 300 seconds Group Not set Data source Producer and consumer metrics of the clients created in that run

docs.title: Consumer behaviour
docs.text: Behavior Value Consumer group identifier monitoring-client Automatic offset commit Disabled Records consumed None; the plugin never polls the consumer Offsets committed None Subscription Optional, through --topics or --topic_regex Effect on topic data None

docs.title: Metric groups
docs.text:
The plugin prefixes every module name with <module_prefix>. The metric part is <metric_group>.<metric_name>, where <node> is the numeric Kafka node identifier.

Source Metric group Example metric names Producer and consumer kafka-metrics-count count Producer producer-metrics connection-count, request-rate, request-latency-avg, outgoing-byte-rate, incoming-byte-rate Producer producer-node-metrics.node-<node> outgoing-byte-rate, incoming-byte-rate, request-rate, response-rate, request-latency-avg Consumer consumer-metrics connection-count, request-rate, request-latency-avg, incoming-byte-rate, outgoing-byte-rate Consumer consumer-node-metrics.node-<node> incoming-byte-rate, outgoing-byte-rate, request-rate, response-rate, request-latency-avg Consumer consumer-fetch-manager-metrics fetch-size-avg, fetch-size-max, bytes-consumed-rate, records-consumed-rate, records-lag-max Consumer consumer-coordinator-metrics commit-latency-avg, commit-latency-max, commit-rate, assigned-partitions

This list is a functional catalogue, not a fixed contract: the exact metric set depends on the Kafka client version and on the state of the clients at execution time. All generated modules use generic_data, with no unit and no description.

The metric definitions published by Kafka for its clients help interpret the values:

  • Consumer monitoring
  • Producer monitoring

docs.title: KVM monitoring plugin
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-09-03.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The KVM monitoring plugin monitors the state of a running KVM environment from Pandora FMS. To gather that state it uses two elements: virsh, which returns the state of the virtual machines (VMs) and their performance metrics, and libvirtd, which reports the state of the KVM server and the resources it is consuming.

The plugin is executed as a Pandora FMS agent plugin: each run prints the generated modules as XML on standard output, and every module belongs to the KVM module group.

docs.title: Compatibility and availability
docs.text: The plugin has been tested on CentOS, Ubuntu 24.04 and Rocky Linux 9, and it is expected to work on Linux-based systems. The package requires libvirt (libvirt-bin or libvirt) together with the virsh command.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. A Pandora FMS Endpoint deployed on your system.
  2. Perl 5.x or newer.
  3. Permission to execute virsh and to connect to the libvirtd instance, for the user that runs the plugin.
  4. The unzip command, required only when the plugin is deployed through collections.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
The plugin is distributed as the pandora_kvm script and its pandora_kvm.conf configuration file. Two deployment paths are available:

  • Manual upload — upload pandora_kvm and pandora_kvm.conf to the endpoint that will run the plugin.
  • Collections — deploy both files to the endpoints through Enterprise collections.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
Once the plugin files are in place, register the plugin in the Endpoint Plugins section of the endpoint:

The plugin reads the list of KVM servers to monitor from its configuration file, pandora_kvm.conf, which the script receives as its argument:

  • One user@server entry per line monitors that remote KVM host.
  • Several lines monitor several KVM servers with a single execution of the plugin.
  • The shipped file contains the single entry root@localhost, which monitors the libvirtd instance running on the host itself.
  • Lines that start with # are comments and are skipped.

Access to the monitored hosts must be unattended. When an entry points to a remote server, copy the SSH public key of the host that runs the plugin to the target servers.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually from the directory that contains it:

./pandora_kvm pandora_kvm.conf

A successful run prints one XML <module> block per generated module on standard output. The sample below shows the output of an execution in local mode — (local) prefix — for a KVM environment with two VMs, ubuntu22.04 running and crc shut:

<module>
    <name><![CDATA[(local) KVM Server status]]></name>
    <type></type>
    <data><![CDATA[1]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[Status of the KVM server. 1 instances of libvirtd]]></description>
    <module_group>KVM</module_group>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[(local) KVM Server RAM usage]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[0]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[RAM usage by the KVM server]]></description>
    <module_group>KVM</module_group>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[(local) KVM Server CPU usage]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[0]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[CPU usage by the KVM server]]></description>
    <module_group>KVM</module_group>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[(local) Number of VMs]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[2]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[Shows the number of available VMs in the KVM system]]></description>
    <module_group>KVM</module_group>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[(local) Status of ubuntu22.04]]></name>
    <type>generic_proc</type>
    <data><![CDATA[1]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[Status of ubuntu22.04: running]]></description>
    <module_group>KVM</module_group>
</module>

    <name><![CDATA[(local) Status of crc]]></name>

</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[(local) Virtual CPU usage of ubuntu22.04]]></name>
    <type></type>
    <data><![CDATA[0,5]]></data>

    <data><![CDATA[100.00]]></data>

    <module_group>KVM</module_group>
</module>

The generated modules are then visible in the Pandora FMS console:

If the run does not print module XML, see Troubleshoot.

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
For every monitored node the plugin reports the state of the KVM server and of each of its VMs:

  • Server level. (<node>) KVM Server status is 1 while libvirtd is running and 0 otherwise. (<node>) KVM Server RAM usage and (<node>) KVM Server CPU usage report the resources consumed by the KVM server, and (<node>) Number of VMs reports the total number of VMs in the KVM system.
  • VM level. (<node>) Status of <vm> is 1 while the VM is running and 0 otherwise; its description carries the libvirt state of the VM, such as running or shut.
  • Running VMs only. (<node>) CPU usage of <vm>, (<node>) Virtual CPU usage of <vm> and (<node>) Virtual memory usage of <vm> are generated only while the VM is running; the last two carry the % unit. The computation of each module is described in Generated modules.

Module names start with the node name between parentheses: (local) when the plugin monitors the local libvirtd instance, and the host of each user@server entry for remote nodes. All modules are emitted with module_group KVM.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
• A node produces no VM or resource modules — the plugin first checks whether libvirtd is running (ps aux | grep libvirtd | grep -v grep) and, when it finds no process, it emits only (<node>) KVM Server status with value 0 and skips the rest of the node. Check that libvirtd is running and that the user executing the plugin may see the process.
  • A remote KVM host is not monitored — the plugin reaches each remote entry over SSH, and the connection must not require user intervention. Copy the SSH public key of the host that runs the plugin to every target server, and make sure each entry uses the user@server form.
  • The plugin prints its usage text and no module XML — the configuration file passed as its argument does not exist, or more than one argument was given. Check the path and run the plugin with a single existing file, for example ./pandora_kvm pandora_kvm.conf.
  • A node with libvirtd running still reports no VMs — the plugin lists the VMs with virsh list --all and falls back to the read-only /usr/bin/virsh -r -c qemu:///system when that command returns no list. Check that virsh is installed and that the user executing the plugin can run it and connect to the libvirtd instance (the package requires libvirt, libvirt-bin or libvirt).

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The plugin monitors the KVM hosts listed in a plain-text configuration file, pandora_kvm.conf, which the script receives as its argument:

Entry Default Description user@server root@localhost One entry per line. Each entry monitors one KVM host as SSH user user on host server; several entries monitor several KVM servers with a single execution of the plugin # comment — A line that starts with # is a comment and is skipped

The file shipped with the plugin contains the single entry root@localhost, which monitors the libvirtd instance running on the host itself. To monitor remote servers, add one user@server entry per server, as described in Configure.

docs.title: Command-line execution
docs.text:
The plugin receives its configuration file as a command-line argument:

./pandora_kvm <config-file>
Condition Behavior The argument names an existing file The plugin monitors every host listed in the file and prints one XML <module> block per generated module on standard output The argument names a file that does not exist The plugin prints its usage text and stops without generating modules More than one argument is given The plugin prints its usage text and stops without generating modules No argument is given The plugin runs in local mode against the local libvirtd instance

On success, the module XML printed on standard output is the stream that the Pandora FMS agent ingests for the endpoint.

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text:
Module names start with the node name between parentheses: (local) when the plugin monitors the local libvirtd instance, or the host of the entry for remote nodes (server in user@server). In the names below, <node> is that prefix and <vm> is the name of a VM:

Module name Meaning Type Unit (<node>) KVM Server status Status of the KVM server: 1 while libvirtd is running, 0 otherwise generic_proc — (<node>) KVM Server RAM usage RAM usage by the KVM server generic_data — (<node>) KVM Server CPU usage CPU usage by the KVM server generic_data — (<node>) Number of VMs Total number of VMs in the KVM system (virsh list --all) generic_data — (<node>) Status of <vm> Status of the VM: 1 while running, 0 otherwise; the description carries the libvirt state, such as running or shut generic_proc — (<node>) CPU usage of <vm> Average of the CPU values reported by virsh vcpuinfo over the vCPUs of the VM; running VMs only generic_data — (<node>) Virtual CPU usage of <vm> Average of the VCPU values reported by virsh vcpuinfo over the vCPUs of the VM; running VMs only generic_data % (<node>) Virtual memory usage of <vm> Used over maximum memory of the VM (virsh dominfo); running VMs only generic_data %

docs.title: MarkLogic monitoring plugin
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The plugin monitors a MarkLogic installation from Pandora FMS. Each run reads the MarkLogic management REST API, takes the inventory of the installation — hosts, databases, forests and application servers — and builds one Pandora FMS agent per entity, holding the modules that describe its state, load and replication.

Nothing is installed on the MarkLogic nodes: the plugin runs on one host, connects over HTTP or HTTPS and delivers the generated agents to Pandora FMS. Every execution reads the whole inventory again, so the plugin keeps no state between runs and the agents always reflect the installation at the moment of the run.

Three groups of settings shape a run:

  • What it collects. Each entity type (hosts, databases, forests, application servers) is enabled or disabled independently, individual entities can be excluded by name, and each type produces either a summary set of modules or a detailed set.
  • How it is identified. A common prefix names every generated agent, and the agents land in a configured group with a configured interval.
  • Where it delivers. The generated agent documents travel with Tentacle or are copied into a local Pandora FMS data folder.

The entity agents are always delivered that way. The as_agent_plugin setting only selects what the plugin prints on standard output: enabled, it prints a Plugin message module for a Pandora FMS agent to collect; disabled, it prints the run result as a number for a server plugin module or a scheduled job.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence MarkLogic management REST API reachable on the configured host and port Required Every collection reads /manage/<api-version>/... with format=json from that host and port An ml_api_version value the installation accepts: V1, V2 or LATEST Required The value is a path segment of every request; the shipped configuration file documents these three values A MarkLogic user allowed to read the management API Required The plugin authenticates with ml_user, ml_pass and ml_realm A Perl runtime providing LWP::UserAgent, JSON, IO::Socket::INET6 and PerlIO::encoding Required The plugin does not start without them Network access from the plugin host to ml_server:ml_port Required The plugin connects to the management API from that host Network access from the plugin host to each application server port, when port checks are enabled Required The port check opens a TCP connection for each application server Network access to the Pandora FMS Tentacle port, 41121 by default, when delivering with Tentacle Required Tentacle delivery is the default mode MarkLogic server version Not validated No MarkLogic version matrix has been recorded for this addon; the shipped file documents LATEST as the MarkLogic 8 API version Operating system of the host that runs the plugin Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all its entries are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions; it is a catalogue-wide statement covering this addon, not a test record

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. A MarkLogic installation whose management API answers on the configured host and port. The plugin and its shipped configuration file use 8002.
  2. A MarkLogic account that can read the management API at /manage/<api-version>/.
  3. A host to run the plugin with the Perl runtime and the modules listed in Compatibility.
  4. A destination for the generated agents: the Pandora FMS Tentacle service, or a local data folder that the Pandora FMS server reads.
  5. Optionally, TCP reachability from the plugin host to each application server port, only when the port check is enabled.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
Download the addon from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.marklogic_monitoring

Install it on the host that will run it, keeping the configuration file pandora_ml.conf next to it. The plugin takes that file as its only argument, so any location is valid as long as the execution uses the same path.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
The plugin takes one argument, the path of its configuration file, and no command-line options:

perl /usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora_marklogic.pl <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

The file holds key = value lines, and the values in it override the built-in defaults. Two parsing rules apply:

  • A line whose first character is # is a comment. A line that starts with spaces is read as a key, so keep comments in the first column.
  • Keys and values are trimmed, and the value keeps any = after the first one. A repeated key keeps its last value; global_alerts is the exception, described in Module decoration.

The shipped pandora_ml.conf is a working base: it enables every entity type, selects summary detail for hosts, databases and forests and detailed information for application servers. Start from it rather than from an empty file. The check_* and show_detailed_* keys have no built-in value — a key missing from the file behaves as disabled, so an incomplete file collects nothing while still reporting a successful run.

docs.title: Connection to MarkLogic
docs.text:
This block is mandatory; without it the plugin has no API to read.

ml_server = <MARKLOGIC_HOST>
ml_port = 8002
ml_user = <USERNAME>
ml_pass = <PASSWORD>
ml_realm = public
use_ssl = 0
ml_api_version = LATEST
  • ml_server and ml_port build every request URL. The plugin uses exactly the port given: there is no fallback to the default port of the scheme.
  • use_ssl switches the scheme from http to https. Enable it when the management API is served over TLS.
  • ml_api_version is inserted as a path segment, so LATEST reads /manage/LATEST/hosts, and V1 or V2 read the corresponding API version. LATEST is used when the key is absent.
  • ml_realm is the authentication realm sent with the credentials. If the server challenges with a different realm, authentication fails.

docs.title: Delivery to Pandora FMS
docs.text:
The generated agent documents leave the plugin in one of two ways. Tentacle is the default and requires the Tentacle address:

mode = tentacle
tentacle_ip = <PANDORA_FMS_URL>
tentacle_port = 41121
tentacle_opts =
tentacle_client = /usr/bin/tentacle_client

The local copy writes the documents into a folder that the Pandora FMS server reads, which is the usual choice when the plugin runs on the Pandora FMS server itself:

mode = local
local_folder = /var/spool/pandora/data_in
  • mode is Tentacle only when its value is exactly tentacle. Any other value, including an empty one, copies the documents into local_folder.
  • tentacle_ip is required when delivering with Tentacle. tentacle_client must name an executable: an empty value does not fall back to tentacle_client in the PATH, and the delivery fails.
  • tentacle_opts passes extra options to the Tentacle client, separated by spaces.
  • temp is where each document is written before delivery, /tmp by default.
  • temp and local_folder must both exist, even when the plugin delivers with Tentacle and never copies anything. A missing directory stops the run before it collects any data.

docs.title: What it collects
docs.text:
Each entity type is collected only when its key is enabled. The shipped file enables all four and the port check:

check_hosts = 1
check_databases = 1
check_forests = 1
check_servers = 1
check_server_ports = 1

Boolean keys are numeric: a value greater than 0 enables the feature; 0, an empty value or a non-numeric value disables it.

The port check monitors the port of each application server and is part of the server collection, so it is only generated while check_servers is enabled.

To leave entities out, list their exact names, comma separated, in the exclusion key of their type. Names are matched as MarkLogic reports them:

exlude_hosts =
exlude_databases = Documents,Modules
exlude_forests =
exlude_servers = Manage

The keys are spelled exlude_*, without the c: the correctly spelled exclude_* is read as an unknown key and excludes nothing.

The detail level adds modules to each entity type:

show_detailed_hosts = 0
show_detailed_databases = 0
show_detailed_forests = 0
show_detailed_servers = 1

A type at 0 produces the summary set described in Understand the results; at 1 it produces every field the API reports for the entity.

docs.title: Agent identity
docs.text:
Every generated agent uses the same header, name scheme, group and interval:

agent_name_header = ML_
agent_group = MarkLogic
agent_interval = 300

The header is the only free part of the name; the rest is fixed by the entity type and the name MarkLogic reports, as described in Generated agents. Use a distinctive header, such as ML_, so the agents of several installations stay apart.

show_server_type_in_agentname (enabled in the shipped file) appends the application server type to those agent names:

show_server_type_in_agentname = 1

Turning it on or off renames every application server agent. The agents created under the previous name stop receiving data and new agents appear, so decide it before the first run.

agent_group is the group the agents are created in, by name, and agent_interval is their interval in seconds. Both apply to every generated agent.

docs.title: Module decoration
docs.text:
These settings apply to the generated modules:

#module_header = Custom_header_
#warning_instructions = Some text to guide the team
#critical_instructions = Some text to guide the team
#global_alerts = critical condition
  • module_header prefixes every module name of every entity.
  • warning_instructions, critical_instructions and unknown_instructions add the corresponding instruction text to every module.
  • global_alerts attaches an alert template to every module. Repeat the key once per template; the value is the alert template name.

docs.title: Create the agent group
docs.text:
The plugin can create the agent group through the Pandora FMS console API before delivering the agents:

autocreate_group = 0
api_url = http://<PANDORA_FMS_URL>/pandora_console/include/api.php
api_user = <USERNAME>
api_user_pass = <PASSWORD>
api_pass = <PASSWORD>
group_icon = Servers

api_url, api_user, api_user_pass and api_pass are used only for this creation; group_icon is the icon the new group receives. Set autocreate_group = 1 only when the group does not exist yet:

Do not enable group creation when the Pandora FMS installation is part of a metaconsole environment. Creating groups on a node with an active metaconsole can break the group synchronisation of the whole set of nodes.

docs.title: Run it from Pandora FMS
docs.text:
The plugin is a command, so Pandora FMS runs it the same way a person does: with the path of the configuration file. Two integration paths are available, and they can coexist:

  • As a plugin module of an agent. The Pandora FMS agent runs the command every interval and collects the Plugin message module the plugin prints. Enable as_agent_plugin = 1 in the file for this path.
  • As a server plugin module or a scheduled job. Keep as_agent_plugin = 0: the plugin prints the result as a number and writes the diagnostics to standard error, which is what a server plugin module records. Scheduling it from the system cron is described in Operate and troubleshoot.

The first path needs a Pandora FMS agent on the host that runs the plugin; the second does not and is the usual choice when the plugin already runs on the Pandora FMS server. Neither path installs anything on the MarkLogic nodes.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin with no argument to confirm that the runtime is complete. It prints its usage summary and stops:

perl /usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora_marklogic.pl

Pandora FMS Plugin for MarkLogic NoSQL Monitoring <version>

At least one parameter is needed by this plugin:
Usage: pandora_marklogic.pl pandora_ml.conf

Then run it with the configuration file:

perl /usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora_marklogic.pl <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

With as_agent_plugin = 1 a successful run prints one Plugin message module on standard output:

<module>
    <name><![CDATA[Plugin message]]></name>
    <type>generic_proc</type>
    <data><![CDATA[1]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[Execution OK]]></description>
</module>

With as_agent_plugin = 0 it prints 1 on standard output and the same message on standard error:

Plugin execution Result:[Execution OK]

A run that cannot read everything prints 0 instead of 1 and lists the failed requests in the description of the Plugin message module, or after Plugin execution Result: on standard error. For example:

Plugin execution Result:[ No response from http://<MARKLOGIC_HOST>:8002/manage/LATEST/hosts?format=json
  No response from http://<MARKLOGIC_HOST>:8002/manage/LATEST/databases?format=json
 ]

Finally, confirm that the agents arrived. The plugin deletes each temporary document only when its delivery succeeds, so a document left in temp is a failed delivery. In Pandora FMS, the generated agents appear with the configured header, and each one carries the modules described in Understand the results.

A run that reports Execution OK does not prove that every entity was collected: an empty inventory produces no error. Compare the number of agents with the inventory of the installation.

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
The plugin creates one agent per entity, in four families, plus a status module when it runs as an agent plugin. The families are independent: a type that is disabled, excluded or unreadable simply produces no agent.

  • Hosts report whether the node is online, whether its status view includes a critical issue, and its rate and load. These agents have no parent.
  • Databases report availability, capacity, replication lag and, in summary mode, size and indexing or rebalancing state.
  • Forests report whether the forest is open and enabled, its load, and its replication lag. Each forest agent is parented to the database that contains it, when databases are collected.
  • Application servers report whether the service is open and enabled, its detailed state, and whether its port accepts connections.

State modules are generic_proc or async_proc modules: 1 is a normal state, 0 is a failure, and a value the plugin cannot map is reported as 3 with the original state in the module description. A database that reports no state at all gets 2. Numeric modules carry the unit the API reports, so rates, loads and sizes keep their MarkLogic meaning. Summary mode keeps the modules that answer "is it healthy and how loaded is it"; detailed mode adds the fields of the entity and drops the summary-only modules, which is why it produces many more modules.

Plugin message summarises the run, not the installation: 1 means every request the plugin attempted returned data, 0 means at least one request failed or a delivery could not be completed.

docs.title: Scheduled execution
docs.text:
The plugin has no internal scheduler, so an external one runs it. A system cron entry on the host, for example:

*/5 * * * * root perl /usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora_marklogic.pl <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

Match the schedule to the agent interval you configured, so the agents receive data at the rate the console expects.

docs.title: Log
docs.text: The plugin writes a log file, pandora_ml.log in the working directory by default. Set log to an absolute path to place it elsewhere. Each run starts a new log, and a previous log larger than 3,200,000 bytes is renamed to .old before the new one starts. Every line carries a timestamp and the execution_id value, MarkLogic when the key is empty, which helps to tell concurrent executions apart.

docs.title: Timeout
docs.text: timeout bounds the whole run, not one request: when it expires the plugin stops with Exceeded execution time on standard error and a non-zero exit status, before delivering anything. The value is in seconds. The shipped file sets 2, which is short for an installation with many entities; raise it when runs are cut off. When the key is absent the plugin uses 60.

docs.title: Debugging a run
docs.text: extra_log = 1 writes the raw JSON answer of each database and forest to the log, in addition to the normal messages, while that type is in summary mode. Use it to check what the API returns for an entity that produces unexpected modules, and disable it afterwards: the output is large.

docs.title: Known limitations of this version
docs.text:
• Application server agents are delivered only while forests are collected. With check_forests = 0 and check_servers = 1 the servers are read but their agents are never delivered.
  • module_interval, module_tags and module_group have no effect. They are accepted and ignored, so the generated modules carry no tags and no module group, and the module interval is not set by the plugin.
  • status min-capacity carries the unit string as its value. The module reports the unit returned by the API instead of the numeric capacity, so its value is not a measurement.
  • The exclusion keys are spelled exlude_*. The correctly spelled exclude_* keys exclude nothing.
  • An empty tentacle_client does not fall back to the PATH.
  • There is no cluster agent. The installation itself has no agent, and application server agents have no parent; only forests are parented, to their database.
  • Detailed mode names modules after the API field. When the same field name appears in more than one section of an entity, the modules repeat the name, and fields with an enum or quantity unit produce no module at all.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Error: Cannot found temporal directory followed by the usage text — the configuration file could not be read, or temp does not exist. The plugin reports the missing temporary directory because it falls back to its defaults when the file cannot be opened, so check the path first, then the directory.
  • Error: Cannot found target directory ... — local_folder does not exist. The directory is required even when the plugin delivers with Tentacle.
  • Plugin message reports 0 with No response from <url> — that management API request failed. Check ml_server, ml_port, use_ssl, the credentials and ml_realm. A wrong port or a disabled management API fails every request of the run.
  • Only one entity type reports No response — its endpoint is unavailable or refused for that path, for example /forests behind a restricted account. The other types still produce agents.
  • Plugin message reports 0 with Failed to retrieve the group id for <server> — the group relation of an application server could not be read. Its modules are still generated.
  • Plugin message reports 0 with There was a problem sending file using tentacle — Tentacle delivery failed. Check tentacle_ip, tentacle_port, tentacle_client and the network path to the Pandora FMS server. The document stays in temp.
  • Plugin message reports 0 with There was a problem copying local file — local_folder is not writable by the user that runs the plugin.
  • Exceeded execution time — the run exceeded timeout. Raise it, or reduce the collected scope.
  • No modules on an entity that exists — its type is disabled, its name is in the exclusion list, or the run finished before reaching it. Enable the type, check the exclusion value and the log.
  • Fewer modules than expected on one entity — it is in summary mode. Enable the corresponding show_detailed_* key.
  • The agents stopped receiving data after a naming change — the name of the agent changed, so the old agent is orphaned. Check agent_name_header and show_server_type_in_agentname, and remove the agents left behind.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The file is passed as the only argument and holds key = value lines. Values in the file override the built-in defaults shown below.

any other value queries http:// ml_api_version No LATEST API version used as a path segment: V1, V2 or LATEST timeout No 60 (2 in the shipped file) Seconds the whole run may take log No pandora_ml.log Log file path execution_id No MarkLogic Text added to every log line; any other value prints the run result as a number agent_name_header No Empty Prefix of every generated agent name agent_group No MarkLogic Group of the generated agents, by name agent_interval No 300 Interval of the generated agents, in seconds show_server_type_in_agentname No Not set (disabled) 1 appends the application server type to its agent name check_hosts No Not set (disabled) 1 collects hosts; the shipped file sets 1 check_databases No Not set (disabled) 1 collects databases; the shipped file sets 1 check_forests No Not set (disabled) 1 collects forests and delivers the application server agents; docs.title: Pandora MongoDB remote / Atlas plugin
docs.text:
Article last updated: 2026-10-27.

Discovery integration recommended

For new installations use MongoDB Discovery, which is the recommended integration for this service. This plugin is the legacy path. The Marketplace entry states that this addon is no longer actively maintained.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The pandorafms.mongodb_remote_atlas addon monitors MongoDB databases from Pandora FMS over the network. Each run connects to a MongoDB deployment with a standard MongoDB connection string and turns the result into Pandora FMS agents and modules: database size and object counters, the statistics of every collection, and, when enabled, the connection, network, operation and latency counters of the server.

A deployment hosted on MongoDB Atlas is monitored the same way, with the mongodb+srv:// connection string that Atlas provides. Nothing is installed on the database host and no Atlas API key is used: the connection string is the only input.

The addon supports two execution models:

  • Server plugin mode (default): each run writes an agent_data XML file into the Pandora FMS data directory, and the Pandora FMS server ingests it.
  • Agent plugin mode (--as_agent_plugin 1): each run prints the generated modules as XML on standard output, for the Pandora FMS agent to ingest. This mode collects a single database.

The addon keeps no state between runs: every execution reads the metrics at that moment.

This page documents the remote monitoring plugin. The MongoDB Discovery addon (MongoDB Discovery) is a different product: it runs Discovery tasks and creates its agents from them, while this plugin creates its agents from its own runs.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Network access from the host that runs the plugin to the MongoDB listener Required The addon connects over the network; nothing is installed on the database host A MongoDB user allowed to run dbStats and collStats on the monitored databases Required Prerequisite for the database and collection modules, not a compatibility statement A MongoDB user with the clusterMonitor role when the server-status group is enabled Required Prerequisite for the serverStatus command, not a compatibility statement MongoDB server versions Not validated No test record establishes compatibility with a concrete MongoDB release MongoDB Atlas cluster tiers Not validated No test record establishes compatibility with a concrete Atlas tier Pandora FMS versions Not validated No test record establishes console or server version compatibility Operating system of the host that runs the plugin Not validated No test record establishes operating-system compatibility

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. A MongoDB deployment — a self-managed server, a replica set, a sharded cluster or an Atlas cluster — reachable from the host that runs the plugin.
  2. A MongoDB user with the roles described in MongoDB access.
  3. Python 3 and the addon dependencies on the host that runs the plugin. The addon ships a requirements.txt; install it with pip3 install -r requirements.txt from the addon directory. The MongoDB driver it lists is required in every case, and the DNS library it lists is what resolves the seed list of a mongodb+srv:// URI.
  4. Pandora FMS: the plugin server, when the addon runs in server plugin mode, or a Pandora FMS agent, when it runs in agent plugin mode.

docs.title: MongoDB access
docs.text:
The addon uses no Atlas administration interface, so an Atlas deployment is granted access like any other MongoDB deployment:

  • Monitoring the databases needs the dbStats and collStats actions on each monitored database. MongoDB's built-in read role includes both.
  • Collecting all databases (-a 1) also lists the databases of the deployment, which needs the listDatabases action. The built-in readAnyDatabase and clusterMonitor roles include it.
  • The server-status group (-s) reads the serverStatus command, which needs the clusterMonitor role. On Atlas, clusterMonitor is a built-in role that can be assigned to the database user.

No official source identifies a narrower set of privileges than these actions; grant only what the options you enable need.

For Atlas, also add the address of the host that runs the plugin to the deployment's access list, and use the connection string that the Atlas interface returns for the cluster.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the addon package from its Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.mongodb_remote_atlas

Register it in the console as a server plugin, or copy the addon script and its requirements.txt to the host that will run it and register the plugin by hand. Either way the plugin is executed by the Pandora FMS plugin server, on the server you select for each module. The plugin command is the path to the addon script on that server; the parameters are the options documented in Command line and in Register the plugin in the console.

The Marketplace entry states that this addon is no longer actively maintained or updated.

The commands in this page use pandora_mongodb as the script name, which is how the console registers it. If the copy on your server keeps the .py extension, use that name in the commands instead.

docs.title: Execution models
docs.text:
Server plugin mode is the default: the addon writes one XML file per agent into the Pandora FMS data directory, and the server ingests them. Select it by omitting --as_agent_plugin, or by giving it a value other than 1.

Agent plugin mode requires --as_agent_plugin 1 and a single database in -d. In this mode the addon prints the modules of the run as <module> blocks on standard output, without an agent_data wrapper, and writes no file. The agent that runs the plugin owns the modules, so the agent name, group and prefix have no effect in this mode.

docs.title: Collect one database or all of them
docs.text:
Exactly one of the two collection scopes must be selected, and the addon stops without collecting anything when neither is:

Scope Option Agents created A single database -d appdb One agent per run All databases the user can list -a 1 One agent per database

When both options are given, -a 1 wins and -d is ignored. All-databases mode skips every database whose name contains local, and processes every other database the user can list, including admin and config when the user can see them.

docs.title: Server plugin mode
docs.text:
This is the minimum command for one database, writing the agent file into the default data directory:

./pandora_mongodb -u '<MONGODB_URI>' -d appdb

Add the group, the agent prefix and the collection statistics of every collection in that database:

./pandora_mongodb -u '<MONGODB_URI>' -d appdb \
    -c 1 -p atlas_ -g mongodb --data_dir /var/spool/pandora/data_in

Collect every database instead, with the server-status counters:

./pandora_mongodb -u '<MONGODB_URI>' -a 1 -s 1 -p atlas_

appdb is an example database name. <MONGODB_URI> is the complete connection string: for a self-managed deployment the mongodb:// form with the host, the port, the user and the password, and for Atlas the mongodb+srv:// string the Atlas interface returns. Connection options such as the authentication database, a replica set name, TLS and a CA file belong to the URI; the addon has no separate option for them and passes the string to the MongoDB driver unchanged.

The prefix is prepended to the name of every agent the run creates; it does not change module names. Use the name of an existing console group: the addon writes the group name it is given and does not create groups. The user that runs the addon must be able to write into --data_dir.

docs.title: Agent plugin mode
docs.text:
./pandora_mongodb -u '<MONGODB_URI>' -d appdb -c 1 --as_agent_plugin 1

The modules of the run are printed on standard output. This mode supports one database: with -a 1 the addon writes the agent files as usual and the flag has no effect.

docs.title: Register the plugin in the console
docs.text:
Open Servers → Plugins → Register Plugin, or upload the addon package, which registers the plugin with its command and parameter string. The parameter string holds one macro per option:

-u _field1_ -s _field2_ -d _field3_ -a _field4_ -p _field5_ -c _field6_ -g _field7_ --data_dir _field8_ --as_agent_plugin _field9_

Each macro is filled when the plugin is used in a module:

Field Description Example value _field1_ Connection URI, credentials included. Enable Hide value <MONGODB_URI> _field2_ Server-status group 1 _field3_ Database to monitor appdb _field4_ All databases 1 _field5_ Agent name prefix atlas_ _field6_ Collection statistics 1 _field7_ Destination group mongodb _field8_ Pandora FMS data directory /var/spool/pandora/data_in _field9_ 1 for agent plugin mode, 0 for server plugin mode 0

That string runs as it is only when every macro has a value: an option whose macro is left empty is followed by the next option instead of a value, and the addon stops with error: argument -X/--X: expected one argument. It also cannot express a single-database run, because -a has no value that disables it. Edit the parameter string for the run you need instead:

Run Parameter string One database -u _field1_ -d _field2_ -p _field3_ -g _field4_ --data_dir _field5_ One database, with collection statistics -u _field1_ -d _field2_ -c _field3_ -p _field4_ -g _field5_ --data_dir _field6_ All databases -u _field1_ -a 1 -p _field2_ -g _field3_ --data_dir _field4_ Agent plugin mode -u _field1_ -d _field2_ -p _field3_ -g _field4_ --as_agent_plugin 1

Omit an optional option to disable it: -s 0 still enables the server-status group, and -c 0 still enables the collection statistics.

The plugin is then available when creating plugin modules, and each module fills the macros individually. The module runs on the Pandora FMS server selected for it, so one registered plugin serves several deployments.

docs.title: Credentials and transport
docs.text:
• The connection string carries the database user and password. The addon accepts it only as a command-line argument, so it is visible in the process list of the host while the run lasts and stays in the shell history when you type it. Store it in a module field with Hide value enabled, restrict who can read the module configuration in the console, and avoid passing it in a shared shell.
  • A plain mongodb:// connection without TLS sends the credentials and the collected metrics unencrypted. Use the tls options of the URI, which the addon passes to the driver, or restrict the deployment to a trusted network.
  • The addon stores no credential of its own: it holds no configuration file and keeps no state between runs.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the addon from a terminal on the host that will execute it, with the same options the plugin will use:

./pandora_mongodb -u '<MONGODB_URI>' -d appdb

A successful single-database run prints 1 and then the number of agents it created, so a run without the server-status group prints 1 twice, and writes one file per agent into the data directory:

/var/spool/pandora/data_in/mongo_appdb.1761483000.data

An all-databases run prints the number of agents it created: one per database, plus one when the server-status group is enabled.

./pandora_mongodb -u '<MONGODB_URI>' -a 1 -p atlas_

In agent plugin mode, a successful run prints one <module> block per generated module. This is an excerpt of a run over one database with collection statistics:

<module>
    <name><![CDATA[collections]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[12]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[database collections]]></description>
    <unit><![CDATA[]]></unit>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[dataSize]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[5242880]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[database dataSize]]></description>
    <unit><![CDATA[b]]></unit>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[size appdb.orders]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[1048576]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[size of appdb.orders]]></description>
    <unit><![CDATA[b]]></unit>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[status]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[1]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[database status]]></description>
    <unit><![CDATA[]]></unit>
</module>

In the console, the agent appears with the name <prefix><database> and its modules after the server has processed the data file. The agent and module inventory is described in Understand the results.

docs.title: Agents created
docs.text:
Property Value Agent name and alias The -p prefix followed by the database name, for example mongo_appdb Description database stats for a database agent, server status stats for the server-status agent Group The -g value, mongodb by default Address 127.0.0.1 Operating system and version Empty: the addon does not report them Interval Empty: the console default applies Timestamp The local time of the run

The number of agents depends on the collection scope and on the server-status group:

Run Agents -d One agent, named after the database -d -s Two agents: the database agent, which also holds the server-status modules, and a second agent named <prefix><host>, with the : of the host replaced by . -a 1 One agent per database, named after the database -a 1 -s The database agents, plus a separate agent named <prefix><host> with the server-status modules

The server-status modules are therefore part of the database agent only in a single-database run.

docs.title: Module groups
docs.text:
• Database group. Always collected for every agent of the run. It reports the counters and sizes of the database and ends with status, which carries the ok value of the statistics command.
  • Collection group. Collected when -c is present. Each collection of the database contributes one module per statistic, named after the collection namespace <database>.<collection>.
  • Server-status group. Collected when -s is present. It reports the connections, network, opcounters and opLatencies counters of the MongoDB server as one module per key returned by the deployment.

Every module of the database and collection groups is created only when the deployment reports the corresponding field, so the list an agent receives depends on its server version and storage engine. The counters of the server-status group follow the keys present in the serverStatus output of that deployment.

The full inventory is in Generated modules.

docs.title: Scheduling and manual execution
docs.text:
• The addon has no daemon mode and no internal scheduler: it runs once and exits. When registered as a server plugin, Pandora FMS executes it with the interval of the module; outside Pandora FMS, schedule it with cron.
  • Every run opens its own connection and closes it at exit, so the addon can be executed manually at any time without disturbing the deployment.
  • A run that collects all databases of a large deployment reads the statistics of every collection and every database in one process. Keep the collection group disabled, or reduce the scope to single databases, when the run does not finish within the module timeout.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• The optional groups cannot be disabled by value. -s 0 and -c 0 still enable the server-status and collection groups, because the addon only checks whether the option was given. Omit the option to disable the group.
  • -a accepts one enabling value. Use -a 1. Any other value leaves both collection scopes disabled and the run stops with an error.
  • The addon needs either -d or -a 1. Without either of them it prints a Python NameError traceback instead of a usage message.
  • Agent plugin mode ignores -a. With -a 1 the agent files are written even when --as_agent_plugin 1 is present; the flag only works with -d.
  • The prefix applies to agent names only, not to module names.
  • Per-collection avgObjSize is collected only in single-database mode. An all-databases run omits it from the collection group.
  • Collection statistics have no collection filter. Every collection of the database is read.
  • There is no timeout, retry or debug option. The plugin server timeout applies to the whole run, and diagnostics are limited to the printed error.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
• Error: <message> followed by exit status 1 — the run stopped. The message is the exception the MongoDB driver or the statistics command returned. For a connection or authentication failure, check the URI, the credentials it carries, the network path and, on Atlas, the access list of the deployment.
  • Error: not authorized on <database> to execute command ... — the user cannot run dbStats or collStats on that database. Grant the actions listed in MongoDB access.
  • error: argument -s/--server_status: expected one argument (exit status 2) — an option in the command line or in the console parameter string is followed by another option instead of a value. Give it a value or remove the option.
  • NameError: name 'count' is not defined — neither -d nor a valid -a 1 was given, or -a received a value other than 1.
  • NameError: name 'db' is not defined — the server-status group was enabled in a run that collected no database.
  • KeyError: 'freeStorageSize', KeyError: 'scaleFactor' or another KeyError — the deployment does not report that field in the collection statistics, so the collection group cannot be built. Disable -c for that deployment.
  • KeyError: 'opLatencies' or another KeyError in the server-status group — the serverStatus output of the deployment does not include that section. Disable -s.
  • Error: [Errno 13] Permission denied — the user that runs the addon cannot write into --data_dir. Fix the permissions or point the option at a writable directory.
  • Error: [Errno 17] File exists — a data file for the same agent and the same second already exists. Repeat the run.
  • The agent appears with fewer modules than expected — the deployment does not report those fields. Compare the agent with the conditions in Generated modules.
  • No agent appears in the console — check that the data directory of the run is the one the Pandora FMS server reads, that the file was created, and that the -g group exists in the console.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
./pandora_mongodb -u <MONGODB_URI> [options]
Name Required Default Description -u, --uri Yes — MongoDB connection string. It carries the hosts, the credentials and the connection options, including the TLS options -d, --database One of -d or -a 1 — Database to monitor -a, --alldatabases One of -d or -a 1 0 1 monitors every database the user can list, except those whose name contains local -s, --server_status No Disabled Any value, including 0, enables the server-status group. Omit the option to disable it -c, --collectionstats No Disabled Any value, including 0, enables the collection statistics. Omit the option to disable it -p, --prefix No mongo_ Prefix of the name of every agent the run creates -g, --group No mongodb Group of the agent in the console; the addon does not create groups --data_dir No /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Directory where the agent files are written in server plugin mode --as_agent_plugin No 0 1 prints the modules on standard output instead of writing agent files. Only with -d --as_discovery_plugin No 0 1 replaces the trailing count with a JSON summary of the agents created. It does not change what is collected or written

-h and --help print the option list. The help header reports the plugin version as 250821.

docs.title: Command output
docs.text: Run Standard output -d, server plugin mode 1, and the number of agents created on the next line -a 1, server plugin mode The number of agents created: one per database, plus one when the server-status group is enabled -d --as_agent_plugin 1 One <module> block per module, then the number of agents created Any run with --as_discovery_plugin 1 A JSON summary with Agents (databases) created by the plugin and the list of databases, instead of the trailing count

docs.title: Database modules
docs.text:
Collected for every agent of the run. The Field column is the field of the dbStats output that each module reads; the module is created only when the deployment returns it.

Module Type Field Unit collections generic_data collections — views generic_data views — objects generic_data objects — avgObjSize generic_data avgObjSize b dataSize generic_data dataSize b storageSize generic_data storageSize b totalFreeStorageSize generic_data totalFreeStorageSize b numExtents generic_data numExtents — indexes generic_data indexes — indexSize generic_data indexSize — fileSize generic_data fileSize b nsSizeMB generic_data nsSizeMB mb status generic_data ok —

docs.title: Collection modules
docs.text:
Collected when -c is present, one set per collection. <ns> is the namespace of the collection, for example appdb.orders.

Module Type Field Unit size <ns> generic_data size b count <ns> generic_data count b avgObjSize <ns> generic_data avgObjSize b storageSize <ns> generic_data storageSize b freeStorageSize <ns> generic_data freeStorageSize b capped<ns> generic_data capped, as 1 or 0 — nindexes <ns> generic_data nindexes — totalIndexSize <ns> generic_data totalIndexSize — totalSize <ns> generic_data totalSize b scaleFactor <ns> generic_data scaleFactor — status <ns> generic_data ok —

avgObjSize <ns> is generated in single-database mode only, and capped<ns> has no space between the name and the namespace.

docs.title: Server-status modules
docs.text:
Collected when -s is present, one module per key the deployment returns. All of them are generic_data without a unit.

Module Section of serverStatus server_status.connections <key> connections server_status.network <key> network server_status.operations <key> opcounters server_status.opetationlatencies.reads <key> opLatencies.reads server_status.opetationlatencies.writes <key> opLatencies.writes server_status.opetationlatencies.commands <key> opLatencies.commands

The opetationlatencies segment of the name is spelled that way in the module names the addon generates.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
In server plugin mode the addon writes one file per agent:

<data_dir>/<agent_name>.<epoch>.data

The file contains an agent_data document with the attributes of Agents created and one <module> block per module. The addon creates the file exclusively, so a second run for the same agent within the same second fails instead of overwriting the first file.
