docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Ver. 03-06-2026

This document describes the functionality of the Oculix plugin and its integration with PandoraFMS. The Oculix plugin enables visual automation of transactions through screenshots, image comparison, and script execution, generating monitoring modules in PandoraFMS.

Type: Plug-in server

docs.title: Compatibility matrix
docs.text: Systems where tested Rocky Linux, Windows Server 2022 Systems where it works Any Linux or Windows system

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Java Runtime Environment The plugin runs an Oculix JAR file, so it is necessary to have Java installed and accessible in the system PATH. Java 17 or higher is recommended.

2. Graphical environment The plugin uses mss to take screenshots, so it requires a running X11 server (graphical environment). If running in a headless environment, a virtual X server such as Xvfb can be used.

3. The agent runs in process mode, and the session cannot be locked or closed. Once launched by the Pandora FMS Agent, it must run in process mode; if it runs in service mode, it will not function properly. Additionally, it will not be possible to lock the desktop session, so it is recommended to use it on virtual machines.

3. Write permissions The plugin needs write permissions in the artifacts directory (--artifacts) to store screenshots, baseline images, and diffs.

4. Tentacle (optional) If the tentacle transfer mode is used, the tentacle_client binary must be installed and accessible on the system.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Script execution parameters

Parameter Description --script Path to the Oculix script to execute. This parameter is mandatory. Supports commas for multiple phases: --script a.py,b.py,c.py --jar Path to the Oculix JAR file. This parameter is mandatory. --conf Path to the .conf configuration file with Pandora and connection parameters. This parameter is mandatory. --workspace Working directory for Oculix script execution. Optional. --debug Debug verbosity (0 silent → 3 very verbose) --console Enables Oculix console mode. Activated with the flag. --native-access Enables --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED in Java execution. Activated with the flag. --checkpoint Enables baseline logic: if no reference image exists, creates one from the current screenshot. Activated with the flag. --artifacts Directory where screenshots, baselines, and diffs are stored. Default "artifacts". --phase-names Phase names separated by commas (e.g. Login,Search,Logout). If omitted, the script stem is used. Also configurable in .conf as phase_names. CLI overrides .conf. --transaction Global transaction name. If set, Global_Status_{name}, Global_Time_{name} and Global_Last_Image_{name} modules are generated. Also configurable in .conf as transaction_name. CLI overrides .conf. --retries Number of retries for the full transaction (default: 1). If any phase fails, all phases are retried from the start. Also configurable in .conf as phase_retries. CLI overrides .conf. --post-command Command to execute after all phases complete. CLI-only argument, not available in .conf.

Pandora configuration parameters (.conf file)

Parameter Description agent_name Name of the agent that will contain the modules. Default: "{script} Oculix". agents_group_name Agent group in PandoraFMS. Default "Oculix". module_prefix Prefix for all modules created by the plugin. interval Agent monitoring interval in seconds. Default 300. agent_plugin Output mode: 1 prints XML to console, 0 writes to file and transfers. Default 0. temporal Temporary directory for XML files. Default "/tmp". transfer_mode Transfer mode: "tentacle" or "local". Default "tentacle". tentacle_client Path to the tentacle_client binary. Default "tentacle_client". tentacle_ip IP address of the tentacle server. Default "127.0.0.1". tentacle_port Tentacle connection port. Default "41121". tentacle_opts Extra options for tentacle connection. data_dir PandoraFMS data directory for local transfer. Default "/var/spool/pandora/data_in/".

docs.title: Execution format
docs.text:
./pandora_oculix.exe --script <path to oculix script> \
--conf <path to .conf file> \
--jar <path to oculix JAR> \
[--workspace <working directory>] \
[--debug <debug level>] \
[--console] \
[--native-access] \
[--checkpoint] \
[--artifacts <artifacts directory>] \
[--phase-names <phase names, comma-separated>] \
[--transaction <transaction name>] \
[--retries <number of retries>] \
[--post-command <command to execute after completion>]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Single script (backward compatible):

./pandora_oculix.exe --script scripts/login.py --conf oculix.conf --jar oculix.jar --debug 1

With baseline and console:

./pandora_oculix.exe --script scripts/login.py --conf oculix.conf --jar oculix.jar --console --checkpoint

Multi-phase transaction with retries:

./pandora_oculix.exe --script login.py,search.py,logout.py --phase-names Login,Search,Logout --transaction "MiApp" --retries 2 --conf oculix.conf --jar oculix.jar --debug 1

With post-command after completion:

./pandora_oculix.exe --script login.py,search.py,logout.py --phase-names Login,Search,Logout --transaction "MiApp" --post-command "echo Done" --conf oculix.conf --jar oculix.jar --debug 1

docs.title: Configuration in PandoraFMS
docs.text:
To configure the plugin in PandoraFMS, follow these steps:

1. Upload the plugin to PandoraFMS, e.g. in the following path:

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin

2. Upload the Oculix JAR and the required .ocx scripts to the server, in a path accessible by the plugin.

3. Create the .conf configuration file with Pandora parameters:

[CONF]
agent_name=Oculix Login Test
agents_group_name=Oculix
module_prefix=
interval=300
agent_plugin=1
temporal=/tmp
transfer_mode=tentacle
tentacle_client=tentacle_client
tentacle_ip=127.0.0.1
tentacle_port=41121
tentacle_opts=
data_dir=/var/spool/pandora/data_in/

4. Go to the plugins section and create a new one:

Add a name, description, and timeout.

5. Add the plugin path in the command and the necessary parameters for its execution.

For each parameter, a macro must be configured. The macro syntax is: `_fieldx_`, where x is the positional number of the parameter.

Example plugin command:

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora_oculix.py --script _field1_ --jar _field2_ --conf _field3_

6. Configure the macros above, adding the parameter value in each one:

Example macros:

  • _field1_ = /opt/oculix/scripts/login.py
  • _field2_ = /opt/oculix/oculix.jar
  • _field3_ = /opt/oculix/oculix.conf

7. Once configured, a module must be created in an agent to run the plugin. In an agent's module menu, create a new plugin-type module:

8. In the module configuration menu, give it a name, select the previously configured plugin, and click "create".

9. The agent with the modules will be created on the next execution of the plugin.

docs.title: Agent and modules generated by the plugin
docs.text:
The plugin creates an agent with the name specified in agent_name (default "{script} Oculix") containing the following modules:

Module name Type Description {script_name} status generic_proc Script execution status. Value 1 if execution was successful, 0 if there was an error or visual difference. {script_name} time generic_data Script execution time in seconds. {script_name} last_image async_string Screenshot in base64 format (PNG image). Only generated when the status is 0 (failure or visual difference).

Example: for a script called login, the generated modules would be:

login status
login time
login last_image

docs.title: Pandora Office 365 Monitoring
docs.text:
Article last updated: 2026-10-27.

Discovery integration recommended

For new installations use Office 365 Discovery, which is the recommended integration for this service. This plugin is the legacy path. The Marketplace entry states that this addon is no longer actively maintained.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Pandora Office 365 Monitoring plugin reports the health of a Microsoft 365 tenant in Pandora FMS. Each run authenticates against Microsoft Entra ID with the credentials of an application registration, reads the health overview of every Microsoft 365 service the tenant subscribes to, and publishes it as one agent with two modules per service: the status Microsoft reports for that service and the list of its unresolved incidents.

The plugin runs as a server plugin: it builds the agent document and delivers it to a Pandora FMS data directory or sends it through Tentacle. It does not print module XML on standard output, so it cannot be run as an agent plugin.

It can also read the service announcements — the messages Microsoft publishes about incidents and planned maintenance — and send them to the Pandora FMS log collector.

This page documents the server plugin pandorafms.office365_plugin. Discovering Microsoft 365 tenants and generating their agents from a Discovery task is a different addon: see Office 365 Discovery.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.office365_plugin, version 1.0 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions. It is a general compatibility statement covering the plugin, not a test record for it The Pandora FMS plugin server, enabled Required The addon is a server plugin and is executed by the plugin server Network access from the host that runs the plugin to login.microsoftonline.com and graph.microsoft.com over HTTPS Required The plugin obtains its token and reads its data from those two hosts; it exposes no option to change either endpoint A Microsoft Entra ID application with the permissions in Microsoft Graph permissions Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement Operating system of the host that runs the plugin Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version

The Marketplace entry states that this addon is no longer actively maintained and that alternative plugins in the library should be considered. That notice is a maintenance statement by the publisher; this page describes the behaviour of version 1.0 as it is distributed.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the host that runs the plugin to login.microsoftonline.com and graph.microsoft.com.
  2. A Microsoft Entra ID application registered in the tenant to monitor, with a client secret and the application permissions described below.
  3. The tenant ID, the client ID and the client secret of that application.
  4. Pandora FMS:
    • The plugin server enabled, to execute the registered plugin.
    • A data directory processed by the data server, or a Tentacle server that receives the agent document. When the delivery uses Tentacle, the tentacle_client executable must be available in PATH on the host that runs the plugin.
  5. The addon package installed in Pandora FMS through the console.

docs.title: Microsoft Graph permissions
docs.text:
The plugin requests an application token with the https://graph.microsoft.com/.default scope, so it receives the application permissions granted to the registered application, with no signed-in user. Each data set it reads is covered by the following Microsoft Graph application permissions:

Microsoft Graph request Used for Application permission /admin/serviceAnnouncement/healthOverviews?$expand=issues Service status and unresolved incidents ServiceHealth.Read.All /admin/serviceAnnouncement/messages Service announcements sent as log entries ServiceMessage.Read.All

Grant only what the run collects: ServiceMessage.Read.All is needed only when log collection is enabled with -l. Both permissions require administrator consent. Do not grant the ReadWrite variants.

The client secret is a credential: store it only in the plugin configuration and revoke it in Microsoft Entra ID when it is no longer needed.

docs.title: Register the application in Microsoft Entra ID
docs.text:
1. Open Microsoft Entra ID and register a new application in App registrations. Register it in the tenant you want to monitor.
  2. In Certificates & secrets, create a client secret and copy its value immediately: Azure shows it only once.
  3. From the application overview, copy the Application (client) ID and the Directory (tenant) ID.
  4. In API permissions, add the Microsoft Graph application permissions listed above and grant administrator consent.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.office365_plugin

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, the plugin is registered with its parameters and becomes available when creating plugin modules.

The contents of the distributed package could not be inspected for this page, so no build or dependency-installation procedure is prescribed here. Use the pandora_o365 executable that the package installs on the Pandora FMS server.

docs.title: Credentials and transport
docs.text:
• The client secret is passed as the value of -s. It appears in the shell history of a manual run and in the operating system process list while the plugin executes, including runs started by the plugin server.
  • The plugin has no option to read the credentials from a protected file: the console plugin fields and the command line are its only input surfaces. Restrict access to the host that runs the plugin and to the users who can edit plugin modules, and revoke and reissue the secret if it is exposed.
  • Authentication and every data request go to the fixed Microsoft endpoints over HTTPS. The plugin offers no way to change them and exposes no proxy option, so a proxy in the path is outside its configuration.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text: The plugin has no configuration file: every setting is a command-line option, documented in Command-line parameters. Choose how it is executed first.

docs.title: Register the plugin in the console
docs.text:
1. Open Servers → Plugins and click Register Plugin.
  2. Set the name, the plugin type Standard, an optional maximum timeout and a description.
  3. In Plugin command, enter the full path of the pandora_o365 executable on the Pandora FMS server, for example <PATH_TO_PLUGIN>/pandora_o365.
  4. In Plugin parameters, pass the options with the plugin macros _field1_, _field2_, ... as placeholders:
-c _field1_ -t _field2_ -s _field3_ -a _field4_ -g _field5_
  1. In Macro parameters, describe each field. The example uses these values:
Field Description Example value _field1_ Application (client) ID <CLIENT_ID> _field2_ Directory (tenant) ID <TENANT_ID> _field3_ Client secret value; mark Hide value — _field4_ Value hashed into the agent name and used as the agent alias Pandora_O365 _field5_ Pandora FMS group for the generated agent <GROUP_NAME>

The plugin writes the agent document itself, so the data directory matters:

  • When the plugin is registered on the Pandora FMS server that processes the documents, the default -d /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ is the right destination and no extra option is needed.
  • When it is registered on a remote Pandora FMS server, add --tentacle_address 127.0.0.1 (and --tentacle_port if the Tentacle server does not listen on 41121), so the document is sent to the Tentacle server of the machine that executes the module.

The module that uses the plugin does not hold the service status: the status and incident modules appear in the generated O365_… agent, not in the agent that owns the module. What the plugin prints on standard output is the summary number described in The printed summary number.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
This is the minimum run: it collects the service status and incidents and writes the agent document to the local data directory.

./pandora_o365 -c <CLIENT_ID> -t <TENANT_ID> -s <CLIENT_SECRET>

A full run, with an explicit agent identifier, prefix, group, interval and log collection:

./pandora_o365 -c <CLIENT_ID> -t <TENANT_ID> -s <CLIENT_SECRET> \
    -a Pandora_O365 -p O365 -g <GROUP_NAME> -i 300 \
    -d /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ -l

./pandora_o365 -h prints the usage summary with every option and exits without contacting Microsoft.

docs.title: Agent name, alias and group
docs.text:
The -a value does not name the agent: it is hashed into the agent name and copied to the alias.

  • Agent name: <prefix>_<MD5 hash of the -a value>.
  • Agent alias: <prefix>_<-a value>.

With the defaults (-a Pandora_O365, -p O365) the agent is named O365_dab294b287a0bc7a39f3596e17e2ef50 and its alias is O365_Pandora_O365. The name is the identifier Pandora FMS uses for the agent, so the readable string lives in the alias. Changing -a or -p produces a different agent name, and therefore a new agent in the console: set both explicitly and keep them stable across runs.

The -g value is written into the agent document. It must be a group that exists in the console; otherwise the agent is assigned to the default unknown group.

docs.title: Choose what to collect
docs.text:
Goal Options Status and incident modules only Default; do not pass -l Status, incidents and service announcements Add -l Service announcements only Add -l -n; -n skips the status and incident modules

Log collection sends the messages to the log collector configured for the generated agent, so that collector must exist in the Pandora FMS environment.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually with a scratch data directory, so the document can be inspected before Pandora FMS ingests it:

mkdir -p /tmp/o365-check/
./pandora_o365 -c <CLIENT_ID> -t <TENANT_ID> -s <CLIENT_SECRET> -a Pandora_O365 -d /tmp/o365-check/

The directory must exist and be writable, and the -d value must end with /: the plugin concatenates the directory and the file name without adding a separator, so -d /tmp/o365-check produces a file named /tmp/o365-checkO365_….data next to the directory instead of inside it.

A successful run prints a single number as its last line (see The printed summary number) and writes:

/tmp/o365-check/O365_dab294b287a0bc7a39f3596e17e2ef50.<EPOCH>.data

<EPOCH> is the time of the run in seconds. The document has one module pair per service the tenant subscribes to; this is an excerpt with illustrative values:

<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<agent_data agent_name='O365_dab294b287a0bc7a39f3596e17e2ef50' agent_alias='O365_Pandora_O365' parent_agent_name='' description='Agent generated by pandora_o365 plugin' version='' os_name='' os_version='' timestamp='2026/10/26 10:00:00' address='127.0.0.1' group='unknown' interval='300'>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[O365_Exchange_status]]></name>
    <type>generic_data_string</type>
    <data><![CDATA[serviceOperational]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[O365_Exchange Online]]></description>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[O365_Exchange_active_issues]]></name>
    <type>generic_data_string</type>
    <data><![CDATA[EX1: Mail flow delay]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[Exchange Online Issues Ids]]></description>
</module>
</agent_data>

In the console, the generated agent appears with its two modules per service after the Pandora FMS server processes the document:

Check, in this order:

  1. The last line of the output is a number, and no ERROR or Error line is printed on standard error.
  2. The .data file exists in the directory passed to -d, and its <agent_data> name and alias are the ones expected.
  3. Every service the tenant subscribes to has a _status module, and one _active_issues module.
  4. The agent appears in the console under the configured group, with the modules receiving data at the next execution.

docs.title: The agent
docs.text:
One execution produces one agent, whatever the number of services: the services are modules of that agent, not separate agents.

Agent property Value Name <prefix>_<MD5 hash of the -a value> Alias <prefix>_<-a value> Description Agent generated by pandora_o365 plugin Address 127.0.0.1 Group The -g value (unknown by default) Interval The -i value (300 by default) Operating system fields Empty

docs.title: Modules per service
docs.text:
For every service returned by Microsoft Graph, the agent has:

Module Type Description <prefix>_<service id>_status generic_data_string The status Microsoft Graph reports for the service, verbatim <prefix>_<service id>_active_issues generic_data_string <issue id>: <issue title> for each incident that is not resolved, concatenated with no separator between incidents; the literal None when the service has no unresolved incident

<service id> is the id Graph returns for the service, and the status module description is <prefix>_<service name> (for example O365_Exchange Online); the incident module description is <service name> Issues Ids.

The service set is not fixed by the plugin: it is whatever the tenant subscribes to at execution time, so two tenants, or the same tenant after a subscription change, do not necessarily produce the same module names.

Two consequences of the value format:

  • The status module carries a text status. The plugin applies no threshold and no mapping to Pandora FMS warning or critical states, so a degraded service does not by itself raise an alert. Alert on the value in the module definition if you need one.
  • Because incidents are concatenated without a separator, two unresolved incidents produce a value such as EX1: Mail flow delayEX2: Mailbox access, which is hard to read and to compare. A single incident has no separator problem, and None is unambiguous.

Microsoft documents the possible status values for a service health object (serviceOperational, investigating, restoringService, serviceDegradation, serviceInterruption, and the other values of the serviceHealthStatus enumeration). The module publishes the string exactly as received.

docs.title: Log entries
docs.text:
With -l, the plugin reads the service announcements and writes one log entry per announcement, with the source <prefix>_<service> of the first service the announcement lists.

  • The request skips the first 100 announcements ($skip=100) and does not follow the paging of the response. A tenant with fewer than 100 announcements therefore produces no log entries at all, and only the announcements after the first 100 are ever collected.
  • The value of the entry is the whole announcement converted to text: the message is serialised as a key/value text with the HTML body turned into plain text, not as JSON and not as the body alone. Entries are long and their keys keep the quoting of that serialisation.
  • The log entries are delivered in a second agent document with the same agent name as the status document; see Operation for the consequence in local delivery.

docs.title: Operation
docs.text:
• The plugin keeps no state between runs: every execution reads the tenant health at that moment and delivers a complete document, so it can be run manually at any time.
  • Schedule it from Pandora FMS through the plugin module or the plugin server schedule. -i only sets the interval recorded in the agent document; the real frequency is the one of the schedule, and -i should be equal to or greater than it.
  • The exit status is 0 in almost every case, including a failed data or log collection: the plugin prints a summary number and exits successfully. Read the number instead of the exit status.
  • Tentacle delivery: the document is written to --tmp and sent with tentacle_client. If the transfer fails, the plugin writes Tentacle error on standard error, the file stays in --tmp, and it still prints its summary number and exits with 0. Check standard error when the agent does not appear.
  • Local delivery with -l: the status document and the log document have the same agent name and are named after the second of the run. When both are written within the same second, the second write fails with ERROR - Could not write file: [Errno 17] File exists and the run stops with status 1. The status document of that run is already in the data directory; the log entries are lost. When the collection of the announcements takes more than a second, the two writes fall in different seconds and both succeed.
  • --utf8 0 writes the incident value as a byte string (b'…') instead of text. Leave the default 1 unless the environment requires raw bytes.
  • The -d and --tmp values are concatenated with the file name without adding a separator: keep the trailing / in both.

docs.title: The printed summary number
docs.text:
The last line of a run is the sum of one contribution per collection stage:

Status collection Log collection (-l) Printed number Collected Not requested 2 Collected Collected 3 Collected Failed 1 Failed Collected 0 Failed Failed -2 Skipped (-n) Collected 1 Skipped (-n) Failed -1 Skipped (-n) Not requested 0

A run that cannot authenticate, or whose status request is rejected by Microsoft Graph, does not reach this summary: it exits with status 1 and prints an error.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Error Auth Token: 'dict' object has no attribute 'reason', exit status 1 — Microsoft Entra ID rejected the token request (wrong tenant ID, client ID or client secret, or an expired secret). The message is the plugin's own error, not the text Microsoft returns: the authentication error handler fails before it can print the HTTP reason, so the real cause is not shown. Verify the three values and the secret expiry in Microsoft Entra ID, and retry.
  • Error requesting url: <reason> (<status>) on https://graph.microsoft.com/..., exit status 1 — Microsoft Graph rejected the health request. A 401 points to a token that Microsoft did not accept; a 403 points to a missing application permission or to consent that was not granted. Check the permissions in Microsoft Graph permissions and grant administrator consent again.
  • The run stops with status 157 and prints no summary — the request for the service announcements failed. This stage exits with that status instead of reporting it, so a 403 here means ServiceMessage.Read.All is missing while -l is enabled. Add the permission or drop -l.
  • error data: ... or error logs: ... with a summary number — Microsoft answered, but the response did not have the expected structure and the document of that stage was not written. Repeat the run; if it persists, check the same request manually with Microsoft Graph and verify the permissions.
  • No agent appears in the console — check, in this order: the .data file was written to the directory that the Pandora FMS server processes; the -d or --tmp value ends with /; the -g value names an existing group; in Tentacle delivery, standard error shows no Tentacle error.
  • The agent appears, but the modules have no data — the document was written by a different execution user than the one the data server reads with, or the data directory is not the one the server processes. Compare the file owner and the directory with the data server configuration.
  • A second agent appears after a configuration change — the agent name is derived from -p and -a. Restore the previous values, or accept the new agent and delete the old one in the console.
  • No log entries although -l is set — the tenant has fewer than 100 announcements, the messages request failed (status 157), or the log collector is not configured for the agent.

docs.title: Command-line parameters
docs.text: Name Required Default Description -c, --clientid Yes — Application (client) ID of the Microsoft Entra ID application -t, --tenantid Yes — Directory (tenant) ID; it is part of the token endpoint -s, --secret Yes — Client secret value of the application -a, --agent_name No Pandora_O365 Value hashed into the agent name and used as the agent alias. It is not the agent name, and its help text advertises a different default (pandora_o365) -p, --prefix No O365 Prefix for the agent name, the agent alias, the module names and the log source -g, --group No unknown Pandora FMS group written into the agent document. It must exist in the console -i, --interval No 300 Agent interval in seconds, written into the document -d, --data_in No /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Local data directory for the agent document. Used only when no Tentacle address is set. Keep the trailing / -l, --logs No Off Send the service announcements to the Pandora FMS log collector -n, --nodata No Off Skip the status and incident modules; useful together with -l --tentacle_address No None Tentacle server address. When set, the document is sent through Tentacle instead of written to -d --tentacle_port No 41121 Tentacle server port --tmp No /tmp/ Directory where the document is written before the Tentacle transfer. Keep the trailing / --utf8 No 1 1 writes text values. 0 writes them as raw bytes

docs.title: Command-line execution
docs.text:
pandora_o365 -c <CLIENT_ID> -t <TENANT_ID> -s <CLIENT_SECRET> [-a <NAME>] [-p <PREFIX>] [-g <GROUP>] [-i <SECONDS>] [-d <DIR>] [-l] [-n] [--tentacle_address <HOST>] [--tentacle_port <PORT>] [--tmp <DIR>] [--utf8 <0|1>]
Condition Behavior A required option (-c, -t, -s) is missing The usage summary is printed on standard error and the run exits with status 2, without contacting Microsoft -h or --help The usage summary is printed and the run exits with status 0, without contacting Microsoft The token request is rejected An authentication error is printed on standard error and the run exits with status 1 The health request is rejected The HTTP reason and status are printed and the run exits with status 1 The announcements request is rejected The run exits with status 157 A collection stage fails after a successful request error data: … or error logs: … on standard error; the run continues and prints the summary number A Tentacle transfer fails Tentacle error on standard error; the run continues, prints the summary number and exits with status 0 The destination file name already exists ERROR - Could not write file: … File exists and the run exits with status 1 Any other completed run The summary number is printed and the run exits with status 0

docs.title: Generated agent
docs.text: Property Value Name <prefix>_<MD5 hash of the -a value> Alias <prefix>_<-a value> Description Agent generated by pandora_o365 plugin Address 127.0.0.1 Group The -g value Interval The -i value Document file <data directory><agent name>.<EPOCH>.data, or the same name in --tmp before a Tentacle transfer

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text:
Module Type Value <prefix>_<service id>_status generic_data_string The service status returned by Microsoft Graph <prefix>_<service id>_active_issues generic_data_string Unresolved incidents as <id>: <title>, concatenated without a separator; None when there is none

The number of modules depends on the services the tenant subscribes to; the plugin does not create modules for anything else, and it does not create the licensing modules that the Discovery addon provides.

docs.title: Addon identity
docs.text: Property Value Marketplace identifier pandorafms.office365_plugin Name Pandora Office 365 Monitoring Version 1.0 Package pandorafms.office365_plugin.1.0.zip Marketplace last update 2025-07-01 Author Pandora FMS Availability Download limited to licensed users License One Maintenance The Marketplace states that the addon is no longer actively maintained and suggests the alternatives listed in the entry

docs.title: Pandora Openshift monitoring plugin
docs.text:
Article last updated: 2026-10-27.

Discovery integration recommended

For new installations use OpenShift Discovery, which is the recommended integration for this service. This plugin is the legacy path. The Marketplace entry advises exploring alternative plugins in the library.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Pandora Openshift plugin monitors an OpenShift cluster from Pandora FMS by running the OpenShift command-line client (oc) on the host where the plugin executes. Each run logs in with a user name and password, selects one project, reads cluster and project objects, and builds Pandora FMS agents from the command output: one agent per node, pod and deployment, one agent per resource group, and a summary agent with element counts.

Every run delivers the agents itself, as agent_data documents, through the Tentacle client or into a local data folder. The plugin does not print modules for a Pandora FMS agent to collect, so it runs as a server plugin or from a scheduler, never as an agent plugin.

This page documents the pandorafms.openshift_plugin addon, the CLI-based monitoring plugin. OpenShift Discovery (pandorafms.openshift) is a different addon: it runs from the Discovery task wizard, talks to the cluster API with a token and generates its agents from the task. It does not use oc, a project or these configuration files. See OpenShift Discovery.

docs.title: Compatibility and availability
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.openshift_plugin, version 1.0 Documented target Version of the Marketplace entry and of the plugin. See Addon identity The oc client on the host that runs the plugin Required Every collection step is an oc command; cli names the binary Network access from that host to the OpenShift API endpoint Required oc login and every command reach the API named in ip An OpenShift account with cluster-wide read access and project access Required The commands in oc commands are cluster-scoped and project-scoped; see Requirements The OpenShift metrics API Required for node and pod metrics The node CPU/memory data and the pod stats agent come from oc adm top nodes and oc adm top pods tentacle_client in PATH Required when mode=tentacle (the shipped value) Delivery runs the Tentacle client A writable local_folder Required when mode is not tentacle Delivery copies the XML into that folder CentOS 7 and Fedora as the operating system of the host Known compatible The previous edition of this guide records those systems as the ones where the plugin was tested; not re-validated for version 1.0 Other operating systems of the host Not validated No other system is recorded. The plugin needs an oc client and a Tentacle client for the host platform OpenShift versions Not validated No version matrix is recorded. The plugin calls oc get cs, an API Kubernetes deprecated and recent clusters may no longer serve Pandora FMS versions Not validated The Marketplace states that all its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later; there is no statement specific to this addon

The Marketplace entry advises exploring the alternative plugins in its library for the latest features and support.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. The oc client on the host that runs the plugin, of a version that can talk to the target cluster. The plugin runs the binary named in cli; it applies no default path and does not check that the file exists.
  2. Network access to the OpenShift API endpoint from that host, normally on TCP port 6443. ip must be the API URL that oc login accepts, scheme and port included, for example https://<TARGET_HOST>:6443.
  3. An OpenShift account able to run the read commands of this plugin. The node, namespace, API-service, component-status and cluster-operator reads are cluster-scoped; the pods, deployments, services, replication controllers, imagestreams and cluster service version reads are limited to the selected project. The previous edition of this guide recommends the cluster-reader role; no narrower role has been validated for this plugin.
  4. The OpenShift metrics API enabled in the project and the cluster, so oc adm top nodes and oc adm top pods return rows.
  5. Pandora FMS to receive the agents: the Pandora FMS server, either through its Tentacle server or through a data folder it reads.
  6. The Tentacle client (tentacle_client) in PATH, when delivery uses Tentacle.

docs.title: Install and register the plugin
docs.text:
The Marketplace package is pandorafms.openshift_plugin.1.0.pspz2. It carries the plugin, a configuration file and the registration definition that the console reads:

File Destination after registration pandora_openshift.pl <attachment_store>/plugin/pandora_openshift.pl pandora_openshift.conf <attachment_store>/plugin/pandora_openshift.conf plugin_definition.ini Read and removed by the registration

To register it, open Servers → Register plugin in the Pandora FMS console, select the .pspz2 file and click Upload file. The console registers a plugin named Pandora Openshift with a single macro, _field1_, whose default value is the configuration file path. The registration values are in Register the package in the console.

The registered default path assumes the default attachment directory, /var/www/html/pandora_console/attachment. If the installation uses another attachment_store, edit the macro value to the real path.

The shipped configuration file cannot collect anything: it has no oc path, no credentials and no Tentacle host, and its project and prefix are both prueba. Edit the configuration file on the server that runs the plugin before the first run, as described in Configure.

The plugin can also be registered by hand from Servers → Plugins with Add plugin, using Plugin command <attachment_store>/plugin/pandora_openshift.pl and the parameters _field1_.

docs.title: Credentials and connection safety
docs.text:
• The OpenShift user and password are stored in plain text in the configuration file. Registration extracts every package file with mode 0755, so the configuration file is readable by every local user until you restrict it. Change it to chmod 600 and make it owned by the user of the Pandora FMS server process.
  • Every run executes oc login -u <USERNAME> -p <PASSWORD> <IP>. The password therefore appears in the command line of the oc process and any local user can read it in the process list while the login runs. There is no password-free input surface in this plugin.
  • oc login stores the session in the kubeconfig of the user that runs the plugin, normally $HOME/.kube/config. The plugin does not delete it, so the token remains on disk between runs.
  • The plugin passes no TLS option to oc, so oc verifies the API certificate with its own defaults. With a self-signed API certificate, make the host trust the cluster CA; otherwise the login fails and every collector returns nothing.
  • The plugin does not read the error output of oc. Messages such as an authentication failure go to the standard error of the run and do not stop it.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The configuration file is a plain-text file with key=value lines. Lines that start with # and blank lines are skipped, keys and values are trimmed and the last occurrence of a repeated key wins. The file has no sections.

Pass the file as the first argument of the plugin:

pandora_openshift.pl <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

The plugin applies no defaults of its own beyond the values in the shipped file, and it validates nothing: a missing key behaves as an empty value, which disables the corresponding step or delivery. This is a complete configuration with placeholders:

# oc client
cli=/usr/local/bin/oc
user=<USERNAME>
password=<PASSWORD>
ip=https://<TARGET_HOST>:6443
project=<PROJECT>

# delivery
mode=tentacle
tentacle_ip=<PANDORA_FMS_SERVER>
tentacle_port=41121

# collectors
prefix=<PREFIX>
as_server_plugin=1
agent_openshift=1
agent_node=1
agent_pod=1
agent_pod_stats=1
agent_deployment=1
agent_imagestreams=1
agent_apiservice=1
agent_services=1
agent_replication_controller=1
agent_component_status=1
agent_operators=1
agent_csv=0
top_imagestreams_count=11

Every key is described in Configuration file keys.

docs.title: Project scope and collectors
docs.text:
The run starts with oc login and then oc project <PROJECT>. The project selects the scope of the pods, deployments, services, replication controllers, imagestreams and cluster service versions that the plugin reads; nodes, namespaces, API services, component statuses and cluster operators are read cluster-wide. One run monitors one project plus the cluster-wide objects, so monitor several projects with several plugin executions and different prefix values.

The agent_* keys enable or disable collectors. 1 enables a collector and 0 disables it; any other value disables it as well. All collectors are enabled in the shipped file except agent_csv.

prefix is prepended to every agent name. It is prueba in the shipped file; with an empty value the agent names start with the underscore, for example _OS_POD_<POD_NAME>.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually on the host that executes it, passing the configuration file as its only argument:

pandora_openshift.pl <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

The plugin is registered as executable; perl pandora_openshift.pl <PATH_TO_CONFIG> produces the same result. With as_server_plugin=1 (the shipped value), a complete run prints a single integer and exits:

Output Meaning 11 All eleven enabled blocks completed and delivered. This is the value with the shipped switches, where agent_csv=0 12 All twelve blocks completed, including the cluster service version collector (agent_csv=1) A lower number All the blocks counted completed; the number is the count of enabled blocks, so it drops when you disable collectors 0 No collector ran: every switch is disabled, or no configuration file was loaded

The printed number counts delivered blocks, not collected data. A block whose oc command returned no rows still completes, so a run can print 11 and produce agents with no modules.

A failing block does not print a number: the plugin stops at that block and exits with status 0. Use as_server_plugin=0 to see which block failed, as described in Reading failures.

After a successful run, confirm in Pandora FMS that the agents named in Agents exist with their modules. Delivery through Tentacle requires that the host can reach tentacle_ip:tentacle_port; the default port is 41121.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text:
Agent Created from Modules <prefix>_Openshift Element counts of seven oc commands Seven counters <prefix>_OS_Nodo_<NODE_NAME> Rows of oc adm top nodes Node state, conditions, allocation and CPU/memory <prefix>_OS_POD_<POD_NAME> Rows of oc get pods Ready, Status, Restarts, Age <prefix>_OS_POD_Stats Rows of oc adm top pods Two modules per pod <prefix>_OS_DEPLOYMENT_<DEPLOYMENT_NAME> Rows of oc get deployments Ready, Up to date, Avalaible, Age <prefix>_OS_Imagestreams Rows of oc adm top imagestreams Two modules per imagestream <prefix>_OS_Api_service Rows of oc get apiservice One module per API service <prefix>_OS_Services Rows of oc get services One module per service <prefix>_OS_Replication_Controllers Rows of oc get rc -o wide Four modules per replication controller <prefix>_Component_status etcd rows of oc get cs One availability module per component <prefix>_Cluster_operator Rows of oc get co One availability module per operator <prefix>_Cluster_service_version Rows of oc get csv One phase module per cluster service version; disabled by default

The per-node, per-pod and per-deployment agents exist only while their oc command returns rows. The grouped agents are delivered even when the command returns nothing, so an agent with no modules means the command produced no rows, not that the plugin failed to run.

docs.title: Values
docs.text:
• Only the summary counters, the condition checks and the cluster checks are numeric: generic_data for the counters and generic_proc for the checks. Every per-resource value is a generic_data_string module that stores the text oc printed, so values such as 2/2, 120m, 10Gi or 2d cannot be used with numeric thresholds.
  • The seven summary counters are line counts of the command output after the header line. An oc command that fails produces no lines and therefore publishes 0; the plugin does not distinguish an empty project from a failed command.
  • The services counter module is named Services — the name ends with a space, which is easy to miss when you search for it in the console.
  • The deployment availability module is named Avalaible, with that spelling. Its value is the AVAILABLE column of oc get deployments.
  • MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure report 1 when oc describe node returns False for the condition, that is, when there is no pressure. Ready reports 1 when the status is True.
  • oc get cs returns the etcd component rows only for components whose name contains etcd. A cluster whose API no longer serves the componentstatuses resource produces no rows and the agent is delivered with no modules.
  • Allocated cpu and Allocated memory are not the allocation percentage. The plugin takes the fourth whitespace-separated token of the cpu or memory row in the node's Allocated resources block, which in the standard oc describe node layout is the absolute value of the Limits column, removes its last two characters and then its first character, and compares the rest with 80 and 90. In the usual layout the result is a mangled number and both modules normally report 1.

docs.title: The node agents
docs.text:
The node collector behaves differently from the rest:

  • Per-node documents are built from oc get nodes and six oc describe node calls per node, but that first pass is not delivered.
  • The delivered agents come from oc adm top nodes. The module list is never reset between the nodes of the first pass, so the agent of the first row of oc adm top nodes receives the Status, Roles, Age, Version, condition and Allocated modules of every node, with the same module names repeated once per node, plus its four adm top metrics.
  • Every other node agent receives only Cpu (cores), Cpu %, Memory and Memory %.

In a cluster with a single node the first agent carries the complete node inventory. In a multi-node cluster its inventory modules mix several nodes and cannot be attributed to one of them, so read node state from oc get nodes or from the CPU and memory modules of the other node agents.

docs.title: Running and scheduling
docs.text:
• A run is one-shot: it logs in, collects, delivers and exits. It keeps no state except the kubeconfig that oc login writes.
  • Schedule the plugin from a plugin module in Pandora FMS, or from cron when it delivers to a local folder. Each execution collects the state of the cluster at that moment.
  • The registered package sets a maximum timeout of 20 seconds. A run starts a new oc process for the login, the project switch, the counts and every collector, and the node collector runs six oc describe node commands per node. A cluster with many nodes can exceed that timeout; raise the plugin timeout when you register it or edit it.
  • Set debug=1 to have delivery errors printed on standard error. Without it, a failed Tentacle transfer or a failed local copy is silent.

docs.title: Reading failures
docs.text:
With as_server_plugin=0, a failing block prints one XML module on standard output instead of the numeric result:

<module>
    <name><![CDATA[Pandora_Openshift]]></name>
    <type>generic_proc</type>
    <data><![CDATA[0]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[Nodes node-01]]></description>
</module>

The description names the block and the resource that failed: Nodes <node>, Pods <pod>, Pods stats, Deployments <deployment>, Imagestreams, Api service, Services, Replication Controllers, Component status, Cluster operator, Cluster service version or Openshift Agent. The global block uses the name <prefix>_Pandora_Openshift instead of Pandora_Openshift.

as_server_plugin=0 does not print the collected modules: on a successful run standard output is empty. The plugin always delivers its agents itself, so it cannot be used as an agent plugin through module_plugin.

The run exits with status 0 whether it delivered everything or nothing. Do not use the exit status to detect a failure.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The login result is never checked. With wrong credentials, an unreachable API or an untrusted certificate, every command returns nothing and the plugin publishes agents with 0 counters and no resource modules, still exiting with 0.
  • The plugin reads one project per run. There is no namespace list, filter or multi-project mode.
  • Only the module detail oc prints is published. The plugin defines no thresholds, alerts or metric transformations of its own.
  • agent_csv is disabled in the shipped file, and oc get csv requires the Operator Lifecycle Manager.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Signal Check A run prints 0 No collector was enabled or no configuration file was read. Check that _field1_ points to an existing file and that the agent_* keys are 1 A run prints nothing and exits with status 0 A block failed to deliver. Repeat with as_server_plugin=0 to get the failing block, and with debug=1 to see the delivery error ERROR: [transfer_mode] set to [tentacle], but no [tentacle_ip] provided. on standard output mode=tentacle has no tentacle_ip. The message does not stop the run; every delivery fails afterwards Agents appear with 0 counters and no resource modules Login or permissions failed. Run oc login and the commands of oc commands with the same user and project on the same host Node agents appear with only four modules Normal behaviour in a multi-node cluster; see The node agents Allocated cpu and Allocated memory are always 1 Documented parsing behaviour; the modules do not measure allocation. See Values <prefix>_OS_POD_Stats has no modules The metrics API did not answer oc adm top pods. Check the metrics server and the project <prefix>_Component_status has no modules oc get cs returned no etcd rows, or the cluster does not serve componentstatuses any more No node or pod agents at all agent_node or agent_pod is disabled, or the corresponding oc command returned no rows Agents are delivered but do not appear in Pandora FMS Check tentacle_ip, tentacle_port and the Tentacle server, or that local_folder exists and is writable by the plugin user The run is killed by the plugin timeout Raise the plugin timeout; see Running and scheduling

docs.title: Register the package in the console
docs.text:
The registration definition of the .pspz2 package sets these values:

Field Value Plugin name Pandora Openshift Description Plugin to monitor a Openshift environment using Openshift CLI Plugin type Standard Maximum timeout 20 seconds Plugin command <attachment_store>/plugin/pandora_openshift.pl Plugin parameters _field1_

The package defines one macro:

Macro Required Default Hide Description and help _field1_ Yes, according to its description /var/www/html/pandora_console/attachment/plugin/pandora_openshift.conf No Conf path (obligatory). Help: Path to conf file

Hide is off, so the console shows the field as plain text. The console does not enforce the macro: an empty or wrong value leaves the run without a configuration file and it collects nothing.

docs.title: Configuration file keys
docs.text:
Key Required Default Description cli Yes Empty Path to the oc binary on the host that runs the plugin user Yes Empty OpenShift user name password Yes Empty Password of that user, in plain text ip Yes Empty API URL accepted by oc login, with scheme and port, for example https://<TARGET_HOST>:6443 project Yes prueba Project selected with oc project; it scopes the pods, deployments, services, replication controllers and imagestreams prefix No prueba Prefix of every agent name mode No Empty Delivery mode. tentacle uses the Tentacle client; any other value copies the XML into local_folder. Empty with local_folder unset delivers nothing transfer_mode No Empty Alias of mode, used only when mode is empty tentacle_ip Yes when mode=tentacle Empty Tentacle server address tentacle_port No 41121 Tentacle server port tentacle_client No tentacle_client Name or path of the Tentacle client executable tentacle_opts No Empty Extra options passed to the Tentacle client local_folder Yes when mode is not tentacle Empty Folder that receives the agent_data files, for example a Pandora FMS data inbox tmp No /tmp Folder where the XML file is written before delivery as_server_plugin No 1 1 prints the block count and suppresses the per-block error module; 0 prints the error module of a failing block as_agent_plugin No Empty Alias that sets as_server_plugin to 0 when it is enabled and as_server_plugin is not set debug No Empty 1 prints delivery errors on standard error module_group No Empty Module group assigned to every generated module module_interval No Empty Module interval assigned to every generated module, in seconds top_imagestreams_count No 11 Number of oc adm top imagestreams output lines passed to the parser, header included, so it yields at most one imagestream fewer agent_openshift No 1 Summary counters agent agent_node No 1 Per-node agents agent_pod No 1 Per-pod agents agent_pod_stats No 1 Pod stats agent agent_deployment No 1 Per-deployment agents agent_imagestreams No 1 Imagestreams agent agent_apiservice No 1 API service agent agent_services No 1 Services agent agent_replication_controller No 1 Replication controller agent agent_component_status No 1 Component status agent agent_operators No 1 Cluster operator agent agent_csv No 0 Cluster service version agent

The defaults in this table are the values of the shipped configuration file. A key that is absent from the file behaves as an empty value, so leaving a key out is not the same as setting it to 1.

docs.title: Collector blocks and the result value
docs.text:
The plugin runs its collectors in this fixed order. The result number printed with as_server_plugin=1 is the count of enabled blocks that completed.

# Switch Command Agent 1 agent_node oc get nodes, oc describe node (six times per node), oc adm top nodes <prefix>_OS_Nodo_<NODE_NAME> 2 agent_pod oc get pods <prefix>_OS_POD_<POD_NAME> 3 agent_pod_stats oc adm top pods <prefix>_OS_POD_Stats 4 agent_deployment oc get deployments <prefix>_OS_DEPLOYMENT_<DEPLOYMENT_NAME> 5 agent_imagestreams oc adm top imagestreams <prefix>_OS_Imagestreams 6 agent_apiservice oc get apiservice <prefix>_OS_Api_service 7 agent_services oc get services <prefix>_OS_Services 8 agent_replication_controller oc get rc -o wide <prefix>_OS_Replication_Controllers 9 agent_component_status oc get cs --no-headers, filtered by grep etcd <prefix>_Component_status 10 agent_operators oc get co --no-headers <prefix>_Cluster_operator 11 agent_csv oc get csv with a name and phase column selection <prefix>_Cluster_service_version 12 agent_openshift Seven count commands <prefix>_Openshift

A block that fails to deliver stops the run before its count is incremented, so a failure never produces a number.

docs.title: Summary agent
docs.text: Module Type Value Services generic_data Line count of oc get services Deployments generic_data Line count of oc get deployments Namespaces generic_data Line count of oc get namespaces Nodes generic_data Line count of oc get nodes Pods generic_data Line count of oc get pods Imagestreams generic_data Line count of oc adm top imagestreams, without the top_imagestreams_count limit Replication controllers generic_data Line count of oc get rc

docs.title: Oracle VM monitoring plugin
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Oracle VM monitoring plugin monitors an Oracle VM environment from Pandora FMS through the REST API of its Oracle VM Manager. Each run reads the manager and what it manages, and turns the result into Pandora FMS agents and modules: the manager state and its job counters, server pool capacity, the OVM Servers with their network ports, the virtual machines with their memory and disks, and the file servers with their file systems. Nothing is installed on the Oracle VM hosts: the plugin runs from a host that can reach the OVM Manager API.

Every execution is one-shot: it authenticates against the API, collects the whole environment and delivers one agent data document per element. Delivery is either through Tentacle or by copying the documents into a Pandora FMS data folder. The plugin has no agent plugin mode and does not print module XML on standard output.

Oracle VM monitoring is a different addon from Oracle Discovery (pandorafms.oracle), which monitors Oracle Database instances and is documented in Oracle Discovery. This page covers the Oracle VM virtualization manager only.

docs.title: Compatibility and availability
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Oracle VM Manager 3.4.5 Known compatible The addon guide linked from the Marketplace entry states the plugin was developed against Oracle VM Manager 3.4.5 Oracle VM Manager versions other than 3.4.5 Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon Reachability from the host that runs the plugin to the OVM Manager REST API Required Every run queries the API An OVM Manager user allowed to read the API resources Required Each request is authenticated with HTTP Basic credentials The Pandora FMS plugin library (PandoraFMS::PluginTools) Required The addon guide lists it as a prerequisite A Tentacle server reachable at tentacle_ip and tentacle_port Required when transfer_mode=tentacle Every generated document is sent to that address and port A writable data folder Required when transfer_mode is not tentacle Every generated document is copied into local_folder Oracle VM guest additions on the monitored virtual machines Required for VM IP addresses The addon guide states that IP collection needs guest additions A specific Pandora FMS release Not validated No version matrix is recorded for this addon. The Marketplace states that its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later A specific host operating system Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version

The addon is distributed through the Pandora FMS Marketplace and its download is limited to licensed users.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. Network access from the host that runs the plugin to the OVM Manager REST API. The example configuration uses HTTPS on port 7002.
  2. An OVM Manager user and its password. The plugin only reads: it requests the manager, the job list, the server pools, the servers, the virtual machines, the virtual NICs, the disks, the file servers and the file systems. Use an account with read access to those resources.
  3. A host to run the plugin with the Pandora FMS plugin library (PandoraFMS::PluginTools), which is part of a Pandora FMS installation. The Pandora FMS server that runs the plugin is the usual choice.
  4. A delivery target that Pandora FMS can read: a Tentacle server, or a data folder read by the Pandora FMS data server.
  5. Oracle VM guest additions inside the monitored virtual machines, only when you want their IP addresses in the agent data.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
The addon guide documents the plugin as the ovm-plugin.64 executable plus the ovm-plugin.conf configuration file. Copy both to the host that will run the plugin; for a console server plugin the recommended folder is /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/.

Download the package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.oracle_vm_monitoring

The shipped configuration file contains sample values. Replace the API URL, the user and the password before the first run, and restrict the file permissions to the user that runs the plugin. If your package names the executable differently, use that name in place of ovm-plugin.64 in the examples.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The plugin takes its settings from three sources, in increasing precedence:

defaults < configuration file < command-line options

The configuration file is a plain-text file of key=value lines. Blank lines and lines that start with # are skipped, keys and values are trimmed, and a repeated key keeps its last value. To use a file, pass its path as the first and only positional argument. Any option can also be passed on the command line as a -key value pair, and the command-line value replaces the file value:

./ovm-plugin.64 -interval 600 -debug 1 <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

There is no help option. A run without a readable configuration and without the required options fails with the error that names the missing settings, followed by a usage line that shows the configuration file as the only argument.

This is the minimum configuration for a Tentacle delivery:

ovmm_api_url=https://<OVM_MANAGER_URL>:7002/ovm/core/wsapi/rest/
user=<USERNAME>
password=<PASSWORD>
transfer_mode=tentacle
tentacle_ip=<PANDORA_FMS_URL>
tentacle_port=41121

docs.title: Connection settings
docs.text:
ovmm_api_url is the base URL of the OVM Manager REST API, up to and including the REST root. The plugin appends the resource names (Manager, Job, ServerPool, Server, FileServer) and follows the resource URIs the API returns. A trailing slash is optional: the plugin adds one when it is missing.

The user and the password are sent with HTTP Basic authentication on every request. Requests ask for application/xml, and the plugin reads the XML responses.

docs.title: Credentials and transport
docs.text:
• Use an https URL. With http the credentials and the collected data travel unencrypted; restrict the API to a trusted network if you cannot use HTTPS.
  • The plugin does not verify the OVM Manager certificate. It accepts any certificate, including a self-signed one, so HTTPS protects the credentials in transit but does not authenticate the server. Keep the API on a management network you control.
  • The password is stored in plain text in the configuration file. Keep the file owned by the plugin user and readable by nobody else, for example with chmod 600.
  • Avoid -password on the command line: the command is kept in the shell history and is visible in the process list while the plugin runs. The plugin has no separate credentials-file option, so prefer the configuration file and pass only non-secret overrides as options.
  • The include key reads another key file at that point in the configuration, so a shared file can hold the connection settings while the main file holds the rest. Keys read after the include line override the included ones.

docs.title: Agent names and renaming
docs.text:
Every generated agent has a default name taken from the OVM API:

Resource Default agent name OVM Manager The manager UUID Server pool The pool ID OVM Server The MD5 hash of the server ID, because the MAC-style server ID is not a valid agent name Virtual machine The VM ID File server The file server ID

The alias is the element name reported by the API (the manager name, the pool name, the server name, the VM name or the file server name). Set alias_as_name=1 to leave the alias empty so Pandora FMS uses the agent name as the alias instead.

The IDs come from the OVM Manager interface: open the element and read its ID field.

To rename an agent, add a configuration key whose name is exactly the default agent name. Any number of renaming keys can be added:

# A virtual machine, renamed by its VM ID.
0004fb0000060000ed21e30c8dbbbb65a=app-vm-01
# An OVM Server, renamed by the MD5 hash of its ID.
a62454d287e230c773f56d618b78500f=ovm-server-01

The renaming keys are ordinary configuration keys, so they follow the same precedence as the rest: a -key value option overrides the file. For a server, the key must be the MD5 hash, not the MAC-style ID, because the hash is the default agent name. The commented default_agent_name1 sample in the shipped file does not rename anything: the key is the ID value, not a field name. Renaming the manager, a pool or a server leaves its children pointing to the default name; see Known limitations.

docs.title: Delivery
docs.text:
transfer_mode Behavior tentacle The plugin writes each document to tmp and sends it with the Tentacle client to tentacle_ip:tentacle_port Any other value, including empty The plugin writes each document to tmp and copies it into local_folder

Tentacle delivery requires tentacle_ip. A delivery mode other than tentacle requires local_folder. The plugin validates both conditions before contacting the OVM Manager, and stops with an error when the required value is missing.

The generated document is removed from tmp after a successful delivery and kept there when the delivery fails. Delivery errors are reported on standard error only when debug=1; by default a failed delivery is silent and the run continues with the next agent.

docs.title: Register the plugin in the console
docs.text:
The plugin can be registered in the Pandora FMS console as a server plugin, so the Pandora FMS server runs it periodically instead of a manual or cron execution. Every execution collects the whole environment and delivers all its agents.

  1. Open Servers → Plugins and click Register Plugin.
  2. Set the name, the plugin type Standard, a maximum timeout and a description. Raise the maximum timeout when a run over a large environment takes longer than the default.
  3. In Plugin command, enter the path to the ovm-plugin.64 executable on the Pandora FMS server, for example /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/ovm-plugin.64.
  4. In Plugin parameters, pass the path to the configuration file as the only argument:
/etc/pandora/plugins/ovm-plugin.conf
  1. Keep the API user and password in that file rather than in console fields.

The same registration can pass individual settings with the plugin macros _field1_, _field2_, ... instead of a file, for example -ovmm_api_url _field1_ -user _field2_ -password _field3_ -transfer_mode tentacle -tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1. In that case mark the password field as hidden.

The value printed by the execution is not the monitoring data: the plugin delivers the agents itself, and the data appears in the generated agents. All the agents of the environment are created or updated by the same execution.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually with the configuration file as its only argument:

./ovm-plugin.64 <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

A successful run ends with the line Complete! and exits with status 0. It prints nothing else unless debug=1 is set. With debug=1 the run also prints its progress, for example:

> Connecting to OVM Manager REST API...
 >> Collecting OVM Manager information...
 >> Creating XML structure for OVM Manager agent...
 >> Transferring OVM Manager agent XML...
> Scanning OVM servers pools...

Then check the console after the first execution:

  1. The OVM Manager agent, named after the manager UUID.
  2. One agent per server pool, one per OVM Server, one per virtual machine and one per file server, under the parent described in Generated agents.
  3. The modules of each agent, listed in Generated modules.

If the manager cannot be reached, the run prints ERROR: Unable to connect to '<URL>' with user '<USER>'. and exits with status 1 without creating or updating any agent. The message repeats the configured URL and user, so avoid running it in a shared terminal.

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
A run produces up to five agent groups. Each group answers a different question:

  • Manager. Whether the OVM Manager is running, and how many of its jobs ended in SUCCESS or in FAILURE.
  • Server pools. How many virtual machines the pool holds, how many of its servers are running, and what share of the pool memory is still usable.
  • OVM Servers. Whether each server is running, its usable memory share, the state of each network port, and how many of its virtual machines are running.
  • Virtual machines. Whether each VM is running, the share of the server memory it uses and how much of each virtual disk is occupied.
  • File servers. The free space share of each file system, with its path.

The state modules are binary: 1 when the resource is in its healthy state (RUNNING for the manager, the servers and the VMs; PORT_UP for a port) and 0 otherwise. The description of each state module repeats the raw state reported by the API, so a stopped resource shows why in the module description.

The percentage modules are computed from the capacities the API reports:

  • Usable memory (%) is the memory still available for virtual machines, not the memory in use. It is usableMemory divided by memory, for a server or summed over the servers of a pool.
  • Used memory on server (%) is the current memory of the VM as a share of the server total memory, not of the memory assigned to the VM. The module description states the current, the server total and the assigned memory.
  • <disk name> on disk size (%) is the space the virtual disk occupies on storage as a share of its nominal size, which shows thin provisioning.
  • <file system> free size (%) is the free space as a share of the file system size.

A zero denominator produces 0 instead of an error. The plugin sets no warning or critical thresholds on the generated modules; add thresholds on the modules you want to alert on.

The agent aliases make the console readable: the alias is the element name, while the agent name is the API identifier. For OVM Servers the agent name is the MD5 hash of the server ID, so the server name only appears as the alias and in the description.

docs.title: Run-time behavior
docs.text:
• The plugin keeps no state between runs. Every execution collects the whole environment, so it can be run manually at any time.
  • Resources are collected in a fixed order: manager, job list, server pools, servers, the VMs of each server, and file servers. Each resource costs at least one API request, and the requests are sequential, so a large environment takes proportionally longer.
  • Every API request uses a three-second timeout. The configuration file has no key to change it; a manager that answers more slowly produces missing agents or missing modules.
  • debug=1 prints the progress of the run and the delivery errors. debug=0, the default, hides both.
  • The run ends with Complete! and status 0 even when one or more deliveries failed. Check the console, or run with debug=1, to confirm that every agent arrived.
  • The plugin collects the whole environment on every run: there is no option to limit it to one pool, server, VM or file server.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
These are behaviors of version 1.0, documented as they are.

  • A manager with fewer than two jobs stops the run. The job counter expects a list of jobs. With zero jobs or exactly one job the run stops with an unhandled error right after the Manager agent has been delivered, so no pool, server, VM or file server agent is produced. This affects a new or quiet OVM Manager.
  • scan_vm_ip=0 does not disable VM IP collection. The setting is enabled unless its value is something other than 0 or 1. To stop collecting addresses, set scan_vm_ip=2 or another value outside that pair.
  • A VM address is collected only from a virtual NIC with more than one IP address. A VM whose NIC reports a single address gets an empty agent address, even with guest additions installed.
  • The shipped rename sample does not work. The commented default_agent_name1=new_agent_name1 lines do not rename anything; the key must be the default agent name, as described in Agent names and renaming.
  • Renaming a parent agent breaks the hierarchy. Every parent reference is written with the default name of the parent (the manager UUID, the pool ID or the MD5 hash of the server), not with the renamed name. If you rename the manager, a pool or a server, its children (pools, file servers, servers and VMs) keep pointing to the old name. Rename only leaf agents, or keep the default names of the agents that have children.
  • Delivery failures are hidden by default. A failed Tentacle transfer or a failed copy leaves the document in tmp, is reported only with debug=1, and does not change the exit status.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text: Symptom Cause and action ERROR: No OVM API URL, user or password provided. and a usage line, status 1 ovmm_api_url, user or password is missing, or the configuration file path does not exist and was therefore not read ERROR: transfer_mode set to tentacle, but no tentacle_ip provided., status 1 Tentacle delivery is selected without a Tentacle server address ERROR: transfer_mode set to local, but no local_folder provided., status 1 transfer_mode is not tentacle and local_folder is empty ERROR: Unable to connect to '<URL>' with user '<USER>'., status 1 The manager URL, the credentials or the network path is wrong. Check that the URL is the REST base and that the user can read the API. The certificate is not verified, so TLS is not the cause Only the Manager agent appears The job list broke the run (see Known limitations), or a later request failed. Run with debug=1 to see where the run stops The Manager agent and the pool agents appear, but no server agent The server list request failed, or the servers were not returned by the API. Run with debug=1 A VM agent has no address Guest additions are missing, or the NIC reports a single IP address (see Known limitations) No delivery error and no new data in the console Delivery failed silently, or the destination is not read by Pandora FMS. Run with debug=1 and check tentacle_ip/tentacle_port or local_folder The agents appear in a group other than group The Pandora FMS server is configured with autocreate_group_force 1, which gives the server autocreate group precedence over the group in the agent data The console shows an unexpected agent name The agent is named after the API ID by default; rename it with a key equal to that name, or check the MD5 hash for OVM Servers

docs.title: Configuration file parameters
docs.text:
The file uses key=value lines. Blank lines and lines that start with # are skipped.

Name Required Default Description ovmm_api_url Yes — Base URL of the OVM Manager REST API, up to the REST root, for example https://<OVM_MANAGER_URL>:7002/ovm/core/wsapi/rest/. The trailing slash is optional user Yes — OVM Manager user, sent with HTTP Basic authentication password Yes — Password for user, stored in plain text group No Servers Group name written in the agent data of the generated agents interval No 300 Agent interval, in seconds, written in the agent data tmp No /tmp Folder where the agent documents are written before delivery transfer_mode No Empty tentacle delivers through the Tentacle client. Any other value, including empty, copies the documents into local_folder local_folder Required when transfer_mode is not tentacle — Folder for the copied documents, for example /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ tentacle_ip Required when transfer_mode=tentacle — Tentacle server address tentacle_port No 41121 Tentacle server port tentacle_client No tentacle_client Name or path of the Tentacle client executable tentacle_opts No Empty Extra options passed to the Tentacle client, separated by whitespace alias_as_name No 0 1 leaves the alias empty so the agent name is used as the alias; any other value uses the element name scan_vm_ip No Enabled Collects the VM IP addresses. Values other than 0 or 1 disable collection; 0 does not (see Known limitations) debug No 0 1 prints the progress of the run and the delivery errors on standard error; 0 hides them include No — Reads another key file at that point. Keys read after the include line override the included ones <default agent name> No — Any key whose name equals a default agent name replaces it. Applies to the manager UUID, pool IDs, VM IDs, file server IDs and the MD5 hash of a server ID

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
./ovm-plugin.64 <PATH_TO_CONFIG> [ -key value ... ]
Condition Behavior A positional argument that names an existing file The file is read and any further -key value pairs override its values No positional argument The plugin reads only the -key value pairs; the required connection keys must come from them A positional argument that does not name an existing file The file is not read and the path is not reported as an error; the run fails with the missing-settings error unless another source supplies them -key value Replaces the value of the same key from the file or the defaults. A trailing token without its pair is ignored An unknown key Accepted silently. Only a key equal to an agent name has an effect beyond configuration
