docs.title: Redis monitoring plugin
docs.text:
Article last updated: 2026-10-27.

Discovery integration recommended

For new installations use Redis Discovery, which is the recommended integration for this service. This plugin is the legacy path.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Redis monitoring plugin turns the statistics of a Redis server into Pandora FMS modules. Each run connects to one Redis instance, reads the INFO sections you select, and publishes every field Redis returns as a module named exactly after that field: server identity and uptime, connected clients, memory, persistence, statistics, replication, CPU, per-command counters, cluster state and keyspace sizes.

Nothing is installed on the Redis server. The plugin connects over TCP from the host that runs it, with an optional password.

The plugin supports two execution models:

  • Server plugin mode (default when neither mode key is set): each run builds an agent document and delivers it to Pandora FMS through Tentacle or a local data folder.
  • Agent plugin mode (requires as_agent_plugin=1): each run prints the generated modules as XML on standard output, for the Pandora FMS agent to ingest.

This page documents the monitoring plugin, which reads the statistics of one instance per run. Discovering Redis instances and generating their agents is a different addon, documented in Redis Discovery.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon redis, version 1.1 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the host that runs the plugin to the Redis listener (TCP, 6379 by default in Redis) Required The plugin opens a client connection to the address in server A Redis password, when the instance requires authentication Required when authentication is enabled Prerequisite of the password key, not a compatibility statement tentacle_client on the host that runs the plugin Required when mode=tentacle Server mode delivery Redis server versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded. The legacy guide only states the plugin was developed against Redis 3.2.12; the plugin itself requires nothing beyond a server that answers INFO Operating system of the host that runs the plugin Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Pandora FMS versions Not validated The Marketplace carries a general banner for all its integrations, not a statement specific to this addon

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Network access from the host that runs the plugin to the Redis host and port.
  2. A Redis password, when the instance has authentication enabled. The plugin sends a password only: it has no user name key, so an instance that requires an ACL user name cannot be monitored with it. Use the default user with requirepass, or an ACL user that authenticates with a password alone.
  3. Pandora FMS to receive the output: the Pandora FMS server in server plugin mode, or the Pandora FMS agent of the monitored host in agent plugin mode.
  4. The Tentacle client (tentacle_client) available in PATH, only when server mode delivers through Tentacle.

The account used by the plugin only reads INFO. No official source identifies a narrower set of Redis permissions; grant only what the instance needs to answer that command.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
Download the package from the free Marketplace entry:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/redis

Copy the redis_monitor executable to the host that will run the plugin, and create its configuration file next to it (see Configure). Nothing is installed on the Redis server, and no Redis client tools are needed on the monitoring host.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
The plugin combines its defaults with two input sources, in increasing precedence:

defaults < configuration file < command-line arguments

The configuration file is optional. When it is used, it must be the first argument of the command line: a file path placed after a flag is not read. It is a plain-text file with one key=value pair per line. Blank lines and lines that start with # are skipped, keys and values are trimmed, and the last occurrence of a repeated key wins.

The file has no sections. The plugin reads only the keys listed in Configuration file keys; a bracketed header such as [THRESHOLDS] is stored as an unused key with an empty value and has no effect.

The two keys that define what is read are:

  • server — the instance to read, as <REDIS_HOST>:<REDIS_PORT>. Include the port: the sample configuration always does.
  • metrics — the INFO sections to read, separated by spaces. all reads every section the server reports.

docs.title: Execution modes
docs.text:
Agent plugin mode is the shortest configuration: the Pandora FMS agent runs the plugin and ingests the module XML it prints.

server=<REDIS_HOST>:<REDIS_PORT>
password=<PASSWORD>
metrics=all
module_group=Redis
as_agent_plugin=1
as_server_plugin=0

Server plugin mode needs an agent name and a delivery target. With Tentacle:

server=<REDIS_HOST>:<REDIS_PORT>
password=<PASSWORD>
metrics=all
module_group=Redis
as_agent_plugin=0
as_server_plugin=1
agent_name=redis-monitoring
temp=/tmp
mode=tentacle
tentacle_ip=<PANDORA_FMS_SERVER>
tentacle_port=41121

Or copy the agent document into a local data folder instead of using Tentacle:

server=<REDIS_HOST>:<REDIS_PORT>
password=<PASSWORD>
metrics=all
as_agent_plugin=0
as_server_plugin=1
agent_name=redis-monitoring
temp=/tmp
mode=local
local_folder=/var/spool/pandora/data_in

The same agent plugin run with arguments only, without a configuration file:

./redis_monitor -server <REDIS_HOST>:<REDIS_PORT> -password <PASSWORD> -metrics all -as_agent_plugin 1

Key points:

  • as_agent_plugin and as_server_plugin select the execution model. When neither is set, the plugin runs as a server plugin. When both are set to 1, both models run in the same execution: the module XML is printed and the agent document is delivered.
  • agent_name is required in server mode: it is the name of the agent created in Pandora FMS. The plugin sends that name only; it reads no agent interval, agent group or version key.
  • mode selects the delivery: tentacle uses the Tentacle client, and any other value, including local, copies the agent document into local_folder.
  • module_group is the name of the module group assigned to every generated module. Pandora FMS resolves it case-insensitively against the existing groups; when the name does not match one, the modules are created without that group.
  • temp is the folder where the agent document is written before delivery. On Linux it defaults to /tmp when the key is absent.
  • metrics is a single value: the section names are separated by spaces, so the whole list goes on one line.
  • Module names are the Redis field names, with no prefix. Run one agent per Redis instance: two instances delivered to the same agent overwrite each other's modules.

docs.title: Credentials and transport
docs.text:
• The Redis connection is not encrypted: the plugin has no TLS option, so the password and the statistics travel in clear text. Keep the connection on a trusted network, or place a TLS tunnel in front of Redis.
  • Inline password is stored in the configuration file in plain text: restrict the file permissions to the user that runs the plugin.
  • Avoid -password on the command line: the command is stored in the shell history and the operating system process list can expose it while the plugin runs. Prefer the configuration file with restrictive permissions (for example chmod 600).
  • debug=1 prints diagnostic dumps to standard output, including the full INFO response. Treat that output as sensitive: do not paste it into public tickets, and do not enable debug together with agent plugin mode (see Operate and troubleshoot).

docs.title: Register the plugin in Pandora FMS
docs.text:
redis_monitor can also be registered in the Pandora FMS console as a standard server plugin, so Pandora FMS executes it on the server that runs the modules instead of in a command line. Registered this way the plugin keeps server plugin mode: every run builds the agent document and delivers it, and the agent with its modules appears in the console.

Use the absolute path of the executable as the plugin command, and the documented keys as parameters. The console substitutes its _fieldN_ macros at execution time, so per-module values can be supplied without editing the plugin:

-server _field1_ -password _field2_ -metrics _field3_ -agent_name _field4_ -mode tentacle -tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1 -tentacle_port 41121
Field Description Example value _field1_ Redis address, including the port <REDIS_HOST>:<REDIS_PORT> _field2_ Redis password. It travels in the module command line, so treat the module definition as sensitive — _field3_ INFO sections to read, separated by spaces all _field4_ Name of the agent that will hold the modules redis-monitoring

-tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1 delivers to the Tentacle server of the machine that runs the plugin, so the agent lands in the Pandora FMS server that executes the module. To copy the document into a local data folder instead, replace the Tentacle flags with -mode local -local_folder /var/spool/pandora/data_in.

Once registered, the plugin is available when creating plugin modules, and each module fills the fields individually. The module is executed on the server selected for it, including a remote Pandora FMS server, so each Redis instance is monitored from the Pandora FMS server closest to it without installing anything on the Redis host.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually from a terminal, passing the configuration file as its first argument:

./redis_monitor /etc/pandora/plugins/redis_config.conf

The relative form ./redis_monitor redis_config.conf works when the terminal is already in the directory that contains both files. Each run executes once and exits.

In agent plugin mode, a successful run prints one XML <module> block per field on standard output, in this form:

<module>
    <name><![CDATA[redis_version]]></name>
    <type>generic_data_string</type>
    <data><![CDATA[7.2.4]]></data>
    <module_group>Redis</module_group>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[connected_clients]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[3]]></data>
    <module_group>Redis</module_group>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[db0]]></name>
    <type>generic_data_string</type>
    <data><![CDATA[keys=12,expires=4,avg_ttl=0]]></data>
    <module_group>Redis</module_group>
</module>

<module_group> is present only when module_group is set.

In server plugin mode a successful run prints nothing, and the agent configured in agent_name appears in Pandora FMS with its modules. The plugin does not report the delivery result in its exit status, so confirm the arrival in the console instead of relying on the command.

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text: Every module is one field of the Redis INFO response. The plugin reads the sections listed in metrics, and for each field it creates a module named after the field, with a group when module_group is set.

docs.title: Module names and types
docs.text:
• The module name is the Redis field name exactly as the server returns it: no prefix, no section prefix. used_memory stays used_memory, and a keyspace line arrives as db0.
  • A value that contains a letter becomes a generic_data_string module: redis_version, role, maxmemory_policy, used_memory_human (1.05M), rdb_last_bgsave_status and db0 (keys=12,expires=4,avg_ttl=0).
  • A value with digits only becomes a generic_data module: connected_clients, used_memory, uptime_in_seconds, maxmemory, mem_fragmentation_ratio, and also the numeric flags redis_git_dirty and aof_enabled.
  • The plugin adds no description, unit or threshold, and no availability module. The module catalog is exactly the set of fields the selected sections return for your Redis version and configuration.

There is no connectivity module: when a run cannot read the instance, it publishes no module at all and the existing modules receive no new data.

docs.title: Sections you can read
docs.text:
metrics accepts any section name the Redis server accepts, separated by spaces; the plugin only passes each name to INFO, so names match case-insensitively as Redis does. all reads every section. The sections commonly used with this plugin are:

metrics value What it reads Representative modules server Identity, version and uptime redis_version, redis_mode, os, arch_bits, process_id, run_id, tcp_port, uptime_in_seconds, uptime_in_days, executable, config_file clients Client connections connected_clients, blocked_clients, client_longest_output_list, client_biggest_input_buf memory Memory used_memory, used_memory_human, used_memory_rss, used_memory_peak, maxmemory, maxmemory_policy, mem_fragmentation_ratio, mem_allocator persistence RDB and AOF state loading, rdb_changes_since_last_save, rdb_last_bgsave_status, rdb_last_save_time, aof_enabled, aof_last_write_status, aof_current_size stats Counters and rates total_connections_received, total_commands_processed, instantaneous_ops_per_sec, keyspace_hits, keyspace_misses, evicted_keys, expired_keys replication Role and replicas role, connected_slaves, master_replid, master_repl_offset; the master_* and slave* fields depend on the instance role cpu CPU consumed by the server used_cpu_sys, used_cpu_user, used_cpu_sys_children, used_cpu_user_children commandstats Per-command counters cmdstat_get, cmdstat_set, with values such as calls=1,usec=2,usec_per_call=2.00 cluster Cluster state cluster_enabled keyspace Keys per database db0, db1, with values such as keys=12,expires=4,avg_ttl=0 all Every section above —

Fields appear or disappear according to the Redis version and the instance configuration (for example, AOF fields exist only when AOF is enabled), so a module that is missing from the output is a field the server did not report in that run.

docs.title: Everyday operation
docs.text:
• The plugin keeps no state: every execution reads the instance at that moment, so it can be run manually at any time.
  • In server plugin mode, schedule it from Pandora FMS, for example through the server plugin scheduler or cron. In agent plugin mode, the Pandora FMS agent executes it according to the configured plugin schedule.
  • Use debug=1 in manual runs to print the connection details, the section list and the complete INFO response. debug writes to standard output, so in agent plugin mode it interleaves with the module XML and the agent cannot parse the output: never enable it in a scheduled agent plugin execution.
  • Because module names carry no instance prefix, keep one agent per instance and use module_group to separate these modules from others in the same agent.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• No module XML is printed in agent plugin mode — check that as_agent_plugin=1 is in effect (when both mode keys are empty the plugin runs as a server plugin), that metrics is not empty, and that the configuration file is the first argument of the command.
  • The agent never appears in Pandora FMS in server mode — the delivery failed silently. Run once with debug=1 to see the reason: a missing mode and a missing local_folder are reported only with debug enabled, and a Tentacle failure prints the client message only with debug enabled.
  • tentacle_client cannot be found or cannot connect — make sure the client is installed and in PATH (or set tentacle_client to its absolute path) and that tentacle_ip and tentacle_port reach the Tentacle server.
  • The local folder delivery fails — check that local_folder exists, is writable by the user that runs the plugin, and names a folder, not a file. The error is printed only with debug=1.
  • NOAUTH or an authentication error from Redis — the instance requires a password and password is empty or wrong. If the instance requires an ACL user name as well, this plugin cannot authenticate (it has no user name key).
  • Connection refused or timeout — the plugin cannot reach server. Check the host, the port, the firewall and that Redis is listening on an address reachable from the monitoring host.
  • Some older modules stop updating after a Redis upgrade or configuration change — the field no longer exists in the INFO output. Adjust metrics or the alerting on that module.
  • The module list is empty — metrics is empty or names sections the instance does not report. Start with metrics=all and narrow it once you see which modules arrive.

docs.title: Configuration file keys
docs.text:
Name Required Default Description server Yes — Redis address, as <REDIS_HOST>:<REDIS_PORT>. Include the port. password No Empty (no authentication) Password sent to Redis. The plugin has no user name key. metrics Yes — INFO sections to read, separated by spaces. all reads every section. as_agent_plugin No 0 1 (or any value greater than 0) prints the module XML on standard output. as_server_plugin No 1 when neither mode key is set 1 (or any value greater than 0) builds and delivers the agent document. When both mode keys are 1, both models run. agent_name Required in server mode — Name of the agent created in Pandora FMS. module_group No Empty (no group sent) Name of an existing module group assigned to every generated module. Resolved case-insensitively; an unknown name leaves the modules without that group. mode Required in server mode Empty tentacle delivers with the Tentacle client; any other value copies the agent document into local_folder. transfer_mode No Empty Alternative key for mode, read only when mode is empty. local_folder Required when mode is not tentacle — Destination folder for the agent document copy. temp No /tmp on Linux Folder where the agent document is written before delivery. tmp is accepted as an alternative key. tentacle_ip Required when mode=tentacle — Tentacle server address. tentacle_port No 41121 Tentacle server port. tentacle_client No tentacle_client Tentacle client executable, resolved in PATH or given as an absolute path. tentacle_opts No Empty Extra options passed to the Tentacle client, separated by whitespace. debug No 0 1 (or any value greater than 0) prints connection details, the section list and diagnostic messages on standard output.

Boolean keys are enabled by any numeric value greater than 0; 0, an empty value or a non-numeric value means disabled.

docs.title: Command-line execution
docs.text:
./redis_monitor [config-file] [ -key value ... ]
Condition Behavior The first argument names an existing file The plugin reads it as the configuration file and applies the remaining arguments over its values The first argument is not a file, or the file path comes after a flag The file is not read; the plugin runs from the defaults plus the arguments -key value Replaces the value of key --key value or -key=value Not recognized: the pair is read as a different key that the plugin ignores, so the documented key keeps its default or file value Arguments that do not form a -key value pair Ignored; a trailing argument without a value is not reported The command line is empty The plugin runs with the default values; no usage text is printed -h or --help No help option exists: it produces no help output and is treated like any other unknown flag

Unknown keys are accepted and ignored: the plugin does not validate the key set.

docs.text: Situation Result mode=tentacle and the Tentacle transfer succeeds The temporary file is removed after the transfer mode=tentacle and the transfer fails The document is not delivered; the client message is printed only with debug=1 Any other mode The document is copied into local_folder and the temporary file is removed mode empty and no transfer_mode alternative Nothing is delivered; the reason is printed only with debug=1 Delivery result Not reflected in the exit status; verify in the Pandora FMS console

docs.title: SAP HANA Database plugin
docs.text:
Article last updated: 2026-10-27.

Discovery integration recommended

For new installations use SAP HANA Discovery, which is the recommended integration for this service. This plugin is the legacy path.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The SAP HANA Database addon monitors a SAP HANA database from Pandora FMS with the SQL queries you write. Each execution opens one connection to the SQL port of a single database, runs every query of a query file and turns each result into one Pandora FMS module. Nothing is installed on the database server, and no SAP command-line tool is needed on the host that runs the addon.

A run is one-shot: it connects, collects, delivers and exits, and it keeps no state between executions. The modules reach Pandora FMS in one of three ways:

  • Data folder (default): the run writes one agent data document into a Pandora FMS data folder and prints 1.
  • Agent plugin: with --as_agent_plugin 1 the run prints the module XML on standard output, for a Pandora FMS agent to ingest, and writes no file.
  • Tentacle: with --tentacle_address the run writes the document and sends it to a Tentacle server.

The Marketplace entry pandorafms.sap_hana_database distributes this query-file collector. An older variant of the same addon, which needs the SAP hdbsql and sapcontrol client tools on the monitoring host and runs a fixed query set from a key=value file, takes different options and produces different module names. This page does not describe that variant.

SAP HANA Discovery (pandorafms.sap.hana) is a different addon: it runs from the Discovery task wizard and creates one agent per database automatically, with a fixed set of metric groups. This addon is configured per execution and publishes what your queries return. See SAP HANA Discovery.

docs.title: Compatibility and availability
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.sap_hana_database, version 1.1 Documented target Version of the Marketplace entry, last updated 2026-06-02. See Addon identity Pandora FMS release Not validated No release-specific record exists for this addon. The Marketplace states that its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later System of the host that runs the addon Not validated Not recorded for version 1.1. The previous documentation of this addon recorded a test on CentOS 7 SAP HANA release Not validated Not recorded for version 1.1. The previous documentation of this addon recorded SAP HANA 2.00.059 SQL access from the host that runs the addon to the database port Required The addon opens one connection with --ip and --port A SAP HANA user able to read every object your queries read Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. See Database access A Pandora FMS data server reading --data_dir Required for the data folder mode The document is only collected when the data server reads the folder where the addon writes it A Pandora FMS server to execute the console plugin Required for the console mode The plugin server runs the registered plugin

The download of this addon is limited to licensed users, according to its Marketplace entry. This page does not describe any further license terms.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. Network access from the host that runs the addon to the SQL port of the target database. The addon has no default port: --port is required.
  2. A SAP HANA user and its password, able to read every object your queries read. The example queries read the views listed in Database access.
  3. A host to run the addon: the Pandora FMS server for a console server plugin, a host with a Pandora FMS agent for agent plugin mode, or any host whose data folder the Pandora FMS data server reads. The addon connects to the database port directly, so the SAP client tools are not required there.
  4. A query file. The addon reads it on every execution; without it the run publishes nothing (see Known limitations).
  5. A Pandora FMS side that receives the output: the plugin server that runs the registered plugin, the data server that reads the data folder, the agent that runs the addon, or the Tentacle server.
  6. Write permission on the data folder for the user that runs the addon, when documents are delivered there.
  7. The Tentacle client (tentacle_client) in PATH, only when the run delivers through Tentacle.

docs.title: Database access
docs.text:
The addon reads only what your queries ask for. The user needs read access to those objects; SAP HANA defines which privilege each view requires, and no narrower grant is documented for this addon. The queries in the example file read:

Object Read by DUMMY, M_DATABASE Timestamp and version M_CONVERTER_STATISTICS Backup size estimate M_DATA_VOLUMES Volume list SYS_DATABASES.M_SERVICE_STATISTICS Requests per second and response time M_SERVICE_THREADS CPU time M_RS_MEMORY Row store fragmentation M_LICENSE License validity, permanence and usage M_VOLUME_IO_TOTAL_STATISTICS Read and write bandwidth PUBLIC.M_CONNECTIONS Running connections M_HOST_RESOURCE_UTILIZATION Memory usage M_BLOCKED_TRANSACTIONS Blocked transactions SYS.M_BACKUP_CATALOG Only the two backup queries of the example set

The addon sends every line of the query file to the database exactly as written, with no restriction to SELECT. Use a dedicated user with read-only access and keep only read statements in the file.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.sap_hana_database

Copy the addon executable pandora_hana and the example query file pandora_hana.conf to the host that will run it. For a console server plugin the recommended folder is /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/. This page invokes the executable as pandora_hana; use the name your copy carries in the commands below.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text: The addon has no configuration file of its own: every setting is a command-line option, and the queries live in the separate file named by --conf.

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
A run needs the database address, its SQL port, a user, a password and the query file:

./pandora_hana --ip <TARGET_HOST> --port 30013 --user <USERNAME> \
    --password <PASSWORD> --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --agent_name sap-hana

SAP HANA publishes one SQL port per database, and the port encodes the instance number NN:

Database Port Tenant database 3NN13 System database (SYSTEMDB) of a multitenant system 3NN13 System database of a single-tenant system 3NN15

With instance 00, for example, a tenant database listens on 30013 and the system database of a single-tenant system on 30015.

--password is passed on the command line: the shell keeps it in its history and the operating system process list shows it while the run lasts. In the console, mark the field that holds the password as hidden, and restrict who can read the server process list. The addon has no option to read the password from a file.

docs.title: Choose the delivery mode
docs.text:
Mode Options Behavior Data folder (default) none Writes one <agent_name>.<epoch>.data document into --data_dir (default /var/spool/pandora/data_in/) and prints 1 Agent plugin --as_agent_plugin 1 Prints one <module> block per module on standard output and writes no file Tentacle --tentacle_address <ADDRESS> Writes the document into --data_dir, sends it with tentacle_client and prints 1

--tentacle_address takes precedence over --as_agent_plugin. Any --as_agent_plugin value other than 1 selects the data folder mode, which is also the default. --tentacle_port defaults to 41121 and is only used when --tentacle_address is set.

Use agent plugin mode when a Pandora FMS agent runs the addon: the agent ingests the printed modules. Use the data folder mode when the plugin server runs the addon in the console and the local data server collects the document. Use Tentacle when the addon runs on a host that must deliver to a remote Pandora FMS server.

--agent_name names the agent that holds the modules; without it the addon uses Sap_Hana. --prefix_module prepends <prefix>_ to every module name, so several runs can publish into the same agent without duplicate module names. -g/--group sets the name of the Pandora FMS group written in the agent document; its default is SAP.

docs.title: Define the queries
docs.text:
The query file has one query per line, split into colon-separated fields:

name:query:module_type[:description]
  • name becomes the module name, module_type the Pandora FMS module type and the optional fourth field the module description. The first three fields are mandatory.
  • The query cannot contain a colon. The line is split on every colon, so a : inside the query shifts the type and the description, and a : inside the description truncates it, both without warning.
  • A line that contains # anywhere is skipped as a comment, not only a line that starts with #.
  • A line is skipped only when it is completely empty. A line holding spaces is read as an incomplete query and stops the run (see Known limitations).
  • Each query produces one module. Every returned row becomes one entry of the module data list, holding the columns of the row joined by ;.
  • Every query in the file is executed on every run, in file order.

The example file that ships with the addon has this shape:

Timestamp:SELECT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP FROM DUMMY;:generic_data_string:Current timestamp
Hana_version:SELECT VERSION FROM M_DATABASE;:generic_data_string:version
Hana_Memory:SELECT HOST, round ( 100 * INSTANCE_TOTAL_MEMORY_USED_SIZE / INSTANCE_TOTAL_MEMORY_ALLOCATED_SIZE, 2), round (INSTANCE_TOTAL_MEMORY_ALLOCATED_SIZE / 1024/1024/1024, 2), round (INSTANCE_TOTAL_MEMORY_USED_SIZE / 1024/1024/1024, 2) from M_HOST_RESOURCE_UTILIZATION:generic_data_string:retrieve memory usages

The complete file is in Example query file. Keep the file readable only by the user that runs the addon: it holds the queries, not credentials, but it reveals the database objects you monitor.

docs.title: Register the plugin in the console
docs.text:
A console server plugin runs the addon from the Pandora FMS server. The plugin server executes it in data folder mode, the addon writes its document and the data server ingests it, so the agent and its modules appear in the console.

  1. Open Servers → Plugins and click Register Plugin.
  2. Set the name, the plugin type Standard, an optional maximum timeout and a description.
  3. In Plugin command, enter the path to pandora_hana on the Pandora FMS server, for example /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora_hana.
  4. In Plugin parameters, pass the connection through the plugin macros _field1_, _field2_, ... and keep the query file at a fixed path on the server:
--ip _field1_ --port _field2_ --user _field3_ --password _field4_ --conf /etc/pandora/plugins/pandora_hana.conf --agent_name _field5_
  1. In Macro parameters, describe each field. The example uses these values:
Field Description Example value _field1_ Database host name or IP address <TARGET_HOST> _field2_ SQL port of the database 30013 _field3_ SAP HANA user that runs the queries <USERNAME> _field4_ Password for that user; mark Hide value — _field5_ Name of the agent that will hold the modules sap-hana

Do not add --as_agent_plugin 1 here: the console run must stay in data folder mode, because the plugin module value is what the addon prints, and in agent plugin mode it prints the module XML instead of 1.

Once registered, the plugin is available when creating plugin modules. Each module fills the fields individually, and the field values can use the Pandora FMS macros documented in the console Plug-in macros help.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the addon manually with --as_agent_plugin 1, so it prints the modules instead of writing a file:

./pandora_hana --ip <TARGET_HOST> --port 30013 --user <USERNAME> \
    --password <PASSWORD> --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --as_agent_plugin 1

A successful run prints one <module> block per query and exits with status 0. The values below are illustrative; yours come from your database:

<module>
    <name><![CDATA[Timestamp]]></name>
    <type>generic_data_string</type>
    <datalist>
    <data>
        <value><![CDATA[2026-10-26 10:14:32.123456789]]></value>
    </data>
    </datalist>
    <description><![CDATA[Current timestamp]]></description>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[Hana_get_stated_connections]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <datalist>
    <data>
        <value><![CDATA[7]]></value>
    </data>
    </datalist>
    <description><![CDATA[retrieve connection status]]></description>
</module>

With the default data folder mode the same run prints 1 and writes one document:

/var/spool/pandora/data_in/sap-hana.1793001234.data

After the first scheduled execution, open the agent named by --agent_name (default Sap_Hana) and check that it holds one module per query of the file.

-h prints the usage summary with its options and one execution example. The summary prints the addon's build marker 270622, which does not match the Marketplace version (see Known limitations).

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
A run creates one agent, or updates the existing one, and never more than one. The agent document declares these properties:

Property Value Agent name and alias --agent_name (default Sap_Hana) Description SAP Hana Group --group (default SAP) Interval Empty; Pandora FMS assigns the interval of a new agent Address Empty

Each line of the query file produces exactly one module:

  • The module name is the first field, prefixed with <prefix>_ when --prefix_module is set.
  • The module type is the third field, written verbatim. Use the Pandora FMS module type your data requires: generic_data for numbers and generic_data_string for text.
  • The description is the fourth field, and it is empty when the field is absent.
  • The value is a data list with one entry per returned row. The columns of a row are joined by ; inside the entry, so a query with three columns returns entries such as host01;30003;7.

Because every column of every row becomes part of one value, write numeric modules with a query that returns one row and one column. A query that returns several rows publishes several entries in the same data list, and a query that returns several columns publishes them concatenated.

A query that returns no rows still produces its module, with an empty data list. A query the database rejects produces no module at all: the failure is reported on standard error and the following queries still run.

The example file groups its queries by subject:

  • Backups and volumes. Backups_Size estimates the backup size and Data_disk_information lists the data volumes.
  • Version and time. Timestamp and Hana_version identify the database and stamp the run.
  • Performance. Hana_service_statics reports requests per second and response time, Hana_cpu_time the service CPU time and Hana_IO_Stats the read and write bandwidth per volume.
  • Memory. Hana_Memory reports the memory in use over the allocated memory, and Hana_rs_fragmentation the row store free ratio.
  • Capacity and health. Hana_license reports license validity, permanence and usage, Hana_get_stated_connections the running connections and Hana_Transactions the blocked transactions.

docs.title: Run-time behavior
docs.text:
• One execution opens one connection, runs every query of the file in order, delivers and exits. The connection is opened before the query file is read, so an unreachable database stops the run before any query is parsed.
  • The addon keeps no state between executions. The query file is re-read on every run, so a query added to the file is collected from the next execution.
  • There is no verbose or debug option. The output is the module XML with --as_agent_plugin 1, a 1 in the other two modes, or an error message.
  • The addon writes one document per run, so a run collects all modules of the agent at the same timestamp.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
These are behaviors of version 1.1, documented as they are.

  • The query file is effectively mandatory. A run without a readable --conf prints Error al conectarse followed by the operating system error, then Error: name 'f' is not defined and 0, and ends with status 0 without publishing anything.
  • A blank line with spaces stops the run with status 0. Only a line that is completely empty is ignored. A line holding spaces or tabs has fewer than three fields, so the run prints It is mandatory to specify name, query and type!, ends immediately and publishes nothing, and the exit status is 0.
  • A query cannot contain a colon and a description loses everything after one. The line is split on every colon, so a colon inside the query shifts the module type, and a colon inside the description truncates it. No warning is printed in either case.
  • A line with # anywhere is skipped. A # inside a query or a description removes the whole line from the run, not only a comment line.
  • A failed Tentacle transfer still prints 1. With --tentacle_address, the addon writes the document, sends it and prints 1 even when tentacle_client fails or is missing; the error goes to standard error and the document stays in --data_dir.
  • Two runs of the same agent in one second collide. The document name uses one-second resolution and the file is created exclusively. A run that starts while the previous document of the same agent is still in the folder ends with ERROR - Could not write file: ... please check directory permissions and status 1, and the modules of that run are lost.
  • The build marker does not match the Marketplace version. The usage summary prints the build marker 270622, the date of the build, while the Marketplace entry publishes version 1.1.
  • No TLS or certificate option is exposed. The addon passes the address, port, user and password to the database client, and leaves any encryption setting to that client's defaults. It has no option to set a certificate or to require an encrypted connection.
  • The password only exists as a command-line option. There is no credentials file and no standard-input form, so the password appears in the shell history and in the process list of the host that runs the addon.
  • --tentacle_port is ignored without --tentacle_address. The port is only used by the Tentacle branch.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text: Symptom Cause and action A traceback from the database client, ending with the connection call, status 1 The connection failed. Check --ip, --port, the user, the password and the network path to the SQL port. Remember that a tenant database and the system database listen on different ports Error al conectarse and then Error: ... and 0, status 0 --conf could not be opened. Check the path and its read permissions It is mandatory to specify name, query and type! A line of the query file has fewer than three colon-separated fields, usually because it is blank or holds only spaces error with the query:<query>.<error> on standard error The database rejected that query. The following lines are still processed A module is missing from the agent Its query failed, or its line was skipped because it contained # A numeric module receives more than one data entry per run The query returns more than one row. Restrict it to one row and one column for numeric modules Tentacle error on standard error and a stored 1 The transfer failed. Check --tentacle_address, --tentacle_port and that tentacle_client is in PATH; the document remains in --data_dir ERROR - Could not write file: ... The data folder is not writable, or a document with the same name exists already (see Known limitations) The agent does not appear in the console The document was written to a --data_dir the Pandora FMS data server does not read, or the run ended with an error. Check the folder and the run output bad interpreter or a missing-interpreter message The interpreter declared in the first line of the executable is not installed on this host, or the file lost its execute permission. Run the addon from a host that has that interpreter, or restore the permission with chmod +x

docs.title: Command-line options
docs.text: Option Required Default Description --ip Yes — Database host name or IP address --port Yes — SQL port of the database (3NN13 for a tenant database, 3NN15 for the system database of a single-tenant system) --user Yes — SAP HANA user that runs the queries --password Yes — Password for that user --conf Yes — Query file. It is read on every run --agent_name No Sap_Hana Name and alias of the agent that holds the modules --prefix_module No — Prefix joined to every module name as <prefix>_<name> -g, --group No SAP Name of the Pandora FMS group written in the agent document --data_dir No /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Folder for the agent data document in data folder and Tentacle modes --as_agent_plugin No 0 1 prints the module XML on standard output; any other value writes the document into --data_dir --tentacle_address No — Tentacle server address. It takes precedence over --as_agent_plugin --tentacle_port No 41121 Tentacle server port, only used with --tentacle_address -h, --help No — Prints the usage summary and exits

docs.title: Query file
docs.text:
Field Required Description name Yes Module name. With --prefix_module, the module name is <prefix>_<name> query Yes SQL statement executed against the database. It cannot contain a colon module_type Yes Pandora FMS module type, written verbatim into the module description No Module description. It cannot contain a colon

A line that contains # is skipped. A line that is completely empty is skipped. Every other line is split on : and executed.

docs.title: Example query file
docs.text:
This is the example file distributed with the addon:

Backups_Size:SELECT SUM(allocated_page_size) FROM M_CONVERTER_STATISTICS;:generic_data:Estimated backup size
Timestamp:SELECT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP FROM DUMMY;:generic_data_string:Current timestamp
Hana_version:SELECT VERSION FROM M_DATABASE;:generic_data_string:version
Data_disk_information:SELECT HOST,PORT,FILE_NAME,STATE,SIZE,MAX_SIZE FROM M_DATA_VOLUMES:generic_data_string:Retrieve Hana disk info
Hana_service_statics:SELECT SERVICE_NAME, DATABASE_NAME, REQUESTS_PER_SEC, RESPONSE_TIME FROM SYS_DATABASES.M_SERVICE_STATISTICS:generic_data_string:Retrieve Hana Requests per second
Hana_cpu_time:SELECT HOST,PORT,SERVICE_NAME, SUM(CPU_TIME_SELF),SUM(CPU_TIME_CUMULATIVE) FROM M_SERVICE_THREADS GROUP BY HOST,PORT,SERVICE_NAME:generic_data_string:Retrieve Hana cpu usage
Hana_rs_fragmentation:SELECT HOST, PORT, TO_DECIMAL(SUM(FREE_SIZE) * 100 / SUM(ALLOCATED_SIZE),10,2), TO_DECIMAL( SUM(FREE_SIZE)/(1024*1024), 10, 2), TO_DECIMAL( SUM(ALLOCATED_SIZE)/(1024*1024), 10, 2) FROM M_RS_MEMORY WHERE CATEGORY = 'TABLE' OR CATEGORY = 'CATALOG'  GROUP BY HOST, PORT:generic_data_string:Retrieve Hana row store fragmentation
Hana_license:SELECT VALID, PERMANENT, PRODUCT_LIMIT, PRODUCT_USAGE FROM M_LICENSE;:generic_data_string:Retrieve license usage
Hana_IO_Stats:SELECT HOST,PORT,TYPE, TO_DECIMAL((TOTAL_READ_SIZE * 1.048576 / (TOTAL_READ_TIME+1)),10,2), TO_DECIMAL((TOTAL_WRITE_SIZE * 1.048576 / (TOTAL_WRITE_TIME+1)),10,2) FROM M_VOLUME_IO_TOTAL_STATISTICS:generic_data_string:Retrieve IO bandwidth
Hana_get_stated_connections:SELECT COUNT(*) FROM PUBLIC.M_CONNECTIONS WHERE CONNECTION_STATUS ='RUNNING':generic_data:retrieve connection status
Hana_Memory:SELECT HOST, round ( 100 * INSTANCE_TOTAL_MEMORY_USED_SIZE / INSTANCE_TOTAL_MEMORY_ALLOCATED_SIZE, 2), round (INSTANCE_TOTAL_MEMORY_ALLOCATED_SIZE / 1024/1024/1024, 2), round (INSTANCE_TOTAL_MEMORY_USED_SIZE / 1024/1024/1024, 2) from M_HOST_RESOURCE_UTILIZATION:generic_data_string:retrieve memory usages
Hana_Transactions:SELECT count(*) FROM M_BLOCKED_TRANSACTIONS;:generic_data:retrieve SAP transaction status

The Marketplace entry also names two backup-catalog modules, Check_no_running_backups and Backup_id_running_backup, that this copy of the file does not include, and its list does not name Data_disk_information, which the file does include. Add the backup lines as your own if you need backup monitoring:

Check_no_running_backups:select * from SYS.M_BACKUP_CATALOG where STATE_NAME = 'running':generic_data_string:Check that no backup is still running
Backup_id_running_backup:select BACKUP_ID from SYS.M_BACKUP_CATALOG where entry_type_name = 'complete data backup' and state_name = 'running' order by sys_start_time desc:generic_data_string:Query to find the BACKUP_ID of the running data backup
