docs.title: Network bandwidth SNMP
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-09-30.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Network bandwidth SNMP plugin retrieves the bandwidth usage of a network device, as a percentage, using SNMP. It reports the amount of information sent and received over a particular time, either for the whole device or for a single interface selected by its index.

The plugin runs as a Pandora FMS server plugin: each execution queries the device, prints one numeric value on standard output, and Pandora FMS stores that value in the module.

  • Result. A single number, the bandwidth usage as a percentage, formatted with 9 decimals (for example 12.345678901).
  • What is measured. By default, the overall bandwidth usage. With -inUsage 1 it reports the input usage only, and with -outUsage 1 the output usage only. If both are enabled, the input usage is reported.
  • Scope. With -ifIndex <n> the plugin measures that interface. Without it, the plugin measures every interface of the device and prints the average of the per-interface percentages, computed over the interfaces that have a usable speed.
  • Measurement window. The value is computed from the difference between the counters read in the current execution and the counters stored by the previous execution. The module interval is therefore the measurement window.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. SNMP read access to the device from the machine that runs the plugin, normally the Pandora FMS server. The default SNMP port is UDP 161.
  2. A device that exposes the IF-MIB objects ifIndex, ifInOctets, ifOutOctets, ifHighSpeed and ifSpeed, and preferably the 64-bit counters ifHCInOctets and ifHCOutOctets. The dot3StatsDuplexStatus object of EtherLike-MIB is optional and is used to detect the duplex mode.
  3. Write permission in the temporary directory (/tmp by default) for the user that runs the plugin. The plugin stores the counters of each execution there to compute the next one.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The plugin is distributed with the Pandora FMS server and needs no separate installation. Its executable is:

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora_snmp_bandwidth

It is registered in Pandora FMS as the server plugin Network bandwidth SNMP, with a maximum timeout of 300 seconds.

docs.title: Choose the SNMP version
docs.text:
• SNMP v1 always uses 32-bit counters, because 64-bit counters do not exist in SNMP v1.
  • SNMP v2c and v3 use 64-bit counters when the device provides them.

On fast links, prefer SNMP v2c or v3. A 32-bit octet counter wraps after 4,294,967,295 octets, which takes about 34 seconds at 1 Gbit/s. The plugin corrects at most one wrap per interval, so long intervals on fast links with 32-bit counters report values lower than the real ones.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
Create one module for each metric and each interface that you want to monitor, using the Network bandwidth SNMP server plugin, and fill in the plugin fields. The plugin returns a numeric percentage; choose the thresholds that fit your environment.

  1. Set SNMP Version(1,2c,3) (1, 2c or 3) and the credentials for that version.
  2. For SNMP v1 and v2c, fill in Community.
  3. For SNMP v3, fill in securityName and, depending on securityLevel, the authentication and privacy fields. See SNMPv3 settings.
  4. Leave Host at its default value _address_, which is the address of the agent, or enter the address of the device.
  5. Set Port if the device does not use the default port 161.
  6. Fill in Interface Index (filter) with the ifIndex of the interface to measure. Leave it empty to measure all the interfaces and obtain their average.
  7. Select the metric:
  8. Overall bandwidth usage: leave inUsage and outUsage empty.
  9. Input usage: set inUsage to 1.
  10. Output usage: set outUsage to 1.
  11. Set UniqId to an identifier that is unique for each module, with no spaces or symbols.
  12. Adjust timeout (seconds per attempt) and retries if the device answers slowly.

Every module needs its own UniqId

The plugin stores the counters of the previous execution in a state file named after the host, or after the UniqId when one is set. Every module that uses the plugin against the same host must have a different UniqId. Otherwise the modules overwrite each other's previous samples and report 0 or wrong values.

docs.title: SNMPv3 settings
docs.text:
Field Behavior securityName Required for SNMP v3. securityLevel noAuthNoPriv (default), authNoPriv or authPriv. Case-insensitive. authProtocol, authKey Required with authNoPriv and authPriv. privProtocol, privKey Required with authPriv. context Optional SNMPv3 context name. Leave it empty to use no context.

An invalid combination or value makes the plugin print nothing.

For the 192-bit and 256-bit AES protocols, choose the one that matches the key localization variant that the device implements: AES192 and AES256 use the Blumenthal extension (Net-SNMP style), while AES192C and AES256C use the Reeder extension (Cisco style).

docs.title: Options not available in the console
docs.text: The options -max, -f, -debug, -parallel, -tmp, -tmp_file, -tmp_separator and -log are not fields of the plugin registration. They can be used only from the command line or from a configuration file. See Operate and Reference.

docs.title: Protect the credentials
docs.text: The community and the SNMPv3 passwords passed as command-line options can be visible in the operating system process list. To keep them out of the command line, store them in a configuration file and pass its path as the first argument. See Use a configuration file.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually with a -uniqid different from the one used by any production module, so that the test does not alter the samples of that module:

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora_snmp_bandwidth -version 2c -community <COMMUNITY> -host <TARGET_HOST> -ifIndex <IFINDEX> -uniqid <UNIQUE_ID>
  1. The first run prints 0.000000000, because there is no previous data yet.
  2. Wait some seconds while the interface carries traffic and run the same command again. The second run prints the real value, for example 12.345678901.

An empty output means that the plugin failed. Run the command again with -debug 1 and read the log file, as described in Debug log.

docs.title: Output and exit status
docs.text:
• The plugin always exits with status 0.
  • On a failure (no SNMP answer, invalid parameters, unreachable device) it prints nothing.
  • Running it without arguments prints the help text.

docs.title: Meaning of the value
docs.text:
For each interface the plugin computes a percentage from the octet counter differences (Δin, Δout), the seconds between executions (Δt) and the interface speed in bit/s:

Metric Formula Bandwidth, half duplex or unknown duplex (Δin + Δout) × 8 / (Δt × speed) × 100 Bandwidth, full duplex (Δin × 8 / (Δt × speed) + Δout × 8 / (Δt × speed)) / 2 × 100 Input usage Δin × 8 / (Δt × speed) × 100, capped at 100 Output usage Δout × 8 / (Δt × speed) × 100, capped at 100
  • If the speed or Δt is 0, the value of the interface is 0.
  • If a counter is lower than in the previous execution, the plugin treats it as a wrap and computes the difference as max − previous + current + 1, where max is 4,294,967,295 for 32-bit counters and 18,446,744,073,709,551,615 for 64-bit counters.
  • Without -ifIndex, the result is the arithmetic mean of the per-interface values.

docs.title: First execution and zero values
docs.text: The plugin prints 0.000000000 when it has no previous data for the counters. This happens on the first execution, after the counter width changes (for example, when the device stops returning 64-bit values), and the first time the plugin runs over a state file written by an earlier version of the plugin.

docs.title: Counter width
docs.text:
• Without -ifIndex, the plugin reads the interface table and uses the 64-bit counters ifHCInOctets and ifHCOutOctets when the device returns numeric values for ifHCInOctets. Otherwise it uses the 32-bit counters ifInOctets and ifOutOctets.
  • With -ifIndex <n>, it uses the 64-bit counters when ifHCInOctets.<n> returns a number, and the 32-bit counters otherwise.
  • With SNMP v1 it always uses the 32-bit counters.

docs.title: Interface speed
docs.text:
The speed, in bit/s, is selected in this order:

  1. The value of -max, when it is set. It overrides the speed reported by the device for every measured interface and is intended for port channels and aggregated links, where the reported speed is not the real one.
  2. ifHighSpeed (in Mbit/s) multiplied by 1,000,000, when it is greater than 0.
  3. ifSpeed (in bit/s), when it is greater than 0.

An interface without a usable speed is skipped: it is not measured and it is not included in the average. With -ifIndex, the plugin prints 0.000000000 in that case.

The value of -max is in bit/s

-max is expressed in bit/s, not in Mbit/s, even though ifHighSpeed is reported in Mbit/s. For a port channel of 2 × 1 Gbit/s, use -max 2000000000. The value -max 2000 means 2 kbit/s: the input and output usage saturate at 100 % and the overall bandwidth reports values far above 100.

docs.title: Duplex mode
docs.text: The plugin reads the duplex mode from dot3StatsDuplexStatus: the value 2 means half duplex and 3 means full duplex. Any other value, or no answer, is an unknown duplex mode, which is handled as half duplex. Use -f 1 to handle an unknown duplex mode as full duplex.

docs.title: Duplicate ifIndex values
docs.text:
When the plugin measures all the interfaces, it identifies each interface by the value of ifIndex. If the device reports the same value in several rows, the plugin keeps a single entry for that value:

  • The last row that has a usable speed replaces the earlier ones.
  • A later row without a usable speed does not remove an earlier valid one.
  • The state file has one line per distinct value, and the average divides by the number of distinct values.

docs.title: Use a configuration file
docs.text:
If the first argument is an existing file, the plugin reads it as a configuration file. Use it to keep credentials out of the command line:

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora_snmp_bandwidth <PATH_TO_CONFIG> -ifIndex 5
  • Each line has the form key=value. The keys are the option names without the leading dash.
  • Lines that start with # are comments.
  • The directive include=<file> includes another file.
  • Options given on the command line override the values of the file.

docs.title: Debug log
docs.text:
With -debug 1 the plugin writes a log file while it runs. The value printed on standard output does not change.

  • The file is <tmp>/pandora_bandwidth_<host or uniqid>.log, with the same character replacement as the state file (see State file). Use -log to write it to another path.
  • Each line has the form <date> - [info] <message>. The first message of an execution truncates the file.
  • The log records the target, the SNMP version, the timeout and retries, the state file, every SNMP request and answer with its timing, the counter width selected and the reason, the speed source and the duplex mode of each interface, the skipped interfaces and the reason, the previous and saved state, the formulas with their values substituted, the averages and the printed value.
  • The community, the authentication and privacy passwords and the SNMPv3 user are never written to the log. Secret values are masked as *** if they appear.

docs.title: Concurrency and timing
docs.text:
• -parallel <N> sets the maximum number of concurrent SNMP requests when all the interfaces are measured. The default is 8. A value that is not a positive integer keeps the default.
  • -timeout sets the seconds to wait for each attempt and -retries the number of retries. Values out of range make the plugin print nothing.
  • Keep the module interval short enough that a 32-bit counter cannot wrap more than once between executions.

docs.title: Command-line syntax
docs.text:
• Options are -name value pairs. A trailing option without a value is ignored.
  • Boolean options (-inUsage, -outUsage, -f, -debug) are enabled with a number greater than 0, for example 1.
  • Short aliases exist for the connection options. See Command line and configuration file options.
  • The option -extra is accepted and ignored.

docs.title: Connectivity check
docs.text: Before it measures anything, the plugin reads sysObjectID (.1.3.6.1.2.1.1.2.0) from the device. If the device gives no answer, the plugin stops without printing anything.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
• The plugin prints nothing. The device did not answer the sysObjectID request, a parameter is invalid, -timeout or -retries is out of range, or the SNMPv3 settings are incomplete. Run the plugin with -debug 1 and read the debug log.
  • The value is always 0.
  • It is the first execution, and the second one has not run yet.
  • Another module uses the same UniqId (or the same host without a UniqId), and both overwrite the previous samples. Give each module its own UniqId.
  • The interface has no usable speed. See "The interface is not measured" below.
  • The time between executions is 0.
  • The counter width changed since the previous execution.
  • The input or output usage is stuck at 100 %, or the bandwidth exceeds 100 %. The speed used is too low. Check that -max is expressed in bit/s and not in Mbit/s, and check the ifHighSpeed and ifSpeed values that the device reports.
  • The values are lower than expected on a fast link. The plugin is using 32-bit counters that wrap more than once per interval. Use SNMP v2c or v3 so that 64-bit counters are used, or shorten the module interval.
  • The interface is not measured. Neither ifHighSpeed nor ifSpeed is greater than 0. Set the speed with -max.
  • The duplex mode is unknown. If the link is full duplex, use -f 1.

docs.title: Console fields (Network bandwidth SNMP)
docs.text:
Field Required Default Description SNMP Version(1,2c,3) No 2c SNMP version: 1, 2c or 3. Passed as -version. Community Yes for v1 and v2c — SNMP community. It may be empty. Passed as -community. Host No _address_ Address of the device. The default is the address of the agent. Passed as -host. Port No 161 UDP port of the SNMP service. Passed as -port. Interface Index (filter) No Empty ifIndex of the interface to measure. Empty measures all the interfaces. Passed as -ifIndex. securityName Yes for v3 — SNMPv3 user name. Passed as -securityName. context No Empty SNMPv3 context name. Empty means no context. Passed as -context. securityLevel No noAuthNoPriv noAuthNoPriv, authNoPriv or authPriv. Passed as -securityLevel. authProtocol Yes with authNoPriv and authPriv — MD5, SHA (or SHA1), SHA224, SHA256, SHA384 or SHA512. Passed as -authProtocol. authKey Yes with authNoPriv and authPriv — Authentication password. Passed as -authKey. privProtocol Yes with authPriv — DES, AES (or AES128), AES192, AES256, AES192C or AES256C. Passed as -privProtocol. privKey Yes with authPriv — Privacy password. Passed as -privKey. UniqId Yes, one per module — Unique identifier of the module, with no spaces or symbols. The plugin needs to store information in the temporary directory to calculate the bandwidth. Passed as -uniqid. inUsage No Empty Set to 1 to retrieve the input usage (%). Passed as -inUsage. outUsage No Empty Set to 1 to retrieve the output usage (%). Passed as -outUsage. timeout No 2 Seconds to wait for each attempt. Passed as -timeout. retries No 1 Number of retries. Passed as -retries.

The plugin registration builds this parameter line:

-version '_field1_' -community '_field2_' -host '_field3_' -port '_field4_' -ifIndex '_field5_' -securityName '_field6_' -context '_field7_' -securityLevel '_field8_' -authProtocol '_field9_' -authKey '_field10_' -privProtocol '_field11_' -privKey '_field12_' -uniqid '_field13_' -inUsage '_field14_' -outUsage '_field15_' -timeout '_field16_' -retries '_field17_'

docs.title: Command line and configuration file options
docs.text:
The same names are valid as keys of the configuration file, without the leading dash.

Name Alias Required Default Description -version -v No 2c SNMP version: 1, 2, 2c or 3. -community -c Yes for v1 and v2c — SNMP community. It may be empty. -host -h No 127.0.0.1 Address of the device. -port -p No 161 UDP port, from 0 to 65535. -timeout — No 2 Seconds per attempt, from 1 to 60. Decimals are allowed. -retries — No 1 Retries, from 0 to 20. -securityName -u Yes for v3 — SNMPv3 user name. -context -n No Empty SNMPv3 context name. -securityLevel -l No noAuthNoPriv noAuthNoPriv, authNoPriv or authPriv (case-insensitive). -authProtocol -a Yes with authNoPriv and authPriv — MD5, SHA (or SHA1), SHA224, SHA256, SHA384 or SHA512. -authKey -A Yes with authNoPriv and authPriv — Authentication password. -privProtocol -x Yes with authPriv — DES, AES (or AES128), AES192, AES256, AES192C or AES256C (case-insensitive). -privKey -X Yes with authPriv — Privacy password. -ifIndex — No Empty ifIndex of the interface to measure. Without it, all the interfaces are measured and averaged. -inUsage — No Disabled A number greater than 0 reports the input usage only. -outUsage — No Disabled A number greater than 0 reports the output usage only. If -inUsage is also enabled, the input usage is reported. -max — No Not set Interface speed in bit/s, used for every measured interface instead of the speed reported by the device. -f — No Disabled A number greater than 0 handles an unknown duplex mode as full duplex. -uniqid — No Not set Identifier used to name the state file and the log instead of the host. Required in practice when several modules query the same host. -parallel — No 8 Maximum concurrent SNMP requests when all the interfaces are measured. -tmp — No /tmp Directory of the state file and the log. -tmp_file — No Not set Full path of the state file. -tmp_separator — No ; Field separator of the state file. -debug — No Disabled A number greater than 0 writes the debug log. -log — No Not set Path of the debug log file.

docs.title: State file
docs.text:
The plugin stores the counters of each execution in a state file:

  • Default path: <tmp>/pandora_bandwidth_<host>.idx, or <tmp>/pandora_bandwidth_<uniqid>.idx when -uniqid is set.
  • Every . in the whole path is replaced with _. For host 192.0.2.10, the file is /tmp/pandora_bandwidth_192_0_2_10.idx.
  • -tmp changes the directory, -tmp_file sets the full path and -tmp_separator sets the field separator.

The file has one line per interface, in this format:

timestamp;ifIndex;inOctets;outOctets;width;

width is 32 or 64. Lines with a missing or different width are ignored, which is treated as having no previous data. Each execution rewrites the file with only the interfaces measured in that execution.

docs.title: OIDs used
docs.text: Object OID Use sysObjectID .1.3.6.1.2.1.1.2.0 Connectivity check ifIndex .1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.1 List of interfaces ifInOctets .1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.10 32-bit input counter ifOutOctets .1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.16 32-bit output counter ifHCInOctets .1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.6 64-bit input counter ifHCOutOctets .1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.10 64-bit output counter ifHighSpeed .1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.15 Speed in Mbit/s ifSpeed .1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.5 Speed in bit/s dot3StatsDuplexStatus .1.3.6.1.2.1.10.7.2.1.19 Duplex mode (2 half, 3 full)

docs.title: Pandora Spark
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Pandora Spark reads the REST API of an Apache Spark server and turns the metrics of every application executor into Pandora FMS modules. Each run lists the applications the endpoint knows about, then the executors of each application, and creates one agent per application with one module per executor metric.

The addon is a server plugin. Each run builds the agent data documents and writes them directly into the Pandora FMS data directory, where the Data Server reads them. It does not deliver through Tentacle, it does not print module XML on standard output, and it does not create Discovery tasks: the agent appears in the console because its data file arrives, not because a task generated it.

The plugin only reads from Spark: it issues two HTTP GET requests per application and never writes to the Spark server.

  • http://<ip>/api/v1/applications — the applications to monitor.
  • http://<ip>/api/v1/applications/<application-id>/executors — the executors of each of those applications.

The same host and port must serve both resources: the plugin builds both URLs from the single value of -i (see Configure).

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.spark, version 1.0 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all its integrations are compatible with these versions. This is a published compatibility statement covering the addon, not a test record for it HTTP access from the Pandora FMS server to the Spark REST endpoint Required The plugin queries http://<host:port>/api/v1/applications and the executors resource of each application One host and port serving both /api/v1/applications and /api/v1/applications/<application-id>/executors Required Both URLs are built from the single value passed to -i A Spark REST endpoint that answers without authentication Required The plugin sends no credentials, token or session Write access to the Pandora FMS data directory Required The plugin writes the agent documents into --data_dir; it has no other delivery path Spark versions Not validated No test record has been published for this addon. The legacy guide stated that it had been tried on CentOS 7 and Fedora; nothing in the available evidence establishes a Spark or operating system range Operating system of the Pandora FMS server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Spark deployments (standalone, YARN, Kubernetes) Not validated The addon depends on the REST resources above, not on the deployment mode

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. A Spark endpoint with the REST API reachable from the Pandora FMS server: the application UI of a running application, or the Spark history server for applications that already finished.
  2. A REST endpoint that answers unauthenticated requests. If Spark is configured to require authentication on its REST API, the plugin has no way to provide it (see Operate and troubleshoot).
  3. A Pandora FMS server with write access to the data directory, by default /var/spool/pandora/data_in/. The plugin writes there, so it runs on the Pandora FMS server itself or on a host that writes to that same directory.
  4. The Data Server enabled, so the documents written into the data directory are read and the agents appear in the console.
  5. The Plugin Server enabled, when the plugin is registered in the console and executed from there.
  6. The pandora_spark executable from the addon package.

docs.title: Expose the Spark REST API
docs.text:
The plugin can read two different views of a Spark deployment, and the port you give to -i selects which one:

What you want to monitor Endpoint that serves it Default port Applications that are running now The application UI of the driver 4040 Applications that already finished The Spark history server 18080

Those are Spark's default ports; the plugin does not assume either of them, it queries whatever port you pass.

For running applications, the UI of the first application binds to 4040 and each additional concurrent application that cannot bind takes the next free port. One run with -i <SPARK_HOST>:4040 therefore sees the applications published on that port, not every application of the cluster.

For finished applications, enable event logging and the history server on the Spark side. In spark-defaults.conf, for example:

spark.eventLog.enabled           true
spark.eventLog.dir               <EVENT_LOG_PATH>
spark.history.fs.logDirectory    <EVENT_LOG_PATH>

The two path keys must point to the same location, and it must be readable by the history server. Start the history server with the script that ships with the Spark installation, next to the master and worker start scripts:

<SPARK_HOME>/sbin/start-history-server.sh

Only the port you actually query has to be reachable from the Pandora FMS server. The plugin makes plain HTTP requests to that port and nothing else, so the master, worker and submission ports that a Spark cluster needs for its own operation are not part of this configuration.

Check the endpoint before configuring the plugin:

curl -s 'http://<SPARK_HOST>:<SPARK_PORT>/api/v1/applications'

The answer must be a JSON list of applications. An empty list ([]) means the endpoint is alive but knows no application: the history server has no event logs yet, or no application has been submitted on that UI port.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.spark

The package is pandorafms.spark.1.0.pspz2. Load it with the console package manager, or register the plugin by hand:

  1. Copy the pandora_spark executable to the Pandora FMS server, for example to /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/, and give it execute permission:

    sudo chmod 0755 /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora_spark

  2. Register it in Servers → Plugins, as described in Register the plugin in the console.

Nothing is installed on the Spark server, and no Spark client tools are needed on the Pandora FMS server.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text: The whole configuration of the plugin is its command line. It reads no configuration file and no environment variable.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
./pandora_spark -i <SPARK_HOST>:<SPARK_PORT>
  • -i, --ip is required and takes host:port without a scheme. The plugin prepends http:// to the value, so include the port of the endpoint that serves the REST API (4040 or 18080 by default, see Expose the Spark REST API). A value with its own scheme builds an invalid URL and the run fails with the connectivity error.
  • -g, --group sets the group of the generated agents. Its default is weblogic, so a run that omits it puts every Spark agent in that group — pass the group you want explicitly.
  • --data_dir sets the directory where the agent documents are written. Its default is /var/spool/pandora/data_in/.

The same run with every option set:

./pandora_spark -i <SPARK_HOST>:<SPARK_PORT> -g <GROUP_NAME> --data_dir /var/spool/pandora/data_in/

There is no option file, no Tentacle delivery, no TLS, no proxy and no credential input: the endpoint is queried over plain HTTP and whoever can reach it can read the metrics.

-h and --help print the usage summary. A run without -i prints the usage line and the missing-argument error on standard error and exits with status 2 without querying anything.

docs.title: Register the plugin in the console
docs.text:
The plugin is designed to be executed by the Pandora FMS Plugin Server, so Pandora FMS runs it on the schedule of a plugin module:

  1. Open Servers → Plugins and register the plugin, with a name, the description you prefer and the maximum timeout you want for a run.
  2. In Plugin command, enter the absolute path of the executable on the Pandora FMS server, for example /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora_spark.

  3. In Plugin parameters, use the plugin macros _field1_, _field2_, ... as placeholders:

    -i _field1_ -g _field2_ --data_dir _field3_

  4. In Macro parameters, describe each field. The example uses these values:

    Field Description Example value _field1_ Spark REST endpoint as host:port, without a scheme <SPARK_HOST>:4040 _field2_ Group for the generated agents Spark _field3_ Pandora FMS data directory /var/spool/pandora/data_in/

Once registered, create a plugin module that executes it, with the same field values. The module runs on the Pandora FMS server and each execution creates the Spark agents. The module itself receives the plugin output (1 on a successful run), while the Spark metrics arrive through the data directory, in the agents named after each application.

The -g value in the parameters is inherited by every execution of that module. If you monitor two Spark endpoints, register the plugin once and create one module per endpoint with its own fields, using a different group for each one so the two sets of agents stay apart.

docs.title: Delivery and permissions
docs.text:
• Every run writes files named <agent-name>.<epoch-seconds>.data into --data_dir. Each Spark application gets its own agent name, so applications do not share documents.
  • The directory must exist and be writable by the user that runs the plugin. When the write fails, the plugin reports nothing and still ends with 1 (see Operate and troubleshoot).
  • The files must be readable by the Pandora FMS Data Server. Do not change their owner or move them: the Data Server deletes them after processing.
  • Nothing travels over the network towards Pandora FMS. If the plugin runs on a remote Pandora FMS server, --data_dir must point to that server's own data directory, not to the main server's.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
1. Confirm that the endpoint answers with a JSON list:

    curl -s 'http://<SPARK_HOST>:<SPARK_PORT>/api/v1/applications'

  2. Run the plugin once from a terminal on the Pandora FMS server:

    ./pandora_spark -i <SPARK_HOST>:<SPARK_PORT> -g <GROUP_NAME>

  3. A successful run prints 1 and exits with status 0. Then the data files are in the data directory:

    ls -l /var/spool/pandora/data_in/Spark_application*

    The files disappear as the Data Server processes them, so an empty listing shortly after the run can also mean that the documents were already consumed. Check the console instead.

  4. In the console, one agent per Spark application appears with its modules on the next data cycle.

If the endpoint cannot be reached, the run prints 0 on standard output and this message on standard error, then exits with status 1:

Error requesting http://<SPARK_HOST>:<SPARK_PORT>/api/v1/applications, please check conectivity

docs.title: Generated agents
docs.text:
The addon creates one agent per application returned by the first request. The agent is named after the application identifier, so an identifier such as application_1630567890123_0001 produces the agent name Spark_applicationapplication_1630567890123_0001: the prefix Spark_application is added in front of the identifier as Spark reports it, with no separator.

Property Value Agent name Spark_application followed by the application identifier Agent alias Spark_application followed by the application name Description Spark_application_detailed stats Address 127.0.0.1 Group The value of -g; weblogic when the option is omitted Parent agent None Interval Not set: the agent keeps the interval Pandora FMS assigns by default

Two consequences are worth knowing before you build alerts on these agents:

  • The address is fixed at 127.0.0.1 and does not identify the Spark server. In the console the agent looks local even when the endpoint is remote.
  • The application name is copied into the agent alias without escaping. A name that contains a single quote (') produces a document Pandora FMS cannot read, and the agent is not created.

docs.title: What one run delivers
docs.text:
• The plugin asks for the executor list of every application, one application after another, and builds each agent document from the executor data of that application.
  • One document is written per executor. Documents are named after the agent and the second of the run, so all the executors processed within the same second produce the same file name: the first one is kept and the following ones are discarded without any message. In practice a run delivers the modules of the first executor of each application, plus those of the executors that happen to be processed in a later second.
  • The module list is not reset between applications. The document of the second and following applications also carries a copy of the modules of the applications processed before it in the same run, so module names repeat inside one document. With a single application — the common case — this has no effect.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
Each executor produces 14 modules whose name is the executor identifier followed by the metric name, concatenated with no separator: an executor with identifier 1 publishes 1hostPort, 1rddBlocks, 1memoryUsed, and so on. The executor identifier is driver for the driver and a number for the other executors. Two applications that reuse the same executor identifiers produce modules with the same names, one set per agent.

id and hostPort are text modules (generic_data_string); the other twelve are numeric modules (generic_data) with no unit. The plugin copies every value as the API returns it: it does not convert, round, rescale or attach units, and it sets no thresholds and no alerts. The full list with the meaning of each value is in Generated modules.

docs.title: Everyday operation
docs.text:
• The plugin keeps no state between runs: every execution queries the endpoint at that moment, so it can be run manually at any time without affecting the next scheduled run.
  • There is no timeout on the requests. An endpoint that accepts the connection and does not answer keeps the run blocked until the Plugin Server timeout terminates it, so set a maximum timeout in the plugin definition.
  • There is no authentication support: no user, password, token or TLS client certificate. A Spark REST API that requires authentication answers 401, the plugin cannot read the answer as an application list, and the run ends with the connectivity error.
  • Only plain HTTP is used: every request goes to http://, so an endpoint that offers HTTPS only cannot be monitored by this addon.
  • The group defaults to weblogic. Agents created by a run that omits -g land in that group and are easy to miss in the console.
  • A failed write is silent: when the data directory does not exist or is not writable, the run still prints 1 and reports nothing. Do not use the output of the plugin to decide that the data arrived; check the console.
  • A run against a Spark endpoint with no application prints 1 and creates no agent. That is the expected result, not an error.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• The run prints 0 and the message Error requesting .../api/v1/applications — the first request did not return a readable application list. Check the port, the firewall between the Pandora FMS server and Spark, and that the endpoint answers curl from the same host. The same message appears when the answer is not JSON, including a 401 from an endpoint that requires authentication.
  • The run prints 0 and the message names .../executors — the application list was read, but the executors of the application in the message could not be. The run stops at that point: the documents of the applications already processed are written, the remaining ones are not. Check that the same port serves the executors resource of that application, which is not the case when the application moved to the history server in the meantime.
  • The run prints 1 but no agent appears in the console — the documents were not written or not read. Confirm that --data_dir is the data directory of the Pandora FMS server that is running, that it is writable by the plugin user, and that the Data Server is enabled. Remember that the plugin does not report write failures.
  • An agent shows fewer executors than the application has — the documents of the remaining executors were written within the same second and discarded because of the file name collision. Run the plugin again later, or accept that the addon publishes the first executor of each application per run.
  • The agent shows modules of another application — both applications were processed in the same run and the module list is shared between them. Run the plugin with one application per execution when you need a clean agent.
  • A module has no value or the agent is missing entirely — check the application name for a single quote, which breaks the document as explained in Generated agents.
  • The agents are in the wrong group — -g was omitted and the default weblogic was applied, or the registered macro has an empty value.
  • The metrics look frozen — the plugin reports the counters of the executor at the moment of the query. A finished application keeps the values of its last state in the history server, so a history-server endpoint shows the same numbers run after run. Use 4040 to follow a live application.

docs.title: Command-line options
docs.text:
Name Required Default Description -i, --ip Yes — Spark REST endpoint as host:port, without a scheme. The plugin calls http://<value>/api/v1/applications and http://<value>/api/v1/applications/<application-id>/executors. -g, --group No weblogic Group assigned to the generated agents. --data_dir No /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Directory where the agent documents are written. Must exist and be writable by the user that runs the plugin. -h, --help No — Prints the usage summary and exits.

The plugin reads no configuration file and no environment variable, and it accepts no credentials. A run without -i exits with status 2.

docs.title: Output and exit status
docs.text:
Situation Standard output Standard error Exit status Successful run 1 — 0 The applications request fails, or its answer is not a JSON list 0 Error requesting <url>, please check conectivity 1 The executors request of one application fails 0 Error requesting <url>, please check conectivity 1 -i is missing — Usage line and missing-argument error 2

A run that cannot write a data document still reports success: the failure is not reflected in the output nor in the exit status.

docs.title: Generated agents
docs.text: Property Value Agent name Spark_application + application identifier, concatenated with no separator Agent alias Spark_application + application name Description Spark_application_detailed stats Address 127.0.0.1 Group -g value; weblogic by default Parent agent None Interval Not set Timestamp Time of the run, YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS Cardinality One agent per application returned by the endpoint

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text:
<executor> is the executor identifier reported by Spark: driver for the driver and a number for each executor.

Module name Type Value <executor>id generic_data_string Executor identifier <executor>hostPort generic_data_string Host and port of the executor <executor>rddBlocks generic_data RDD blocks held by the executor <executor>memoryUsed generic_data Memory used, in bytes <executor>diskUsed generic_data Disk space used, in bytes <executor>activeTasks generic_data Tasks running in the executor <executor>failedTasks generic_data Tasks that failed in the executor <executor>completedTasks generic_data Tasks completed by the executor <executor>totalTasks generic_data Tasks assigned to the executor <executor>totalDuration generic_data Accumulated task time, in milliseconds <executor>totalInputBytes generic_data Bytes read by the executor <executor>totalShuffleRead generic_data Bytes read in shuffles <executor>totalShuffleWrite generic_data Bytes written in shuffles <executor>maxMemory generic_data Memory available to the executor

The two text modules are published with an empty unit; the numeric ones carry no unit. Values are forwarded as the API returns them, so a field that Spark reports with a unit in its text (as it does for maxMemory) reaches the module with that text, and the comparison, thresholds and representation of the module are up to Pandora FMS.

docs.title: Addon identity
docs.text: Field Value Marketplace identifier pandorafms.spark Marketplace name Pandora Spark Addon version 1.0 Marketplace package pandorafms.spark.1.0.pspz2 Marketplace last update 2025-06-27 License One — download limited to licensed users Marketplace type Miscelaneus Workflow Monitoring plugin, server plugin mode Executable pandora_spark

docs.title: Sybase monitoring plugin
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Sybase monitoring plugin monitors a Sybase ASE (Adaptive Server Enterprise) server from Pandora FMS. Each execution collects two kinds of data and turns them into Pandora FMS modules:

  • Server state, read with SQL. Through the Sybase isql utility the plugin reads the Adaptive Server catalogs: databases and their allocated and used space, transaction log and segment usage, user connections, locks, blocked processes, offline engines, suspect databases and suspect indexes.
  • Local process state. From the process list of the host the plugin reports whether the Adaptive Server and the backup server processes are running, and the memory and CPU they consume.

The plugin runs as a Pandora FMS agent plugin: every execution prints one XML <module> block per generated module on standard output, and the Pandora FMS agent installed on that host ingests them into the endpoint's agent. The plugin creates no agent and delivers no data by itself, so it is not a server plugin.

Because the process modules read the local process list, run the plugin on the host where the ASE server runs. Executed against a remote server, it reports the processes of the machine it runs on.

docs.title: Compatibility and availability
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.sybase, version 1.0 Documented target Marketplace entry; see Addon identity Windows 10 Known compatible The previous edition of this guide records Windows 10 as the tested system, and the Marketplace package is a Windows executable. Not re-validated for version 1.0 Operating systems other than Windows Not validated No test record; the Marketplace entry distributes a single Windows executable Sybase ASE versions and editions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded. The Marketplace states that all its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later A Sybase environment script that exists on the host Required The plugin stops with exit status 1 when sybase_env_script does not name an existing file The Sybase isql utility reachable from the host Required Every SQL check is executed through isql A Pandora FMS agent on the ASE host Required The plugin is executed as an agent plugin

The addon is published in the Pandora FMS Marketplace, with free download:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.sybase

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. A Sybase ASE server reachable from the host that runs the plugin, with the server name and port you configure.
  2. The Sybase isql utility and the Sybase environment script on that host. isql resolves from PATH by default, and on Unix-like systems the environment script is sourced before every query.
  3. A Sybase login that can read the catalogs and run the procedures of the checks you enable; see Sybase login.
  4. A Pandora FMS agent on the same host, which executes the plugin and ingests its modules.
  5. On Windows, the command-line utilities the plugin calls: grep, wc, tail, head, sed and gawk in PATH, together with tasklist and typeperf from Windows.

docs.title: Sybase login
docs.text:
Each check reads ASE system tables or runs an ASE stored procedure. The login needs access to the objects of the checks you enable:

Check Reads Sybase Databases in <server> sp_helpdb Sybase Max Size Available, Sybase Used Size global, Used size<database> master..sysdatabases, master..sysusages, curunreservedpgs, @@maxpagesize Sybase Connections Used Ratio, Sybase Connections Remaining master..sysprocesses, master..syslogins, sp_configure 'number of user connections' Sybase Num Blocked Processes sp_who Sybase Blocker Processes master..sysprocesses Sybase Engines Offline master..sysengines Sybase Suspect Databases master..sysdatabases Sybase Mirror Devices master..sysdevices Sybase Locks Remaining sysconfigures, syslocks Sybase Suspect Index sysindexes Log Space Used <database> sp_helpsegment logsegment Sybase Segment space [<segment>][<database>] sp_helpsegment

No official source defines a narrower grant list than these reads; grant only what the checks you enable need, and use a dedicated login for Pandora FMS.

The password is stored in the configuration file in plain text and passed to isql on its command line, so it is visible in the host process list while a query runs. Restrict the configuration file to the account that runs the agent and use a dedicated Sybase login.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text: Download the addon from its Marketplace entry. The entry distributes the executable pandorafms.sybase.1.0.exe: copy it to the plugins directory of the Pandora FMS agent on the ASE host, for example C:\Program Files\Pandora_Agent\plugins\, and create the pandora_sybase.conf configuration file next to it. The complete file is documented in Example configuration.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The plugin receives its configuration file as its only positional argument:

pandorafms.sybase.1.0.exe <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

The file is plain text with one key = value per line. Blank lines and lines that start with # are skipped, keys and values are trimmed, and when a key is repeated the last value wins.

Every scalar key can also be overridden on the command line without editing the file, with -key value pairs after the file path:

pandorafms.sybase.1.0.exe <PATH_TO_CONFIG> -debug 1 -username <USERNAME>

The per-target lists and the thresholds are read only from the file: passing them as flags has no effect (see Command-line execution).

docs.title: Connection settings
docs.text:
These keys identify the client environment and the main login:

GLOBAL_SERVERNAME = <ASE_SERVER_NAME>
sybase_env_script = /opt/sybase/SYBASE.sh
isql = isql
encryption = 0

username = <USERNAME>
password = <PASSWORD>
servername = <ASE_SERVER_NAME>
port = 5000
  • GLOBAL_SERVERNAME identifies the local Adaptive Server. It must appear in the command line of the local dataserver process, because the two status modules look for that process by this value.
  • sybase_env_script is the Sybase environment script. The plugin requires the file to exist on every platform and stops with Error, cannot found sybase environment script at [...] and exit status 1 when it does not. On Unix-like systems it is sourced before each isql call, so it must be safe to source in a non-interactive shell. On Windows it is not sourced, and the Sybase environment must already be present in the environment of the Pandora FMS agent.
  • isql is the command or full path of the Sybase isql utility. The default, isql, resolves it from PATH.
  • encryption = 1 adds the -X option to the isql invocation, which requests an encrypted connection. It requires the Sybase client to be configured for it.
  • username and password are the login used by every check that does not define its own credentials.
  • servername and port are passed to isql as -S <servername>:<port>. When the port key is absent, only the server name is passed.

docs.title: Per-database checks and login checks
docs.text:
Three numbered lists add checks on top of the server-wide modules. Each entry has a numeric suffix and its own format:

List Format Generated module check_dbsizeNN <database> Used percentage, log space, availability, and one segment module per segment of that database check_instanceNN <user>;<password>;<database> Sybase Instance '<database>' availability custom_checkNN <user>;<password>;<database> Sybase Login check <database> 
check_dbsize01 = <DB_NAME>
check_instance01 = <USERNAME>;<PASSWORD>;<DB_NAME>
custom_check01 = <USERNAME>;<PASSWORD>;<DB_NAME>
  • The suffix only distinguishes entries; the reference file numbers them from 01 upward. There is no total-count key: every entry present in the file is read.
  • Two entries that name the same database produce a single set of modules.
  • The third field of check_instanceNN and custom_checkNN is a database name, not an ASE server name: the plugin logs in to that database to test the credentials. The reference configuration file labels that field as an instance.
  • check_dbsizeNN entries use the main username and password, never their own.
  • The per-database modules of check_dbsizeNN, and the check_instanceNN modules, are generated only when the main login succeeds (see Understand the results). custom_checkNN modules are generated even when it fails.

docs.title: Enable the modules you need
docs.text:
Every server-wide and local module has its own switch. The value 1 enables the module; 0, an empty value or a missing key disables it. All switches are disabled by default, so the configuration file states explicitly which modules you want:

sybase_main_status = 1
sybase_backup_status = 1
sybase_memuse = 1
sybase_cpuusage = 1
sybase_count_databases = 1
sybase_max_size = 1
sybase_used_size = 1
sybase_connections_used_ratio = 1
sybase_available_connections = 1
sybase_blocked_processes = 1
sybase_offline_engines = 1
sybase_suspects_databases = 1

The full list, with the module each switch enables, is in Module switches.

docs.title: Register the plugin in the agent
docs.text:
The Pandora FMS agent executes agent plugins declared in its configuration file, pandora_agent.conf. Add one module_plugin line with the executable and the configuration file:

module_plugin "C:\Program Files\Pandora_Agent\plugins\pandorafms.sybase.1.0.exe" "C:\Program Files\Pandora_Agent\plugins\pandora_sybase.conf"

Restart the agent after the change. The agent executes the plugin at every agent interval and ingests the modules it prints, so the module interval is the interval of the agent that holds them. When the agent configuration is managed from the console, add the same line through the console instead of editing the file on the host.

Only one agent should run the plugin for a given ASE server: two agents executing it against the same server create two separate sets of modules.

docs.title: Credentials and transport
docs.text:
• The configuration file holds the main password and the password of every check_instanceNN and custom_checkNN entry in plain text. Restrict its permissions to the account that runs the agent.
  • Every query passes the password to isql as a command-line argument, so the password is visible in the process list of the host while a query runs. Keep the credentials in the configuration file: a -username or -password override typed on the command line also remains in the shell history of the host.
  • encryption = 1 adds -X to every isql call, which asks the Sybase client for an encrypted connection. Confirm that the client and the server are configured for it before enabling the option; otherwise the login checks fail.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually, passing the configuration file as its only positional argument:

pandorafms.sybase.1.0.exe <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

A successful run prints one XML <module> block per generated module on standard output and exits with status 0. The excerpt below shows four of them; the values are illustrative:

<module>
    <name><![CDATA[Sybase ASE status]]></name>
    <type>generic_proc</type>
    <data><![CDATA[1]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[The status of the Adaptive Server]]></description>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[Sybase Memory Use]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[120.63]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[Sybase memory use in MB]]></description>
    <unit><![CDATA[MB]]></unit>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[Sybase Database <DB_NAME> availability]]></name>
    <type>generic_proc</type>
    <data><![CDATA[1]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[Availability for <DB_NAME>]]></description>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[Log Space Used <DB_NAME>]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[18.40]]></data>
    <unit><![CDATA[%]]></unit>
</module>
  • pandorafms.sybase.1.0.exe -h prints the usage summary and exits with status 0. The summary goes to standard error, not standard output, and -h is recognised only as the first argument.
  • A run that cannot find the environment script prints Error, cannot found sybase environment script at [...] on standard error, followed by the usage summary, and exits with status 1.
  • A run whose queries fail still exits with status 0: the failing modules are simply missing from the output. Use debug = 1 to see the reason (see Operate and troubleshoot).

Once the agent is restarted, the modules appear in the console under the endpoint's agent:

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
The modules fall into four groups:

  • Local host. Sybase ASE status and Sybase ASE Backup server status report 1 while the local dataserver and backupserver processes are running, and 0 otherwise. They are process checks, not connectivity checks: they say nothing about whether isql can reach the server. Sybase Memory Use and Sybase CPU Busy describe the local Adaptive Server process.
  • Server-wide. Sybase Databases in <server>, Sybase Max Size Available, Sybase Used Size global, Sybase Connections Used Ratio, Sybase Connections Remaining, Sybase Num Blocked Processes, Sybase Blocker Processes, Sybase Engines Offline, Sybase Suspect Databases, Sybase Mirror Devices, Sybase Locks Remaining, Sybase Suspect Index and Used size all databases are read with SQL from the configured server.
  • Per database. Every check_dbsizeNN entry adds Used size<database>, Log Space Used <database>, Sybase Database <database> availability and one Sybase Segment space [<segment>][<database>] module per segment of the database.
  • Login checks. Every check_instanceNN entry adds an availability module and every custom_checkNN entry adds a login check module, both reporting 1 when the login succeeds and 0 otherwise.

The main login gates the SQL modules. Before the server-wide checks, the plugin logs in with username and password. When that login fails, the server-wide modules and the check_dbsizeNN and check_instanceNN modules are not generated at all, and no module reports the failure; only the local modules and the custom_checkNN checks still appear. Use debug = 1 to see the isql error.

Thresholds. Numeric modules carry the warning and critical thresholds defined in the configuration file under thresholds.<key>.<wmin|wmax|cmin|cmax>; Pandora FMS evaluates them as any other module threshold. See Thresholds for the keys and the reference values.

Order. The modules generated from check_dbsizeNN, check_instanceNN and custom_checkNN are not emitted in configuration order and their order varies between runs.

docs.title: Operate and troubleshoot
docs.text:
The plugin keeps no state between runs: every execution queries the server and the local process list at that moment, so it can be executed manually at any time without affecting the next scheduled run.

Set debug = 1 to publish diagnostics on standard error. Every message is prefixed with a timestamp, and the channel reports the isql error text and the segment parsing failures; without it the plugin stays silent about failed queries.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
These behaviours belong to the current version:

  • Error-log modules. sybase_errorlog_size, sybase_errorlog and sybase_errorlog_updates exist as switches, but no configuration key sets the Sybase log directory in this version. The size module reports 0.00, the path module reports an empty value and the update counter receives no directory, so leave the three switches disabled.
  • sybase_logsize. The reference configuration file sets this key, but no check reads it.
  • Per-database percentage name. The module concatenates the prefix and the database name without a separating space: a database named master produces Used sizemaster.
  • Per-database percentages. sybase_used_size_percent enables only Used size all databases; the per-database percentages are created by check_dbsizeNN.
  • Memory unit. Sybase Memory Use publishes the value with unit MB; on Unix-like systems the value is the sum of the %MEM column of the process list.
  • No failure module. A failing main login leaves no module behind; diagnose it with debug = 1.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• Error, cannot found sybase environment script at [...] and exit status 1 — sybase_env_script is empty or does not name an existing file. Point it at the Sybase environment script of the host, for example C:\SAP\...\SYBASE.bat on Windows or /opt/sybase/SYBASE.sh on Unix-like systems. The plugin requires the file even on Windows, where it does not source it.
  • The plugin prints the usage summary and no module XML — -h was passed as the first argument, or the configuration file path does not exist. A path that does not exist is not reported as a missing file: it is read as a configuration override, and the run then stops with the environment-script error.
  • No server-wide module appears, but the local modules do — the main login failed, so every SQL module was skipped. Run with debug = 1 and check the isql error: wrong username or password, a servername or port that does not resolve, or a login without access to the catalogs.
  • Sybase ASE status is 0 while the server is running — GLOBAL_SERVERNAME does not appear in the command line of the local dataserver process. Set it to the name that the process reports.
  • Sybase Memory Use and Sybase CPU Busy report 0 — the plugin is not running on the host of the ASE server, or the local account cannot see the server process in the process list.
  • A check_dbsizeNN database has no modules — the main login failed, or the database name in the entry does not exist. A missing database produces the availability module with value 0; the segment modules are then omitted and, with debug = 1, the segment parsing error is reported.
  • Sybase Segment space [...] modules are missing for a database — system databases sybsystemprocs, sybsystemdb, model and tempdb are skipped by design, and a database whose segments cannot be read produces no segment module.
  • Used size<database> or Log Space Used <database> reports 0 — the login cannot read master..sysusages or run sp_helpsegment, or the database does not exist.
  • The error-log modules report 0.00, an empty path or nothing — this version does not read the Sybase log directory from the configuration, so sybase_errorlog_size, sybase_errorlog and sybase_errorlog_updates cannot produce a value. Leave them disabled; see Known limitations.
  • The modules are not in the console — check that the module_plugin line points to the executable and the configuration file, that the agent was restarted, and that the agent can execute the file. The agent log records the execution result.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The file uses key = value lines. Blank lines and lines that start with # are skipped, keys and values are trimmed, and the last occurrence of a repeated key wins. Numbers are read as text, so write 1 to enable a switch and 0 to disable it.

Name Required Default Description GLOBAL_SERVERNAME Yes — Name of the local Adaptive Server. It must appear in the command line of the local dataserver process and it is used in the error-log module name. sybase_env_script Yes Empty Sybase environment script. Sourced before every isql call on Unix-like systems; the file must exist on every platform. isql No isql Command or full path of the Sybase isql utility. encryption No 0 1 adds the -X option to every isql call. username Yes — Login for the main checks and for check_dbsizeNN. password Yes — Password of username. servername Yes — ASE server name, passed to isql with -S. port No Absent (no port) Port passed to isql as <servername>:<port>. When the key is absent, only the server name is passed. debug No 0 1 prints timestamped diagnostics on standard error. check_dbsizeNN No — <database>. Adds the used percentage, log space, availability and segment modules of that database. check_instanceNN No — <user>;<password>;<database>. Adds Sybase Instance '<database>' availability. custom_checkNN No — <user>;<password>;<database>. Adds Sybase Login check <database>. grep_log No Empty Path of the grep_log helper used by the error-log update check. That check cannot produce a value in this version. custom_error_terms No Built-in term list Regular expression of terms counted by the error-log update check.

docs.title: Module switches
docs.text:
Key Module enabled sybase_main_status Sybase ASE status sybase_backup_status Sybase ASE Backup server status sybase_memuse Sybase Memory Use sybase_cpuusage Sybase CPU Busy sybase_count_databases Sybase Databases in <server> sybase_max_size Sybase Max Size Available sybase_used_size Sybase Used Size global sybase_used_size_percent Used size all databases; the per-database percentages come from check_dbsizeNN sybase_connections_used_ratio Sybase Connections Used Ratio sybase_available_connections Sybase Connections Remaining sybase_blocked_processes Sybase Num Blocked Processes sybase_blocker_processes Sybase Blocker Processes sybase_offline_engines Sybase Engines Offline sybase_suspects_databases Sybase Suspect Databases sybase_mirror_devices Sybase Mirror Devices sybase_locks_remaining Sybase Locks Remaining sybase_suspect_index Sybase Suspect Index sybase_errorlog_size Error Log Size; cannot produce a value in this version sybase_errorlog Sybase ErrorLog path; cannot produce a value in this version sybase_errorlog_updates Error-log update counter; cannot produce a value in this version

The reference configuration file enables twelve of these switches and also sets sybase_logsize, a key that no check reads. To enable the error-log size module, use sybase_errorlog_size.

docs.title: Thresholds
docs.text:
Each numeric module publishes the thresholds defined for its key. A key whose value is empty leaves the threshold unset; 0 is a real value. These are the values in the reference configuration file:

Key Module wmin wmax cmin cmax sybase_used_size Used size<database> 90 95 95 100 sybase_used_size_all Used size all databases 85 90 90 100 sybase_memuse Sybase Memory Use — — — — sybase_cpuusage Sybase CPU Busy — — 90 100 sybase_connections_used_ratio Sybase Connections Used Ratio 85 — 90 — sybase_available_connections Sybase Connections Remaining 5 15 0 5 sybase_blocked_processes Sybase Num Blocked Processes 0 0 1 0 sybase_blocker_processes Sybase Blocker Processes 0 0 1 0 sybase_offline_engines Sybase Engines Offline 0 0 1 0 sybase_suspects_databases Sybase Suspect Databases 0 0 1 0 sybase_locks_remaining Sybase Locks Remaining 50 100 0 50 sybase_segment_space Sybase Segment space [...] 80 0 90 0 sybase_suspect_index Sybase Suspect Index 0 0 1 0 sybase_errorlog_size Error Log Size 100 — 250 —

The threshold keys have no effect on modules that do not publish thresholds, such as Sybase Max Size Available and Sybase Used Size global.

docs.title: Command-line execution
docs.text:
pandorafms.sybase.1.0.exe [config-file] [-key value ...]
Condition Behavior The first argument is -h Prints the usage summary on standard error and exits with status 0 No argument at all Prints the environment-script error and the usage summary on standard error and exits with status 1 The first argument names an existing file Runs with that file and the remaining flags The first argument names a file that does not exist Treats the path as a configuration override and stops with the environment-script error; exit status 1 -key value Overrides the configuration value with the same key -key=value Not an override: the whole token becomes a configuration key and has no effect An odd trailing argument Ignored check_dbsizeNN, check_instanceNN, custom_checkNN or thresholds.* as a flag No effect; these are read only from the configuration file

The plugin leaves the exit status at 0 when individual queries fail, and reports the failure only through the missing modules and the debug = 1 diagnostics.

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text:
In the names below, <server> is the value of servername, <database> a database of a check_dbsizeNN entry and <segment> a segment of that database:

Module name Type Enabled by Meaning Sybase ASE status generic_proc sybase_main_status 1 while the local dataserver process matching GLOBAL_SERVERNAME runs, 0 otherwise Sybase ASE Backup server status generic_proc sybase_backup_status 1 while the local backupserver process matching GLOBAL_SERVERNAME runs, 0 otherwise. On Windows the process is bcksrvr.exe Sybase Memory Use generic_data, unit MB sybase_memuse Memory used by the local Adaptive Server process, as reported by the process list Sybase CPU Busy generic_data, unit % sybase_cpuusage CPU used by the local Adaptive Server process Sybase Databases in <server> generic_data sybase_count_databases Databases listed by sp_helpdb, excluding those marked dbo use only Sybase Max Size Available generic_data, unit MB sybase_max_size Space allocated to all databases, excluding log segments Sybase Used Size global generic_data, unit MB sybase_used_size Used space of all databases, excluding log segments Used size all databases generic_data, unit % sybase_used_size_percent Used percentage of the space allocated to all databases; 0 when the allocated size cannot be read Sybase Connections Used Ratio generic_data, unit % sybase_connections_used_ratio User connections in use against the configured maximum Sybase Connections Remaining generic_data sybase_available_connections Configured maximum minus the connections in use Sybase Num Blocked Processes generic_data sybase_blocked_processes sp_who entries in lock sleep state Sybase Blocker Processes generic_data sybase_blocker_processes Processes holding locks and blocking other processes Sybase Engines Offline generic_data sybase_offline_engines Engines reported as offline in master..sysengines Sybase Suspect Databases generic_data sybase_suspects_databases Databases with status 256 or 320 Sybase Mirror Devices generic_data sybase_mirror_devices Devices configured for mirroring that are not currently mirrored Sybase Locks Remaining generic_data sybase_locks_remaining Configured locks minus the locks in syslocks Sybase Suspect Index generic_data sybase_suspect_index Indexes marked as suspect Used size<database> generic_data, unit % check_dbsizeNN Used percentage of the space allocated to the database Log Space Used <database> generic_data, unit % check_dbsizeNN Used percentage of the transaction log segment of the database Sybase Database <database> availability generic_proc check_dbsizeNN 1 when isql logs in to the database, 0 otherwise Sybase Segment space [<segment>][<database>] generic_data, unit % check_dbsizeNN Used percentage of each segment of the database Sybase Instance '<database>' availability generic_proc check_instanceNN 1 when the entry credentials log in to the database, 0 otherwise Sybase Login check <database> generic_proc custom_checkNN 1 when the entry credentials log in to the database, 0 otherwise

docs.title: Example configuration
docs.text:
# Local server identification
GLOBAL_SERVERNAME = <ASE_SERVER_NAME>

# Sybase client environment
sybase_env_script = /opt/sybase/SYBASE.sh
isql = isql
encryption = 0

# Main login
username = <USERNAME>
password = <PASSWORD>
servername = <ASE_SERVER_NAME>
port = 5000

# Per-database checks
check_dbsize01 = <DB_NAME>

# Login checks
custom_check01 = <USERNAME>;<PASSWORD>;<DB_NAME>

# Modules
sybase_main_status = 1
sybase_backup_status = 1
sybase_memuse = 1
sybase_cpuusage = 1
sybase_count_databases = 1
sybase_max_size = 1
sybase_used_size = 1
sybase_connections_used_ratio = 1
sybase_available_connections = 1
sybase_blocked_processes = 1
sybase_offline_engines = 1
sybase_suspects_databases = 1

# Thresholds
thresholds.sybase_used_size.wmin = 90
thresholds.sybase_used_size.wmax = 95
thresholds.sybase_used_size.cmin = 95
thresholds.sybase_used_size.cmax = 100
thresholds.sybase_segment_space.wmin = 80
thresholds.sybase_segment_space.cmin = 90
